### `sw.js` [verified 2026-10-06, `CACHE_VERSION` "oros-v0.39.06"]

- **Caches:** `oros-shell-<CACHE_VERSION>` (precache), `oros-runtime-<CACHE_VERSION>` (everything fetched while controlled), `oros-map-tiles` (outside the version, survives updates), and `oros-television-api` (owned by the Television app, only kept alive here). `activate` deletes every other cache of the origin.
- **Install:** `skipWaiting()`; one `fetch(new Request(u, {cache:"reload"}))` + `cache.put` per URL (SWK-1: straight from the network, never from the HTTP cache). A server error (404) is logged (`[SW] precache MISS`) and does not abort the install. **SW-T2 (2026-10-11):** while an older worker is active (an update), a NETWORK failure on any URL fails the install, so the old release keeps serving instead of activating half a precache and deleting the old one; the attempt leaves `PARTIAL_MARK` in the new shell cache and the next attempt downloads only what is missing. The first install stays tolerant. **SW-T4 (2026-11-01):** a phone stayed on 4.66.00 for a day while main reached 4.92.00: one precache file that the network never delivered failed every update attempt, and an attempt the browser killed (a request that never answered) left no marker, so each attempt started over. Now each precache download fails after `PRECACHE_FETCH_MS` (30 s, aborted); a file that failed gets `PRECACHE_TRIES` (2) tries per attempt; the update writes `PARTIAL_MARK` at the START with the attempt number, so a killed attempt resumes; attempts count across releases (the highest marker in any older shell cache); from attempt `PRECACHE_GIVE_UP` (3) the release activates without the files it could not reach (logged), and they come from the network when used. Tests: tests/sw-network.test.js.
- **Incremental update (SW-U1/SW-U2, 2026-10-18):** a release no longer downloads the whole precache (1,658 files, 46 MB in 3.19.00). The release stamp on main (`stamp-assets.js`, after the `?v=` and CSP pass) writes `var PRECACHE_HASH = {url: first 16 hex of SHA-256}` into sw.js. At install a file whose copy in a previous `oros-shell-*` cache hashes to that value is copied from it; anything else (changed, no entry, no old copy, no `crypto.subtle`) is downloaded as before. The old copy is hashed in the worker before reuse, so a stale copy or a stale table costs a download, never old code. At most `PRECACHE_POOL` (4) files at a time, `priority: "low"`, so the page keeps the network. Measured at 10 Mbps: background update 73 s → 15 s, 49 MB → about 1.6 MB.
- **`PRECACHE_URLS` (127 entries):** the shell page and its 8 scripts + 2 stylesheets, `apps.json`, manifest, icons; for each of the 24 apps `<app>/`, `index.html`, `.css`, `.js` (plus `time/astro.js`, `minimalism/content.js`); `vendor/leaflet.css`, `vendor/leaflet.js`, `vendor/jspdf.umd.min.js`, `vendor/hls.light.min.js`, `vendor/NotoSans-Regular.ttf`; five Nunito `woff2` files. All UNVERSIONED (no `?v=`). Not in the list: `vendor/xlsx` (A51).
- **Activate:** purge old caches → `trimTileCache()` → `clients.claim()`; a 30 s guard claims anyway if the cleanup hangs (the timer is cancelled on the normal path, SWK-2). **It claims**, so `controllerchange` fires on a first install too: the broker ignores that one (SW-4).
- **Fetch (GET only):**
  - Tile hosts (`TILE_HOSTS` + any subdomain): cache-first in `oros-map-tiles`; only `resp.ok` is stored; a legacy opaque hit is a miss for a CORS request; trim to `TILE_MAX` 2000 every 100 puts and once per activation; offline and uncached → `Response.error()`.
  - Other origins: untouched.
  - `…/apps.json` (`isAppsList()`): network-first with `{cache:"no-store"}`, cached copy as the fallback. SW-T3 (2026-10-11): the old test matched every 9-character path too (`/shell.js`, `/vault.js`, `/icon.svg`), so those went network-first.
  - **Network timeout (SW-T1, 2026-10-11):** both network-first branches go through `networkFirst()`. The network gets `NET_TIMEOUT_MS` (3 s); then a cached copy answers and the network answer, if it still arrives, refreshes the cache in the background. With no cached copy the request keeps waiting for the network. After one timeout, for `NET_SLOW_MS` (30 s) network-first answers from the cache at once; a network answer inside the timeout ends that spell.
  - **App frames (SW-F1, 2026-10-18):** a navigation of an app frame (destination `iframe`/`frame`, path not `/` or `/index.html`) is answered at once by THIS release's precached page (`releasePage()`: `SHELL_CACHE.match(origin + pathname, {ignoreVary})`, see SW-K1; a redirected copy does not count); only a miss goes network-first as below. Network-first made every app open wait up to `NET_TIMEOUT_MS` on a bad connection, and when a newer release was already live the fresh page fetched every script under its new `?v=` from the network (Calendar showed about 10 s of empty boxes). The precached page and its scripts are one release (`releaseCopy()`), and a new release reaches the frames through the worker update and the broker's `controllerchange` reload. The shell page (`/`, also `?solo=` frames) and a direct app open in the top window stay network-first. `tests/sw-network.test.js` also checks that every app page and every script/stylesheet it loads is precached.
  - **Shell page and apps.json (SW-F2, 2026-10-18):** the same holds for EVERY navigation (the shell page `/` with any query, `?solo=` frames, direct app opens) and for `apps.json`: this release's precached copy answers at once, network-first only on a miss. Right after a release the old network-first shell page fetched every shell script under the new `?v=` from the network while the update downloaded beside it: measured 72 s on a slow connection (3.35.00 → 3.36.00), 0.55 s now. A new release arrives in the background (sw.js checked on every navigation, `update()` from the broker on every load) and the broker's `controllerchange` reload brings it at the first safe moment (SW-2). The broker comment in index.html no longer says the page is network-first.
  - **Exact keys, no ignoreSearch scan (SW-K1, 2026-10-20):** `releasePage()` and `releaseCopy()` look up `origin + pathname` (the precache keys carry no query) instead of `match(request, {ignoreSearch})`. Chrome answers an ignoreSearch match by reading every entry of the cache (about 1,800 in the shell cache), so on the first open after the browser started each shell script cost about 180 ms through the worker, one after another: 8.8 s of "--:--" before the desktop at 4× CPU, the same in every app frame; 1.0 s now. The only ignoreSearch matches left are the offline fallback and the small WebLLM cache. `tests/sw-network.test.js` checks that no lookup of this release scans the shell cache.
  - Navigations: `fetch(…, {cache:"no-cache"})`; stored when `ok`, not redirected (SWK-4) and without `code=`; offline → the cached page; else, for the TOP window, the precached `./index.html`; for an app frame a small bilingual "not saved for offline use yet" page with status 503 (SWK-3: it used to load the shell inside the frame).
  - Sub-resources: cache-first by EXACT URL; then the release copy (below); then the network (a 200 is stored in the runtime cache); offline and still nothing → a loose `ignoreSearch` match across caches.
- **Release copy (SW-D1, 2026-10-06):** `RELEASE` = `CACHE_VERSION` without `oros-v`. A sub-resource request whose `?v=` equals `RELEASE` and has no exact hit is answered from THIS release's precache (`releaseCopy()`: `SHELL_CACHE.match(request, {ignoreSearch, ignoreVary})`). A request with any other stamp, or with none, takes the old path. Each `.js` / `.css` is now downloaded once per release instead of twice (measured). No change to `PRECACHE_URLS` and none to the pipeline: it only relies on the Action writing the same version into `CACHE_VERSION` and into `?v=`, which it does in one pass.
- The comment "full banner history in CHANGELOG" is stale (the changelog is Part XII of this file).

### `fs.js` (orosFS) [verified 2026-10-06, `FS_VERSION` 0.1.0]

- One IIFE, ES5 + promises. One mount, `/internal`. Paths are absolute (`/internal/a/b.txt`); `..` is rejected; `/` alone is the mount root.
- **Two drivers, one API:** OPFS (handles under the OPFS root directory `internal`) and IndexedDB (`oros-ofs`, store `nodes`, key = full path, value `{ dir, mtime, blob }`). They are two different places: a file written through one is invisible through the other.
- **Backend choice (FS-1, FS-2):**
  - OPFS counts only when the page can WRITE it: `navigator.storage.getDirectory` AND `FileSystemFileHandle.prototype.createWritable` (Safari has the first since 15.2 and the second only since 26).
  - The choice is pinned per device in `oros-ofs-backend` (`opfs` | `indexeddb`). Pinned `indexeddb` → IndexedDB whatever the browser offers. Pinned `opfs` → OPFS, and if it cannot be opened the disk is unavailable (`EIO`), never a second empty disk. Not pinned yet: an existing OPFS disk wins, else an existing IndexedDB disk, else OPFS when writable; a failed OPFS open without a pin falls back for the session and pins nothing.
- **Public API (`window.orosFS`):** `version`, `INTERNAL_ROOT`, `ready()` → mode, `capabilities.opfs`, `mode()`, `read` / `readBlob`, `readText`, `write` / `writeBlob`, `writeText`, `ls` → `[{name, dir}]` sorted by name, `mkdir` (recursive), `rm` (recursive), `mv`, `stat` → `{path, dir, size, mtime}`, `exportDisk()`, `importDisk(payload, {wipe?})` → `{applied, failed[]}`, `isDirty`, `clearDirty`, `usage()` (origin-wide estimate), `wipe()`, `selftest()`. R35: never rename, only add.
- **Errors:** an `Error` with a STRING `code`: `ENOENT`, `EISDIR` (also "a file is where a directory is needed" and the reverse), `EINVAL` (bad path, move into itself), `EPERM` (remove the root), `EIO` (backend unavailable). On OPFS a mapped error keeps the DOMException `name` too (`NotFoundError`, `TypeMismatchError`). Both drivers answer the same code for the same situation (verified).
- **Rules both drivers follow:** write creates missing parent directories; writing over a directory, creating a directory over a file, and moving a file onto a directory fail with `EISDIR` and change nothing; `mv(a, a)` and `mv(dir, dir/inside)` are refused; a directory moved onto an existing directory merges into it; `ls` and `exportDisk` of a never-written disk are empty, not errors.
- **Export format:** `{ ver:1, backend, at, entries[{ path, dir, mtime, data? }] }`, file content as a base64 data URL (the whole disk in memory: fine for a small disk, not for a large one). `importDisk` MERGES by default (never deletes what the payload lacks) and collects per-entry failures instead of aborting.
- **Dirty flag** `oros-ofs-dirty` (`wipe()` clears it). **Vault notifications (FS-6):** after a successful `write` → `orosVault.fileChanged(path)`; after `rm` → `orosVault.touchTree(path)`; after `mv` → `touchTree(src)` and `touchTree(dst)`. `mkdir` and `wipe` report nothing (empty folders are not synced; an emptied disk is not a set of deletions).
- Boot line `[orOS] fs.js v0.1.0 booted (backend: opfs|indexeddb, binary-ready: yes)`, or `backend: NONE — all ops will fail`.
- OPFS and the PWA: both drivers need a secure context; files live in the browser profile, subject to the browser's storage eviction (the shell asks for `storage.persist()`).

### `dialogs.js` (orosDialog) [verified 2026-10-06]

- One IIFE, ES5, no dependencies, no version number. Boot line `[orOS] dialogs.js ready — native|download`. Feature detection only, never browser sniffing.
- **`saveFile({ blob | text, filename, mime, types? })`** → `Promise<{ ok, mode }>`; it never rejects.
  - With `showSaveFilePicker`: picker (`suggestedName`, optional `types` passed through) → `createWritable()` → `write(blob)` → `close()` → `{ok:true, mode:"native"}`. `AbortError` (the user cancelled) → `{ok:false, mode:"native"}`. A failed write aborts the writable (DLG-2); it and every other failure (`SecurityError` after the activation expired, a malformed `types`) end in the download fallback.
  - Without it: `downloadFallback()`: hidden `<a download>` clicked and removed at once, blob URL revoked after 40 s (DLG-1) → `{ok:true, mode:"download"}`. "ok" then means "dispatched": the browser owns the rest.
  - Defaults: `filename` "orOS-export.txt"; `text` becomes a `text/plain` Blob unless `mime` says otherwise.
- **`openFile(accept)`** → `Promise<File|null>`; **`openFiles(accept)`** → `Promise<File[]|null>`. Native picker when present, UNFILTERED (`accept` is ignored there; accepted, see Part IX); otherwise a one-shot hidden `<input type="file">` that honors `accept` and resolves `null` on the `cancel` event.
- **`mode()`** → `"native"` only when both pickers exist, else `"download"`.
- The shell hosts it; apps reach it through `window.parent.orosDialog` (R33). A click inside an app frame activates the parent document too, so pickers and downloads started from the parent work (download path verified from a child frame).
- Known limits: a browser without the `cancel` event (before Chrome 113 / Firefox 91 / Safari 16.4) never resolves a dismissed input pick; the input fallback after a native failure needs a still-valid user activation.

### `vault.js` (Vault Drive, `window.orosVault`) [verified 2026-10-06; the file says version "0.1.0", older notes call it v0.1.1]

- One IIFE, ES5. Everything is late-bound (`orosSync`, `orosSync.storage`, `orosSync.vaultCrypto`, `orosFS`), so loading before `fs.js` is fine (A24 closed for this file). Usable only when connected AND unlocked.
- **Cloud (VD-KEY, 2026-10-06):**
  - `key.json` = `{ ver:1, wraps:[…] }`: one random 32-byte vault key, each wrap = that key sealed with a passphrase (`encryptJson({k})`). Created with a create-only write; `sync.js` re-wraps it on a passphrase change.
  - From the vault key: an AES-GCM key (SHA-256 of `"orOS-vault-enc:"` + key) and an HMAC-SHA-256 key (`"orOS-vault-name:"` + key).
  - `manifest.json` = envelope `0x02 | iv(12) | AES-GCM(JSON { ver:2, files{ <full path>: { h, s, m, mime } } })`; `h` = SHA-256 of the plaintext, visible only inside the manifest.
  - `objects/<hex HMAC(h)>` = the same envelope around the file content. The provider sees neither names, nor contents, nor content hashes.
  - LEGACY (written before VD-KEY): a manifest that is passphrase-sealed JSON text (first byte `{`), objects `objects/<h>` in the passphrase envelope. Read as entries marked `v:1`; an entry is converted when a device that holds the file pushes it again (done automatically at the next sync); the legacy object is deleted only after the new manifest has landed.
  - The vault key lives in memory only (`vaultKeys`). It is looked up again when a manifest cannot be opened with it, and whenever the cloud has no manifest (the vault is being created or was wiped).
- **Local keys (device-local):** `oros-vault-ondemand` and `oros-vault-offline` (VD-OD below), `oros-vault-queue` (map path → generation; an older list is still read), `oros-vault-manifest` (cache of what this device has synced), `oros-vault-rev` (manifest revision of the last sync in which every file was applied; lets an idle check skip the download), `oros-vault-absent-at`, `oros-vault-seeded` (this device's disk was queued once), `oros-vault-conflicts` (path → remote hash already kept as a copy).
- **API:** `version`, `fileChanged(path)`, `fileDeleted(path)` (both queue the path), `touchTree(path)` → promise of the count queued (every synced path at or under it + every file found there now), `status()` → `{ usable, queued, busy, lastError, lastOkAt }`, `sync(reason)` → `{ ok, stats{downloaded, uploaded, deleted, kept, failed} }` or `{ ok, skipped }`, rejects `vault busy` when one is running, `isQueued`, `queueLength`, `onStatus(fn)` → unsubscribe function (`start`, `done`, `fail`, `conflict-retry`, `file-fail`, `stats`, and the silent `queue`), `manifestEntry(path)`, `localPaths()`.
- **Triggers:** 3 s after the last queued change; tab hidden (only if something is queued); tab visible; `online`; 4 s after boot; and after every successful engine cycle (`orosSync.onAutoSync` "done"): one metadata call when nothing moved.
- **One sync = `attempt()`:** disk ready (`orosFS.ready()`, an `EIO` stops here) → fetch manifest → apply remote → if anything is queued, upload and write the manifest conditionally on the rev just fetched (`null` = "no manifest may exist yet") → on `storage-conflict` start over, at most 2 retries.
- **Rules (2026-10-06, each one a reproduced loss before):**
  - VD-1 · An ABSENT manifest deletes nothing. Everything this device holds as synced is queued again and goes back up. Deletions are inferred only from a manifest that exists.
  - VD-2 · The 60 s "absent" cache is used only while this device has nothing queued and nothing synced.
  - VD-3 · A queued path whose file is gone is a deletion (`ENOENT`); a queued folder is skipped; any other read error leaves the path queued.
  - VD-4 · Before a remote version replaces a local file, and before a remote deletion removes one, the local content is checked (`localState`: size, then SHA-256) against what was last synced. Content the vault never synced stays and is queued ("local wins", the same rule as the queue).
  - VD-5 · A path leaves the queue only if its generation is still the one the sync picked up; a file saved during a sync stays queued.
  - VD-6 · Files are processed one at a time, the local manifest is saved after each applied change, and a failing file is counted (`failed`) without stopping the others.
  - An object is uploaded only when no manifest entry already has its hash AND an existence probe confirms it is really stored.
  - FILES-V · The module's own writes and removals (`ownWrite`, `ownRemove`) are path-counted so the notification `fs.js` sends back for them is ignored, while a user change to another file at the same moment is not.
  - FILES-V · Both sides changed one file (local content is neither what was synced nor what the cloud has): local stays at its path and is pushed, the cloud's version is written beside it as a conflict copy (once per remote version). Deleted here while edited elsewhere: the edit is restored.
  - FILES-V · `seedOnce()`: the first sync of a device queues every file of its disk.
  - VD-H (2026-10-07) · A downloaded object is accepted only when its plaintext hashes to the manifest entry's `h` (`checkedPlain`, legacy objects too); otherwise the file counts as failed and local stays. AES-GCM alone does not bind an object to a path: anyone with write access to the app folder could swap or roll back objects.
- **VD-OD · orOS Drive folders on demand (2026-10-16).** Files under `/internal/Drive` (folders the native orOS Drive app, koulaxizis/oros-drive, mirrors from computers and phones) are not downloaded by a sync unless this device already holds them or a folder above them is kept offline:
  - a cloud entry under `/internal/Drive` that this device never held (no cached entry, nothing at the path, not queued) goes into `oros-vault-ondemand` (path → entry, device-local) instead of being downloaded; the list is rebuilt from every downloaded manifest and kept as it is on an idle check (`same`), cleared when the cloud has no manifest;
  - **the manifest a device writes = its local manifest + every cloud entry it did not apply** (`manifestToWrite`: on-demand entries and entries whose download failed in this sync, minus the paths this push deletes). Before, a device wrote only its local cache, so a file whose download failed was dropped from the cloud and every other device deleted it (reproduced in `tests/vault-ondemand.test.js`);
  - `fetch(path)` downloads one on-demand file (hash-checked, `ownWrite`), moves its entry into the local manifest, and from then on it syncs like any other file; `evict(folder)` removes from the disk the Drive files under it that are exactly what was synced (VD-4 "clean") and moves their entries back to the on-demand list; queued, edited or kept-offline files stay; nothing is deleted in the cloud. Both run between syncs (`betweenSyncs`), never inside one;
  - `oros-vault-offline` (device-local list of Drive folders): `setKeptOffline(folder, on)` forgets the cached rev and syncs, so the folder is downloaded and kept; a kept folder is never evicted;
  - deleting a downloaded Drive file deletes it everywhere (it is an ordinary synced file); deleting a folder in the disk view of Files deletes only the files of it this device holds;
  - **VD-OD-RM (2026-10-17) · delete in the cloud:** `removeRemote(path)` (between syncs; a path strictly under `driveRoot`, never the root itself) takes every on-demand entry at or under `path` into the local manifest exactly as listed and queues it. With nothing on the disk the next push reads it as a deletion (VD-3), the same as a synced file deleted here; a version changed elsewhere in the meantime has another hash, so the pull downloads it and the edit wins (VD-4). Files › orOS Drive deletes a row (bin button or Delete key, confirm dialog naming how many files are only in the cloud) by moving what the disk holds to the Files Trash first (if that fails nothing is deleted in the cloud), then `removeRemote`, then a sync. orOS Drive on computers and phones moves its copies to its trash (mirror rule). Tests in `tests/vault-ondemand.test.js`;
  - API: `driveRoot`, `remoteOnly(prefix)` → `[{ path, h, s, m, mime }]`, `isRemoteOnly`, `fetch`, `evict`, `removeRemote`, `offlineFolders`, `isKeptOffline`, `setKeptOffline`. Status event `fetched`.
- **VD-GC · clean-up of unused objects, only on request (2026-10-31).** Deleted and replaced content stays in `/vault/objects/` until the person asks: Settings › Sync › Unused files in the cloud › Check (`usage()`, changes nothing) and Clean up (two taps, `cleanUp()`). Never automatic. The rules are orOS Drive's (`koulaxizis/oros-drive` `vault/clean.go`), each against a way to lose a file:
  - the cloud manifest is read fresh (never the local cache, which lacks on-demand and failed entries) and its revision must be the same before and after the read;
  - no manifest, a manifest that cannot be opened, no vault key, or an entry without a hash: nothing is removed (`hold` "no-manifest" / "mismatch"; VD-1);
  - an object is in use under every name an entry can have: the keyed name and the legacy `objects/<h>`, whatever its `v`;
  - only keys `objects/<64 lowercase hex>` are ever removed (stricter than Drive, which takes any name directly under `objects/`); the manifest, `key.json` and anything else never;
  - only objects the provider stored 30+ days ago (`cleanMinAgeDays`; Dropbox `server_modified`, WebDAV `getlastmodified`; no time = never old);
  - fewer than nine in ten of the named objects listed: nothing is removed;
  - the manifest revision is checked before every removal; when it moved the clean-up stops (`stopped`, run it again);
  - afterwards the manifest is read again; an object it names again (Dropbox keeps the old time for the same bytes, so a device re-uploading old content just before its manifest write can race the removal) is put back from this device's hash-checked copy (`healed`), otherwise reported by path (`lost`);
  - the uploading side: every object a push uploaded is in `oros-vault-sent` (device-local, path → [hash, time]) and looked at again at the end of the following syncs until one at least 10 s after the upload still finds it; a missing one is queued again and the next push uploads it (objectStored).
  - Storage contract: `storage.listInfo(prefix)` → `[{ key, size, modified }]` (files only), Dropbox and WebDAV. API: `usage()` → `{ files, fileBytes, objects, stored, unused, unusedBytes, free, freeBytes, missing, otherBytes, hold }`; `cleanUp()` → `{ removed, bytes, stopped, healed, lost }` or rejects `clean-no-manifest`, `clean-mismatch`, `clean-moved`, `clean-unsupported`. Tests `tests/vault-clean.test.js` (Dropbox, and WebDAV through `sync-webdav.test.js`).
- Limits: whole-file encryption in RAM; deleted and replaced content stays in `/vault/objects/` until a clean-up (VD-GC); empty folders are not part of the vault.

### `pet.js` + `pet.css` (Screen Pet, shell component) [verified 2026-10-06; header "v0.3", comments mention v0.3.2 and v0.4]

- One IIFE, ES5. Lives in the shell document (own layer `#pet-layer`, z-index 400, `pointer-events:none` except the canvas and the HUD). Loads before `shell.js`; at parse time it needs only `orosSync` (loaded earlier) and `document.body` (A24 closed).
- **Three slices, all with a `mergeFn` and a storage key:**
  - `pet` (`oros-pet-data`): `{ ver:1, sm, deleted{ <petId>: ts }, pet{ id, name, palette, birthTs, lastFed, lastPetted, wokeAt, awakeE, asleepSince, asleepE }, fm{ name, palette } }`. Stats are DERIVED (`computeStats`), never stored.
  - `petEvents` (`oros-pet-events`): `{ ver:1, clearedAt, events[{ id, ts, type, name }] }`, union by id, max 100, a clear wins by `clearedAt`. The Calendar reads this key directly.
  - `petSettings` (`oros-pet-settings`): `{ ver:1, calFeed, calFeedTs, enabled, enabledTs, minimized, minimizedTs }`; mirror `oros-pet-calendar-sync` for the Calendar.
- Device-local: `oros-pet-pos`. Legacy keys migrated once at boot: `oros-pet-enabled`, `oros-pet-minimized`, `oros-pet-calendar-sync`.
- **Merge rules (2026-10-06):**
  - PT-1 · A pet nobody has touched is PROVISIONAL (`sm` 0, `fm` 0) and is stored without marking dirty; any real pet beats it. `writePet()` (every care action, rename, palette) stamps it.
  - PT-3 · `canonPetState()` is the single shape for getter and merge: fixed key order, tombstones sorted, exactly one active energy anchor pair (`normalizeAnchors`: the newer of `asleepSince` / `wokeAt` is the active one). Two different pet ids: the newer `sm` wins WHOLE, nothing of the other is mixed in. Same id: care clocks = max, anchors = newest of each kind then normalized, name / palette by `fm` (tie → greater value), `birthTs` = earliest.
  - PT-2 · `petSettingsCanon()` is the single shape for getter, setter and merge; a tie between stamps resolves to `true` on both devices.
- **Public surface:** `window.orosPet` (`enable`, `disable`, `toggle`, `isEnabled`, `isActive`, `openLog`, `clearLog`, `calendarFeedOn`, `setCalendarFeed`; since 0.44.00 the Pet World bridge: `snapshot`, `sprite`, `line`, `feed`, `pat`, `sleepToggle`, `rename`, each returning a plain JSON clone), `window.__orosOpenPet(eventId?)`, `window.__orosPetSyncApi` (`dirty`, `_suppress`), `window.__orosPetCalFeedEnabled`.
- **Pet World bridge (0.44.00):** `pet.js` stays the ONLY writer of `oros-pet-data`. The `petworld/` app reads `snapshot()` (id, name, palette, `colors`, `birthTs`, `ageDays`, derived food/happy/energy/asleep, `mood`, `provisional` = sm 0) and asks for care through `feed` / `pat` / `sleepToggle` / `rename`, the same functions as the HUD buttons (their companion visuals run only while the companion is active; `spawnHearts` returns early otherwise). `sprite(pose)` returns the 16×16 grid of `spriteGrid(pose)`, the pixel art `drawSprite` now draws from (output identical to the old `drawSprite` on 448 poses). `line(group)` returns a speech line from a whitelist of pools. Since 0.45.00 `feed(kind)` takes a food (`kibble` default, `carrot`, `strawberry`, `mushroom`, `apple`; table `FOODS` in `pet.js`): every food sets `lastFed`; happiness bonuses move `lastPetted` forward to the target value; an energy bonus wakes the pet with `awakeE` raised. Effects only move clocks forward, so two devices feeding offline still merge by the existing max rules. Each pet has one favourite food (`favouriteFood(id)`, a hash of the pet id over the four garden foods, +25 happiness, `speech.fav` line, hearts); `snapshot().favFood` names it and `feed` returns `favourite`. Since 0.45.03 the companion READS `oros-petnest-data` (or, on a device that never opened Pet World, sync's carry copy `oros-remote-carry`.petnest) every 2 s: while a walk is under way (`now < start + minutes`) the sprite is hidden and a "🎒 On a walk · back HH:MM" sign (opens the app) stands in its place; speech and the catch game pause; when the walk ends the pet says a `speech.back` line. It never writes that key. Since 0.45.08 `play(cost)` (0…15) ends a Pet World game: `lastPetted = now` and, when awake, a fresh anchor pair `wokeAt = now`, `awakeE = energy − cost` (the catch-game way); hearts only with the companion on; no event is logged (the log keeps care, not play). Since 0.45.11 `sprite(pose)` also takes `pose.acc` (`bow`, `scarf`, `hat`, `glasses`, `crown`, `bell`; anything else is ignored): `dressSprite` draws the accessory over the body and under the Zzz, in colours 5–9 that `spriteColors` (and so `snapshot().colors`) now carries for every palette. The companion reads `oros-petprogress-data`.`wear.id` (or sync's carry copy `.petprogress`) with the walk check every 2 s and dresses the desktop pet the same way; it never writes that key. HUD: a "Forest" / "Δάσος" button opens the app (`__orosOpenApp("petworld")`).
- **Runtime:** one `requestAnimationFrame` loop while enabled (it stops with the tab hidden); HUD refreshed once a second; language re-read on every HUD refresh (PT-4); `--pet-floor-lift` read at most once a second (PT-6).
- **Keys (no modifiers, pet active, no input focused, no dialog open):** F feed · S sleep / wake · C catch · L activity log.
- Notifications: `ns:"pet"`, key `pet-bday:<id>:<ymd>`; `pet` is not in `KNOWN_APPS` (no toggle, A7).
- `pet.css`: the layer sits at `bottom: calc(var(--tb-h, 0px) + safe-area)` (the old 48 px fallback served a bottom taskbar that does not exist); `--tb-h` and `--pet-floor-lift` are hooks that nothing sets today. A running app covers the pet (z-index 900 over 400).

### To-Do app (`todo/`) [verified 2026-10-07, `?v=0.39.18`; header "v0.4"]

- `todo/index.html` (tabs, quick-add, controls, item dialog, list dialog, saved-filter dialog, selection bar, toast), `todo/todo.js` (two IIFEs: the app, and the deep-link bridge `__orosTodoOpen` / `sessionStorage["oros-todo-open"]`), `todo/model.js` (`OrosTodoModel`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/todo-model.test.js`: priorities, subtasks merge, smart lists, saved filters, sorting, repeat after completion, `dedupeMoved`), `todo/todo.css`.
- **Keys:** `oros-todo-data` (synced slice `todo`, live registration with `mergeTodoStates`); `oros-todo-prefs` (device-local, TD-8: `{ activeList, hideCompleted, smart, sort }`, the open tab, the "hide completed" switch, the open smart list / saved filter (`"today" | "week" | "nodate" | "p1" | "f:<id>"`, TD-14) and the sort per view (`{ <list id | smart id | f:id>: "manual" | "prio" | "due" }`, only when not the default: manual for a list, due date for a smart view)). Search, label filter, open subtask checklists (`expanded`), the selection and the "ticked here" set of a smart view (`justDone`) are session-only.
- **Schema (`DATA_VER` 3):** `{ ver, sm, om, activeList, hideCompleted, deleted{ id: ts }, labels[{ id, name, color, mtime, om, pos }], lists[{ id, name, mtime, om, pos, recurrence, lastReset, nextReset, items[{ id, text, done, due, notes, labels[], info[{ id, label, value }], recurrence, mtime, om, pos, fm{ text, done, due, notes, labels, info, recurrence }, prio?, subs?[{ id, text, done, mtime }], xf?{ prio, subs, so, list } }] }], filters?[{ id, name, labels[], prios[], due, from, to, text, mtime, pos }], fom? }`. `recurrence` = `{ every, unit, weekday, after? }`.
- **TD-14 fields (wave "closer to Todoist"), all ABSENT when unused, so data that never used them keeps the previous shape byte for byte** (normalised on load and on every merge result by `normNewFields` / `normFilters`):
  - `prio` 1 / 2 / 3 = P1 urgent / P2 / P3; absent = P4 (no priority). Colours on the round checkbox (`--p1/--p2/--p3`) and a flag in the meta row.
  - `subs` = the checklist (≤ 100, text ≤ 300). Each subtask has its own `mtime`; a removed one is tombstoned in `deleted` like a task.
  - `xf` = stamps of the new fields, kept OUTSIDE `fm` because the previous `todo.js` rebuilds `fm` from its seven fields in `canonItem` (an extra key in `fm` would make the two versions' canonical forms differ and both upload forever); extra item keys survive the previous version untouched. `xf.prio` (priority changed), `xf.subs` (a subtask changed), `xf.so` (subtask order), `xf.list` (moved into this list). `touchedByOldCode` takes `xf` into account; `touchXf(it, f)` stamps.
  - `recurrence.after: true` = "repeat after completion": the next due date is `nextAfterDone(today, rec)` (months clamp to the month's last day); absent = the fixed schedule as before. A recycled task (either kind) and a list cycle also untick its subtasks.
  - `filters` / `fom`: saved filters (labels any-of, priorities, due `"" | overdue | today | week | month | none | range` + `from`/`to`, text), whole-entity LWW like labels, order from the side with the newer `fom`, deletion by tombstone. Left out of the root when there are none.
  - `dav` (CalDAV W5, 2026-11-01): `[{ id: <list id>, url, mtime }]`, the list linked to a server task list (newer wins per list, `url ""` = unlinked). Part II "CalDAV / CardDAV W5".
- **Merge of TD-14:** `mergeItem` takes `prio` from the newer `xf.prio` (tie → greater serialization), merges `subs` one by one (`Mdl.mergeSubs`: union by id, newer `mtime` per subtask, order from the newer `xf.so`, tie → id sequences like `pickRef`), every `xf` stamp = max. `canonState` then (1) drops tombstoned subtasks (`dropDeadSubs`), (2) runs `dedupeMoved`: a task id found in two lists (moved on one device, still in the old list on another) stays only in the list of the copy with the newest `xf.list` (tie → greater list id), its content the `mergeItem` of all copies — so a note written on the other device in the old list survives the move; (3) writes the root in one key order (`ROOT_KEYS`, extras sorted). A device on the previous version shows a moved task in both lists until it updates (its merge doesn't dedupe; the new one cleans up when they meet) and drops `filters` from its own merge result (a union, so nothing is lost). While such a device keeps syncing with a moved task or saved filters around, the two versions' results differ and uploads alternate until it updates.
- **Moving (`moveItems`)**: from the task window's `List` select (at close), the quick menu (right-click / 500 ms long press; touch callout and text selection off on coarse pointers) or the selection bar. The task goes to the top of the target with its subtasks; both lists get a new `om`; Undo (`undoFn`) moves each back to its old index.
- **Smart lists / saved filters**: tabs before the lists (`.tab.smart`, `data-smart`, icon only ≤ 480 px for the four built-in ones; the list tabs keep `data-list-id`, the deep-link bridge is unchanged). `today` = due ≤ today, `week` = due ≤ today + 6 (overdue included), `nodate`, `p1`. They show open tasks plus those ticked there this session; ticking, opening, the quick menu and sorting work as in a list; no drag handles. Quick-add in a smart view writes to the last open list with what makes the task show there (due today, P1, the filter's labels / single priority) and says where it went. Sort per view (`Mdl.sortRows`: prio → due → stored order, or due → prio; ticked last). Quick-add also takes `p1`–`p4`.
- **Seeds:** two lists with fixed ids (`tdl-general`, `tdl-groceries`), every stamp 0: identical on every device, they collapse into one and never override real data.
- **Stamps:** labels carry `mtime` (whole-entity LWW); a list header carries `fm{ name, cycle }` (TD-9: "cycle" = recurrence + lastReset + nextReset together), `mtime` = the newest; the root carries `sm` (activeList / hideCompleted) and `om` (order of lists and labels); a list carries `om` (order of its tasks). **A task carries one stamp per field (`fm`, TD-3)**, written by `touchField(it, field)`; `mtime` = the newest of them and decides life against a tombstone (an edit newer than its tomb resurrects). A task whose `mtime` is newer than all of `fm` was last touched by a device on the previous `todo.js`: `mtime` then speaks for every field (`touchedByOldCode`).
- **Merge (`mergeTodoStates`):** settings by `sm` (tie → lexicographic), lists paired by id (header LWW, `om` = max, tasks through `unionItems` → `mergeItem`: each field from the side with the newer stamp, tie → greater serialization), order from the side with the newer `om` (`pickRef`; on a tie the two id sequences are compared as sequences, restricted to the survivors: TD-12; positions renumbered on copies), a list present on one side only still drops its tombstoned tasks; result through `canonState`. Never returns an empty state.
- **Canonical form (`canonState`, TD-4), used by the getter and the merge:** tasks with fixed key order and `fm` always spelled out; `deleted` with sorted keys, pruned at 30 days against the NEWEST stamp in the data (`canonDeleted`), never the device clock; the tombstone of a default list (`tdl-general`, `tdl-groceries`) never expires (TD-10); list headers with fixed key order and `fm` spelled out (`canonList`).
- **View (TD-8):** `view` / `loadView` / `saveView` / `setActiveList`; a tab switch or the "hide completed" switch saves nothing in the data and marks nothing dirty. `activeList`, `hideCompleted` and `sm` stay in the data, untouched, for devices on the previous version.
- **Undo (TD-1):** one level; its toast stays 8 s (plain toasts 4 s). It puts back ONLY what the action removed (task, list with its tasks, label and its attachments), stamped newest; nothing else is re-stamped.
- **Item dialog (TD-2, TD-5):** values are read once at open (`openValues`); extra-info rows are edited on a dialog-local copy (`dlgInfo`); `commitItemDialog()` writes back only the fields the user changed, on every close path and when the app itself is closed (`pagehide`, `beforeunload`, `visibilitychange:hidden`). Label toggles save at once.
- **Recurrence:** a ticked recurring task reopens with its next date (fixed schedule, or counted from today with `after`); a list cycle un-ticks every task at its reset date (stamps only `done`, plus ticked subtasks).
- A failed save raises an inbox item (`save-fail:<hour>`). Only the Undo toast is local (`#toast`); every plain message goes through `orosNotifs.transient` (TD-11, local fallback when standalone); confirm is a native `<dialog>` built in JS; dialogs are centred by `dialog { margin: auto }` in `todo.css`.
- Debug handle `window.__todoDebug` = `{ merge, canon, state() }`.

### Notes app (`notes/`) [verified 2026-10-07, `?v=0.39.18`; header "v0.17.0"]

- `notes/index.html` (tree pane, splitter, title input, `#md-toolbar`, `#page-body` = textarea + `#page-preview`), `notes/notes.js` (one IIFE, ES5), `notes/md.js` (pure, `window.OrosNotesMd`, Node-tested in `tests/notes-md.test.js`), `notes/notes.css`. Footer buttons, notebook menu button, Today button, toolbar buttons, chips, link strip, search overlay, tag panel, menus and dialogs are built by JS. Pages are stored as plain text (Markdown source); `[[wiki links]]` and backlinks are computed live, nothing stored.
- **Keys:** `oros-notes-data` (synced slice `notes`), `oros-notes-prefs` (device-local: open nodes, current page, current notebook, tree width, `view` edit | preview | split).
- **Schema (`DATA_VER` 3):** `{ ver, notebooks[{ id, name, mtime, pos }], pages[{ id, nb, parent, title, text, mtime, pos, labels[], pinned, ct, st, h[], hx?, cf? }], labels[{ id, nb, name, color, mtime, pos }], tombs{ <pageId> | "lbl:"+id | "nb:"+id : ts } }`.
- **Three clocks per page (NO-3):** `mtime` = anything changed (life and death against tombs); `st` = structure changed (pin, position, parent, notebook, labels; `touchStruct`); `ct` = title or text changed (`touchContent`). `h` = content stamps this text descends from, one step per sync round (`editedSinceSync` is cleared whenever the engine reads or writes the slice), at most 60 (`hx` = truncated). A page whose `mtime` is newer than both `ct` and `st` was last touched by a device on the previous `notes.js`: for that version `mtime` speaks for everything (`touchedByOldCode`).
- **Merge (`mergeNotesStates`):** tombs union (max); notebooks and labels per-id LWW by `mtime` (tie → lexicographic JSON) minus tombs; dead notebook references are repaired BEFORE two versions are compared; pages per id through `mergePage`: structure from the newer `st` (tie → key of the fields the merge never rewrites), content from the newer `ct`, `mtime` = max. If the two texts differ, the losing one is not empty and the winner does not descend from it (`descendsFrom`), the losing text becomes a page `"<id>~c<ct>"` with `cf:1` next to the original (a tomb on that id keeps it deleted). The result goes through `canonNotes`.
- **Canonical form (`canonNotes`, NO-2), used by the getter AND the merge:** fixed key order per entity, notebooks and labels by (pos, id), pages by (mtime, id), `ct` / `st` always spelled out, tombstones by `canonTombs` (a tomb of something alive is dropped; tombs older than 30 days are pruned against the NEWEST stamp in the data, never the device clock), and the untouched seed notebook is left out.
- **Seed notebook (NO-1):** id `nb-default`, `mtime` 0, created locally whenever no notebook exists; not part of the slice until it holds a page or a label or is renamed.
- **Saving:** typing updates the state at once and saves after 500 ms; `beforeunload` and `visibilitychange:hidden` flush (verified: text typed just before returning to the desktop is stored). `markDirty` once per settled burst.
- **Editor refresh (NO-4):** when the data of the open page changes underneath (a pull), title and text fields are updated even while focused, caret and scroll kept (`syncField`).
- Notifications through `orosNotifs` (`transient`; save failure as an inbox item keyed per hour); local toast only as fallback. Dialogs are native `<dialog>` built in JS, centred by one rule in `notes.css`. Export: page `.txt`, notebook(s) `.zip` (store-method writer, no dependency), both through `orosDialog`. Import from other apps: see NOTES-IMP below; from Notion: platforms.js.
- Touch: long-press on a page row opens the page menu; the notebook menu opens from `#btn-nb-menu` (NO-6).
- **Markdown wave (Obsidian/Joplin parity; no schema change, no new synced field):**
  - **Renderer (NO-MD1):** `OrosNotesMd.render(text, { wiki })` returns an HTML string in which every character of the text is escaped and only allow-listed tags are built (h1–h6, p, br, strong, em, del, code, pre, blockquote, ul/ol (+ numeric `start`), li, `input[type=checkbox][data-line]`, table/thead/tbody/tr/th/td (+ `al-l|c|r` class), hr, a, span, div). Links only `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:` (`safeUrl`: no whitespace, quotes, `<>` or control characters), always `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`; anything else keeps its label as text. Raw HTML and images are never built (shown as text / a link). Wiki links become `<a class="md-wiki ok|amb|new" data-wiki>` opened by the app. Hard line breaks inside paragraphs (Obsidian default). Not supported: setext headings, footnotes, HTML, images, reference links.
  - **Views:** `prefs.view` edit | preview | split (device-local); split needs `(min-width: 900px)` and reads as edit below it. Preview renders on page change, on sync refresh and (split) 150 ms after typing. A checkbox in preview flips `[ ]`/`[x]` on its source line (`toggleTask`, line index carried in `data-line`), then `touchContent` + the usual debounced save. Toolbar (`format`: bold, italic, heading cycle # → ## → ### → none, list, task, link, code / fenced block) goes through `execCommand("insertText")` so the browser's Undo works; fallback sets the value and fires `input`. Ctrl/Cmd+B, Ctrl/Cmd+I.
  - **Links across notebooks (NO-MD2):** `[[Page]]` → same notebook first (first in data order), else the ONE page of that title elsewhere, several → ambiguous (search opens with All notebooks), none → missing (click creates a sub-page of the current page). `[[Notebook/Page]]` → when the text before the first `/` names exactly one notebook, Page in it (missing → created at the top of that notebook); otherwise, or when that finds nothing, the whole text is a plain title. `[[Target|label]]`. Case and surrounding spaces ignored. Backlinks = pages of any notebook whose links resolve to this page (prefiltered by `[[` + title substring). The link strip is debounced 300 ms while typing.
  - **Daily note:** the calendar button in the editor header opens the child titled `yyyy-mm-dd` (local date) of the top-level page titled Daily / Ημερήσιες (either name, case-insensitive) of the current notebook, creating both when missing with FIXED ids `dly-<nbId>` and `dly-<nbId>-<yyyymmdd>` (a random id only if that id is taken by a renamed page), so two devices that create the same day before syncing make one page (different template times → the usual NO-3 conflict copy). Text from the template titled Daily / Ημερήσιες under Templates, else the built-in `daily.tpl`.
  - **Templates:** every page under a top-level page titled Templates / Πρότυπα in ANY notebook (current notebook first). Footer button + page menu `New page from template…` → pick → title prompt (suggested: the template title filled) → new top-level page in the current notebook. Placeholders `{{date}}` (yyyy-mm-dd), `{{time}}` (HH:MM), `{{title}}`; unknown `{{…}}` stay.
  - **Search:** `All notebooks` checkbox in the overlay (session-only, shown with ≥ 2 notebooks); hits show their notebook and open through `revealPage` (switches notebook, unfolds ancestors).
  - **Export:** page `.md` (`pageMarkdown`: `# Title`, the text, blank line, `---`, the orOS line), notebook(s) `.zip` of `.md` files (same folder layout as `.txt`, file `notes-<date>-md.zip`). The footer export button always opens a menu (current / all × txt / md, plus the open page). The page menu's `Export notebook` now exports the CURRENT notebook (it exported all of them).
- **Import from other note apps (NOTES-IMP, `notes/import.js`, `window.OrosNotesImport`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/notes-import.test.js`):** footer upload button + notebook menu `Import notes…` → dialog `#nt-imp` (folder picker via `webkitdirectory` where the browser has it, file picker for .md/.txt/.json/.zip). `collect` reads text files only (zip via `atelier/zip.js`), caps: 200 MB of text, 1 MB per page, 5,000 pages, 300 new labels; dot-folders (.obsidian, .trash, .git) and `__MACOSX` are never notes (a `.obsidian` path marks an Obsidian vault). `parse` → Obsidian / generic Markdown (folders → parent pages, `A.md` beside `A/` is that folder's page, front matter `tags`/`title` taken out and other keys kept, `#tags` outside code → labels, `[[a/b/Note#H|x]]` → `[[Note|x]]`, a leading `# Title` equal to the file name and the orOS export line dropped) or Standard Notes backup (decrypted only; encrypted items counted; Tags with `TagToParentTag` → `parent/child`; pinned; archived under an `Archive` page; trashed out; Super notes = Lexical JSON → Markdown). `plan` gives stable ids `nb-imp-`/`imp-`/`lbl-imp-` + cyrb53(source | root name | path), so a second import of the same source adds only what is new (texts replaced only with the tick); pages tombstoned here are not revived while the notebook lives; a deleted notebook imports fresh. Wave 2 sources: Evernote `.enex` (notes by regex over the XML, `<data>` dropped unread; ENML through `htmlToMd`: own tokenizer → tiny tree → Markdown, script/style/comments/doctype dropped, links only http/https/mailto, `--en-todo` lists and `<en-todo>` → tasks, tables, `<en-media>` → `📎 file name` by order; several files → one parent page each), Google Keep Takeout (`Keep/*.json`: lists → tasks, labels, pinned, archived under `Archive`, trashed out, link annotations kept), Simplenote (`notes.json`: first line = title, `systemTags` pinned, trash counted), Joplin `.jex` (own ustar/pax reader `tarOpen`) or RAW folder (items with `type_` 1/2/4/5/6: notebooks nest, tags via note_tag, to-dos as a task line, `[x](:/id)` → `[[Title|x]]`, deleted_time out). Detection order: Standard Notes, Simplenote, Keep JSON, any .enex, Joplin items (≥ half of the .md files), else Markdown. One write (`importApply`: notebook, labels, pages, all with `ct`/`st` = now, no schema change) + Undo (tombstones the new pages, unused new labels and the then-empty notebook). Only text reaches the data; md.js renders it escaped as always.
- Debug handle `window.__notesDebug` = `{ version, state, merge, canon, sliceGet }`.

### Files app (`files/`) [verified 2026-10-06, `?v=0.39.07`]

- `files/index.html` (toolbar, tree, list, status bar, name and delete dialogs), `files/files.js` (about 4,500 lines since wave 3, one IIFE, ES5), `files/files.css`. Search bar, import button, "More" button, column headers, storage bar, recents, context menu, preview overlay and the sync pill are built by JS.
- All disk access goes through `window.parent.orosFS`. Device-local keys: `oros-files-data` (view prefs; since wave 3 also `layout` "list"|"grid" and `contents` for content search), `oros-files-recents` (journal of 30, `{ p, at }`), `oros-files-storage-cache`, `oros-files-trash-swept` (time of the last 30-day sweep), `oros-files-disk-meta` (`{ ts, dirty }`). Synced: `oros-files-favs` (slice `files`, wave 3).
- **How the disk syncs (FILES-V, 2026-10-06): per file, through Vault Drive.** The app reports nothing. `fs.js` tells `vault.js` about every mutation of the disk (`notifyVault`: a write → `fileChanged(path)`; a delete or a move → `touchTree(path)`), whoever made it; the vault uploads, downloads, deletes and resolves conflicts in the shell, with the Files app open or closed.
  - The app only SHOWS it: the pill reads `orosVault.status()` (off / pending / synced) and a listener (`onStatus`, unsubscribed on `pagehide`) refreshes the list when the vault changed the disk, never under an open editor.
  - Same file changed on two devices: both versions are kept, the cloud's one as `name (conflict YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS).ext`; toast `sync.conflictKept`.
  - The old blob model is gone: no `orosFilesDisk` bridge, no `oros-files-disk-cache` / `-pending` / `-meta`, no conflict dialog, no `files-disk` slice (retired in `sync.js`, SY-R).
- Preview / Quick Edit: text ≤512 KB, images ≤10 MB; Markdown preview makes only `http`, `https`, `mailto` and relative links clickable; Quick Edit decodes strictly (a file that is not UTF-8 is not editable), keeps a BOM, and warns before discarding unsaved text.
- Touch: first tap selects, a second tap on the same row opens it; "More" opens the actions menu (the context menu has no touch equivalent on iOS). Since wave 3 a long press (500 ms, 10 px slop, the next click swallowed; a touch `contextmenu` is ignored) or the header check box opens Select mode.
- `files.css`: no `margin` reset (dialogs are centred by the browser); ends with the `[hidden]` guard; 44 px targets under `(pointer: coarse)`.
- **Wave 3 (Explorer / Nautilus / Google Files parity).** Pure logic in `files/files-core.js` (`OrosFilesCore`, tested in `tests/files-core.test.js`); `files/index.html` also loads `../atelier/zip.js` (reader). Session-only `view` = `files` | `recent` | `trash` (body classes `v-recent`, `v-trash`); rows of those views carry their own `path` (`entryPath(e)`).
  - **Trash (FILES-T).** Files' own Delete (button, key, menu, Select bar, drop on the Trash node) = `moveToTrash`: write `/internal/.trash/<id>.json` `{ v:1, path, name, dir, at }` FIRST, then `orosFS.mv(item, /internal/.trash/<id>/<name>)`; a failed move takes the record back. `<id>` = deletion ms in base 36 (9 digits) + `-` + random, so a folder whose record has not arrived still has an age. One record per item, never a shared index file: two devices trashing at once would turn one index into a Vault conflict copy. Shift+Delete and everything inside the Trash delete for good (`orosFS.rm`). Other apps' `orosFS.rm` is untouched (no trash). Restore: `mkdir` of the old parent (falls back to the root), free name (`uniqueName`), `mv` back, then remove the record (`trashDiscard`). A trashed empty folder reaches other devices only as its record (empty folders don't sync): Restore makes it again with `mkdir`. A file whose record arrived before its content shows faded and refuses Restore ("not on this device yet"). Sweep (`trashSweepLoad`): at boot every 12 h (4 s after boot) and whenever the Trash view opens, records older than 30 days and leftover id folders with neither item nor record (what a remote restore leaves behind) are removed. Empty Trash = `orosFS.rm("/internal/.trash")`. Sync: these are plain moves/writes/removals, so Vault Drive carries them (verified two-context: trash on A → the file leaves its folder on B and B's Trash shows it; restore on B → back on A, A's Trash empty).
  - The `.trash` folder is hidden from every Files view, the folder tree, the Move/Copy chooser, Files' search and the universal search provider (`files/search.js` 1.0.1); the name `.trash` is refused at the root (`err.reserved`) and an import of that name becomes `_trash`. Deep links into it open the Trash view. The storage figure still counts it.
  - **Favourites (slice `files`, key `oros-files-favs`).** `{ v:1, items:[{ p, dir, m, del? }] }` sorted by `p`; per item bigger `m` wins, a tie goes to the removal, then the larger JSON (R5, R17, R26); at most 300 tombstones kept (newest). Stamped only at the mutation site (`favCommit` compares JSON first, R27); the setter never marks dirty (R6). A rename/move in Files carries favourites (`favMove`), trashing drops them (`favDrop`). Shown under "Recent" at the top of the tree with an unpin star; a missing path is faded (not pruned: it may still be syncing). Verified two-context: pin on A shows on B, unpin on B converges, idle syncs stay clean.
  - **Recent.** Device-local journal of 30 (was 10); the main folder still shows 10, the Recent view all of them with the folder and age; renames and moves inside Files rewrite journal paths (`recentsMove`).
  - **Search.** Names (folded: case, accents, final sigma; `fold()` keeps string length so snippet indexes map to the original) everywhere under the open folder, then, with `Contents` on, text files ≤ 4 MB (`contentKind`: txt, md, csv, json, html stripped of tags, code, …, no extension; a NUL in the first 4 KB = binary, skipped) and PDFs ≤ 30 MB (PDF.js `getTextContent`, first 300 pages, stops at the first matching page). Progress line, skipped count, no cap: 100 shown, "Show more" adds 100. A new query or `refresh()` restarts it (`renderToken`).
  - **ZIP.** Writer `zipBuild` in files-core.js (UTF-8 flag, method 0 or 8, no ZIP64: Error `zip-big` past 65535 entries / 4 GB), deflate through `CompressionStream("deflate-raw")` when present and smaller, already-compressed kinds stored (`shouldStore`). Caps: 10,000 files / 300 MB per new ZIP. Reader = `AtelierZip.open` (whole file in memory, ≤ 300 MB here; 20,000 entries; 80 MB per entry). `extractPlan`: `..`/absolute/drive paths dropped (no escape), bad characters → `_`, `__MACOSX` and `.DS_Store` skipped, clashes and file-vs-folder collisions get " (1)", 1 GB total cap; a single common top folder becomes the target folder itself (no `Docs/Docs`). Extraction never overwrites (new folder, free name). The .zip preview lists up to 500 entries.
  - **Grid view** (`#entries.grid`, per device). Thumbnails for images and the first PDF page (≤ 20 MB), made lazily (IntersectionObserver, 2 at a time) on a 192 px canvas → WebP object URL, memory cache of 150 keyed by path + mtime + size, never stored.
  - **Select mode** (`body.select-mode`): check boxes replace icons, bottom `#sel-bar` (Done, count, Select all, Restore in the Trash, Favourite for one item, ZIP, Move, Copy, Delete). Esc leaves it.
- **The whole Dropbox (since the Files Dropbox wave 1).** `files/dropbox-core.js` (`OrosDropboxCore`, pure, tested in `tests/files-dropbox.test.js`) + `files/dropbox.js` (`OrosFilesDropbox`) + `files/dropbox-callback.html/.js`. A "Dropbox" node under the disk in the tree switches the app to `body.dbx-mode`: the disk toolbar, list and status are hidden, `#dbx-bar` (up, crumbs, refresh, account) and `#dbx-panel` (search, list, status) are shown; `navigate()` leaves it. Read only in wave 1: browse (`files/list_folder`, 2000 per page, 50 pages), search names (`files/search_v2`, 100), preview (text ≤512 KB UTF-8 as text, images ≤10 MB) and download (through `orosDialog.saveFile`).
- **orOS Drive (VD-OD, 2026-10-16).** `files/drive.js` (`OrosFilesDrive`): an "orOS Drive" node right under the disk in the tree switches the app to `body.drv-mode` (same pattern as `dbx-mode`; `navigate()`, `openView()` and the Dropbox view leave it; `placeActive()` replaces `dbxActive()` for tree selection and the selection bar). It lists `/internal/Drive/<cwd>`: the disk's entries plus `orosVault.remoteOnly()` files and the folders they imply (cloud mark, `.drv-cloud`). Opening a cloud file calls `orosVault.fetch()` then Files' own `openFileAt()`; the bar has "Keep on this device" (`setKeptOffline`) and "Free up space" (`evict`); each row has a bin button (also the Delete key) that deletes it everywhere (VD-OD-RM: disk part to the Files Trash through `ctx.trash`, cloud-only part `removeRemote`). Device-local view state `oros-files-drive-view`. Strings EN/EL inside the module. Without a usable vault it says to turn on sync.
- **This computer (PC-FILES, orOS USB only, 2026-10-31).** `files/computer-core.js` (`OrosComputerCore`, pure + a fetch client, tested in `tests/files-computer.test.js`) + `files/computer.js` (`OrosFilesComputer`). Shown only where the orOS launcher answers `GET /__oros/fs/roots` (oros-portable `launcher/computerfs.go`, turned on by oros-usb with `OROS_COMPUTER_FILES=1`); on useoros.online, Portable and the installers nothing appears. Files paths `/computer/home/…` and `/computer/disks/<name>/…` map to the API paths `/home/…`, `/disks/<name>/…`; anything else is refused before a request (`badpath`). A "This computer" node under orOS Drive switches Files to `body.cmp-mode` (same place pattern: `navigate()`, `openView()`, Dropbox and orOS Drive leave it; `placeActive()` counts it). Top view: Folders (home + the existing XDG folders, English on disk, shown translated through `c.f.*`) and Disks (`oros-system disks` rows; open = `op mount`, eject = `op unmount`; Windows NTFS read-only is decided by oros-usb). Folder view: preview (pictures, video, sound through the raw URL; text, first 256 KB with Range), new folder, rename, Trash of this computer (freedesktop, its own view: put back, delete for good, empty). Copies: "Copy to the orOS disk…" (Files' own folder picker, confirm above 500 MB because sync uploads it) and, from the disk, "Send to This computer…" (context menu + selection bar `sb-pc`; own picker over home and writable disks). Names that are taken get " (2)"; nothing is overwritten. **Never synced:** `/computer` is not an orosFS path; `sync.js`, `vault.js` and `fs.js` never see it (test). The service worker returns before any cache for `/__oros/` (test): a cached listing showed folders as they were. Device-local view state `oros-files-computer-view`. The API needs the launcher's per-start HttpOnly cookie (set on orOS's HTML) plus `X-Oros-FS: 1`.
- **Shell side of This computer.** `shell.js` `computerFiles()` runs only on `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`: when `roots` answers it sets `<html data-oros-computer-files="1">` (the oros-usb System extension then opens disks in Files instead of a file:// window), listens for the DOM event `oros-files-open` (detail `/disks/<name>` or `/home/…`, anything else ignored) and opens Files with `__orosOpenAt("files", {computer: path})`; Files' `openSearchTarget` passes `{computer}` to `OrosFilesComputer.openAt`, which waits for the probe if it has not answered yet. Every 5 s while visible it lists `disks`; a USB volume not seen before brings a transient notification (`pc.stick`, `pc.stickBody`, action `pc.open` = mount, then Files). Chris (2026-10-31): a notification only, nothing opens by itself.
- **Open and save on This computer (PC-DIALOG, wave 4).** `pcdialog.js` (`window.orosPcDialog`, loaded after `dialogs.js`; pure helpers tested in `tests/pcdialog.test.js`). When `computerFiles()` sees `roots` answer it calls `orosPcDialog.enable()`, which swaps `orosDialog.saveFile`, `openFile`, `openFiles` and `mode()` (→ `"computer"`) for an orOS window (`<dialog id="oros-pcd">`, centered, R32/R33) over `/__oros/fs/`: This computer › Home / disks › folders; Open lists folders and the files that match `accept` (extensions, `type/*` families, common MIME types); Save has a name field and New folder, read-only disks are shown but not enterable. Apps change nothing: they already call `parent.orosDialog`. Rules: a file opened through it is remembered by name for this page (`dir`, `path`, `mtime` from `X-Oros-MTime`); saving that name back to the same path replaces it in place with `ifmtime`, and a 412 `changed` never overwrites but offers "Save as a copy" (`name (2).ext`); replacing any other existing file asks first; a 409 `exists` asks too. Save starts in the folder the file was opened from, else the last folder (`oros-pcdialog-dir`, device-local), else `/home/Documents`; a last folder that is gone (stick removed) starts at the top. Reads above 512 MB are refused. Nothing here touches orosFS or sync; outside orOS USB `enable()` is never called and `dialogs.js` behaves as before. Strings `pcd.*` (EN/EL in `translations.js`, DE in `i18n/de/shell.js`). Since 4.81.00 also `orosPcDialog.opened(name)` → `{path, mtime}`, `stat(path)`, `list(dir)`, `read(path)` → File, `write(path, blob, ifmtime, replace)` → stat entry (errors carry `.code`; ifmtime refuses a moved or removed file as `changed`), no window; used by Pad to save in place.
- **This computer in orOS Portable and the desktop apps (PC-PORTABLE, 2026-10-31).** The same API, served by the oros-portable launcher on Windows and Linux (oros-portable #16: `fsconsent.go`, `computerfs_{linux,windows}.go`). Consent per computer: `GET /__oros/fs/consent` answers `{state: "on"|"off"|"ask", fixed}` (`fixed` = orOS USB, always on); `POST consent {on}` keeps the answer under a hash of the machine ID; until "on" every other call answers 404 `off`. `shell.js` `computerFiles()` asks first: "ask" opens `#pcfiles-dialog` (`pc.ask.*`; Esc = no answer, asked again next start), "on" starts as before, "off" does nothing; a launcher without `consent` (older orOS USB) falls back to `roots`. Settings › System card `pcfiles` (switch `pc.on`, device scope; `s.pcfiles` is null where nothing asks) calls `window.__orosPcFilesSet`; off removes `data-oros-computer-files` and `orosPcDialog.disable()` restores the browser dialogs; Files and open apps follow when they next open (a call answers `off` → `c.e.off`). Windows (`roots.os === "windows"`, `OrosComputerCore.isWindows`): disks are drive letters `/disks/C` named "Label (C:)" (the launcher's `disks` pairs by `mount: "/disks/C"`), no eject (Windows' "Safely remove"), Windows' own folders and hidden/system items never listed, delete = Recycle Bin (`c.deleteW`…; a removable drive answers 409 `norecycle` → `c.e.norecycle`), the bin button runs `op recyclebin` (Explorer opens it) instead of the Trash view. The Portable folder and its data folder are never reachable.
  - **A second Dropbox app, not sync's.** Sync's app (`sync.js`, App folder) is untouched. This view needs a Dropbox app with **Full Dropbox** access (a Dropbox app's access type cannot change after creation): `OrosDropboxCore.APP_KEY` (`fv6idclg1tn5hq8`, Chris's "orOS Files" app, set 2026-10-14) or the user's own key (device-local `oros-files-dbx-key`, `[a-z0-9]{8,32}`). Scopes on the Dropbox app: `files.metadata.read`, `files.content.read`, `files.content.write` (the last for wave 2 moves and wave 3 uploads). Redirect URI `https://useoros.online/files/dropbox-callback.html`.
  - **Sign-in:** OAuth 2.0 + PKCE as a public client with `token_access_type=offline`, popup first, whole-tab redirect when blocked (back to `/?open=files`), state checked against `oros-files-dbx-pkce`; the same pattern as Chess › Lichess. The token record `{ access, refresh, exp, key, who }` is sealed with a non-extractable AES-GCM key in IndexedDB `oros-files-dbx` (in the factory-reset list), never in localStorage, never synced. An expired access token is refreshed once (single flight); a refused refresh drops the record. Disconnect revokes the token (`auth/token/revoke`).
  - **Sync folder guard:** a folder whose listing holds `orOS-data.json` (or `vault` + an `orOS-backup-*.json`) is sync's own encrypted folder; its lower-case path goes to device-local `oros-files-dbx-sync`, the folder shows a lock and a notice instead of its contents, and search results inside it are dropped.
  - Every Dropbox name is shown with `textContent`; `Dropbox-API-Arg` escapes every character from U+007F (Greek names). Browsing never touches the disk, the vault or a sync slice. Device-local `oros-files-dbx-view` `{ on, path }` reopens the last place.
  - **Copy / Move into the disk (wave 2, 1.97.00).** Rows have checkboxes (header: all shown); a selection bar and the preview offer `Copy to orOS disk` / `Move to orOS disk`; the destination comes from Files' own folder chooser (`pickFolderDialog`, shared with Move/Copy). `planItems` expands selected folders (`list_folder` recursive), makes each name disk-safe (`localName`), skips sync's folder, non-downloadable files, files over 300 MB and anything past 1000 files / 1 GB. Each file: download → Dropbox `content_hash` check (a damaged download never lands) → SHA-256 → write through `orosFS` under a free name (`uniqueName`, never over a file). The disk write reaches the vault through fs.js as always.
  - **Move deletes only confirmed copies:** after the copies, the view runs `orosVault.sync` until nothing of the job is queued (5 min cap), then for each file `confirmedCopy(item, orosVault.manifestEntry(dst), orosVault.isQueued(dst))` must hold (synced manifest has the destination with the same SHA-256) before `files/delete_v2` with `parent_rev` = the copied rev (a file changed meanwhile stays). Deleted files go to Dropbox's deleted files (30 days). A selected folder is deleted only when every file of it was deleted and a fresh recursive listing finds no file left. Moving is refused unless `orosVault.status().usable`.
  - **Job journal:** device-local `oros-files-dbx-job` `{ mode, dest, folders, items: [{ src, rev, hash, size, rel, dst, h, st }] }`, saved before every write (the destination name is fixed first, so a resume finds its own file by SHA-256 and never duplicates). An interrupted job is offered as `Continue` / `Discard` when the view opens; `Stop` ends a job without removing any original. Resuming a move without usable sync turns it into a copy and keeps every original.
  - **Send to Dropbox (wave 3, 2.03.00).** On the disk, the context menu and the selection bar offer `Send to Dropbox…` (not in Trash). A Dropbox folder chooser (`pickDbxFolder`, starts at the last Dropbox folder; sync's folder is hidden and can't be chosen) picks the destination; `planExport` walks selected folders (`orosFS.ls` + `stat`), never sends the trash, refuses a destination inside sync's folder and keeps the wave 2 limits (1000 files / 1 GB, 300 MB per file). Each file: read through `orosFS` (the disk holds plaintext; the vault encrypts only what leaves for sync) → Dropbox `content_hash` computed locally → `files/upload` (≤ 150 MB) or an upload session in 8 MB pieces, always `mode: add, autorename: true` (never overwrites; a clash gets " (1)") → the returned `content_hash` must match, else the file counts as failed. The view then opens at the destination. Copies only: nothing on the disk changes. No journal: `Stop` ends after the current file and files already sent stay.

### Help app (`help/`) [verified 2026-10-09, `?v=0.48.00`]
- **What:** the orOS guide (EN/EL, offline, searchable). Category System. No sync slice, no stored state.
- **Pages:** plain-text files in a strict Markdown subset, NOT `.md` (GitHub Pages runs Jekyll and would turn `.md` into HTML): topics in `help/topics/<id>.<lang>.txt` (order in `help/topics.json`), one page per app in `<appId>/help.<lang>.txt`. App list comes from `apps.json` (menu grouping). Missing page → "soon" tag; missing EL → EN with a note.
- **Format:** `# Title` (once) · `##`/`###` (anchor = folded slug of the text) · paragraphs · `-` / `1.` lists (one level, two-space continuation) · `> tip` · `>! warning` · `**bold**` · `` `UI label` `` · `[[Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H]]` key chips · `[text](app:<id> | help:a/<id>[#slug] | help:t/<id>[#slug] | https://…)`. No HTML, images, tables. Rendered with `textContent` only. App outline: intro · Getting started · task sections · Sync and backup · Keyboard shortcuts (if any) · Tips · Limits (if any); EN and EL keep the same ##/### outline. Write from the code; exact UI labels in backticks.
- **Routes:** `#t/<id>`, `#a/<id>`, optional `/<slug>`; `location.replace` only (no history entries). Fetches carry `?v=` of `help.js` so a release never serves the previous release's page (SW `releaseCopy`).
- **Shell (`shell.js`):** `openHelp(route)` (default: the running app's page), taskbar `#help-btn` (shown only when `apps.json` lists `help`; ≤480 px: hidden on the desktop, replaces `#btn-lang` while an app runs; `body.app-running` set by `openApp`/`returnToDesktop`), `SC_DEFS` H, `window.orosHelp = { open(route), openApp(id) }`. Strings `bar.help`, `sc.desc.help`.
- **Search:** in-memory index of every page in the current language, built in the background; accent-, case- and final-sigma-insensitive (`fold`); every term must match; title 12 / heading 5 / text 1.
- **Precache:** `help/` files, every topic and every registered app's `help.*.txt` (the app's release commit adds its two lines; `tests/help.test.js` fails otherwise once Help is precached).

### Settings app (`settings/`) [verified 2026-10-10, `?v=0.50.00`]
- **What:** "Settings" / "Ρυθμίσεις", category System. The settings of orOS itself, moved out of the menu (Chris 2026-10-09). Sections: Appearance (theme, skin, wallpaper, Dock, screen pet) · Notifications · Sync · Backups · Language & search · System (version, updates, install, links, shortcuts, factory reset). Wide: sidebar + page; < 720 px: list → page with Back and Esc.
- **Storage:** none. The app never writes storage; it reads a snapshot and calls `parent.orosSettings` (`set`, `act`), notifications through `parent.orosNotifs`. No sync slice, nothing to migrate. Each card shows its scope ("All devices" / "This device") from `core.js` `SCOPE`.
- **Shell:** `window.orosSettings` (bridge table above); `settingsNotify()` batched, called at the end of `renderMenu` and on auto-sync events. `open(section)` uses `__orosOpenAt("settings", { section })`.
- **Ways in:** menu row "Settings" (above Device info and Info) · System category · sync dot when sync is off or locked → Sync · Info window button `sc.reset.moved` → System · Device info sync card → Sync · universal search (`settings/search.js`, section topics, `{ section, item }`) · `Search settings` inside the app.
- **Menu section** (since launcher 1.3.0): `menu` sits between Appearance and Notifications. Snapshot `menu: [{ id, name, cat, catName, shown }]` (null when the launcher lacks `menuHidden`/`setMenuHidden`); `set("menu:<id>", shown)` (ids checked against the internal apps), `act("menu.showAll")`, `act("menu.hideAll")` → `orosLauncher.setMenuHidden`. The list is grouped by category, with a find field (memory only) and an "n of total shown" line. Scope "All devices".
- **Accessibility section** (gap audit 2026-10-27 item 3, Chris approved): `accessibility` sits between Appearance and Menu. Owner `shell.js` section 5e; device-local key `oros-a11y` = `{ size: 100|115|130|150, contrast: "auto"|"on"|"off", focus: bool }` (never synced: size depends on the screen, "auto" on each device's system setting; a failed write toasts `a11y.savefail`, R30). Snapshot `a11y: { size, sizes, contrast, focus, high, forced, capped }`; `set("textSize" | "contrast" | "focusRing", v)`. Scope "This device" (`SCOPE.a11y`).
  - **Text size** = CSS `zoom` through `--oros-zoom` on `#oros-running > iframe` and on `#app-menu > *` (the menu widens with it). A zoomed frame lays its app out like browser zoom (smaller viewport, consistent pointer coordinates), so no app changes; verified in Chromium (frame 1280 px at 130 % → app viewport 985 px). Capped at `innerWidth / 320` (WCAG 1.4.10: an app keeps ≥ 320 CSS px), recomputed on resize; the card says when it is capped. An engine that grows the frame box without scaling its page gets the zoom on the page root instead (`data-oros-zoom` on the app's `<html>`; untested, no such engine in CI). The top bar, desktop, Dock, toasts and shell dialogs keep their size: zooming the shell root would mix coordinate spaces in the desktop/Dock/context-menu code (style.left from clientX).
  - **High contrast** = `data-oros-contrast="high"` on the shell root; style.css overrides the palette tokens for both themes at specificity (0,2,1), so the 16 skins need no twins; plain desktop (no wallpaper, no `#wp-live`). Apps get it through `inheritPalette`: on every change of the high state the shell sets `data-skin` again, which their `watchPalette` observes (G3). "auto" = `prefers-contrast: more` or `forced-colors: active`, live through matchMedia listeners.
  - **Injected CSS** (`A11Y_CSS`, `<style id="oros-a11y-css">`) goes into the shell and, on every frame `load` (`a11yWireFrame`, also for multitasking frames) and every change, into each same-origin app document, with `data-oros-contrast` / `data-oros-focus` on its root: 3 px accent focus ring on `:focus-visible` (wins over an app's `outline: none`), underlined links and readable placeholders in high contrast, and under `forced-colors: active` a Highlight focus ring plus an outline on `aria-checked/pressed/selected/current` (state shown by background colour would otherwise vanish). A standalone app (`?standalone`, no shell) gets none of it.
- **Suggested wallpaper per skin (SKIN-WP):** every `SKINS` entry names one existing wallpaper in `wp` (never `custom` or `clear`): adwaita dusk · lumo nebula · oros sand · ubuntu plum · fedora nordic · mint forest · arch midnight · debian ember · elementary aurora · tux mono · manjaro borealis · opensuse forest · nixos hex · gentoo obsidian · popos ember · zorin terrazzo. `setSkinUser` calls `maybeFollowSkin(old, new)`: the wallpaper moves to the new skin's `wp` only while it is still `DEFAULT_WALLPAPER` (`sand`) or the old skin's `wp`; any other wallpaper, "Mine", "None" and a device picture are never touched. Stateless on purpose (no new synced field): only a user action follows, a sync pull sets skin and wallpaper as stamped. Picking exactly the suggestion of the current skin counts as following. The snapshot carries `suggested` (the current skin's `wp`); the Settings grid marks that tile `.wall.sugg` (★, name + "Suggested for this colour") with a hint under the grid. Tests: `tests/skin-wallpaper.test.js`. Replaces the old `WALLPAPERS[].pair` (from the default wallpaper only, 11 skins).
- **Rule:** new shell settings go into Settings, never back into the menu.
- **Search settings** (Chris 2026-10-27): a `Search settings` field (`#f-find`, built by `buildFind()`) at the top of the section list; while it holds text the list shows matches instead of sections (query in memory only, kept across Back on phones; Escape or × clears). Index = `core.js` `FIND`, one row per setting `[id, section, label, card, alt, need]` with its words in `w.<id>` (EN/EL inline, DE in `i18n/de/settings.js`); `findSettings(lang, q, ok)` matches every typed word (accent, case and final-ς folded) against the label, path and words of the UI language plus English and Greek, sections included (`s:<id>`), name-starts-with first, then page order. `need` (`dock`, `seasonal`, `osk`, `multitask`, `install`, `phone`, `push`, `translate`, `app:<id>`) drops rows this device cannot show (`findOk` in the app). A pick opens the section, finds the label on the page by its text (card heading, row label, button, link row), scrolls it to the middle, outlines it for 2.6 s (`.find-hit`) and focuses its control; when the label is not there (Dock off, lock off, sync not connected) the `alt` label lights up instead (the switch that enables it), else the section just opens. A new setting row: add a `FIND` row + `w.<id>` (en, el, de); `tests/settings.test.js` checks labels, words and the German pack. Deep link `{ section, item }` lights up the same way; the menu search provider (`settings/search.js`, third TOPICS column) now lands on the setting.

### Rules for every app

- **CSS:** `[hidden]{display:none!important}` is the LAST rule of every app stylesheet. Per-element display rules are guarded with `:not([hidden])`. Shell CSS variables are the only styling truth (`inheritPalette` + `watchPalette`, G3). `LABEL_PALETTE` is data, not skin.
- **i18n:** EN/EL only, EN default. Locales el-GR / en-GB. Greek dates: dd/mm/yyyy, no comma after the day.
- **Data:** additive-only migrations; idempotent normalize on load AND on merge results; rescue backup before any reseed; the device-local whitelist is never synced.
- **File I/O:** R33. **Popups:** R32. **Cloud:** R34.
