The ref's item is kept on the card (`ui.ref`), and the card is checked again every time it is drawn. Tests `tests/assistant-actions.test.js`.
- **AS-HIST (wave A6: change history).** Every add, change and link the user applied (`remember()`: change_item, create_items, link_contact, link_items) goes to IndexedDB `oros-assistant` store `log` (DB version 2) with its undo data: device-local, never synced, exported or sent, deleted by factory reset; entries older than 30 days or past 500 are dropped at load (core.js 10c `histPrune`). A card's Undo, the `change_history` card and the conversations list's `Change history` dialog undo through the same app undo (`runUndo`, scripts loaded first), which refuses a record changed since; undo data comes from memory or the log by the card's id, never from a stored or synced chat, and goes from the log once used. Tool `change_history` {from, to, app} answers "what did you change yesterday?": the model hears when, the app, what, titles (≤ 50 per entry), undone / can_undo, never the undo data, and only apps the user still lets it read. `Clear history` empties the log (the data stays). This replaces "Undo until you leave the Assistant" (AS-ADD, wave 48).
- **AS-FREE (services with a free plan, Assistant phase 5 wave 3).** New providers in `core.js` PROVIDERS, all `kind: "openai"`, `key: "yes"`, `free: 1`, files as device-read text (no `att`): `groq` (api.groq.com/openai/v1), `cerebras` (api.cerebras.ai/v1), `github` (GitHub Models, models.github.ai/inference; model list from the catalog `modelsUrl`, a plain array; key = fine-grained PAT with Models:read), `cohere` (compatibility API api.cohere.ai/compatibility/v1; models from api.cohere.com/v1/models?endpoint=chat), `huggingface` (router.huggingface.co/v1), `sambanova` (api.sambanova.ai/v1), `pollinations` (gen.pollinations.ai/v1, `pk_` key). Each has a default `model` used until the user picks one. `parseModels` drops non-chat ids (NOT_CHAT) for every hosted provider except OpenRouter, and Groq guard/whisper/tts models; OpenRouter models priced 0/0 or ending `:free` carry `free: true`, and `provs.openrouter.free` (synced) = `Only free models` filters the list. Settings: `Test the connection` (`#as-test`) sends one "Reply with the single word: OK" through `callModel` with a 30 s timeout; a network failure says the service does not accept browser calls (CORS) or, for a local server, to check it runs and allows this site; offline is told apart. Tests: `tests/assistant-freeprov.test.js`.
- **AS-MODELS (model list in Settings).** The loaded models are shown in a plain `<select>` (`#as-model-pick`, "name (id)", first option = pick prompt) under the free-text `#as-model` box; picking one fills the box and `provs.<pid>.model`. No `<datalist>`: browsers only suggest datalist entries that match the text already in the box, so with the default `claude-opus-5-5` only Opus models showed (Chris, 2026-10-18). The list loads by itself when Settings open with a saved key, for hosted providers only (local servers wait for `Load models`).
- **AS-THINK (Claude thinking blocks, 3.40.01).** A Claude thinking block (`thinking`, `redacted_thinking`) is bound to everything sent before it: system prompt, tools and earlier messages. The system prompt carries the time and the allowed apps, so it changes with every new question, and Claude refuses an earlier question's block ("Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation"). **Rules:** (1) `anthropicReq` sends thinking blocks back only for the turn in progress (the assistant messages after the last user question: the tool rounds); earlier answers go back with their other blocks (text, tool use, web search), and an answer that held nothing but thinking goes back as its text; removing blocks from the front is allowed; (2) if Claude still refuses a thinking block (400 naming `thinking` and `signature`, `core.thinkingRefused`), `callModel` sends the same request once more with `noThinking` (no thinking block at all); (3) the stored `raw.blocks` stay unchanged, so nothing in a conversation file or sync changes. Tests: `tests/assistant.test.js`.
- **AS-CONT (answers cut at the output limit).** An answer must not end at the provider's output limit. **Rules:** (1) Claude's `max_tokens` is the model's real ceiling (`core.claudeMax`: 128K for the 4.6+ and 5 families, 64K for Sonnet 4/4.5, Opus 4.5, Haiku 4.5, 3.7; 32K Opus 4/4.1; older less; unknown names `MAX_TOKENS` 64K); requests stream, so a big ceiling is safe; a 400 that names a lower ceiling (`core.maxTokensRefused`) is retried once with it. Other providers get no limit (their default is the model's own). (2) A cut answer (`max_tokens`, `length`, `MAX_TOKENS`) drops what can't go back: a tool call whose input never ended, thinking without its signature, a server search without its result; complete tool calls still run. (3) A cut answer with no tool call to run is stored with `cut: 1`, a hidden user message `{ r: "user", cont: 1 }` (sent as `CONT_TEXT`: continue where it stopped, no repeat, no introduction; no provider takes a prefill) follows, and the model goes on, at most `CONT_ROUNDS` (4) times per question; only then the note "The answer was cut off" shows. Device models (built-in, WebLLM) don't continue (too little room). (4) A `cont` message is not a new question for AS-THINK: the cut answer keeps its thinking blocks. (5) The chain asst(cut) → user(cont) → … → asst shows as one answer (one bubble, one Copy, the live view shows the whole text); `cont` messages are never drawn. Tests: `tests/assistant-cont.test.js`.
- **AS-QUICK (desktop menu, quick access wave 1).** Shell component `quickmenu.js` (like `launcher.js`; `window.orosQuick`, attached by shell.js with `{ desktop, apps, open, running, icons, lang, label, toast }`, not in a single app). Right-click, long press (550 ms, 10 px slop, the click that ends the press is swallowed) or the context-menu key on an EMPTY spot of `#oros-desktop` (not an icon, note, the pet, the Dock, a field; never while an app runs) opens `.qm-menu`: `Ask the Assistant…` (opens it), the user's tasks (k `ask`/`brief`), the user's apps (k `app`), items other desktop components add through `window.__orosDeskItems` (functions `(x, y) → [{ label, run }]`; Sticky Notes adds New note / Tidy / Open and leaves the right-click to this menu when `orosQuick.ownsDesktop()`), `Change wallpaper…` (Settings › appearance) and `Edit this menu…`. A task opens the Assistant with `__orosOpenAt("assistant", { ask })`: the text waits in the box; `{ ask, send: 1 }` only when the user ticked `Send on tap` for that task (the tap is the user's own; the Assistant's Ask first cards still come first). `{date}` = today's long date, `{clipboard}` = `navigator.clipboard.readText()` on the tap (failure → toast, the text waits unsent), `{selection}` reserved for wave 3. `brief` → `{ brief: 1 }`. Items for a missing app or a bundle without the Assistant are hidden, never removed. Editor: a `<dialog id="qm-dlg">` in the shell (also from the Assistant's Settings › `Desktop menu`): add task / add app / edit / up / down / remove / `Restore the examples`; a sync pull never wipes a form being typed. **Data:** own slice `quickmenu` (key `oros-quick-menu`, not a field of slice `assistant`, so an older bundle's `mergeAssist` can't drop it): `{ ver:1, items:[{ id, k ask|app|brief, n ≤60, p ≤2000 (ask), app (app), send 0|1 (ask), o, d 0|1, m }] }`; examples `d-brief`, `d-today`, `d-week` exist unstored (empty n/p = translated text, following the language) and a stored item with the same id replaces one; removal = tombstone `d:1`; fractional order keys (one item per move, renumber when keys get too close); LWW per id by `m`, tie → greater canonical JSON; fresh device stores nothing. Tests: `tests/quickmenu.test.js`.
- **AS-MINI (mini Assistant, quick access wave 2, quickmenu.js 1.1.0).** `orosQuick.mini(target)` and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Q (SC_DEFS `q`) open `#qa-mini`, a panel (z 960, bottom right, 420×620; a sheet under 600 px) with `assistant/index.html?mini=1` in an iframe and its own bar: New conversation, Open in the Assistant, Close. The desktop menu's Assistant items (Ask, tasks, Briefing) go to it. **One live Assistant at a time:** when the full app runs or is alive behind (`host.running()`, `host.isOpen`), targets go to it through `__orosOpenAt` instead; opening the full app closes the panel (MutationObserver on `#oros-running`); the frame is removed on close; Open in the Assistant refuses while an answer is coming (toast) and otherwise closes the panel and opens the full app with `{ chat: id }` (quickmenu.js 1.3.1), which shows the same conversation; a panel with no conversation yet opens the full app on a new one (AS-FRESH). **Mini mode in the Assistant (`MINI`):** `body.as-mini` hides the toolbar and the conversation list; starts a new conversation; takes its first target from `orosQuick.takeMini()` (not `__orosTakeTarget`, so the full app never gets it twice), later ones through `__orosOpenAt`; exposes `window.__asMini { busy, newChat, chatId }`; **never registers the sync slice** (its frame is not an app frame, so the engine could not reap it on close): settings changes still save and mark dirty, and a `storage` event on `oros-assistant-data` reloads them so the panel never writes back an older copy.
- **AS-DEL (deleting a chat removes its file, Chris 2026-10-30 "Έχω σβήσει τα chats από τον Βοηθό, αλλά τα βλέπω ακόμη στα Αρχεία").** Until 4.47.01 a deleted chat left a tombstone file `<id>.json` `{id, m, del: 1}` for good (a missing file is written again, so deletion needed a mark), and every card answered between two writes of a chat (ui.st, the tool result text) made `mergeChat` see a fork and keep a `<id>x<m36>.json` copy. Now: (1) `mergeChat` compares what messages said (`msgSig`: role, text, continue mark, tool/result/attachment ids), not card states; a continuation takes the newer side's messages plus the longer side's tail, refs merged. (2) A deletion with chat sync on goes into `prefs.gone` and the one list `CHAT_DIR/deleted-chats.json` (`normGone`/`mergeGone`: union, newest m per id, ≤ 5000, ≤ 400 days; conflict copies of the list are folded in and removed); the chat's file is removed. A chat whose m ≤ its list m is deleted on every device (`goneWins`); one changed after the deletion stays. (3) Old tombstones are folded into the list and removed. A live file that comes back for an id this device already cleared (`prefs.clr`, i.e. a device on an older orOS wrote it back) gets a tombstone `{id, m, del: 1, r: 1, at}` that old devices read, removed after 30 days. (4) A copy `<parent>x…` whose messages all start its live parent (`spareCopy`) is deleted like any chat; a real fork stays. (5) Reconcile collects file work per path and runs it at the end, so a later decision replaces an earlier one. With sync off a deletion stays this device's only (files kept, as before). A device away > 400 days may bring a deleted chat back (never loses one).
- **AS-FRESH (every opening starts a new conversation, Chris 2026-10-27).** The Assistant, full app and mini window, opens on a new conversation every time it starts (`boot` clears `prefs.open`); the earlier ones stay in the conversation list (and synced, unchanged). What it was opened with comes after through `openTarget`: `#quick-ask[=text]`, selected text, a share or a deep link `{ ask }` (text in the box of the new conversation, as before), a task `{ ask, send: 1 }`, the Briefing `{ brief: 1 }`, and `{ chat: id }` (only a stored conversation; an unknown id changes nothing), used by the mini window's Open in the Assistant. An Assistant that is already running (multitasking window, app alive behind) is only brought forward: switching to it keeps the conversation on screen.
- **AS-SEL (selected text, quick access wave 3, quickmenu.js 1.2.0).** quickmenu.js wires every same-origin iframe in the shell on load (capture `load` on the shell document; apps, side and hidden frames). A mouse right-click on selected text the app leaves alone (not `defaultPrevented`, no Shift, not in a text field, which keeps the browser's Cut/Paste) opens a menu: Copy, Explain, Summarize, Translate (into the UI language, or English when already in it), Fix spelling and grammar, Ask about it…, then the user's tasks whose text has `{selection}` (those never show in the desktop menu). Touch selections, and selections in text fields, get a small Assistant button (`.qm-chip`, z 970, under the selection, 30 px lower on touch to clear the phone's handles) that opens the same menu; it hides on scroll, key, tap, resize and app change, and can be turned off per device (`oros-quick-selchip` = "0", editor checkbox). Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Q with text selected in the focused app frame opens the menu, else the mini window (`orosQuick.mini()` without a target). Each entry goes through `ask()` (mini window or the open full app) and only prefills the box; a task's own Send on tap still applies. The text is cleaned (`cleanSel`: control characters out, max 8000, a toast says when cut); `expand` caps a question at 12000. **Never offered:** frames whose window sets `__orosNoSelAsk` (Writer: its own Ask menu), the `assistant` and `passwords` folders, password and other non-text inputs, the mini frame.
- **AS-OUT (from outside orOS, quick access wave 4, quickmenu.js 1.3.0).** `#quick-ask` opens the mini window, `#quick-ask=<text>` with the text quoted in its box (`qm.selp.ask`, `cleanSel`: max 8000). A fragment never reaches the server; quickmenu.js takes it at attach and on `hashchange`, removes it from the address bar and acts once the shell's app list is in (`orosQuick.ready()` from `loadApps`, not in SOLO). Users: the web manifest's first shortcut "Ask the Assistant" (`/#quick-ask`, so Android's four include it), the browser add-on 1.1 (context menu on `selection`, `OrosExt.askUrl`), the Android widgets' Assistant button and the Quick Settings tile `AskTile` (`Widgets.askIntent`: launchUrl + `#quick-ask`; single apps remove the tile). **System share sheet:** sw.js adds `share-pick=1` to text and link shares for orOS (not for a single app); the shell then opens the "Send to…" sheet (BR-SEND, kind `link` or `text`; text without a link comes too) instead of going straight to Bookmarks, so the user picks Bookmarks, the Assistant, Notes…. The bookmarklet and add-on links (no `share-pick`) still open Bookmarks directly. Nothing is sent before Send.
- **AS-LOCAL (open-source models, Assistant phase 5 wave 4).** Local servers: `core.js LOCAL_KITS`/`KIT_IDS` (ollama :11434, lmstudio :1234, llamacpp :8080, jan :1337, localai :8080, vllm :8000, koboldcpp :5001, all `http://localhost:<port>/v1`); `provs.local.kit` (synced) remembers the choice; Settings → `Server` (`#as-kit`) fills the address and shows that program's CORS step with the site's own origin (`kit.<id>`, + Chrome local-network prompt `kit.pna`). In-browser model: provider `webllm` (`kind: "webllm"`, `device: true`, no key), `vendor/webllm/web-llm-0.2.86.js` (@mlc-ai/web-llm 0.2.86, Apache-2.0, ES module loaded with `import()` only when used) in the module worker `assistant/webllm-worker.js`; `WEBLLM_MODELS` = 11 prebuilt q4f16 models (no Gemma, per the no-Google rule), default Llama 3.2 3B. Weights come from huggingface.co (model libraries from raw.githubusercontent.com) into WebLLM's Cache API caches `webllm/model|wasm|config`; `sw.js` never deletes those on activate and serves `vendor/webllm/*` cache-first from `oros-webllm` (version in the file name), so a downloaded model works offline across releases. Only `Download the model` (`#as-wl-get`) downloads; `ready()` needs WebGPU and the model in cache (checked from the cache without loading the library); `Remove from this device` = `deleteModelAllInfoInCache`. Chat only for now (`device` = no tools, no web search, no Briefing, like `browser`); `webllmMessages` fits the 4,096-token window (`WEBLLM_CHARS` = 7,000 characters, oldest turns dropped, the newest user message kept); Qwen 3.x get `enable_thinking: false`; Stop calls `interruptGenerate`. Tests: `tests/assistant-local.test.js`.
- **AS-NOTOOLS (models without tools, Assistant phase 5 wave 5).** `noTools(pid)` = `device` providers (browser, webllm) or a local server with `provs.local.nt` = 1 (`This model can't use tools`, synced; a local 400 that mentions tools says to tick it, `err.noTools`). For them `runTurn` calls `preSearch` before the model: `core.searchWords` (stop words EN+EL dropped, ≥ 3 letters, at most `PRE_WORDS` = 3, longest first) → one `orosAssistSearch` per word → `mergeHits` (same item once, best score) → `packHits`; "Always" apps shared, "Ask first" on the usual consent card, "Never" not read; refs registered as for `search_data`. The shared result rides on the user message as `m.found = {q, text}` (stored with the chat) and `userOut` prefixes it as a marked data block (`foundBlock`, ≤ `FOUND_MAX` = 4,000 characters); a note line says what was searched and shared. The system prompt (`builtin` + `pre`) tells the model about it and never to invent data. Briefing now works for every provider (Assistant `briefCan`, Today `canBrief`); for `noTools` models `briefText(b, true)` drops refs and `propose_entry` and cuts the summaries to `BRIEF_DEV` = 4,500 characters. Files already go as device-read text (AS-ATT2). The who-line says `Stays on this device`. Tests: `tests/assistant-notools.test.js`.
- **AS-VOICE (wave 48), removed.** Voice input removed 2026-10-14 at Chris's request: Web Speech recognition sends audio to Google. `#mic-btn`, its strings and the dialog are gone; an old `voiceOk` in `oros-assistant-prefs` is ignored on load and dropped on the next save. orOS has no speech recognition anywhere (`tests/assistant-edits.test.js` checks the source has none).
- **AS-NL (newsletter by chat, wave N1, Chris 2026-10-25, plan /mnt/project-files/newsletter/newsletter-chat-compose-plan.md).** Tool `newsletter_add {blocks: [{kind: heading|text|quote|button|list|divider|spacer, text?, level?, by?, url?, items?, ordered?, align?}], subject?, issue_ref?}`, offered when Newsletter is installed and the model takes tools (also in Chat only). `core.normNewsletter` maps each block to Newsletter's own shape (`h` with `lv` 1|3, `p`, `quote`, `btn` with an http(s) `href`, `list` one item per line + `ord`, `hr`, `sp` 24) and refuses unknown kinds, empty text, a button without an http(s) url and more than `NL_MAX` (20) blocks; N2 adds `image {image_url?, alt?, url?}` → `img` (a banner is a linked picture) and `picture_text {image_url?, heading/text, button_text + button_url, side}` → `imgtxt`, with `image_url` https only (no user/password, `picUrl`) sent as `src`; N3 adds `products {products: ≤ 9 × {name, url, price?, currency?, text?, image_url?}, button_text?}` (other sites: price × 100 → cents, currency 3 letters else EUR) and `shop_products {count 1-9 = 1, search?, button_text?}` → an empty `prod` with `shop: {n, q?}` (the card says it is read from the shop when added); the prompt keeps the user's own products to shop_products, never a web search; N4 adds `section: top|news|products|promo|end` per block (refused otherwise; default `prod` for products, `promo` for image, else `news`) sent as `sec` (`NL_SECS`), and tool `newsletter_check {issue_ref?}` whose card `Ready to send?` › `Open the check` calls `__orosOpenAt("newsletter", {check: {issue}})` (the model calls it when the user says the issue is ready or asks to send); the card shows the address, never the picture (AS-R); the error goes back to the model and shows no card. `issue_ref` (a ref search_data returned for a Newsletter issue) becomes the issue id when the card is made. The card lists the blocks in words; `Open in Newsletter` re-runs the check and calls `__orosOpenAt("newsletter", {asAdd: {blocks, subj, issue}})`; `Dismiss` only marks it. The system prompt tells the model to summarise a link in its own words (read_page first when it can), quote at most one or two sentences, never say the blocks were added or sent. The Assistant never sends a newsletter.
- **AS-PUB (publisher helper, P14, 3.82.00).** `propose_entry` `post` → Publishing `{asNew:{post:1,…}}`, `settlement` → Stock `{asNew:{settle}}`; `app_summary` `stock` = `stockMonth` (sales per product and place in a month).
- **AS-COVER (book cover by chat, publisher P3b, 2026-10-25).** Tool `book_cover {title*, subtitle?, author?, back_text?, publisher?, isbn?, price?, pages?, trim (core `COVER_SIZES`), front_picture?, logo?}`, offered when Layout is installed and the model takes tools. A picture is a number (1 = the first picture of the user's latest message with pictures) or a file name (newest message first). `core.normCover` checks the ISBN check digit and every length; errors come back as `ui.k "coverErr"`. The card (`ui.k "cover"`) lists the fields and pictures; `Open` writes the ORIGINAL attached files (`attOrig`, kept in session memory only, ≤ 40 MB each) to `/internal/Pictures/Covers/<name>-<rnd>.<ext>` (never over an existing file) and calls `openAt("layout", { cover: {…, img, logo} })`; the person presses Create in Layout.
- **AS-ATT-MEM (attachments kept while orOS is open, WR-FMT, Chris 2026-10-27 "Ναι σε όλα").** Supersedes AS-ATT rule (1) "after the Assistant closes the chip says not kept": `attMem`, `attText` and `attPages` live in the shell window, `window.orosAssistAtt = { mem: {}, text: {}, pages: {} }` (`shell.js`, before `orosAssistOpen`), taken by `assistant.js` as `attStore` (a local `{}` set when there is no shell). Opening another app replaces the Assistant frame but not the shell, so a file read in one turn is still sent on the next. Still never stored, synced, exported or written to a conversation file; gone when the tab closes or reloads. `ATT_KEEP` = 400 MB of base64 kept per session; past that `attTrim()` drops the oldest files (their chips say `not kept`). Why: Chris's two PDFs showed as `not kept` after Writer opened, and the model then said it had never read them.
- **AS-GONE (honest note for a file that is gone).** `core.attNote(a, "gone")` tells the model it read the file earlier, that what it wrote stands, and that when the request needs the file again it must say so at the start of the reply and ask for it again. The system prompt (every provider with files) says a bracketed note means a file was not sent this time and that the model must never write as if it had read a file it did not get. Tests `tests/assistant-attach.test.js`, `tests/assistant-openfile.test.js`.
- **AS-OPENFILE (open an attached file in Writer, WR-FMT).** Tool `open_file {file*, app}` (`core.TOOL_OPEN_FILE`, `app` enum = keys of `OPEN_FILE_APPS` = `writer`: .pdf .docx .odt .rtf .html .htm .md .markdown .txt), offered when Writer is installed and the provider takes tools (`toolsFor({openFile})`); the system prompt says to use it for an attached document instead of retyping it. `normOpenFile(args, files)`: the file by name (case-insensitive, whole name first, then part, newest message first) among the chat's attachments; errors name the attached files, a type Writer does not open, a file that is no longer kept (`f.kept` = its data is in `attMem`) or no file at all. The result is a card (`ui {k:"file", app, id, name, st}`, `drawFile`): `Open in Writer` builds a `File` from `attMem` and calls the shell's `orosFileOpen.openIn(app, file)`, which hands it to Writer's normal Open → import dialog (new document / append / replace). Nothing is written before the user picks. A card whose file is gone says so (`file.gone`). `propose_entry` `document` now takes Markdown (`{.center}`, `{.right}`, `{.justify}` after a paragraph or heading; nested lists, `start` numbers) and goes to Writer as `newDoc: {title, text, md: true}`; the card list shows the words without marks (`mdPlain`). Tests `tests/assistant-openfile.test.js`, `tests/assistant-additems2.test.js`.
- **AS-DEV (files for an app only, LY-RB wave R2, 4.10.00).** The paper clip menu's `For an app only…` (`att.dev`) attaches files the model never receives: any type, `DEV_MAX` 200 per message, `DEV_FILE` 1 GB each, `DEV_TOTAL` 2 GB kept in the tab (`DEV_PHONE` 500 MB when `isPhone()`), checked by `core.checkDev(list, kept, f, phone)` → `"" | "size" | "count" | "total"` (toasts `att.dev.*`). The `File` is copied into the shell realm (`ownFile`) and kept in `window.orosAssistAtt.blob[id]` (memory only; never base64, never storage, sync or export; dropped on remove, clear and tab close). `normAtt` keeps `dev: 1` (exactly 1) and is the only way an unknown type passes. `userOut` replaces such a file with `attNote(a, "dev")` (name, size, "stays on their device and is not sent to you", which tools can use it); `attBudget` never counts it. Chips say `stays here` (`att.devOnly`). Why: Chris 2026-10-28 asked to lift the count and size limits so the Assistant can rebuild a 60 MB print PDF with its originals; sending them to a provider would be slow, costly and pointless, since Layout does the work on the device.
- **AS-RB (rebuild_in_layout, LY-RB wave R2).** Tool `rebuild_in_layout {pdf*, sources[], folder}` (`core.TOOL_REBUILD`), offered when Layout is installed and the provider takes tools (`toolsFor({rebuild})`, prompt line under the files block). `normRebuild(args, files)`: `pdf` an attached PDF by name (as `findFile`) or an `/internal/` path; `sources` attached pictures / texts by name (default: every kept picture and text other than the PDF); `folder` an `/internal/` folder of originals (no `..`, depth ≤ 3, ≤ `RB_FOLDER_MAX` 400 files); refusals name what is attached. The card (`ui {k:"rebuild", key, pdf, src, folder, st}`, `drawRebuild`) runs nothing until `Rebuild`: then each file goes through `orosFileOpen.hand(file)` (one-shot token, as BR-FO) and the shell opens Layout with `__orosOpenAt("layout", {rebuild: {pdf, src, folder, key, chat}})`. Layout (`openSearchTarget` → `rebuildFor`) takes the tokens, runs `LY.io.rebuild` (R1, `REBUILD_MAX` 1 GB) and writes `orosAssistAtt.rb[key] = report` (or `{failed: 1}`), then calls `orosAssistAtt.onRb()` if an Assistant frame is alive; the report dialog has `Back to the Assistant` (`__orosOpenAt("assistant", {chat})`). The Assistant (`takeRebuilt`, on load and on `onRb`) puts the report on the card and replaces the tool result with `core.rebuildReport(rep)` (numbers and replaced font names only, never text, style names or file names), saves the chat, then deletes `rb[key]`; a `pagehide` clears `onRb` only if it is still its own. `do_action open` takes `page` (whole number 1–999, app `layout` only) → `openAt("layout", {page})`, which scrolls after 120 ms (the editor needs its size first) or toasts `rb.noPage`. Edits go through Layout automations (RECIPES v1), including the new `style` step. Tests `tests/assistant-rebuild.test.js`.
- **AS-RB-SLA (a Scribus file through rebuild_in_layout, 4.15.00).** The tool also takes `sla` (an attached `.sla` / `.sla.gz` by name or an `/internal/` path); `pdf` is then optional (that file's print PDF), and `required` is gone from the schema (`normRebuild` asks for `pdf` unless `sla` is given; `rbFile` shared). The card (`ui.sla`, `rb.sla*` strings) says `Open in Layout` / `Open`; `runRebuild` hands `{rebuild: {sla, pdf, src, folder, key, chat}}`; Layout's `rebuildFor` opens it with `LY.io.openSla(sla, pictures of src + folder, pdf)` (LY-SLA-LINK, LY-FIT) and writes back `{sla: 1, pages, items, skipped, placed, missing, fit}`; `rebuildReport` turns it into `{kind: "sla", pages, objects, picturesPlaced, picturesMissing, simplified, lines?, inPlace?, percent?, pdfMatched?}` (counts only). Tests `tests/assistant-rebuild.test.js`.
- **AS-HS (house style tools, 4.23.00, wave H6; Layout LY-HS, LY-AUTO).** Three tools offered when Layout is installed (`toolsFor({house})`, prompt line `opts.house`): `learn_house_style {documents*[] ≤ 40, name}`, `layout_book {manuscript*, house, title, subtitle, author, isbn, year, publisher, keep_front}`, `add_house_rule {rule* ≤ 400, does titlePage|titleOdd|kwn|firstFlush|hyphOff, house}` (`HS_DOES` = Layout's `OWN_ACTS`, a test keeps them equal). `normHouse(name, args, files)`: names trimmed and de-duplicated; the manuscript by `rbFile` (attached by name, or an `/internal/` path) with `.docx .odt .rtf .html .htm .txt .md .markdown`; details ≤ 200 characters each. The card (`ui {k:"house", op learn|book|rule, house, key, st, docs, name | doc, meta, keepFront | text, does}`, `drawHouse`) runs nothing until its button; `runHouse` hands `__orosOpenAt("layout", {house: {op, house, key, chat, docs, name | doc {token|path}, meta, keepFront | text, does}})` (the manuscript as an `orosFileOpen.hand` token). Layout (`openSearchTarget` → `houseFor` → `LY.house.run(rq, file, back)`): learn finds each document by its name (exact, else contained, newest first; house styles and newer-model documents left out) and runs the usual learn and report; book takes the named house style (or the most recently changed one), fills the details the Assistant left out from the Publishing title of the same name (subtitle, author, ISBN, year), and runs the usual automatic layout and report (both report dialogs then have `Back to the Assistant`, `rb.back`, to the card's conversation); rule opens the house style, adds an own rule (with `does`, a style setting, else a check) through the sheet's `save`, and shows the sheet. The report goes back as for a rebuild (`assistBack(rq)` → `orosAssistAtt.rb[key]`, `onRb`; `takeHouse`), and `core.houseReport(op, rep)` keeps numbers only: learn `{works, frontPages, backPages, roles, rulesFromWorks, missing}` (the names the model gave), book `{pages, bodyPages, titles, titlesGuessed, emptyLinesDropped, manuscriptFrontLeftOut, fixes{quotes, dashes, ellipses, spaces}, fieldsFilled, contentsEntries, picturesLeftOut, rolesWithoutStyle?, pagesToCheck[{page, why}]}`, rule `{added, changes}`, failure `{failed, why noDocs|noHouse|read|learn|rule, missing}`. Strings `hs.*` (Assistant, EN, EL, DE), `hs.noNamed` (Layout). Tests `tests/assistant-house.test.js`.
  - **The book's questions (4.26.00, LY-IN wave Q3).** `layout_book` also takes the answers that differ from the series: `answers {<id>: value}` with `core.BOOK_Q` (Layout's `QUESTIONS` ids and values without "as in the series"; a test keeps them equal), `margins {top, bottom, inside, outside}` mm, `first_page_number`, `sections {prologue|thanks|notes|bio|links: front|back|out}`, `typography {<part of BOOK_PARTS = Layout's PARTS>: {font serif|sans|mono, size, leading, align left|centre|right|justified, bold, italic, caps, tracking}}`, `dedication`, `motto`, `photos [attached picture names or /internal/ paths]` (≤ 300; .jpg .png .webp .gif, or an attached image by type) and `photos_after n` (after the n-th title; left out: the end). `bookSheet` turns them into Layout's sheet `{v, a, ty, drop: [], ded?, motto?}` (an unknown question or value, or a wrong section, is a refusal the model can act on; nothing given: no sheet). The prompt line asks the model to ask first, in one message, whether everything is as in the series or what differs (photos only when there are some), to pass only the answers that differ and never guess one. The card lists them in Layout's words (`lb.*`, copies of Layout's `in.*` labels in EN, EL, DE; labels without their parenthesis) then "everything else as in the series", and has `All the questions…` (`hs.all`) beside `Lay out`. `runHouse(ui, c, all)` adds `sheet`, `all: 1`, and `photos [{token|path}]`; Layout's `houseFor` takes the photos (one not received is counted, `missed`) and `LY.house.run(rq, f, back, photos, missed)` lays out with `overSheet(I.defaults(house), rq.sheet)` (the series' kept answers, the Assistant's on top): straight on, or with `all` the questions dialog first, filled in and with the photos listed; closing it reports `{failed, why: "cancel"}` (card `hs.cancel`). So every book the Assistant lays out now goes through LY-IN (all answers as in the series when nothing differs). The report adds `photosPlaced`, `textDoesNotFit`, `sectionsMoved`, `sectionsLeftOut` (card `hs.repPhotos`, `hs.repPhotosOut`, `hs.repOverset`).
- **AS-EDIT (edit_in_app / read_in_app, 4.30.00, wave AC1 of the "Assistant controls the apps" plan; Atelier first).** The Assistant changes anything in an app's documents only through that app's fixed command catalog. Contract every app follows (Layout joins in 4.33.00, see the Layout bullet):
  - **Catalog module** (Atelier: `atelier/commands.js`, `window.AtelierCommands`, also loaded by the Assistant): `CATALOG` (RECIPES spec format, `recipes/core.js` `normStep`), `ORDER`, `GUIDE` (the model's text), `MAX_STEPS` 40, `check(list) → {ok, steps} | {ok:false, err}` (English errors that go back to the model), `targets(data, folders, open, designs, name)` (designs `open|named|folder|all`), `preview(data, ids, steps) → {n, d, per, cut, notes}` (the app's own dry run on JSON copies, before Apply), `outline(doc)` (what `read_in_app` gives the model: ≤ 300 elements, text ≤ 300 characters, ids, never asset ids or file contents), `apply(doc, st, env)` (pure, returns the count). One field name has one JSON type across every catalog the Assistant declares (`recipes/share.js` too; recipes' `q` is the only known exception and is described on its tool); a test checks it.
  - **Picking**: `ids` (element ids from `read_in_app`), `pages` (`""`, odd, even, first, last, `2-4,6`), `what` (text, photo, video, shape, icon, line, table, chart, bg; `""` = everything but page backgrounds), `has` (words in the text or a photo's file name). A locked element is moved or removed only when named by id. Atelier's 17 commands: replace, settext, textstyle, recolor, colors, photo, cutout (async, `AT.recipes.cutOne`), place, align, arrange, remove, pages, delpages, movepage, bg, bleed (print designs only), rename (open or named design only). Lengths are in the design's unit.
  - **Assistant** (`assistant/core.js` `editTool`/`readAppTool`/`normEdit`/`normReadApp`, `EDIT_APP`; `assistant.js` `editCats`, `readInApp`, `proposeEdit`, `runEdit`, `drawEdit`, `editUndo`). Offered when the provider takes tools, data search is on and the app may be read (`toolsFor({edits})`, prompt line). `read_in_app` asks like any read unless the app is `Always share`. `edit_in_app` shows a card (`ui {k:"edit", args, key, st}`) with the commands in words and the preview counts, recomputed whenever drawn; nothing changes before `Apply`; removals or more than `EDIT_CONFIRM` 50 changes ask once more. Nothing matching is an error back to the model.
  - **Apply goes through the app frame, never storage** (an open app would overwrite a direct write): `__orosOpenAt(app, {edit: {key, chat, docs, steps}})`. The app checks the commands again, applies, keeps undo data on the device and writes `orosAssistAtt.rb[key] = {ok, n, d, per:[{name, n}], cut, notes, tok, stopped?} | {failed, why}` (AS-RB pattern, `onRb`). The card shows the report; the model gets counts and note codes (`maxPages`, `lastPage`, `photoBg`, `screenBleed`, `locked`, `noCut`).
  - **Undo is app-side**: `tok` names a record (Atelier: IndexedDB `oros-atelier-assist` store `undo`, 30 days, 50 entries) with each design's state before and a fingerprint after. `__orosOpenAt(app, {editUndo: {key, tok}})` restores (Atelier `AT.restoreDoc`, as a new edit) only if no design changed since, else `{failed, why: "changed"}`; `gone` / `undone` otherwise. The Assistant's change history (AS-HIST) records `{edit: {app, tok}}`, and `runUndo` sends it to the app (60 s timeout). The card never replays inverse commands.
  - **Wave AC2 (4.31.00).** More Atelier commands: `animate` (entrance `anim` fade|rise|pop|wipe|type|none on picked elements, type on texts only), `pagetime` (page background `dur` 1-60 s and `ptr` transition), `add` (a new text, shape, icon or line on `page`; left-out position centred, size sensible; `icon` is a word Atelier matches against the icon library's ids and EN/EL keywords), `brand` (the brand kit `oros-atelier-brand`: texts ≥ 75 % of the largest size get the heading font, ≥ 50 % the subheading font when set, the rest the body font; the design's most used colours other than white and black become the kit's colours in order; no kit → note `noBrand`), `resize` (`sizes [{w, h, u}]`, `copies` true by default: a copy per size through `AT.io.relaid` + `AT.addCopies`, and the commands after it change the copies; false: the design itself to the first size), `export` (fmt png|jpg|pdf, scale, dpi: Atelier renders the files and then asks with its own `Save…` dialog, because a save picker needs a press inside Atelier), `create` (first command only; `edit_in_app` `designs: "new"`, set by `normEdit` whenever the first command is create: `AX.newDesign` with title, w, h, u, n pages, fill, then the rest of the commands fill it in). Preview and report add `made` (copies and new designs) and `files`; the undo record lists made designs as `{id, fp, made: 1}` and Undo removes them with `AT.dropDoc` (refused, like the rest, if one changed since). The tool schema gives list fields their object fields (`specSchema`), so `sizes` is an array of `{w, h, u}`.
  - **Wave PL1 (4.35.00): Photo Lab.** Catalog `photolab/commands.js` (`window.PhotoLabCommands`, also loaded by the Assistant); Photo Lab's synced slice holds only the project index, so the Assistant's `EDIT_SRC.photolab` is marked `disk`: it picks projects on the index (`oros-photolab-data` `projects`) and reads each picked project's `doc.json` from the orOS disk (`docPath(id)`, at most 200 at a time, kept while the index `m` is unchanged) before the card counts (`editLoad`; the card says "Counting…" until they are read). Layers are picked with `ids`, `what` (photo, text, shape, adj) and `has` (layer name or text). Command kinds: `doc` (layer properties, order, position, remove, duplicate counting, texts, layer styles, adjustment layers, new text and shape layers, rename: `apply()` on the record, in the app inside one `PL.docChange`), `px` (tone, look, gray, blur, sharpen, noise with the automations' fields so `recipesteps.job` runs them, plus `dup` and `watermark`: the editor's own commands on each picked layer; without a pick every visible, unlocked photo layer), `size` (crop, canvas, resize, rotate, flip: the editor's commands; the preview keeps `w × h` so later commands count right), `out` (export: saved into `Pictures`, counted as files, no save dialog needed). Apply (`photolab/assist.js`, loaded with `commands.js` on the first request so Photo Lab's first open stays within its budget) opens each project in the editor, clears the selection (whole layers), runs every command as one History step and saves; the undo record (IndexedDB `oros-photolab-assist`, 30 days, 50 entries) keeps each project's `doc.json` before and its `m` after. Undo is refused when a project's `m` changed since (`changed`) or a tile the old record names is gone (`gone`); tiles are content-named and never removed (`store.gc` is not called), so the old record's pixels are still there; Undo writes the old record with a new `m` (`PL.putIndex`) and opens each project once so its thumbnail follows. Photo Lab writes the open project to `oros-photolab-prefs.doc` ("the open picture"). `photolab/search.js` (names and sizes from the index) makes Photo Lab a searchable app, which is also what lets the Assistant's permissions cover it. Card words: `edT(app, key)` tries `key + "." + app` first (`ed.will.photolab` says pictures; `ed.op.resize.photolab` "Image size").
  - **Wave SL1 (4.37.00): Slides.** Catalog `slides/commands.js` (`window.SlidesCommands`, needs `slides/core.js`; the Assistant loads both on the first turn or card that needs them, `EDIT_LAZY`, so its first open stays within budget). Slides keeps every presentation in one synced store, so `EDIT_SRC.slides` is marked `view`: the catalog's `view(data)` lists the decks as documents (each carries the canonical store, non-enumerable, for `outline`), and the open one is `oros-slides-prefs.deck` (`open: "deck"`). A presentation is worked on as a small store of its own (`part(data, deckId)`: the deck, its slides and their objects in core.js data shape), so core.js mutations (`addSlide`, `duplicateSlide`, `moveSlide`, `deleteSlide`, `applyLayout`, `setAspect`, `setNotes`, `setItemParas`, `setAnim`) do the work and `normItem` keeps every value in bounds. Objects are picked with `ids`, `pages` (slides), `what` ("" every object, or text, title, photo, shape, line, table, chart) and `has` (text, or a picture's description); a locked object is moved, aligned, restacked or removed only when named by id (note `locked`). Commands: replace (texts, table cells, chart titles and, when no object is named, the picked slides' speaker notes; a match across formatting runs makes the paragraph one run in the first run's look), settext, textstyle, colors, photo (fit, round, alt), place, align, arrange, remove, animate (entrance: effect, fly side, start), add (text, shape, line), pages (n slides at the end, before or after a slide, as copies or with a layout), delpages (one slide stays), movepage, slide (layout, transition and its length, hide), bg, notes (set or append), deck (theme, aspect, footer, numbers, date), rename. Apply (`slides/assist.js`, loaded with `commands.js` and `recipes/core.js` on the first request) runs the commands on a copy and writes it back with `SL.putDeck` (app.js `applyState` for any deck: fresh stamps, so it syncs like any edit; the open deck gets one undo step); the undo record (IndexedDB `oros-slides-assist`, 30 days, 50 entries) keeps each deck's state before (`SL.deckState`) and a fingerprint after; Undo is refused when the fingerprint changed (`changed`). Card words: field labels also go through `edT` (`ed.f.pages.slides` "slides"), `ed.v.pages.*` names all, odd, even, first and last. Export stays in Slides' own menu (PDF and PowerPoint need the save dialog).
  - **Wave WR1 (4.40.00): Writer.** Catalog `writer/commands.js` (`window.WriterCommands`, needs only `recipes/core.js`; the Assistant loads it on first use, `EDIT_LAZY.writer`). Writer keeps every document in one synced slice, so `EDIT_SRC.writer` is marked `view` (`view(data)` lists the live documents, named by title or, untitled, by their first words; each carries its slice record, non-enumerable) and the open one is `oros-writer-prefs.active`. A document's text is Writer's stored html (browser serialization, sanitized); the catalog reads it with a small tag-aware parser (`parse` / `ser`, no DOM, so Node tests run it as it is) and writes anew only the nodes a command touches, so everything else comes back byte for byte. Paragraphs (blocks: top-level paragraphs, headings, quotes, code, tables and each list item; loose top-level text is one paragraph, wrapped in `<p>` only when a command needs an element) are picked with `paras` (positions as `pages`), `what` ("" or para, heading, h1-h4, item, quote, code, table) and `has`; footnote numbers (`sup.fn-ref`) and tracked deletions (`del.tc`) are not text. Commands: replace (per text run group; a match across formatting goes into the first run's look; with nothing picked also the header, footer and footnotes), settext (more lines make more paragraphs of the same kind), textstyle (bold, ital, under, strike on/off for whole paragraphs, or on for the words `find` matches; only the looks a run lacks are added, so twice changes nothing; align as `text-align`), style (tag p, h1-h4, quote, code, bullet, number: lists are made, joined with a following list of the same kind, switched, or split when an item leaves; `brk` adds or removes the `page-break-marker` before a paragraph or list), add (one paragraph or list item per line, start, end, before or after a paragraph; text, never markup), remove, page (paper as `PAPER_SIZES`, margins t/b/l/r 0-100 mm, header, footer; a single space clears), meta (author, tags, category, lang auto/en/el/none), rename. Footnotes whose number left the text are dropped with it (as Writer's own clean-up). Apply (`writer/assist.js`, loaded with `commands.js` on the first request through `WriterAssistHost`, which writer.js sets up) flushes the editor, runs the commands on `work(record)`, puts the new html through `WriterIO.sanitizeHtml`, writes the changed fields and stamps only the WR-6 clock groups that changed (c, m, p), then re-renders the open document so the next save sees no difference. The undo record (IndexedDB `oros-writer-assist`, 30 days, 50 entries) keeps the fields before and a fingerprint of the fields after with the html sanitized again (opening the document is not a change); Undo writes the fields back as a new edit, refused when the fingerprint changed. With Track changes on, the change is not tracked (note `untracked`). Not covered yet: images, links, tables' structure, comments, footnote text by number.
  - **AC4, Assistant side (4.41.00): My style.** `EDIT_SRC.atelier.style` names localStorage `oros-atelier-style` (the profile `atelier/style.js` keeps on the device, Part IV "ATELIER v1, My style"). `read_in_app` of a design passes the stored profile to `AtelierCommands.outline(doc, style)`, so the outline carries the summary for the design's kind. `read_in_app` with `designs: "style"` (Atelier only; `name` = a kind: square, 4:5, 9:16, 16:9, A portrait, bookmark, banner, or none for every kind) returns `{app, style: {kind: summary}}` through `styleOf`, behind the same read card as a design (`askRead`, title "My style", `ed.myStyle` EN/EL/DE) unless Atelier's permission is "always"; no profile or no such kind returns a note naming the kinds there are. Never written into the tool text or the system prompt.
  - **Wave SS1 (4.42.00): Spreadsheet.** Catalog `spreadsheet/commands.js` (`window.SheetCommands`, needs `recipes/core.js`, `functions.js` and `sheetkit.js`; the Assistant loads all three on first use, `EDIT_LAZY.spreadsheet`). The documents are the workbook's sheets: `EDIT_SRC.spreadsheet` is `view` (`view(data, lang)` lists the sheets by position, named as the app shows them; a seed sheet also answers to its English and Greek names) and `raw` (the open sheet is the plain id in `oros-spreadsheet-active`, not JSON; none stored → the first sheet, as the app opens). Cells are picked with `range` in A1 notation (`B2`, `B2:D9`, whole columns `B`/`B:D`, whole rows `3`/`3:5`, which cover only the cells in use; `""` = every cell in use) and, for format and clear, `has`. Commands: `set` (text from the range's top-left cell, lines = rows, tab = cells; one value over several cells is filled like the fill handle with `FX.shiftFormula`; "" empties; formats stay; the sheet grows), `replace` (values only; a formula that matches is left and noted `formulas`), `clear` (part values|format|fill|border or all), `format` (bold, ital, under, align, valign, c, fill, numfmt gen|0|2|pct|eur|date → nf, wrap, border all|outer|bottom|none as the Format menu does), `size` (w 40-400 px per column, h 18-400 px per row; the default removes the entry), `insert` / `remove` (rows or cols; the same moves as `structural()`: `FX.adjustFormula` in every sheet, cw/rh shift, rules and charts follow `KIT.adjRange`; removing keeps the sheet's size, as the app does; a full sheet notes `maxDims`), `sort` (as `sortSelection`: values worked out by an `FX.engine` over the copy, heading on|off or guessed, formulas shifted to their new row; `by` outside the range notes `sortBy`), `merge` (each row|col; only the top-left value stays, noted `mergeLost`), `unmerge`, `freeze` (`cell`: rows above and columns left; A1 unfreezes; FZ limits), `rename` (24 characters as the tab editor; a formula naming the old name notes `sheetRefs`). At most 100,000 cells per command (`big`). Field names keep one JSON type across catalogs (`range`, `rows`, `cols`, `by`, `cell` strings; `desc` bool). Spreadsheet (`spreadsheet/assist.js`, loaded with `recipes/core.js` and `commands.js` on the first `edit` / `editUndo` target, through `window.SheetAssistHost`) applies the list to a copy of the whole workbook (`work`), then writes only what differs: cells with `rawSet` / `rawDel` (per-field stamps SS-5, tombstones), changed sheets' size, widths, heights, frozen panes and name with a new mtime, charts and rules with `applyObj`; the same writes are pushed as one step of the app's own Undo. Undo record in IndexedDB `oros-spreadsheet-assist` (30 days, 50 entries): every written cell's earlier copy (with `cv`), each sheet's earlier parts and each object's earlier record, plus a fingerprint of what was written; Undo is refused when any of it changed since or a sheet is gone. Tokens start `ss-`. Charts and rules are not commands in this wave; new and deleted sheets stay in the app.
  - **Wave MT1 (4.43.00): Montage.** Catalog `montage/commands.js` (`window.MontageCommands`, needs `recipes/core.js` and `montage/core.js`; the Assistant loads core and catalog on first use, `EDIT_LAZY.montage`). The documents are video projects in the one synced slice `oros-montage`: `EDIT_SRC.montage` is `view` (`view(data)` lists the projects newest first through `MontageCore.projectList`, each carrying its project non-enumerable for `outline`), and the open project is `oros-montage-prefs.open` (`open: "open"`), which Montage now writes when a project opens and clears on the projects view (this device only; the field is not read back at start, so the app still opens on the projects view). Clips are picked with `ids`, `what` ("" or video|image|audio|title|shape), `row` ("" or main|overlay|text|music|voice, the app's own row names; not `track`, which is letter spacing in Atelier and Slides) and `has` (words in a title), in timeline order (main row first). Commands: `replace`, `settext` (titles), `textstyle` (font sans|serif|mono|display, size 2-40 % of the frame, c, stroke, fill = the text box or a shape's colour, back = a title card's background, align l|c|r, anim none|fade|rise|pop), `clip` (speed 0.25-4, vol 0-200, mute on|off for video and sound; fi/fo; opacity; flt, fit, rot 0|90|180|270, flip h|none, bright/contrast/sat/warmth for video and pictures; secs = length: a picture or title lasts that long, video and sound are cut at the end, a clip with a speed curve keeps its length and notes `ramp`), `transition` (trans none or MontageCore.TRANSITIONS, secs 0.1-2; into main clips after the first), `move` (`after` an id or start for main clips, `time` for the other rows, x/y/w/h in % for boxes), `add` (title on the text row, card = a full-screen title on the main row at the end or after `after`, shape on the overlay row; ids from the app's `uid`; `maxClips` at MontageCore.MAX_ITEMS), `split` (at `time`, through MontageCore.split; a clip not running through it notes `noClips`), `remove` (needs a pick; tombstones), `project` (ratio, fps 30|60, back, duck 0-90), `rename`. Every change goes through MontageCore's own edits (`setItem`, `addItem`, `delItem`, `moveMain`, `split`, `setProject`), so values are normalised and stamped as by hand; a command counts the clips that differ plus one for the project's own fields. Montage (`montage/assist.js`, loaded with `recipes/core.js` and `commands.js` on the first `edit` / `editUndo` target, through `window.MontageAssistHost`) applies the list to a copy of each project (`work`) and merges the copy into its data (`MontageCore.merge`, newer stamps win), saves once and refreshes; when the open project changed, its earlier copy goes on Montage's own Undo first. Undo record in IndexedDB `oros-montage-assist` (30 days, 50 entries): each project's earlier copy and a fingerprint of the projects as written; Undo brings them back with `MontageCore.restoreProject` (a newer edit, so it syncs) and is refused when any of them changed since or is gone. Tokens start `mt-`. Keyframes, speed curves, chroma key, borders, reframing, stickers, subtitles from files and media itself stay in the app.
  - **Wave ST1 (4.44.00): Studio.** Catalog `studio/commands.js` (`window.StudioCommands`, needs `recipes/core.js` and `studio/core.js`; the Assistant loads both on first use, `EDIT_LAZY.studio`). The documents are song projects in the synced slice `oros-studio-data` (flat lists of projects, tracks, sources and clips): `EDIT_SRC.studio` is `view` (`view(data)` lists the projects newest first; each doc carries the whole slice non-enumerable as `store`, and its id names the project), and the open project is `oros-studio-prefs.cur` (`open: "cur"`; none stored → the newest, as Studio opens). Tracks are picked with `tracks` (numbers from the top, names or ids, comma separated) and `what` ("" | audio | midi = instrument tracks); clips also with `ids` and `has` (words in the clip's name: the recording's or the MIDI clip's). Commands: `clip` (gain GAIN_MIN..GAIN_MAX dB, fi/fo, `time` or `bar` = start, `secs` = length through `trimEnd`, audio never past its file → note `short`), `split` (at `time` or the start of `bar`, `splitClip`; MAX_CLIPS → `maxClips`), `notes` (MIDI clips: `semis` -24..24, never on a drum track → note `drums`, clamped at 0/127 → note `range`; `vel` 1-127 for every note), `remove` (clips; needs a pick), `track` (vol dB, pan, mute, solo, `c` snapped to the nearest of Studio's eight colours, `title` = name, `after` a track or start = new order), `addtrack` (at the bottom, audio or midi with `inst` of midi.js ORDER, named in the user's language through `env.trackName`; MAX_TRACKS → `maxTracks`), `deltrack` (tracks with their clips; asks once more on the card like `remove`), `project` (bpm, MIDI clips retimed with `retimeClip` as Studio's `setProject` does, audio stays in time; sig 2-7; master vol; `loop` on|off; `bars` "a-b" = the loop from bar a to the end of bar b at the new tempo and beats), `rename`. Every change is written as Studio's `put()` / `remove()` write it: normalised by StudioCore and stamped `max(now, tombstone + 1, m + 1)`, deletions as tombstones; a command counts the entities whose content (without stamps) changed. Track numbers and bars mean the song as it is when the command runs, `semis` moves the notes again on a second run, and the card's word for a track is "κανάλι" in Greek as in Studio. Studio (`studio/assist.js`, loaded with `recipes/core.js` and `commands.js` on the first `edit` / `editUndo` target, through `window.StudioAssistHost`) refuses while recording, dragging or editing in the piano roll (`busy`), applies the list to a copy of each project (`work`), merges the copy with `StudioCore.mergeStudio`, saves, redraws and replays; when the open project changed, its earlier copy (`snapshot()`) goes on Studio's own Undo first. Undo record in IndexedDB `oros-studio-assist` (30 days, 50 entries): each project's earlier copy (`snapshot(data, pid)`) and a fingerprint; Undo writes it back with `restore()` (Studio's own restore: entities not in the copy are tombstoned, the rest written with newer stamps) and is refused when a project changed since or is gone. Tokens start `st-`. Studio gained a search provider (`studio/search.js`, apps.json `search`; hits open with the target `{ project }`), because the Assistant offers only apps the person can allow it to read, and those are the searchable ones. Effects, automation lanes, single notes, recording and audio files stay in Studio.
  - **Wave WB1 (4.45.00): Whiteboard.** Catalog `whiteboard/commands.js` (`window.WhiteboardCommands`, needs `recipes/core.js` and `whiteboard/core.js`; the Assistant loads both on first use, `EDIT_LAZY.whiteboard`). The documents are boards in the synced slice `oros-whiteboard-data`: `EDIT_SRC.whiteboard` is `view` (`view(data)` lists the boards newest first by their last edit; each doc carries the whole slice non-enumerable as `store`), and the open board is `oros-whiteboard-prefs.board` (`open: "board"`; none stored → the newest). Objects are picked with `ids`, `what` ("" | note | text | shape | arrow | pen | image | frame), `has` (words in the text) and `frame` (a frame's name or id: what lies inside it, as `inFrame`; not found → note `noFrame`). Commands: `replace` and `settext` (notes, texts, shapes, arrow labels, frame names; a text's height follows its lines through `textHeight`), `style` (`c` as #rrggbb snapped to the nearest of the board's ten colours, strong or soft shade; `shape` and `fill` of shapes, `size` of free text, `ends` and `dash` of arrows, `sw` of pen lines), `move` (`dx`/`dy`, or `x`/`y` for the first picked one with the rest keeping their places, `w`/`h` through `resized`, `order` front|back above or below everything), `arrange` (a grid of `n` columns, default about square, `gap`, from `x`/`y` or the first one; arrows, pen lines and frames stay), `add` (note, text, shape or frame; without `x`/`y` to the right of everything; frames under the rest), `connect` (an arrow stuck to two objects named by id or by words of their text; not found → note `noEnd`), `remove` (needs a pick; arrows stuck to a removed object come loose, as by hand) and `rename`. A board holds at most 2000 objects (note `full`), as in the app. Every change goes through `WhiteboardCore.apply` and `putBoard` (new stamps, tombstones). `whiteboard/assist.js` (`WhiteboardAssistHost`, IndexedDB `oros-whiteboard-assist`, tokens `wb-`) merges with `WhiteboardCore.merge`; a change to the open board is one step of that board's own Undo (the rows before and after). Undo from the card restores the board through `restore()` (every object as it was and the name, as new edits) and is refused when the board changed since. Nothing is applied while a gesture or a text edit is under way (`busy`). The Assistant's card names a new object's kind even when it is the default one (all catalogs).
  - **Wave MM1 (4.46.00): Mind map.** Catalog `mindmap/commands.js` (`window.MindmapCommands`, needs `recipes/core.js` and `mindmap/mm-core.js`; the Assistant loads both on first use, `EDIT_LAZY.mindmap`; mm-core attaches `MMCore` to `this`, the page's window). The documents are maps in the synced slice `oros-mindmap-data`: `EDIT_SRC.mindmap` is `view` (`view(data)` lists the maps newest first by their last edit, named by the centre's text; each doc carries the whole slice non-enumerable as `store`), and the open map is `oros-mindmap-prefs.map` (`open: "map"`). Ideas are picked with `ids`, `has` (words), `branch` (an idea by id or words: it and everything under it) and `level` (1 = main branches, by `depthOf`); `to`, `from` and `branch` name one idea by id, whole text or words (`noIdea` when none). Commands: `replace`, `settext`, `add` (one idea or a list read by `parseOutline` and written by `treeToRows` under `to`, at the end, as the app's paste does; c, emoji and note on the top ideas; MAX_NODES → note `mapFull`), `node` (`c` as #rrggbb snapped to the eight branch colours, `emoji`, `note`, `url` (http/https only), "none" clears these three, `done`, and the style row: `shape`, `fill`, `border`, `nodesize` s|m|l (m = the default ""), `bold`), `move` (under `to`, at the end, order keys from `placeAt` with respacing; never inside itself → note `loop`), `sort` (the ideas under each picked idea, or the centre's, A-Z by `localeCompare` numeric, `desc` Z-A, new keys from `spread`), `link` (a cross-link with `text` as label), `frame` (a boundary `kind` box or a summary brace, `text`, `c`, at most 50 ideas → note `frameMax`), `remove` (with everything under, the cross-links touching it and a frame left without members; never the centre → note `centre`), `map` (`layout` map|org|tree|time as a layouts row, "map" writes the default ""; `sides`) and `rename` (the centre's text; a map with only the drawn centre gets a real centre row). Every row is built with mm-core's normalisers and stamped above its own stamp and any tombstone, as the app's put*() and nextM() do. `mindmap/assist.js` (`MindmapAssistHost`, IndexedDB `oros-mindmap-assist`, tokens `mm-`) merges with `MMCore.merge`; a change to the open map is one step of Mind map's own Undo (the host `touch`es every row of the map in the old and new data inside one `begin` / `commit`, so undo and redo re-apply a side with fresh stamps). Undo from the card restores the map through `restore()` (rows written again, newer ones tombstoned; positions, pictures, styles and layout kinds get a default row, as `tombRow` does) and is refused when the map changed since. Nothing is applied while an idea is being typed or dragged (`busy`).
  - Private material (Chris's Canva corpus, books) never goes into the repo, tests or this Bible; tests build their own designs. Tests `tests/atelier-commands.test.js`.
  - **Layout (4.33.00).** `layout/commands.js` (`window.LayoutCommands`, also loaded by the Assistant with only `designkit/model.js` and `layout/recipesteps.js`, never the text engine): the catalog is Layout's automation steps (LY-RC, Q5) without preflight and export, plus `rename {title}`: text, pstyle, style, master, margins, pages, delpages, fit, numbering, bleed, grey, imgfit, rename. Styles and masters by id or any language's name, pages by position (`S.pageTest`). `targets` takes designs `open|named|all` (`folder` is refused: Layout has no folders; `M.needsNewer` documents are skipped). `preview` counts black and white on fake copies (`a+"~"`). Without the text engine `fit` counts 1 and adds note `fitLater`, and `pages` adds pages with `flow: 0`; Layout runs both for real on Apply. `outline(doc)`: size, margins and bleed in mm, first page number, paragraph styles (name, paragraphs using it, size, font, align), masters, and per page (≤400) its master, the start of each story (≤6 × 160 characters, a story listed once) and its picture count, never asset ids. `layout/assist.js` (`LY.assist.edit/undo`, IndexedDB `oros-layout-assist`, tokens `le-…`): checks the commands again, makes black and white copies through `LY.recipeGrey` (recipes.js `greyCopies`), applies the open document through `LY.op` (one undo step) and others through `LY.putDoc`, undo through `LY.restoreDoc` when the fingerprints still match. Card words: `ed.op.*`, `ed.f.*`, `ed.f.<op>.<field>` (a field one command names its own way: `ed.f.numbering.n`), `ed.v.font.*`, `ed.v.brk|hyph|on|mode.*`, `ed.note.fitLater`. Tests `tests/layout-commands.test.js`.

`apps.json` lists 24 apps (verified 2026-10-06; details in Part VIII). The 2026-10-01 note counted 22: weather, time, files, calculator, todo, kanban, notes, calendar, quote, minimalism, contacts, storage, spreadsheet, writer, prompter, characters, mood, habits, cycle, bookmarks, dice, radio. Screen Pet and Notifications are shell components, not `apps.json` apps. **[log]** A later note says the count should have been 23 with `maps`, and `television` (category `video`) was added after that → 24 expected. Re-count when `apps.json` is on the table (A8).

### Device-local keys (never synced)

- **Shell (verified 2026-10-05):** oros-last-version, oros-autoexport-last, oros-fs-folder-name, oros-fs-lapsed, oros-wx-cache, oros-wx-last, oros-cal-reminders-fired, oros-files-disk-pending, oros-reset-db (factory-reset marker), oros-lang (mirror), oros-backup-enc ("1" = backup files encrypted, BK-E); sessionStorage `oros-skip-splash` and the bridge staging keys (table in Part II). IndexedDB `oros-fs` (store `handles`: `backup-folder` handle, `backup-key` = BK-E `{ key (non-extractable AES-GCM), s, it }`). Also device-local but owned by `sync.js`: oros-sync-* engine keys, oros-slices (registry).
- **CalDAV / CardDAV sync state (W3, 2026-11-01):** IndexedDB `oros-dav`, store `state`, one record per linked collection (`cal|<url>`, Contacts `card|<url>` since W4, To-Do `todo|<url>` since W5): `{ link, st: { v: 1, token, items, raw } }` (ETags, hashes, ids and the server's own text of each item). Device-local, never synced or exported; in the factory reset list. See `davsync.js`.
- **CalDAV / CardDAV background pass (W6, 2026-11-01):** `oros-davbg-off` ("1" = the Settings switch is off; absent = on) and `oros-davbg-last` (`{ at, apps: { calendar|contacts|todo: { at, err, held } } }`, the last round and each app's last result). Device-local, never synced; removed by the factory reset with every `oros-*` key. See `shell.js` section 10e.
- **CalDAV / CardDAV account (W2, 2026-10-31):** `oros-caldav-conf` (`{ url, user, relay?, principal, calHome, cardHome }`), `oros-caldav-pass` (the app password), `oros-caldav-cols` (the collections found at the last check). Written only by `davkit.js` after the probe passed; removed by Disconnect and by a factory reset. See `davkit.js`.
- **Screen lock (LK, 2026-10-27):** `oros-lock` (slow hash + options), `oros-lock-tries`; sessionStorage `oros-lock-seen`. See `lock.js`.
- **Error journal (DIAG, 4.67.00):** `oros-diag-log` = `[{ t, app, kind: "error"|"promise", msg, at, n? }]` (last 60, written by `diag.js` with what `i18n.js` catches, read only by Settings › System › Report a problem; `orosDiag.clear()` empties it).
- **On-screen keyboard (OSK, 2026-10-27):** `oros-osk` = `{ v:1, mode?: "auto"|"button"|"off", layouts?: ["en","el","de"…], last? }` (absent fields = the device default; `last` = the layout used last). See `osk.js`.
- **Desktop widgets (WG, 4.54.00):** `oros-widgets` = `{ v:1, list:[…] }` (absent = the default for the screen). See `widgets.js`.
- **Do Not Disturb (QS, 4.53.00):** `oros-dnd` = `"on"` (until turned off) or the end time in ms; an ended or unreadable value is off. See `notifications.js` and `qsettings.js`.
- **Universal search (2026-10-09):** `oros-search-prefs` (per-app on/off switches) and sessionStorage `oros-open-at` (generic deep-link staging, one-shot).
- **Shell keys that TRAVEL in the `shell` slice:** oros-lang, oros-theme, oros-skin, oros-wallpaper, oros-wallpaper-art (since 0.45.04), oros-autoexport, oros-weather, oros-alarms, oros-shell-stamps, oros-alarm-tombs. (`oros-files-disk-cache`, `-pending`, `-meta` are legacy: removed at boot by `fdMigrateLegacy`.)
- `oros-auto-snapshots` (listed here until 2026-10-05): the subsystem is gone, but the KEY stayed on devices that had it (up to 5 full unencrypted DB copies, MBs). Since 0.52.02 (SY-Q2) `legacyLsMove()` moves it at boot into IndexedDB **oros-legacy** (store `kv`, same key) and removes it from localStorage only after the write committed. Factory reset deletes `oros-legacy`.
- **Weather:** oros-wx-cache, oros-wx-last, oros-wx-tray (device-local tray switch, since 2026-10-09).
- **FS:** oros-fs-*.
- **Pet:** oros-pet-enabled, oros-pet-pos, oros-pet-minimized, oros-pet-calendar-sync (read-only legacy mirror of oros-pet-settings).
- **Radio:** oros-radio-recents, oros-radio-cache:*; since W42 `oros-radio-history` (`[{t (ms), s (title ≤ 200), n (station name), u (stationuuid)}]`, newest first, ≤ 300: "what was playing" from ICY / Icecast metadata, device only, never synced), sessionStorage `oros-radio-wake` (one-shot: the next `__orosRadioOpen` came from a wake-up alarm, so it fades in).
- **Calendar:** oros-cal-reminders-fired, oros-cal-feedvis (on/off of the Holidays / Name days / World days chips, device-local), oros-cal-days (weekly cache of calendar/days.json, device-local), oros-cal-pending (event deep links `calendar:{evId}:{ymd}`). `oros-calendar-chips-open` (since 0.80.01: phone-width chips list open/closed, device-local). Since Calendar wave 8: `oros-cal-subs-cache` (subscribed calendars' events, per device), `oros-cal-free-prefs` (Share free times choices). `oros-cal-month-names` (since 4.47.01: "1" = Month cells show event names instead of dots; removed when off; device-local). **[log]** sessionStorage `oros-cal-new` (new-event prefill, BR-W8-2).
- **Maps [log]:** oros-maps-route (last-known route snapshot), oros-maps-rescue (copy of an unreadable oros-maps-data), oros-maps-prefs (`{ lat, lon, zoom, layer }`, R10 view state), oros-maps-open (staging), oros-maps-recent (up to 10 recent places `{ name, sub, lat, lon }`, newest first, since 0.43.00), oros-maps-route-prefs (`{ avoid: ""|toll|motorway|ferry, headUp: bool }`, the car's avoid choice since 1.55.00, heading-up navigation since 2026-10-31; absent headUp = north up), oros-maps-transit (`{ stops: 0|1, live: 0|1 }`, the public transport map switches, since 1.63.00), oros-maps-overlay (the quest overlay id: lit | surface | sidewalk | address, absent = none, since 1.67.00), oros-maps-fav-prefs (`{ hide: [gid], fold: [gid | "_none"] }`, favourite groups hidden from the map / folded in the list, since 1.75.00), oros-maps-fav-rescue (copy of an unreadable oros-maps-fav-data), oros-maps-discover (`{ tab: places|wiki|photos, cat, open: 0|1 }`, the Discover sheet's choices, since 1.78.00), oros-maps-packs (`{ src? }`, an own PMTiles source for offline map packs, absent = newest Protomaps build; wave 51). OPFS `maps-packs/` (offline map packs, device-only, removed by the factory reset: shell `wipeMapPacks`). sessionStorage `oros-maps-nav` (timestamp of a running navigation, refreshed every 30 s, removed on exit / arrival / clear route). Cache Storage `oros-map-tiles` (deleted by the factory reset since Dose 2).
- **Television [log]:** oros-television-recents (cap 20), oros-television-volume, oros-television-files (wave 43: opened playlist / guide files). sessionStorage `oros-television-open` (staging). Cache Storage `oros-television-api` (24 h TTL; since wave 43 also `pl-*`, `epg-*-<ymd>`, `epgf-*`).
- **Mail (since 0.46.00):** oros-mail-prefs (`{acct, folder, plain}`). IndexedDB `oros-mail` (stores `keys`, `creds`, `folders`, `heads`, `bodies`; v2 since 0.66.00 adds `outbox`: unsent messages, ≤ 50, sent automatically when back online): passwords sealed with a non-extractable AES-GCM key (never synced, never exported), folder lists, header caches (≤ 500 per folder) and message bodies (≤ 200 / 60 MB). Added to the factory-reset IndexedDB list. The Wave 0 key `oros-mail-creds` is not used.
- **Connected services (integrations wave 1):** oros-links-prefs (`{mode: {acctId: "direct"|"query"|"relay"}}`). IndexedDB `oros-links` (`keys`, `creds`; in the factory-reset list). The accounts themselves travel in slice `links` without keys.
- **Vault [log]:** the manifest revision key (`REV_KEY`; the stored name is not recorded).
- **Writer:** oros-writer-prefs (`{open[], active, seen{}, view{focus, unit p|s, tw, wc}}`: open tabs plus the View choices, focus mode, sentence or paragraph focus, typewriter scrolling, word count chip).
- **Memory:** oros-memory-prefs (`{lv, mode, set}`), oros-memory-session (the game in progress, resumable), oros-memory-sfx ("1" = sound on), oros-memory-data-broken (rescue copy of unreadable data).

Two devices (wave 50, `remote-play.js`): oros-connect4-pair (`{role: host|guest, code, rid, kind, at}`, the pairing, kept 24 h from the last contact) and oros-connect4-net (the host's game on two devices: the session shape with `mode: "net"`, `ai: 2`, kept on the host only); both removed by `Leave the game`.
- **Dots & Boxes:** oros-dots-prefs (`{mode, lv, n, first, nextAi}`), oros-dots-session (`{mode, lv, n, starter, ai, moves[], done, series[2]}`; the board is replayed from `moves`), oros-dots-device (id of this device's counter row), oros-dots-sfx, oros-dots-data-broken.

Deep link `__orosOpenAt("chess", { pgn: "<text>" } | { openFile: { token } })` opens a PGN (≤ 5 MB) for review; `.pgn` is in fileopen.js / manifest file_handlers.

Re-drawn on a canvas (long side ≤ 1200 px, JPEG 0.8, white background): no EXIF / location, no foreign bytes. A replaced or removed photo leaves the disk 12 s later when no live product points at it (Undo window); so does a deleted product's photo.

The timer's draft description lives in page memory only. The shell reads `oros-timesheet-data` (never writes it) through `timesheet/core.js` (`window.orosTimesheetCore`, loaded by `index.html` since 0.57.05) for the top-bar timer chip `#ts-tray-chip` and the forgotten-timer notice. Wave 46 (time away): oros-timesheet-idleprefs (`{on 0|1, min}`, default off / 10 min) and oros-timesheet-idle (`[{id, from, to}]`, periods away the shell noticed: Idle Detection API after the user granted it in Settings — checked with `permissions.query({name: "idle-detection"})`, the shell never prompts — plus tick gaps ≥ max(min, 2 min) for sleep), both device-local, never synced. The shell still never writes `oros-timesheet-data`: the chip menu (`#ts-tray-pop`: Stop / Open Timesheet / Keep / Take it out / Take out and stop) calls the app receivers `__orosTimesheetStop(id)` / `__orosTimesheetIdle(mode, rec)` when Timesheet runs, else sets sessionStorage `oros-timesheet-toggle = "stop:<id>"` or `oros-timesheet-idle-act` and opens the app; `core.idleApply` turns a choice into a model for `mergeTimesheet` (take out = end the entry at `from`, a copy carries on from `to`; stop = end at `from`). Tests: `tests/timesheet-idle.test.js`.

- **Typewriter:** oros-typewriter-prefs (typewriter mode on/off, key sound, paper tint, open page `cur`, side panel open on desktop).
- **Time › Stage:** `oros-time-stage-run` (`{ev, cur, startedAt, pausedAt, adj, log: {itemId: {s, e}}}`: the open event, the live item and its clock, actual start/end per item) and `oros-time-stage-prefs` (`{sound}`). Never synced: a phone at home never moves the clock on stage. Since 1.52.00 also `oros-time-stage-show` (`{black, layout: full|timer|agenda, mirror, logoAt, msg: {text, on, flash, color, at}}`): what the stage output shows. It is read by the in-app view and by display.html. IndexedDB `oros-time-stage` (store `files`, key `logo`): the logo picture, on this device only. Since 1.54.00 also `oros-time-stage-devices` (PC): `[{code, role: remote|display|moderator, rid, kind, at}]`. These are the paired devices, restored after a reload. Entries with no allowed id, or unused for 3 days, are dropped. `oros-time-stage-join` (device): `{code, rid, at}`. These let a reload rejoin without a new Allow. "Leave", or the PC disconnecting the device, clears it. A paired device keeps what it is sent in memory only. It never writes the synced `oros-time-stage` and never syncs anything new.
- **Time (wave 5):** `oros-time-timers` (`[{id, name, dur, tot, left, end, st: idle|run|pause|done, sound: beep|chime|bell|digital|gentle, aid}]`: the kitchen timers; `aid` is the running timer's shell alarm `tmr-<id>-<n>`), `oros-time-sw` (`{run, start, base, laps: [total ms]}`: the stopwatch, computed from the wall clock so it survives closing), `oros-time-plan` (`{open, places: [{tz, city}]|null, wf, wt, len}`: the meeting planner). None is synced.
- **Moon & Sky:** oros-sky-prefs (`{tab, night, lines}`: open tab, red night view, constellation lines). Location comes from Time's chain (oros-time-data `astro` → oros-weather → orosWeatherTray.location() → session-only geolocation, never stored).
- **Score Keeper:** oros-scores-prefs (`{tab, cur, draft:{g, v[]}, timer:{on, len}, game}`: home tab, open match, unsent round entry, round timer on/length, stats filter), oros-scores-data-broken.
- **Podcasts:** (W42: oros-podcasts-local gains `cors{origin: [ok 0|1, at]}` and a third `stats` column = seconds saved by skip silence; oros-podcasts-gpodder and IndexedDB `oros-podcasts-sync`, see PODCASTS v1) oros-podcasts-prefs (`{tab, filter, sortOld}`: tab now | new | lib | dl | find, episode filter, per-show oldest-first flags), oros-podcasts-local (`{pos{epId: [pos, dur, ts]}, meta{epId: episode}, cur, last{p, at}, spd}`: exact positions, ≤ 400, and the details of what plays and of the queue, written by the shell host; since 0.57.00 also `stats` listening seconds per day/show (device only, never synced), `nt{showId: stamp}` new-episode marks and `bg` last background check), oros-podcasts-top (Apple charts cache, 12 h; since the 2026-10-16 browse wave `{v: 2, lists: {"cc:genre": {at, list}}}`, at most 12 lists, expired ones swept on write; prefs also hold `br{m: top|genres|countries, cc, g, chip}`), IndexedDB `oros-podcasts` v1 (stores `feeds` showId → `{id, at, etag, mod, show, eps[]}` parsed feed cache, `files` epId → `{id, s, blob, type, size, at}` downloaded episodes).
- **Word Search:** oros-wordsearch-prefs (`{lang, mode, size, theme}`: word language en|el, mode d|f, size e|m|h, Free play theme `random` | a theme id | `u:<own theme id>`), oros-wordsearch-session (`{"<lang>:<mode>": {lang, mode, day, size, theme, tname, n, grid, words[{w, r, c, d}], found[], hint, hinted, ms, done, ext}}`, one puzzle per language and mode; `ext` = the daily puzzle was solved on another device), oros-wordsearch-device, oros-wordsearch-data-broken.
- **Solitaire:** oros-solitaire-prefs (`{v, draw, score, suits, bg}`: variant k|f|s|p, draw 1|3, score c|n, Spider suits 1|2|4, table felt|plain), oros-solitaire-session (`{"k"|"f"|"s"|"p": {g, u, t, c}}` (Pyramid `g`: `tab` = 28 places of 0 or 1 card, `ps` = passes used, `fd[0]` = removed cards): one deal in progress per variant with up to 150 undo positions, elapsed ms, counted flag), oros-solitaire-streak (`{<key>: n}` current streaks, local because they do not merge across devices), oros-solitaire-device, oros-solitaire-data-broken.

Word lists: `wordsearch/words-*.js` (Word Search's files).

Two devices (wave 50, `remote-play.js`): oros-xeri-pair (`{role: host|guest, code, rid, kind, at}`, the pairing, kept 24 h from the last contact) and oros-xeri-net (the host's match on two devices: the session shape + `net: true`, kept on the host only); both removed by `Leave the game`.
- **Device Info:** oros-device-prefs (`{closed[]}`: ids of the cards folded on this device). Reads, never writes: every `oros-*` key (length only), `oros-slices`, `oros-sync-last-backup`, `oros-autoexport`, `oros-autoexport-last`, `oros-fs-folder-name`, `oros-last-version`.
- **Assistant:** oros-assistant-prefs (`{open (the conversation on screen; cleared at every start, AS-FRESH), keep, usage{"YYYY-MM": {pid: {i, o}}} (last 3 months), sealOk{pid: tail}, gone{chatId: m} (this device's copy of the deleted-chats list, AS-DEL), clr{chatId: 1} (deleted chats whose file this device removed, AS-DEL)}`). IndexedDB `oros-assistant` (stores `keys` = non-extractable AES-GCM device key, `creds` = API keys sealed with it `{iv, data, m}`, `chats` = conversations). In the factory-reset IndexedDB list. Never exported.
  - Assistant: when "Sync conversations" is on, the orOS disk folder `/internal/Assistant/Chats/<chatId>.json` holds one file per conversation (synced by Vault Drive, not a slice). (since 0.67.00) Since 4.47.02 (AS-DEL) the same folder holds `deleted-chats.json` `{kind: "oros-assistant-deleted", gone: {chatId: m}}` (≤ 5000 ids, ≤ 400 days); a deleted chat's file is removed, and a tombstone `{id, m, del: 1, r: 1, at}` is written only when a device that does not read the list writes the chat back (kept 30 days).
- **Generic:** oros-*-open staging keys, and all *-prefs / *-cache / *-seen keys.
- **Correction vs older Bible:** oros-pet-events is SYNCED now (petEvents slice).
