## Part IV — Data models

### Common contracts

- **Entities:** `{ id, mtime, … }` — union by id, LWW by mtime, tie → lexicographic JSON/id.
- **ids:** `uid() = Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,7)`. Seeds are deterministic (R16).
- **Day keys:** local calendar `YYYY-MM-DD` built from `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate` (no ISO/timezone bugs). DST-safe walking via `setDate(+1)`.
- **Timestamp discipline:** time-of-day and day boundaries are DERIVED from entry ts at render time, never stored.
- **Merge purity:** `uid()`/`Date.now()` inside a merge is a non-determinism bug. Strict sanitizers DROP invalid rows instead.

### Per-app schemas

- **NOTES v2:** `{ ver, pages[], labels[], tombs{} }`. Wiki-links `[[Title]]` are regex-derived (zero storage); pinned notes.
- **KANBAN v5:** `{ ver, boards[{id,name,columns,labels,tombs,mtime,color?,archived?}], boardDeleted{}, activeBoardId (device-local) }`.
  - **[log]** Imported boards carry prefixed ids (`imp-k-` Kanri, `imp-t-` Trello); a re-import replaces the same ids.
  - **K1 (Trello/Planka/Jira wave), still `ver: 5`.** Merge and canon live in `kanban/model.js` (`OrosKanbanModel`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/kanban-merge.test.js`); board helpers (rules, lanes, table sort, timeline range, export/import, CSV, templates) in `kanban/tools.js` (`OrosKanbanTools`, `tests/kanban-tools.test.js`). Both load before `kanban.js`.
  - **Card** `{ id, text, notes, due, labels[], subtasks[{id,text,completed,m?}], info[], mtime, att?[{id,name,file,kind,size,m}], cover?, lane?, fm? }`. New keys appear only when set; canon keeps the old key order (old keys first, the rest sorted), so an untouched old card is byte-identical and never re-uploaded.
  - **`fm` field stamps:** `{ m, a, c, d, k, l, n, p, s, t, x }` = mtime copy, attachments, cover, due, lane, labels, notes, placement (column + position), subtasks, text, info. `fm` counts only when `fm.m === card.mtime`; otherwise (an older device edited the card) the card is legacy and every group counts at its `mtime`. Merge per group: the newer stamp wins; both sides legacy → the whole newer card wins (the old rule); full tie → the old JSON + column tie-break. A result equal to neither input gets `mtime = max + 1` so an older device adopts it instead of ping-ponging. The card sits in the column (and position) of the side whose `p` wins.
  - **Subtasks and attachments merge per item** by `m` (a legacy side's items count at that card's `mtime`); a deleted item leaves a board tombstone `tombs["<cardId>/<itemId>"]`.
  - **Transitional upload:** `fm` is written only when a card is edited on a K1 device or merged into a mix of both sides; nothing is rewritten on load, so there is no mass re-upload. An older device keeps merging whole cards by `mtime` and carries `fm` along untouched; when it edits a card, `fm.m` no longer matches and the legacy rule above takes over.
  - **Column** `{ id, name, cards[], wip?, auto?{done,today,label,top} }`: WIP limit (a warning, not a block) and arrival rules ride the column, merged with the board header LWW, so older devices keep them. **Label** `auto: "overdue"` marks the board's Overdue rule label: on boot, every 5 min and on focus, a card past its due date (not in the last column, not on archived boards or templates) gets it, unless its labels were edited after the due date passed and after the rule was switched on.
  - **Templates** are boards with id `tpl-…` and `archived: true` (nothing new on the root: old merges drop unknown root keys); older versions show them as archived boards. Calendar feed, Today, search and the board list skip `tpl-`. Built-ins (Personal, Software sprint, Content calendar, EN/EL) live in `tools.js`, not in data.
  - **Attachments:** files at `/internal/Kanban/Attachments/<random>.<ext>` through `parent.orosFS` (they travel with the disk via Vault Drive, not in the slice). Photos re-encoded on a canvas (long side ≤ 1600 px, JPEG 0.82: EXIF gone); PDFs (header checked) and other files ≤ 10 MB kept as is, 20 per card; only photos and PDFs are viewed in orOS. A file is deleted 12 s after its last reference goes (`usedFiles`). `cover` is a palette colour or `a:<attId>`.
  - **Export:** `{ app: "oros-kanban", kind: "board", ver: 1, exported, board, files?{} }` (files base64, ≤ 25 MB total); import gives every id a fresh prefix and writes the files back. CSV cells starting with = + - @ get an apostrophe.
  - **Device-local:** `oros-kanban-prefs.views[boardId] = { v: board|table|timeline, lanes: ""|label|lane, sort, dir }`.
  - **Label edit (KN-LBL, 4.47.03):** **Label** `{ id, name (≤ 24), color, mtime, pos, auto? }`. The pencil (`labelEditBtn`) in the card's label list and in the filter popup opens `#dlg-lbl` (name, the 8 `SWATCH_COLORS`, delete). It commits on any close, like the column dialog: only a real change sets `name`/`color` and `touch(label)` (label LWW by `mtime` in `unionEntities`); cards hold the id and are never re-stamped. `auto: "overdue"` is kept, so the Overdue rule follows a renamed label.
- **MOOD v3:** `{ ver, trigSeeded, sm, om, entries[{id,ts,mtime,emotions[],loc,person,trig,habits,note,acts?,fm?}], cols, deleted{}, vocab?, goals? }`. 9 built-in emotions (keys never change); order is ts DESC (tie → id), derived at sort. `fm` (field → stamp) appears at an entry's first edit; device-local rescue key `oros-mood-data-broken`.
  - **Wave 30 (DATA_VER stays 3, all additive):** pure logic in `mood/vocab.js` (`OrosMoodVocab`, loaded before `mood.js`; tests `tests/mood-vocab.test.js`). `vocab = { emo: [def], act: [def], eo: {ids, m}, ao: {ids, m}, rs? }`, `def = { id, mtime, lab?, no?, ic?, col?, hid?, pos? }`: id = a built-in key (emotion key or habit field) or `c-<uid>` for the user's own; `lab` overrides the translation (habits: the yes side, `no` the no side; cleared = back to the translation), `ic` an emoji (no markup characters), `col` `#rrggbb`, `hid` hidden from Capture only, `pos` = a custom feeling counts as positive (momentum, recap). Defs merge per item by mtime (tie → larger JSON), the two orders whole by `m`; display order = saved ids that exist, then missing built-ins, then missing custom ids by id. Nothing is ever deleted (hide only), so old entries keep their meaning. Factory reset writes `vocab.rs = now`: every def/order stamped at or before it disappears on every device; goals get `x`. `goals = [{ id, act, n, per: "w"|"m", mtime, x? }]` (n ≤ 7 a week, ≤ 31 a month), merged per item by mtime, soft delete. Progress = distinct local days in the current Monday-week / month with the activity marked (built-in habit `"yes"`, or the custom id in `acts`), plus how many of the last 8 weeks / 6 months reached it. Entries gain optional `acts: [custom ids]` (sorted). `acts` is an OPTIONAL entry field: it gets an `fm` stamp only once an entry has the field or the stamp, so entries that never used it keep their exact old canonical form (a device still on the previous mood.js would otherwise drop the stamp on every merge and both would upload forever). `vocab` / `goals` are written only once non-empty, for the same reason; an old device drops them in its own merge, but union by id means its copy can never delete them. Year in pixels (Insights): 12 month columns × 31 rows, colour = the day's strongest feeling (tie → first met, newest first), tap = that day's entries; ignores range and filters. The search provider shows the user's own names (`d.vocab`); the Calendar's read-only cross-app feed still knows only the nine built-in keys.
- **TIME v1:** zone entities `{tz,mtime}` plus scalar prefs LWW via smtime. Alarms travel IN the shell slice.
- **TIME › STAGE v1 (1.49.00):** `oros-time-stage` = `{ v: 1, events: [{ id, name, date "YYYY-MM-DD"|"", start "HH:MM"|"", yellow s, red s, flash, mtime }], items: [{ id, ev, pos, title, speaker, kind "down"|"up"|"until"|"clock", dur s, until "HH:MM"|"", auto, yellow s|null, red s|null, notes, mtime }], tombs: [{ id, t }] }`. Ids `^[a-z0-9]{4,24}$`; strings trimmed and length-capped; everything drawn with textContent.
- **CALENDAR:** `{ ver, events[{id,date,dateEnd,start,end,title,note,location,labelId,recur{freq,interval,until,exdates,every?,byday?,pos?,wday?,count?,wkst?},remindMin,mtime,tz?}], labels[], deleted{}, subs?[{id,url,name,color,mtime}], dav?[{id,url,mtime}] }` (`dav`: CalDAV links, label id → server calendar, Part II "CalDAV / CardDAV W3"). Fixed key order for deterministic tie-breaks.
  - **Subscribed calendars (wave 8).** `subs` = ICS feeds by address (`calendar/subs.js`, OrosCalSubs, Node-tested in `tests/calendar-wave8.test.js`). `url` https/http only (webcal(s):// → https://, no user:password, ≤ 2000), `name` ≤ 40 ("" = the feed's X-WR-CALNAME, else its host), `color` from `VALID_COLORS`, `mtime`. Merge: LWW per id (equal mtime → smaller JSON, like events/labels) and the SAME `deleted` tombstones (delete wins ties, a newer sub resurrects); the key is left out when empty so older blobs keep their exact bytes. The feed's events are NOT synced: each device reads the address and keeps device-local `oros-cal-subs-cache` `{ <subId>: { url, at, ok, err, n, name, total, dropped, events[] } }` (events in the Calendar's own shape via `calendar/ics.js`, no reminders, note ≤ 300, one-off events that ended > 366 days ago dropped, ≤ 3000 kept nearest to today; re-checked by `cleanCache` + `normRecur` on load). Decision: per-device cache because a feed can be thousands of events (holidays, fixtures) and is re-fetchable; syncing it would bloat the slice and fight on every refresh. Fetch: `feeds/fetch.js` `fetchOne` (lazy-loaded with `feeds/core.js`; direct GET first, then the relay's existing `web` op; relay address = Reader setting `relay`, else Mail's); relay/ unchanged. Read on open when the copy is > 30 min old, every 3 h while the Calendar is open (10-min check), on `online` for errored ones, and by `Refresh`. Rows: virtual label `sub-<id>` (chip after the app feeds; hidden state device-local in `oros-cal-feedvis` as `sub-<id>: false`), `_feed:true` + `_sub`, opened read-only in `#sv-dlg` ("Copy to my calendar" → `__orosCalendarNew`). Never exported, never in Stats or search; the phone bridge's feed calendar gets them like any feed row.
  - **Quick add (wave 8).** `calendar/quickadd.js` (OrosCalQuick.parse(text, {today})), pure, EN + EL mixed: date (relative words, weekdays with this/next / «την άλλη», d/m[/y], d.m.y, ISO, "15 Nov" / «15 Νοεμβρίου», "in N days"), time or range (am/pm, μμ/πμ, «το πρωί/βράδυ», "at"/«στις», 10-12; a bare 1–6 without am/pm or minutes = afternoon; a bare number without a marker is not a time), repeat (every [N|other] day/week/month/year/weekday/weekdays + weekday lists, daily…, «κάθε…», «τις Τρίτες»), location after at/@/«στο/στη/στην/στον/στα/στους» up to the next date/time, title = the rest. Folding keeps 1 char → 1 char so match positions map back to the original text. The result opens the New event window through `__orosCalendarNew`, which now also takes `allDay: true` and `recur` (normalised with `normRecur`); nothing is saved until Save.
  - **Free times (wave 8).** `calendar/free.js` (OrosCalFree.busy / slots), pure: busy = own timed events + the visible subscribed calendars' timed events, as device-day minute ranges (no end = 60 min, overnight spans split, all-day never busy); slots on a min(len, 30)-minute grid inside the chosen hours and weekdays, after now + 15 min on today, ≤ 400. Sent as Send-to-someone kind `slots` (below); prefs device-local `oros-cal-free-prefs` (length, days, hours, weekend, title, name, email, place).
  - **Print (wave 8).** `More › Print…` builds a plain copy of the current view into `#print-area` (month = table with up to 5 "HH:MM title" lines per day, week / agenda / day = lists per day, year = 12 mini months with event days bold) and calls `window.print()`; `@media print` hides everything else; cleared on `afterprint`.
  - **More menu (wave 8).** `#cal-more` (nav) holds Subscribe…, Share free times…, Print…; `#ev-quick` "Quick add" sits next to Add.
  - **Repeats (Calendar wave, OrosCalOccur 2.0.0).** All rule logic is pure in `calendar/occur.js` (Node-tested in `tests/calendar-occur.test.js`; also loaded by the shell reminders, Today, search and `phone.js`). `freq` D/W/M/Y. `interval` stays the legacy field (2 only for weekly, else 1) so older builds keep reading the common case; any other "every N" goes in `every` (2..999, omitted when it equals `interval`). `byday` (weekly: sorted weekdays 0=Sun..6, omitted when it is just the start's weekday), `wkst` (week start of the N-week grid, only with byday). Monthly/yearly by weekday: `pos` 1..5 or -1 (last) with `wday`; without `pos` the old sticky month-end clamp holds. `count` (1..9999) also derives `until` (the last occurrence's day), so a build that ignores `count` still stops on time. The start date always counts as the first occurrence (RFC 5545); exdates still count toward `count`. New keys are appended after `exdates` and only when set, so old events keep their exact bytes (`normRecur` is idempotent).
  - **Repeat + span.** `dateEnd − date` is the length of every occurrence, series included (the old "repeat or span" rule is gone). `end < start` is kept only when `dateEnd > date` (overnight spans).
  - **Time zone.** Optional `tz` (IANA name, regex-validated in the sanitizer so it is deterministic across devices; Intl only at display) on timed events, appended last and only when set. Wall times are in `tz`; `OCC.instance()` converts each occurrence to the device zone (may move it to another day), the views show a ◷ mark and the original time. All-day events never carry `tz`. Zone list from `Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")`, else a short built-in list.
  - **Version skew.** An older build strips the new keys on its next save. Because the richer JSON sorts smaller only on equal mtimes, a mixed pair can re-upload the same event until the older device updates; no data is lost on the newer device (it keeps the richer copy unless the old device edits the event).
  - **Views and moves.** Views `day` / `week` / `month` / `year` / `agenda` (`curView`, device-local, not in the slice). Fill (#647): `fillHeight()` sets `--fill-h` on `#cmain` (window height under the bars, stopping where `#day-title` is still visible, `FILL_MIN` 300) after every render and on ResizeObserver of `#cmain`/`#cal-top`/`#view-bar`/`#lbl-bar`; Month rows (`grid-auto-rows: 1fr`), desktop Week columns and the Day grid take it. Month cells show coloured dots (≤ 6, label colours) by default; with the `Names` toggle next to the views (`#vw-names`, aria-pressed, shown in Month only; device-local `oros-cal-month-names`, since #698) they show event names (time from 700 px), `fitMonth()` hides what does not fit and shows `+N`; `.cal-evs` has `contain: size` so a busy day never grows its row. Day: hour grid 60 px/h (events under 45 min on one line), all-day strip, overlap columns, now line refreshed every 60 s. Year: 12 mini months, up to 3 dots per day. Desktop drag (payload `cal-ev:<id>|<day>|<occ>`) in Month and Week: a span moves whole; a series asks This occurrence (override copy + exdate on the master) / Entire series (shifts date, dateEnd, exdates, until and byday; recomputes pos/wday); Undo restores copies with a fresh mtime and tombstones the added override.
  - **[log]** Read-only app feeds: Contacts, Habits, Cycle, Mood, Kanban, To-Do (`lbl-feed-todo`), Screen Pet. Feed rows carry `_feed:true` and per-render keys; they are never stored, synced or exported to .ics. Feed labels come from `FEED_LABELS`. Each feed has a ~1 s micro-cache, reset in `setFromSync`. Since 0.60.04 also Timesheet "Work time" / «Ώρες εργασίας» (`lbl-feed-time`, cyan `#56b6c2`, in `STICKY_FEEDS`): one all-day row per project per day from `orosTimesheetCore.dayFeed(data, day, now)`; a click opens `__orosOpenAt("timesheet", {day})`, a `{day}` target of Timesheet's single open-at receiver (alongside the search targets). Since 0.61.03 also Family Tree "Death anniversaries" / «Επέτειοι θανάτου» (`lbl-feed-famtree`, slate `#9aa4b0`): calendar/index.html loads ../familytree/ft-core.js; `FTCore.deathDays(blob)` (index rebuilt only when `oros-familytree-data` changes) + `deathAnniversaries(idx, day)`; exact death dates only (full day, no abt/bef/aft), 29 Feb also on 28 Feb of common years, same name + date in two trees once, not on the death day itself; a row opens `__orosOpenAt("familytree", {person})`. Family Tree's receiver also takes `{ contact }` (Contacts card "Family tree" button): the person linked to that contact (current tree first), else the Build-from-Contacts preview starting there. Family Tree never writes Contacts; Contacts never reads Family Tree data. Since 0.62.00 also Media Shelf "Media Shelf" / «Το ράφι μου» (`lbl-feed-shelf`, berry `#d16ba5`, owner Media Shelf), Moon & Sky (`lbl-feed-sky`, owner Moon & Sky, OPT-IN: off by default via `OPT_IN_FEEDS`, `true` kept in `oros-cal-feedvis`; rows from `sky/core.js` `feedFor(date, lang)`, a row opens `__orosOpenAt("sky", {date})`): calendar/index.html loads ../shelf/feed.js (`window.OrosShelfFeed`: `byDay`, `label`); finishes (session k "d", one row per title per day) and release dates (`rel`) of wishlist (`st` "want") titles; a row opens `__orosOpenAt("shelf", {item})`; rows never stored.
  - **[log]** New-event prefill through `window.__orosCalendarNew` (BR-W8, Part VI).
  - **Filters (chips).** Device view only, nothing in the slice changes. `No label` / «Χωρίς ετικέτα» (virtual id `lbl-nolabel`, `NO_LABEL`) covers own events with no `labelId` or one not in `state.labels` (`eventVisible(e)`: month/week/day, year dots, search, Stats "upcoming"). A long press (touch, 550 ms), right-click or Alt+click on any chip shows only that chip (`soloChip`); the same gesture on the only chip still on = `All`. Quick filters before the chips: `All` (every chip on except the opt-in feeds `OPT_IN_FEEDS`, which turn on only from their own chip), `None`, `My events` (own labels + No label, feeds and subscriptions off). Every bulk change goes through `applyVis` → `saveFeedVis`, so sticky/opt-in feeds and `sub-…` keep their device-local memory in `oros-cal-feedvis`; own labels and No label reset on load as before. The row is redrawn under the finger, so one shared stamp (`chipPressAt`, 700 ms) swallows the click/contextmenu that follow a long press.
- **PLANTS v1** (slice `plants`, key `oros-plants-data`; logic in `plants/core.js`, shared by the app, the shell engine and the Calendar feed):
  - `{ ver, plants[plant] sorted by id, log[entry] sorted by id, tombs{id: deletedAt} sorted }`, at most 300 plants.
  - `plant = { id, m, name (≤ 40), sp (ready species id or ""), room (≤ 30), out 0|1, em (icon), w (water every 1–60 days), ww (winter interval 0–90, 0 = same), f (fertilize 0–180), mi (mist 0–30), r (repot 0–1095 days, the UI says months × 30), st (ymd: schedule start = last watered when added), sn{kind: ymd} (postponed until), notes (≤ 500) }`.
  - `entry = { id, p (plant id), k water|fert|mist|repot, d (ymd), s 1 = skipped, m }`.
  - The next due day is NEVER stored: base = the newer of `st` and the newest entry of that kind (done or skipped); due = base + the interval in force on the base day (winter Nov–Feb north / May–Aug south, device-local hemisphere); a postponement only moves it later and is cleared when the task is done. Day arithmetic on whole UTC days (DST-proof).
  - Merge: plants LWW (newer `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON); entries union by id (same LWW); tombs max; a tomb ≥ `m` hides a plant or an entry; Undo of a deletion writes a fresh `m`. Entries of a plant that is not alive drop. Clock pruning, in the merge and therefore everywhere: entries older than 730 days go except the newest per plant + kind, tombs older than 180 days go (`tests/plants.test.js`).
  - Wave 34: optional `sci` (scientific name, ≤ 80, cleaned; key absent when empty so older plants keep their bytes) placed right after `room`: at equal `m` the larger canonical JSON wins and `,"sci"` > `,"out"`, so a copy an older build handed back (which drops the key) never beats the one that has it. Filled by hand or by "Identify from a photo": `plants/identify.js` (pure: request URL, results, errors, genus → ready species) + `plants.js` POST `multipart/form-data` (`organs=auto`, one JPEG re-drawn on a canvas, long side ≤ 1280, no EXIF) to `https://my-api.plantnet.org/v2/identify/all?api-key=<own key>&lang=el|en&nb-results=5` only when the person presses Identify (`credentials: omit`; a 400 in Greek retries once in English). The person's OWN free key (orOS ships none), device-local in `oros-plants-prefs.pnKey`, never synced. Browser use needs the key's "expose my API key" + the orOS origin under "Authorized domains" in the person's Pl@ntNet account (Pl@ntNet rejects CORS from other origins; not verifiable from the build sandbox). The results dialog shows Pl@ntNet's attribution sentence (terms of use). Tests: `tests/plants-identify.test.js`.
  - Photo identification (Pl@ntNet, wave 38) is switched OFF since 2026-10-14 (`plants/identify.js` `ENABLED = false`): Pl@ntNet reportedly says one sign-up per app user goes against its terms, so the `Identify from a photo` button and the key field are hidden until Pl@ntNet agrees (Chris's call). The code, the device-local `pnKey` pref and its tests stay.
- **QUOTE:** entities + shared tombstone map. Computed totals are PURE (never stored). Numbering OFF-YYYY-NNN.
- **STORAGE v1:** `{ ver, ents[{id,type,name|bi,parentId,pos,qty?,note?,mtime,del}] }`. Cascade delete tombstones every descendant with a fresh mtime.
- **HABITS v2** (wave 4; v1 data loads unchanged, `ver` becomes 2):
  - `{ ver, habits[{id,name,icon,color,days[0..6 Monday-first],mtime,del, num?, per?, rem?}], comps[{id:"<habitId>|<YYYY-MM-DD>",habitId,date,mtime,del, v?, sk?, nt?}], set? }`.
  - Habit options (present only when set): `num {u unit ≤16, t target > 0, c "ge"|"le", s step}` = measurable (absent = yes / no); `per ["w"|"m", n]` = n times per week (Mon–Sun, 1–7) / per calendar month (1–31), `days` then `[]`; `rem` = reminder minute 0–1439.
  - Completion row: `mtime/del` = the yes / no tick (toggle-off = tombstone, as v1); `v {<deviceId>: [number, m]}` = measurable value as per-device shares, day value = their sum (concurrent +1 on two devices both count; a typed total sets this device's share = total − others); `sk [0|1, m]` = skipped / frozen day; `nt [text ≤200, m]` = note. Device id `oros-habits-device` (device-local).
  - `set {st 0|1, sg steps goal 100–200000, m}` = the Steps row switch and goal (defaults on / 8000).
  - Merge (`habits/model.js` OrosHabitsModel, tests/habits-core.test.js): habits LWW by mtime, tie → tombstone → the row with more fields (an older orOS strips num/per/rem without a new stamp) → larger JSON; completions merged field by field (tick LWW tie → not ticked, each device share / sk / nt LWW by its own stamp); `set` by m. Canonical form for getter and merge: rows sorted, fixed key order, empty completion rows (not ticked, no value, no skip, no note) older than 30 days before the newest stamp pruned (HB-3/HB-11).
  - Rules (`habits/core.js` OrosHabitsCore v2, shared by the app, Calendar feed, Today, shell and phone bridge): done = ticked, or for measurable the value meets the target (`le` needs a logged value); `dueOn` = not done, not skipped, fixed weekdays on their days, per-period while the period count (done + skipped) is below n; flexible never due. Streaks: days (skipped and unscheduled days transparent, today not a break) or whole weeks / months for per-period. Strength (`score`, `scoreSeries`): Loop-style EMA, M = 0.5^(√freq/13); fixed days step once per scheduled day with the day's progress (partial amounts count in part); per-period and flexible (as 1/week) step daily with min(1, (progress + skips) of the last 7/30 days ÷ n); skipped days freeze; today counts only once it helps.
  - Reminders: `dueReminders(data, now)` from the time for 4 h on days `needsReminder` (not done / skipped; fixed: its days; per-period: period not met; flexible: any day). Shell engine `habitsCheckTick` (index.html loads habits/core.js) emits ns `habits`, key `r-<habitId>-<ymd>`, deep link `habits:0`; phone.js `reminderRows` adds the same rows (`habits:r-…`) for the next 48 h so the Android app rings them with orOS closed.
  - UI: day dialog (value with −/+, Done, Skip this day, Note) from a tap on a measurable / skipped cell, right-click or long-press on any cell; details dialog (strength, streaks, check-offs, 12-month strength chart, GitHub-style year heatmap with year arrows, latest notes) from the habit's icon / name, the calendar gutter or a Stats row; settings (gear) for the Steps row. Stats: per-period rate = periods met ÷ periods (running one only once met), skipped days out of rates, today not a miss, strength + sparkline per habit, average of amounts.
  - **App feeds (since 0.47.00):** read-only rows from other apps. A provider ships one script that `habits/index.html` loads before `habits.js` (`../<app>/core.js`) and that pushes `{ id, app, name{en,el}, hint{en,el}, color, icon (static SVG), keys[], read() }` onto `window.orosHabitFeeds`; `read()` returns null (no row) or `{ days: {"YYYY-MM-DD": true} }`. Feed rows are daily, drawn in the list and calendar views with read-only dots, a streak and an "Auto" badge; a tap opens the provider (`__orosOpenApp`). They are never stored, synced or counted in Stats; a `storage` event on one of `keys` (a pull applied by the shell) or a return to the tab redraws them. First provider: Water; Fitness is next. Since Habits wave 4 a provider may also return `vals {"YYYY-MM-DD": number}` and `goal` with a static `unit{en,el}`: a measurable read-only row (value in its cells, today's value / goal in the meta). `habits/steps.js` (OrosHabitsSteps) is the Steps row: Health's `st` entries (tombstones honoured, highest reading per local day), hidden when Health hides Steps or the Habits `set.st` is 0, done on days ≥ `set.sg`; opens Health. `typing/due.js` (TypingDue) is the Typing practice row: minutes a day from oros-typing-data (every device added up, reset rows left out), done on days ≥ the daily goal; opens Typing Tutor.
- **WATER v1 (`oros-water-data`, slice `water`, model in `water/core.js`):**
  - `{ ver: 1, sips: [{id, ts, ml, m} | {id, m, del: 1}], goals: [{id: "YYYY-MM-DD", ml, m}], prefs: {glass, bottle, unit, rem{on, from, to, every}, habits}, pm }`, arrays sorted by id.
  - A drink's day is derived from `ts` in local time. Limits: drink 1–5,000 ml, goal 500–10,000, glass 50–1,000, bottle 100–3,000, reminder interval 30–480 min, window minutes 0–1440 with `to > from`. `unit` ml | glass | oz is display only (always stored in ml).
  - A goal applies from its day on; days before the first goal use it; no goal → 2,000 ml. Setting the goal again on the same day raises its stamp.
  - Merge: per id the newer `m` wins; equal `m`: a tombstone wins, then the larger JSON (symmetric). Undo of a delete re-adds with a fresh stamp (R17). Prefs travel as one record: higher `pm` wins, equal `pm` → larger JSON. Defaults: glass 250, bottle 500, unit ml, reminders off 09:00–21:00 every 120 min, Show in Habits on.
- **WEATHER v1:** `{ ver, sm, om, active, deleted{}, cities[], shellWx, units }`. Units are RENDER ONLY; the slice is always metric.
  - **Wave 38 (official warnings, rain now, air & pollen, models):** cities may carry `cc` (ISO country, from the geocoder; old cities: one look-up of the label per city and device, nearest result within 0.3°, `prefs.bf`), `adm` (the region name from the geocoder) and `wa: { n: area name, g: EMMA_ID }` (the warnings area the user picked with "My area"). All three are plain extra city keys: `cloneCity` keeps them (sorted after the fixed keys), they travel with the city's `mtime` (every write stamps it: a tie would keep the copy without them), old builds carry them untouched. No new root keys (an old build's merge would drop a root key and ping-pong).
  - **Device-local, never in the slice:** `oros-weatherapp-prefs` `{ model, cmp[3], warnOn (default true), notify ("off" default | "severe" | "all"), bf{} }`; `oros-weatherapp-warn` `{ feeds: { <slug>: { at (last try), ok (last success), list (active warnings only, ≤ 300), err, via } } (≤ 4 countries), sent{} }`, written by the app and the shell tick. The forecast cache entry gains `tzn` (IANA zone name of the answer), `model`, `min15` (`[{t, p mm, s cm}]`, Open-Meteo `minutely_15` from the current slot) and `air` (≤ 72 hours `{t, a, s{pm25,pm10,no2,o3} EAQI sub-indices, c{…} µg/m³, pol{type: grains/m³}}`); `aqi` stays for the shell. A cache of another model is not fresh (`maybeFetch`).
  - **Pure logic:** `weather/core.js` (`OrosWeatherCore`, UMD; also loaded by the shell): lenient regex XML reading (no DOM, CDATA, entities, markup stripped, links http(s) only), `parseAtom` (MeteoAlarm legacy Atom: areaDesc, EMMA_ID geocodes, event, severity → level 1–4, kind from awareness_type or words, onset/expires, CAP link), `parseCap` (the info block in the UI language, else English), `activeList` (Actual, not Cancel, not expired, yellow+, one per id + area, worst first), `forCity` (saved `wa` by EMMA_ID or folded name; else a guess: Greek → Latin folding, c→k / th→t / y→i…, tokens of ≥ 4 letters matched by a common prefix of ≥ 4 and ≥ 60%, score over `adm` + label, a unique best area only), `slugFor` (ISO code, else the zone name: `ZONES`), `minutelySlots` / `nowcast` / `nowcastText` (wet ≥ 0.1 mm per 15 min; rate from the peak ×4: < 2.5 light, < 7.6 moderate, else heavy; minutes from now, rounded to 5, never 0), `airHours` / `airDays` (worst AQI, its hour and dominant sub-index; pollen levels on the US NAB count scale per group: trees 1/15/90/1500, grass 1/5/20/200, weeds 1/10/50/500), `MODELS`, `parseCompare` (`_<model>` suffixed daily columns). Tests: `tests/weather-core.test.js`.
  - **Network:** the feed `https://feeds.meteoalarm.org/feeds/meteoalarm-legacy-atom-<slug>` and the CAP link go through the Reader's `feeds/fetch.js` `fetchOne` (direct, then the Mail relay's `web` op; `relay/` untouched); without a relay a blocked feed shows "set up the relay in Mail" in the city dialog and no banner. The air request asks the EAQI sub-indices, µg/m³ and six pollen types for 4 days; the forecast asks `minutely_15=precipitation,snowfall` (`past_minutely_15=1`, 10 slots) and `models=` when not best match. "Compare models" is one request on demand (`models=a,b,c`, daily max/min/precipitation, 7 days), kept 30 min in memory.
  - **Decisions:** warnings are shown for the guessed or saved area, the rest of the country folds into "Warnings elsewhere"; an area can only be picked while it has a warning (no area list without a feed entry). Warning colours are fixed (official meaning), all other colours come from the palette. The notice is the shell's (one per warning, off by default, device-local); the app never emits it. The rain radar map is deferred (data-source terms need an owner decision); wave 52 adds a satellite rain map instead (below).
  - **Wave 52 (rain map):** `Rain map` section after the 7-day forecast, closed by default, open/closed state per session only (nothing stored or synced). Opening it lazy-loads the vendored Leaflet (`../vendor/leaflet.*`), asks GIBS DescribeDomains once (`…/wmts/epsg3857/best/1.0.0/IMERG_Precipitation_Rate_30min/default/GoogleMapsCompatible_Level6/all/<from>--<to>.xml`, last 24 h; the newest end of the time `<Domain>` ranges, kept 15 min in memory); when that can't be read it probes one z0 tile per half hour from 3 h ago back (24 probes, 4 at a time, newest first; GIBS answers an error for a time it doesn't have). Overlay `…/best/IMERG_Precipitation_Rate_30min/default/<YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:00Z>/GoogleMapsCompatible_Level6/{z}/{y}/{x}.png` (native zoom 0–6, map zoom 1–9, opacity 0.75) over OSM standard tiles, centred on the city (zoom 5) with a dot; slider over the newest 12 half hours (time = start of the half hour, shown in the city's clock with "n h ago"), play steps 1.2 s and stops at the newest; legend from the GIBS IMERG colour map (rain and snow, 0.1–53 mm/h, log scale). Label EN+EL "Satellite estimate of rain (NASA IMERG), a few hours old — not live radar". Offline: a message and `Try again`, no request. Latency seen 2026-10-14: newest time ≈ 6 h behind (19:25 UTC → 13:30). `IMERG_Precipitation_Rate` (no suffix) is the DAILY layer, not used. Pure logic `weather/rainmap-core.js` (`OrosRainMapCore`: `isoTime`, `tileTemplate`/`tileUrl`, `domainsUrl`, `parseDomains`, `frames`, `probeTimes`, `hoursAgo`, legend); UI `weather/rainmap.js` (`OrosRainMap.update(city, tz)` from `renderExtras`). City labels go into the map as text nodes only. Tests: `tests/weather-rainmap.test.js`.
- **FILES:** view prefs in oros-files-data (device-local). FAVS v1 (slice `files`, key `oros-files-favs`): `{ v:1, items:[{ p "/internal/…", dir, m, del? }] }` sorted by `p`, merge `OrosFilesCore.mergeFavs`. Trash records on the disk: `/internal/.trash/<id>.json` `{ v:1, path, name, dir, at }` beside `/internal/.trash/<id>/<name>` (Part II, Files app). The old "files-disk" blob slice is retired (FILES-V, SY-R).
- **CONTACTS:**
  - `{ ver, contacts[{id,name{},phones[],emails[],addresses[],web[],im[],events[],notes,photo,relations[{with,type}],starred,labelIds[],mtime,del}], cols{}, deleted{} }`.
  - Relations are stored on the initiator; the inverse is computed at render.
  - **CardDAV link (W4, 2026-11-01, optional):** top-level `dav` `{ url, mtime }` (newer wins; `url ""` = unlinked; absent until a first link). Part II "CalDAV / CardDAV W4".
  - **Wave 26 keys (optional, absent on old data):** `keep` `{n: 1–99, u: "w"|"m"} | null` (keep-in-touch cadence), `seen` `"YYYY-MM-DD" | ""` ("Contacted today"), `log` `[{id, k: call|meet|msg|gift|note, d: "YYYY-MM-DD", tx ≤ 1000, m}]` (≤ 500, sorted by id), `logDel` `{id: m}` (interaction tombstones), `fm` `{field: stamp}` over given…photo, keep, seen and `log`. `sanitizeContact` keeps a key only when the stored contact has it, so data saved before wave 26 loads and canonicalises byte-identically (no re-upload). The phone bridge (`phone.js` `contactRows` / `applyContactChanges`) neither reads nor drops them: row hashes are unchanged and a phone edit (`Object.assign(old, changes)`) keeps them (`tests/contacts-keep.test.js`).
  - **CT-NP no photos (2026-10-15, Chris: "Πλήρης αφαίρεση φωτογραφιών"):** contacts keep no photos; they filled localStorage and stopped sync (SY-Q1), even after CT-PS (2.32.01) made them 128 px. The `photo` field is gone: `sanitizeContact` drops it (key order: `avatar` takes its place), and a load that found any photo saves once, which also marks sync dirty, so the cloud copy and other devices lose them. Each contact shows its initials or, if picked in the editor (`Picture`: `Initials` / `8-bit avatar`, `Another one` draws a new seed), an 8-bit avatar: `avatar: "px:<seed>"` (`PX_RE` `/^px:[a-z0-9]{1,12}$/`), a 12×12 mirrored pixel robot drawn as SVG from the seed (FNV hash + mulberry32; 3 eye styles, 3 mouths, no/one/two antennas, ears or not; head, eye, body and background palettes). Robots, not faces: Chris 2026-10-15 13:27 asked for gender-neutral avatars and picked robots; orOS never guesses gender from a name, cached in memory, never stored as an image. Gone: upload, Find photos online (Gravatar / Libravatar, #374), `shrinkPhotos`, Google import photos (`photos` no longer requested), vCard `PHOTO` (ignored on import; export writes `X-OROS-AVATAR` instead and reads it back), import-review photo fill, the phone bridge's photos both ways (`phone.js` sends `photo: null`, takes none in). `merge.js` and `assistant/edits.js` stamp `avatar` instead of `photo`.
  - **CT-PF per-field merge** (`contacts/merge.js`, `OrosContactsMerge`, Node-tested): To-Do TD-3 / Mood MO-3 pattern. Each field wins on its own stamp (equal stamp → larger JSON); `mtime` = newest stamp and still decides life against a tombstone. No `fm` on either side → whole-object as before (no stamps invented). A copy whose `mtime` is newer than all its stamps was written by mtime-only code (an older orOS, `phone.js`): its `mtime` speaks for every old field. `keep` / `seen` are never written by such code, so they always use their own stamp, and a copy without the key (older code drops unknown keys) has stamp −1 and never wins them. `log` merges per item (newer `m`; tombstone ≥ `m` hides; an edit after the delete comes back), tombstones max per id, never pruned. Output key order = the sanitizer's. Stamps are set in ONE place: `saveState` → `restamp(stored, current, now)` stamps exactly the fields whose value changed (no change → no stamp, R27), so every write path (Save, merge duplicates, import review, undo, card, log) is covered. `__orosPhoneReload` restamps contacts the phone just changed against the in-memory copy, so only the fields really changed by the phone take the new stamp (with Contacts closed, the mtime-only rule applies).
  - **Keep in touch** (`contacts/keep.js`, `OrosContactsKeep`, Node-tested, also loaded by the shell): last contacted = later of `seen` and the newest interaction dated today or earlier; due = last + cadence (months clamp to month end); never contacted → counts from the day the cadence was set (`fm.keep`). Card: "Keep in touch" (Last contacted, cadence + due, Contacted today, ＋ Log) and "Timeline" (newest first; tap = `#ix-dlg` edit / delete with Undo). Quick filter "⏰ Reach out · n" (shown once a cadence exists) lists overdue contacts, longest waiting first; overdue rows elsewhere get a ⏰. Edit dialog: `ct-keep-n` + `ct-keep-u` ("keep" in DLG_FIELDS, CT-2 diff save).
  - **Reach-out reminder** (shell `keepCheckTick`, 60 s): off by default; device-local `oros-contacts-keep` `{on, hour}` (set from the Reach out bar, never synced). From that hour, when `reachOut` is not empty: one notice per day, ns `contacts`, key `keep-<ymd>`, body up to 3 names; deep link `contacts:<id>` for one person, `contacts:@reachout` (→ `__orosContactsOpen("@reachout")`, the Reach out list) for several. orOS closed = nothing fires; the next boot the same day catches up.
  - **Any CSV** (`contacts/csvmap.js`, `OrosContactsCsv`, Node-tested): Google's own CSV (numbered "Phone 1 - Value" columns or "Group Membership") keeps the automatic reader; any other opens `#csv-dlg`: delimiter `,` `;` or tab detected on the first line (RFC 4180 quotes, BOM dropped), per column a target guessed from EN/EL header words (given, middle, family, full, nickname, org, jobTitle, phone, email, website, street, city, zip, region, country, birthday, note, labels; "type" columns and Outlook's honorific "Title" skipped) with a type for phones / e-mails / websites / address parts, header-row switch, birthday order dmy (default) / mdy guessed from the column, preview of the first 3, then the same `openReview`. One address per type, one birthday; a row without a name is named by its e-mail or phone.

First use on a device shows a notice and downloads only on "Download and read" (device-local flag `oros-contacts-ocr`); the language data is cached by Tesseract in IndexedDB. The text lands in an editable box (pasting text works without OCR); `parse` → new-contact form prefilled (name, company, title, phones typed by label / Greek 69… mobile, e-mails, website, address with Greek postcode), unplaced lines + fax → note. Nothing is saved before Save.
  - **[log]** JSON backup file: `{ app:"contacts", ver, labels, contacts, deleted }` (tombstones included). Restore merges through `mergeContacts` → `setFromSync`.
- **CYCLE v1:**
  - `{ ver, periods[{id,start,end|null,flow?,mtime,del}], days{d-YYYY-MM-DD:{sym[],meds[],note?,mtime}}, cols{}, prefs{remind}, deleted{} }`.
  - Whole-day LWW; absence is never imputed; prefs edits stamp BOTH sm and om.
  - Wave 34: a day record may carry `fl` (1|2|3, the flow of THAT day), `bbt` (basal body temperature, integer hundredths of °C, 3400–4300) and `cm` (cervical mucus 1 dry · 2 moist · 3 creamy · 4 egg white), each with its own CY-3 stamp `fm.fl / fm.bbt / fm.cm` (merge = per field by stamp, equal stamps → larger JSON, a clear keeps its stamp so it beats an older value; `cycle/core.js` `mergeExtras / ownExtras`, used by `mergeDay / canonDay / touchDay`). Keys absent when never set, so older days keep their canonical bytes; `dayView` counts the extra stamps in `max(fm)`. Old data: `period.flow` stays and is the fallback of every day in the period without its own `fl` (`core.dayFlow`); bars show the most frequent day flow (tie → heavier), else `period.flow` (`core.periodFlow`). An older build keeps an extra verbatim under the whole-day rule and drops it under its canonDay; the newer build's own stamps win it back at the next merge (no loss while one new-build device holds it). `prefs.bbt` (boolean, absent = off) shows the temperature / mucus fields and the Insights card; it rides in `prefs` (LWW by `pm`).
  - Wave 34 fertile window (`core.fertility`, symptothermal, Sensiplan-style, render-only, never stored): temperature = first reading higher than the 6 before it (coverline = their max), then 3 higher readings on consecutive days with the 3rd ≥ coverline + 0.20 °C, else a 4th higher one; mucus peak = last day of the best quality (≥ creamy) before a next-day drop, confirmed 3 days later, void if that quality returns within 3 days; end = the later of the two confirmations (temperature alone when no mucus was logged that cycle); start = cycle day 6 (first-5-days rule), or min(first higher temperature day of ≥ 12 earlier cycles) − 8, or the first day with mucus (≥ moist) when earlier. UI and help say "an estimate, not contraception". Doctor report: unchanged (no BBT yet). Tests: `tests/cycle-fertility.test.js`.

(since 0.76.00: `[{id, m, name, subject, html}]`, LWW by m, shared tombs, ≤ 30, html ≤ 8000 chars), rules?   - Root folder "unsorted" is permanent (never nested, never a parent).
  - Dedupe via the shared `dupeKey()` (wave 35, `bookmarks/core.js`): scheme, `www.`, host case, default port, fragment, trailing slashes and tracking parameters (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `msclkid`, `mc_cid`, …) ignored; the rest of the query kept, sorted. One rule for quick-add, edit, imports, the Raindrop plan and the duplicate finder.

    - *Nesting:* `folder.parent` (absent = top level, so old folders keep their bytes). The effective tree is computed, never written: `parentOf` treats a missing parent, `unsorted` or the folder itself as top level, and a cycle (two devices nesting A↔B at once) breaks at the cycle's smallest id, so every device draws the same tree. `canMoveFolder` refuses itself, its own branch and Unsorted. Tabs = top-level folders; the open folder shows a path strip (`#crumbs`: path, subfolder chips, New subfolder). Moves: folder dialog `Inside` select, the tree picker `#dlg-pick` (every Move to… of a bookmark, the selection, a folder), drag (row/tab/chip onto a chip or a crumb; chip onto a tab; tab onto tab stays a reorder). Folder names are unique among siblings. Deleting a folder moves its bookmarks to its parent (Unsorted from a top folder) and its subfolders up one level; Undo restores parents too. A move bumps the folder's `modified` (entity LWW as before).
    - *Side records:* `chk {s: ok|dead|moved|err|skip, at, code?, to?}` (link check) and `arch {at, f, n?, img?}` (saved copy; `f: ""` = removed). Present only when set. They never move `modified` and merge on their own by larger `at` (equal: larger canonical JSON) whichever side wins the entity, so a check on one device cannot undo an edit on another; an older app that drops them loses nothing because the newer side keeps them.

The reader view (`#reader`) re-sanitises the file and shows it in a sandboxed srcdoc frame (no scripts, opaque origin, CSP, palette colours). Files of tombstoned bookmarks with no live reference are removed 12 s after a save (`sweepArchive`; a not-yet-synced bookmark's file is never touched).
    - *Link check:* on request only (folder with subfolders, all, one), `orosFeedsFetch.fetchFeeds` 10 per call, 2 s between calls, ≤ 500 per run, Stop. `core.classify`: 404/410 and relay `network` → dead; 2xx whose final address has another `dupeKey` → moved (`to`); relay `type`/`too-big` → ok; 401/403/429/5xx/timeouts → err (not dead); private hosts → skip; `norelay` → nothing stored. "Use new address" updates the url (Undo). Filter "Broken and moved links" in the tag-filter row.
    - *Duplicates:* merge into the oldest (`core.mergeInto`): tags union (≤ 12), distinct notes joined, star if any, visits summed, newest check, a saved copy it lacked; Undo restores tags/note/star.
    - *Import* (`core.parseImport`, one button, `.html/.htm/.csv`): Netscape (browsers, Raindrop, Pinboard, Linkding: nested `<DL>`, `TAGS`, `ADD_DATE` s/ms/µs, the description line after a link, `DATA-IMPORTANT`), Pocket HTML (`<h1>` Unread / Read Archive) and CSV (`title,url,time_added,tags(|),status`) → folder `Pocket` and `Pocket › Archive`, Raindrop CSV (`folder` split on `/`, `note` else `excerpt`, `created`, `favorite`), any CSV with a url column. Folders by path (sibling name match, else created); a first part named Unsorted = Unsorted; addresses already here (or twice in the file) skipped; `added` = the file's date. Undo (toast) tombstones what came in and removes the new folders while empty, innermost first.
    - *Export:* `core.buildNetscape`: nested `<H3>/<DL>`, Unsorted at the top level, `ADD_DATE`, `LAST_MODIFIED`, `TAGS` (commas inside a tag become spaces), the note as a description line (`<br>` for newlines); branches without bookmarks left out.

Only http(s); when `share-url` is empty the first http(s) URL in `share-text` counts (Android). Bookmarks opens its item dialog in add mode, prefilled; nothing is stored until Save; an already-saved link opens its own dialog instead. `sw.js` never caches `?share-` navigations. No `launch_handler` on purpose: `focus-existing` could swallow the Dropbox OAuth return on Android. Target platforms: Windows, Linux, Android (Safari/iOS best-effort only). Since AS-OUT (wave 4 of quick access) the system share sheet's GET carries `share-pick=1`: the shell opens the "Send to…" sheet (link or text) instead, so the user picks Bookmarks, the Assistant or another app; links without `share-pick` (bookmarklet, add-on) still go straight to Bookmarks.

Not an app folder (no index.html), never precached. Store steps in `extension/README.md`, privacy text `extension/PRIVACY.md`, tests `tests/extension.test.js`. Add-on version lives in `extension/manifest.json`, separate from APP_VERSION. **2.0.0 (PW-AF1, 5.00.00):** renamed "orOS" (the Gecko id `send-to-oros@useoros.online` never changes); the toolbar button opens a popup (Passwords + "Save this page to orOS"), `_execute_action` Ctrl+Shift+L, `send-page` Alt+Shift+O; permissions `activeTab`, `alarms`, `contextMenus`, `scripting`, `storage`, host `https://useoros.online/*`, optional `https://*/*`, `http://localhost/*`, `http://127.0.0.1/*` (asked when needed); still no content scripts and no network requests of its own. Zip built by `.github/workflows/addon.yml`, published on main to the GitHub release `browser-addon` (`oros-addon.zip`), linked with install steps from the download page (`#addon`, `#addon-el`). Part IV "Desktop autofill".

- **MEMORY v1:**
  - `{ ver, br, best{lv:{id,ts,moves,ms}}, games[{id,ts,lv,mode,set,moves,ms,s?}] }`; lv ∈ {e,m,h,x}, mode ∈ {solo,duo}, set ∈ {shapes,icons,letters}; `s` = [p1, p2] for duo only.
  - Games are immutable: union by id (byte tie-break), newest first, cap 50. Best per level: fewer moves → less time → earlier → id (total order, symmetric); every solo game in the merged history is also a candidate.
  - Reset = `br` stamp (max-merged): games and records with `ts <= br` drop on every device. No tombstones.
  - Merge is symmetric and idempotent; not strictly associative when a record's game falls off the cap, converges in one more merge (Node, 20,000 rounds).
- **CONNECT4 v1:**
  - `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[won,lost,drawn]}}} }`: results vs the computer only (2-player series stay on the device).
  - Each device increments only its own row (id in the device-local `oros-connect4-device`). Merge per row: larger epoch `b` wins, equal epochs take the per-cell max; rows with `b < br` drop. A join: symmetric, associative, idempotent (`tests/games.test.js`).
  - Reset = `br` stamp; a device whose row is older starts a new row at `b = br` on its next result.
- **DOTS v1:**
  - `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{<level><size>:[won,lost,drawn]}}} }`, keys `e3` … `h5` (level e|m|h × board 3|4|5 boxes): results vs the computer only.
  - Same join and reset as CONNECT4 v1 (device id in the device-local `oros-dots-device`); unknown keys and bad cells drop in `normRow`.

  - `{ ver, cards[{id, m, user, disp, pron, loc, langs, since, email, phone, web, bio, motto, links[{l,u}] (≤8), tags[] (≤12, unique), hide[] (sorted field keys not shown on the card), st (oros|terminal|paper|mint|rose), av{s: seed, px: "" | 144 digits 0–6, t: 0|1 transparent}}] sorted by id, tombs{id: deletedAt} sorted }`.

  - The avatar is NOT an image: `s` seeds a deterministic mirrored 12×12 face (`genAvatar`, FNV-1a + mulberry32) and `px` holds only hand-painted pixels (R30).
  - A new card stays an unsaved draft until its first edit (R16 lazy). Every export and the share link need a username.

  - Recipe (shared by the app and the shell, `wallpaper/art.js` `normRecipe`, fixed key order): `{ seed (text, spaces collapsed, ≤ 40, never empty), style (waves|flow|orbits|grid|nebula), pal (oros|ember|ocean|forest|dusk|pastel|mono), dens 0–100, chaos 0–100, grain 0|1, light 0|1 }`. The picture is a pure function of the recipe, the shape of the canvas and, for `pal: "oros"`, the skin colour: geometry is in units of the short side and counts scale with the area in those units, so every size of one shape gives the same picture. A nebula is always dark.
  - Slice `wallpaper` (oros-wallpaper-data): `{ ver, favs[{id, m, r: recipe}] sorted by id, tombs{id: deletedAt} sorted }`. Merge as NETIZEN v1 (newer `m`, equal `m` the larger canonical JSON; tomb ≥ `m` drops, R17). At most 60 favourites.

  - No image is stored or synced (R30): the shell draws the recipe at its own screen size (long side ≤ 3840) and keeps the picture in IndexedDB `oros-wallpaper`, not on the Files disk (that one syncs file by file through Vault Drive).

Merge as NETIZEN v1 (newer `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON; tombs max; a tomb ≥ `m` hides the wheel; Undo writes a fresh `m`) (`tests/wheel.test.js`).

- **QR v1:**
  - Slice `qr` (oros-qr-data): `{ ver, codes[{id, m, name (≤ 40), type, f (fields), st (look)}] sorted by id, tombs{id: deletedAt} sorted }`, at most 100 codes. `type` ∈ url, wifi, vcard, event, text, email, phone, sms, geo; `f` holds only that type's keys (`FIELDS` in `qr/qr-payload.js`, strings capped, enums and booleans coerced; WiFi passwords sync too, Chris 2026-10-08); `st` = `{sd?, se?, sl?, ecl L|M|Q|H, fg, bg (#rrggbb), mg 0–10, rd, cap, ct (≤ 40)}`. v1.1 keys (wave 19), present only when set so a v1.0 look keeps its exact JSON: `sd: "dots"` (separate round dots; `rd` is forced true with it, so a v1.0 device draws rounded dots), `se` ∈ square|rounded|circle (corner/eye style; absent = square with square dots, rounded otherwise), `sl` the logo, a `data:image/(png|jpeg|webp|gif);base64` URL ≤ 80 000 characters (made ≤ 192 px, WebP where the browser writes it, so it can sync). While `sl` is set the code is encoded at level H whatever `ecl` says, and the middle 22% of its width is left empty for the logo (encoder max 25%: at 30% small versions stop reading). The new keys come first in `normStyle` and sort after `ecl`, so at equal `m` the copy that still has them is the larger canonical JSON and wins over one a v1.0 device stripped; a newer edit on a v1.0 device still wins (LWW) and drops them (`tests/qr-scan.test.js`). Merge as NETIZEN v1 (newer `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON; tombs max; a tomb ≥ `m` hides the code; Undo writes a fresh `m`) (`tests/qr.test.js`).
  - The text inside the code is derived from `type` + `f` on every render, never stored.
- **PASSWORDS v2 (Password Manager, wave 47) — security design, written before the code and implemented as written:**
  - **Threat model.** Protected: anyone who holds the synced blob, a cloud backup copy, an exported orOS backup or this device's localStorage (the cloud provider, a thief of the disk or of a backup, a script that reads localStorage) sees only ciphertext plus a public header; a lost or stolen device while the vault is locked; shoulder surfing (secrets hidden until Show); a password left on the clipboard (cleared after 30 s). NOT protected: a device or browser that is compromised while the vault is open (malware, keylogger, a hostile extension, an XSS in the orOS origin: the shell and the app frame share one origin, Part V); a weak master password (offline guessing is slowed by Argon2id, not stopped); a forgotten master password AND a lost recovery key (no server, no reset: the data is gone). Desktop autofill (PW-AF1) goes through the orOS add-on, which keeps its own ciphertext copy and its own unlock ("Desktop autofill" below); a hostile extension or a compromised browser can read whatever the add-on fills into a page, like any password manager's add-on. Phone autofill (PW-AF2) keeps a sealed copy in the orOS Android app that only that phone's Keystore opens, the values only after a fingerprint, face or screen lock; a rooted or compromised phone, or an app that reads its own fields, sees what is filled into it. Saving a login (PW-AF3) hands it to the open orOS page in memory only (never in a URL or storage) and stores it only on the editor's Save; on the phone it waits sealed with a Keystore key for at most a day.
  - **Crypto.** KDF Argon2id (hash-wasm 4.12.0 by Dani Biró, MIT, `vendor/hash-wasm/argon2.umd.min.js`, WebAssembly, loaded only by this app) with m = 64 MiB, t = 3, p = 1, 32-byte output, 16-byte random salt. Fallback when WebAssembly is missing or fails: PBKDF2-SHA-256 with 600,000 iterations (WebCrypto), recorded in the header. Bounds when reading a header (a crafted one must not hang the tab): Argon2id m 8 MiB–1 GiB, t 1–20, p 1–8; PBKDF2 600,000–5,000,000. Key hierarchy: the KDF output imports as a non-extractable AES-256-GCM key-encryption key (KEK) that unwraps a random 256-bit vault key VK (wrap = AES-GCM, random 96-bit IV, AAD `oros-pm/1/pw/<kid>`). VK goes through HKDF-SHA-256 (salt = kid) into EK (AES-256-GCM, info `oros-pm/1/enc`) and IK (HMAC-SHA-256, info `oros-pm/1/iv`), both non-extractable; the raw VK bytes are zero-filled at once. Each blob = AES-256-GCM of the canonical JSON snapshot of the vault (no compression), AAD = `oros-pm/1|kid|id|t|sup` so its cleartext header cannot be swapped or edited. IVs: random 96-bit for every save; a merge blob (below) gets IV = first 12 bytes of HMAC(IK, id), and its id is a hash of the blob ids it merges, so the same IV only ever seals the same plaintext. Recovery key: 128 random bits shown once as 26 Crockford base32 characters in groups; it wraps VK a second time through HKDF-SHA-256 (salt = kid, info `oros-pm/1/rk`, no slow KDF: it is random), AAD `oros-pm/1/rk/<kid>`. Randomness only from `crypto.getRandomValues`.
  - **Stored where.** Slice `passwords` = localStorage `oros-passwords-vault`: `{ v: 1, vaults{kid: {c, kt, kdf{alg, salt, m, t, p | i}, pw{iv, ct}, rk{iv, ct}|null, blobs{id: {t, sup[], iv, ct}}}}, gone{kid: t} }`. That is ciphertext plus a public header: the KDF settings, when the vault was made, when its password last changed, and blob ids/times. No titles, counts, URLs or user names. `oros-passwords-prefs` (device-local) gains `lock` (auto-lock minutes 1|2|5|15|30|60, default 5) and `lockHide` (lock when the app is hidden, default 1); no secret. In memory only while unlocked: EK, IK, the decrypted entries and the session's generated passwords; Lock drops them and empties every field. Never: plaintext in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, the console, URLs, notifications (toasts are local and generic: "Copied"), Today, search providers or the Assistant (Passwords is in `NEVER_APPS`); the app registers no search provider. **Rule (Chris 2026-11-01 19:44): the Assistant never sees anything from Passwords, for any reason** — no consent setting (a synced "always" still gives "off"), no search provider, no Today feed, no Send/Assistant bridge, no `EDIT_APP` catalog; later waves (OTP, add-on, Android autofill) keep it so. Pinned by `tests/assistant.test.js` "Passwords never reaches the Assistant".
  - **Entries** (inside the ciphertext): snapshot `{ v: 1, e[{id, c, m, title (≤ 200), user (≤ 500), pw (≤ 4,096), urls[≤ 20 × 2,048], notes (≤ 20,000), totp (≤ 2,048: an otpauth:// URI or a base32 secret), tags[≤ 30 × 60], fields[≤ 50 {n ≤ 200, v ≤ 10,000, h 0|1}], fav 0|1, hist[≤ 5 {pw, t}]}] sorted by id, d{id: deletedAt} sorted }`.
  - **What syncs.** Only the slice above, inside the orOS sync blob (itself sealed with the sync passphrase: two independent layers). The sync merge (`PmVault.mergeSlice`, pure, no keys, live registration with the app open): vaults joined by kid (a kid in `gone` is dropped); per vault the header with the larger `kt` wins (tie: larger canonical JSON), `c` = min; blobs = union, minus every blob whose id is in another blob's `sup`. Per-entry merge needs the keys, so it runs only when the vault is open: every blob is decrypted and the entries merged (newer `m` wins, equal `m` the larger canonical JSON; a tombstone ≥ `m` hides the entry, an edit after it brings it back; tombstones are kept). When more than one blob is left the app writes one merge blob (id `x` + SHA-256 of the sorted ids, IV from IK, `t` = max, `sup` = those ids + their `sup`, sorted, ≤ 64): two devices that merge the same blobs write the same bytes, so no upload loop. A save writes a fresh blob of the full snapshot with `sup` = every current blob. A locked device only unions blobs. Two vaults made on two devices before they synced (two kids): the oldest `c` is the vault; the other is offered as "another vault": open it with its own password and its entries move in (its kid goes to `gone`), or delete it.
  - **Never leaves the device:** the master password, the recovery key (shown once), VK/EK/IK, decrypted entries. Exports are made only on request: Bitwarden JSON (plaintext: a strong warning and a tick box first) or KeePass KDBX 4 (encrypted with a password the user types: Argon2id 64 MiB / 3 passes, AES-256-CBC, ChaCha20 inner stream, gzip).
  - **Recovery.** No server, no reset. (1) The recovery key opens the vault and asks for a new master password at once; a new recovery key can be made while open (the old one stops working). (2) The data itself is backed up by sync (cloud copy + 7 daily backups, SY-D2) and by KDBX exports. Changing the master password re-wraps VK only: older cloud backups still open with the old password (stated in help). Without both the password and the recovery key nothing can be recovered.
  - **Locking and clipboard.** Lock after the chosen minutes without a key, click or touch; at once when the page is hidden (option, default on) and on pagehide; closing the app unloads the frame. Every copy of a password, code or hidden field clears the clipboard after 30 s (if the app has no focus then, at the next focus; best effort); Lock clears it too when a copy is pending.
  - **TOTP** (RFC 6238): SHA-1/256/512, 6–8 digits, period 15–120 s, from a base32 secret or an otpauth://totp URI (otpauth://hotp is refused: a counter cannot sync safely); code + countdown; QR read with the camera or a picture (BarcodeDetector, else the vendored jsQR, loaded on demand); the QR app's scanner is internal and keeps a history, so it is not used (a secret must never land in that history).
  - **Import** (always into the open vault, new ids, duplicates — same title, user, password and first URL — skipped): Bitwarden JSON (unencrypted; an encrypted export is refused with a message; folders → tags, cards and identities → custom fields, hidden fields kept hidden, password history), CSV (Bitwarden, Chrome/Edge, Firefox, KeePassXC, 1Password headers), KeePass KDBX 3.1 and 4.x (own reader, `passwords/kdbx.js`: AES-KDF, Argon2d/Argon2id; AES-256 or ChaCha20; Salsa20/ChaCha20 inner streams; password and/or key file; groups → tags, recycle bin skipped, `otp` and KeePass TimeOtp fields → TOTP, history → password history). Twofish is refused with a message.
  - **Entry types (PW-K1, wave 1 of the cards / identities / OTP / autofill plan, 2026-11-01):** `passwords/pmkinds.js` (`PmKinds`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/passwords-kinds.test.js`). An entry is a login unless it carries the reserved field `{n: "oros:k", v: "card"|"identity"|"address"|"note"}`; typed values are reserved fields `oros:<cc|id|ad>.<key>` inside the existing `fields` (never new entry keys: 4.96.00 and older `normEntry` drop unknown keys and would write that loss into a merge blob that supersedes the newer one; reserved fields pass through them byte for byte, a test runs the 4.96.00 `pmcore.js` kept in `tests/fixtures/`). Card `holder, num (h), exp "MM/YYYY", cvv (h), pin (h), bank` + `urls` (bank site); identity `honor, first, middle, last, birth (YYYY-MM-DD), email, phone, company, idno (h), idexp, pass (h), passexp, lic (h), licexp, tax (h), ssn (h), ins (h)`; address `name, street, line2, floor, city, zip, region, country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, free text kept), phone`; a note keeps its text in `notes`, shown only after Show. Non-login types clear `user`, `pw`, `totp`, `hist` (and `urls` except cards). Order on save: marker, typed values in spec order, then the person's fields (≤ 50); reserved fields of another type or an unknown marker are kept untouched by both editors. Unknown marker = login. `normEntry` also keeps `x`, a small plain object (≤ 40 keys, string/number values, ≤ 8,000 chars canonical) for later fields, absent unless set, so existing entries are byte-identical. Search skips reserved names and hidden values; `dupKey` adds the typed values (two cards with one title are two entries). Imports: Bitwarden types 3 / 4 / 2 and the readers' `card` / `identity` / `note` items go through `fromLabels` (English labels → keys; an identity with an address gives a second entry, id `hexId(id + "|address")` or a new id; an identity that holds only a name and an address is an address); a login that `legacyKind` recognises (no user / password / 2FA, card or identity labels) offers Convert with Undo. Bitwarden export writes types 3 / 4 (addresses as identities) / 2 with the extra values as custom fields under the `EN` labels, so the round trip is lossless. Card checks: Luhn, network by IIN, expiry `expired` / `soon` (≤ 60 days, valid to the month end); document expiry likewise. Nothing typed ever leaves the vault (Passwords stays in `NEVER_APPS`, no provider, no notification).
  - **Two-factor codes (PW-OTP2, wave 2, 2026-11-01):** kind `otp` ("2FA code", `PmKinds` 1.1.0): a login with the marker `oros:k = otp`, no password and no history; the issuer is `title`, the account `user`, the secret `totp`, sites optional; an older orOS shows it as a login. New › 2FA code opens the login editor in that mode (password, generator and meter hidden; a scanned otpauth:// link fills an empty service / account; a valid secret is required). Imported codes that match no entry become `otp` entries (`import.js` `apply`). **Codes screen:** tabs `Entries` / `Codes` above the toolbar (`view.screen`); every entry with a valid TOTP, sorted by title, filtered by the search; codes are computed only for rows on screen (`IntersectionObserver`) and only while the vault is open, one 1 s timer (`totpTimer`) that stops when the list leaves the page or the vault locks; in the last 5 s a row also shows the next code and a tap copies the next one (still valid on paste); copies use the 30 s clipboard clear. **QR per account:** `QR code` in an entry's code row opens a dialog with a warning; the QR (orOS's own `qr/qr-encode.js`, loaded on demand, ECL M) is drawn on a canvas only after a second tap and the canvas is wiped on close or lock. **Export** (`passwords/otpexport.js`, `PmOtpExport` 1.0.0, pure, Node-tested in `tests/passwords-otp.test.js`): two-factor codes only, valid TOTP, one per secret + account; `Aegis (.json, encrypted)` = Aegis vault v1 with db v2, random 32-byte master key + AES-256-GCM over the list, one password slot scrypt N 2^15 r 8 p 1 (the importer's `scrypt`) + AES-256-GCM over the master key, file password ≥ 8 characters typed twice; `2FAS (.2fas, NOT encrypted)` = schema 4 services list behind the same tick-to-confirm as the plain Bitwarden export (2FAS' password-protected format needs a password-check field whose content is not published; not guessed). Notes and tags are not exported. Both files are read back by our importer in the tests, and the Aegis file is also opened with Node's own scrypt + AES-GCM. HOTP and code notifications stay out (wave 47). Same rule as every Passwords wave: nothing reaches the Assistant, search, Today or notifications.
  - **Desktop autofill (PW-AF1, wave 3, 2026-11-01, add-on 2.0.0):** in the orOS browser add-on (`extension/`, Part IV "Browser add-on"). **Code:** `extension/pm/` holds byte-for-byte copies of `passwords/pmcrypto.js`, `pmcore.js`, `pmkinds.js` and hash-wasm's Argon2id + LICENSE (`node .github/scripts/ext-pm.js`; `tests/extension-pm.test.js` and the add-on workflow fail on a stale copy), so the add-on opens the vault exactly as orOS does; the extension CSP is `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`. **Copy** (`pmvault.js`, `OrosVault`): the `oros-passwords-vault` slice is read with `scripting` from an open tab on the orOS address (host permission for that origin only, asked with "Allow access to orOS"; on every finished load of an orOS tab while the permission is held, and when the popup opens) and kept in `storage.local` merged with `PmVault.mergeSlice` (never replaced, an older tab cannot drop blobs); a slice from a newer orOS is kept whole and never opened. **Unlock:** the master password opens the vault key (`openVK`, Argon2id or PBKDF2 as stored); only `{kid, vk, until}` is kept in `storage.session` (memory, not readable by pages or content scripts); every use moves `until` forward by the lock time (options: 1/5/15/30/60 min, default 15) and alarm `pm-lock` removes it; the master password is never stored. **Matching** (`pmfill.js`, `OrosFill.fits`): page host = saved host or a sub-domain of it (never the other way, no Public Suffix list: `a.github.io` never fits `b.github.io`), a saved https site never fills an http page (a bare host counts as https), IP addresses need host and port equal, a single-label host other than localhost fits nothing, only http(s) pages. `matches`: logins and 2FA codes, exact host first, then favourites, then title. **Fill:** only on a click in the popup; `scripting.executeScript` into the top frame of the active tab with `fillInPage(payload)` (self-contained); it returns -1 and fills nothing when the tab's origin changed since the popup opened. Fields by `autocomplete` token first, then by name / id / placeholder / aria-label / label text, lower-case without accents (EN/EL/DE regexes); a field whose `autocomplete` names another known token is never guessed; values set through the native setter with `input` + `change` events (React / Vue). Payload: login {user, pw, current 2FA code}; 2FA-only {user, code}; card {holder, number, month, year, CVV}, never the PIN; identity / address {names, e-mail, phone, company, street, line 2, city, postcode, region, country, birthday}, never document numbers; notes never. Cards, identities and addresses are offered on any site (the person picks), logins only where `fits`. The top frame needs no host permission (the toolbar click grants `activeTab`). **Payment frames:** for a card, when the top page filled fewer than 2 fields, `framesInPage` (top frame) lists the https origins of visible frames from other sites (≥ 20×10 px, max 5, addresses only); the popup names them ("The card number is in a payment frame from …") and only after `Fill in the payment frame` requests those origins (optional host permission, the browser's own prompt) and runs a second `fillInPage` pass with `allFrames` and `frames: [origins]`, in which the top page fills nothing and each frame fills only if its own origin is in the confirmed list. **Not covered yet:** logins inside frames, passkeys (saving new logins: PW-AF3 below). Tests: `tests/extension-pm.test.js` (copy, fits, matches, payload, pmvault with a fake browser API); a Playwright run with the real add-on (login, 2FA, card in Greek labels, address, look-alike host refused, navigation refused, lock empties the session).
  - **Phone autofill (PW-AF2, wave 4, 2026-11-01):** Android Autofill Framework service in the orOS app (`OrosAutofillService`, chosen by the person in Android Settings; BR-PHONE v8). **Switch:** Passwords › Menu › `Autofill on this phone`, only when `window.parent.orosPhone.available()` (the orOS Android app); device-local option `prefs.af` (`passwords.js`, never synced). **Sealed lists** (`passwords/afindex.js`, `PmAfIndex` 1.0.0, loaded on demand): `names` = per entry `{i, k, t, s, w (http(s) sites), a (Android packages from androidapp:// sites), o (has a valid TOTP)}`, no secrets; `index` = `{i, k, t, u, p, o: {k base64 TOTP key, a, d, n}}` for logins / 2FA-only, `c: {name, num, mm, yyyy, cvv}` for cards, `h: {…}` for identities and addresses, exactly the add-on's fill values (tested); never card PINs, document numbers, notes, custom fields or password history; notes entries not at all. Each list: fresh AES-256-GCM key, wrapped with RSA-OAEP SHA-1 (Android Keystore's OAEP supports MGF1 with SHA-1 only; WebCrypto uses one hash for both) for its Keystore key. Sent 2 s after unlock and after every save while the switch is on; the vault, its key and the master password never leave the page. **Suggestions** (`OrosAutofillService`): reads `names` only; fields by autofill hints, HTML `autocomplete`, input type, then words (`AfMatch`, same EN/EL/DE words as `pmfill.js`, accents removed); a web domain counts only when a known browser package reports it (`AfMatch.BROWSERS`), with `fits()` = the add-on's rule (and an unknown scheme counts as http); in any other app only `androidapp://<package>` sites or a link made on this phone count; nothing inside orOS itself or on useoros.online; at most 6 suggestions, every one locked with `setAuthentication`. **Tap** (`AfAuthActivity`): BiometricPrompt (BIOMETRIC_STRONG or device credential; Android 9 and older the confirm-credential screen), then `index` is opened in memory and only that entry's values go to the fields of this form; the 2FA code is computed there (RFC 6238, `AfMatch.totp`, checked against the RFC vectors). An app no login names gets one locked "Choose a login from orOS": after unlock the person picks a login and confirms "Use … in <app> (<package>)"; the link is kept on this phone only (`oros-autofill` `links`). A new fingerprint invalidates the index key: the service then deletes keys and copies and asks to turn it on again. Saving from the phone: PW-AF3 below; the single app "orOS Passwords" follows when it gets a bridge of its own (it shares the origin's storage with orOS, so loading the full `phone.js` there would push Contacts / Calendar to a package without those permissions). Tests: `tests/passwords-autofill.test.js` (lists, add-on parity, seal opened by Node's RSA-OAEP + AES-GCM, bridge / service / manifest / strings); Java compiled against Android 15 and `AfMatch` rules + TOTP vectors run on a JVM; the APK is built by `android.yml`. Not tested here: a real phone, fingerprint, real apps and browsers.
  - **Saving new logins (PW-AF3, wave 5, 2026-11-01):** a login typed elsewhere reaches the Passwords editor and is stored only when the person presses Save there. **Sources:** (a) the add-on: `Save the login from this page` (a click) runs `readLogin` (`extension/pmfill.js`) in the top frame of that tab: a field with `autocomplete=new-password` first, else with three password fields the second (current, new, confirm), two equal ones the first, else the last; the user name is an `autocomplete` username/email field, else the last filled text field before the password; only the page origin, the title, the name and the password leave the page; the popup asks "Send the login for <host> (<user>) to Passwords in orOS?", and on a yes `background.js` (accepting it only from its own popup) focuses an orOS shell tab (path of the orOS address) or opens one and posts `{type:"oros-pw-save", n, item}` from its isolated world into that page, retrying every 750 ms for 30 s until the shell answers `{type:"oros-pw-saved", n, ok}`; (b) Android: with autofill on (the copies are stored), every form with a password or new-password field carries a `SaveInfo` (password, user name optional, `FLAG_SAVE_ON_ALL_VIEWS_INVISIBLE`); on the person's yes `onSaveRequest` reads the typed values (same password rule, `AfMatch.pickPassword`; the user name from an earlier screen of the same app or site when the last has none), never for orOS itself or useoros.online, builds `{url: scheme://host (browsers only) | app: package, user, pw, title}`, seals it with a third Keystore key (`oros-af-save`, AES-256-GCM, no user authentication; at most 10, kept at most 24 h; removed with the other copies when autofill goes off), opens orOS (Android 9+, the save callback's IntentSender) and sends it over the bridge (`af-save`, BR-PHONE v8) on every channel until the page answers `applied`. **Shell** (`shell.js`): `window.__orosPwSave(item)` keeps it in memory only (max 10, 10 minutes), brings Passwords to the front (`__orosPwPoke`) or opens it; Passwords takes them with `__orosTakePwSave()` at start; the window `message` listener accepts only messages whose source is the shell window itself and whose origin is its own. **Passwords** (`PmApp.saveLogin`, `PmAfIndex.saveItem` / `findSave`): an item needs a password and an http(s) page (kept as its origin) or a valid package (`androidapp://<package>`); the entry of the same place (host without `www.`, or the package) and user name (case ignored), newest first, gets the editor with the new password and a note (the old one goes to the history through `withHistory`), the same password only a toast, otherwise a new login prefilled with title, user name, password and site. Waiting items show one at a time after an editor closes; a locked vault shows "A login from … is waiting" and opens them after unlock; locking an open vault drops them. Tests: `tests/passwords-autofill.test.js` (saveItem, findSave, memory-only and source checks, Android parity); Playwright in the real shell (EL 390 px, EN 1280 px: update with history note, new entry from the window message with the answer, a message from another window ignored, same password, two waiting, locked → unlock, Passwords not running, nothing in web storage) and with the real add-on in Chromium (nothing typed, the confirmation, a new orOS tab opened, the editor prefilled, a second save into the same tab); Java compiled against Android 15. Not tested: a real phone (the save prompt, the IntentSender), Firefox.
- **ZEN v1:**
  - Slice `zen` (oros-zen-data): `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, d{"YYYY-MM-DD": [sessions, seconds, breaths]}}} }`. Each device writes only its own row and its counters only grow. Per row: larger epoch `b` wins; equal epochs take per day the max of each counter; rows with `b < br` drop; a row keeps its 400 newest days. A join (`tests/zen.test.js`).
  - Reset = a new epoch: `br` past every row; each device starts its own row again at `br`. Stats (today, this week, streak, sessions, last 7 days) are sums over rows; a session counts only after one whole breath.
- **NAMES v1:**
  - Slice `names` (oros-names-data): `{ ver, favs[{id, m, k: handle|title|regal, s (≤ 80, spaces collapsed)}] sorted by id, tombs{id: deletedAt} sorted }`, at most 1,000 favourites. `id` = "n" + two FNV-1a hashes (base 36, 7 + 7) of `k|s`, so the same name kept on two devices is one favourite; an id that does not match its text drops. Merge as NETIZEN v1 (newer `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON; tombs max; a tomb ≥ `m` hides the name; a new star or Undo writes `m` past the tomb) (`tests/names.test.js`).
- **TICTACTOE v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[won,lost,drawn]}}} }`, results vs the computer only; same join and reset as CONNECT4 v1 (device id in `oros-tictactoe-device`).
- **PETWORLD v1:** `{ ver, br, pet{id, ts}|null, rows{deviceId:{b, c{item:[in, out]}}} }`. `br` = max. `pet` (which pet this forest belongs to): later `ts` wins, a tie takes the greater id. Rows: larger epoch `b` wins whole; equal epochs take per item the max of `in` and of `out`; rows with `b < br` drop. Item ids `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,23}$`, at most 64 per row, counts integers 0…1e9; well-formed UNKNOWN items are kept (a newer version's items must survive an older device's merge, else two versions re-upload forever); the UI shows only known items. Balance of an item = Σin − Σout over rows. A fresh start sets `br` past every row and rebinds the pet; this device's next move starts a row at epoch `br`. A join (`tests/petworld.test.js`). Phase 1 writes only the binding; phases 2–5 fill the ledger. Phase 2 spends foods and seeds through `out` (seeds bought later will come in through `in`).
- **PETGARDEN v1** (slice `petgarden`, key `oros-petgarden-data`, since 0.45.00): `{ ver, br, plots{"0"…"9":{s, t, n, wn, tot{item:count}}} }`. `s` crop id ("" = empty bed), `t` planting time (the bed's cycle), `n` harvests taken this cycle, `wn` the growth (by `n`) that was watered, −1 none, `tot` everything this bed ever yielded. Join per bed: larger `t` wins whole; same `t`: larger `s` wins whole, else max of `n`, `wn`, and per item of `tot`; beds with `t < br` drop. Yields are deterministic per (bed, `t`, `n`) (FNV hash), so the same harvest taken on two offline devices merges into one. Stock of an item = start pack + Σ ledger (`in` − `out`) + Σ `tot`, never below 0. Crops (hours): carrot 4, strawberry 8, mushroom 12, sunflower 24 (seeds only), apple tree 72 then fruits every 24; watering once per growth cuts a quarter of it. 4 beds; bed 5 opens at level 4 and bed 6 at level 8 (since 0.45.11, PETPROGRESS v1), and a bed in use always shows. Since 0.45.11 every harvest also yields acorns (1, or 2 for sunflower and apple), part of the fixed yield. A fresh start sets `br` and empties the beds. New data areas go in NEW slices: phase-1 `mergeWorld` drops unknown top-level keys. A join (`tests/petworld.test.js`).
- **PETNEST v1** (slice `petnest`, key `oros-petnest-data`, since 0.45.03): `{ ver, br, built{key: ts}, rows{deviceId:{b, v, w{startTs: minutes}, sum{item:n}}} }`. `built`: nest stages `n1`…`n5` and decorations (`path`, `lantern`, `flowers`, `garland`) with their build time; per key max, `ts < br` drops. Their COST is derived from what is built (n1 pebble 3; n2 twig 8; n3 twig 6 + leaf 4; n4 leaf 10; n5 moss 6; path pebble 6; lantern twig 3 + pebble 2; flowers sunflower 2; garland leaf 6), so a stage built on two offline devices is paid once. Stages go in order; decorations need a stage (path 1, lantern 2, flowers 2, garland 4). `rows`: walks, one row per device that started them, written ONLY by that device; larger (b, v) wins whole, a tie takes the greater canonical JSON; `b < br` drops. `w` = walks (start → 15 / 30 / 60 min; any 1…1440 kept for newer versions; newest 32 kept).
