A walk's loot is fixed by (device, start, minutes) (FNV + mulberry32): 15 min 2–3 materials, 30 min 4–5 + 25% a seed, 60 min 8–10 + 50% a seed + 25% a find (feather, shell, clover); materials twig 35% / leaf 35% / moss 15% / pebble 15%. Since 0.45.11 a walk also brings acorns (15 min 1, 30 min 2, 60 min 4), added after every other draw so older loot is unchanged. Loot counts once the walk is over. The owner folds finished walks except the newest into `sum` (v + 1): same totals, small row. One walk at a time (refused while any walk is under way); the pet must be awake with energy ≥ 20; walks do NOT change the pet's stats (energy model untouched, decision 4). Stock = START_PACK + ledger + garden `tot` + Σ `sum` + loot of finished walks − built costs, never below 0. A join (`tests/petworld.test.js`).
- **PETGAMES v1** (slice `petgames`, key `oros-petgames-data`, since 0.45.08): `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{game:{best, n}}}} }`, games `catch`, `hide`, `follow` (well-formed unknown ids kept). Per row: larger epoch `b` wins whole; equal epochs take per game max `best` and max `n`; rows with `b < br` drop. Shown: best over rows, plays summed. A game stopped at score 0 leaves no trace; any other finished or stopped game records and calls `orosPet.play(cost)` (catch 6, hide 4, follow 4 energy). A join (`tests/petworld.test.js`).
- **PETPROGRESS v1** (slice `petprogress`, key `oros-petprogress-data`, since 0.45.11): `{ ver, br, days[day…], wear{id, ts} | null }`. `days` = the UTC day numbers (`floor(ts / 24 h)`, the same on every device) on which the pet was fed or patted, taken from `pet.js`'s care log `oros-pet-events` (any device) every 10 s and right after care in the app, only while the forest is bound to a non-provisional pet; a set: union, sorted, newest 4,000 kept, days before `floor(br / 24 h)` drop. `wear` = the accessory worn (`""` none): later `ts` wins, a tie takes the greater id, `ts < br` drops; the app shows it only while the accessory is owned. DERIVED, never stored: XP = 10 × care days + 2 × crops harvested (Σ garden `tot` of crop items) + 1 × materials and finds brought home by finished walks + 25 × nest stages and decorations + 3 × games played + 20 × achievements; level = the highest L in 1…20 with 20·L·(L−1) ≤ XP; achievements (13): first harvest, 50 crops, 100 things from walks, a find, the nest finished, all four decorations, 25 games, Catch it 25, Hide and seek 8, Follow me 8, 7 care days in a row, 30 care days, 3 accessories owned. Acorns are ledger item `acorn` (start purse 5): games add `acornsFor(kind, score)` (catch ⌊score/8⌋, hide ⌊score/2⌋, follow score − 2; 0…5) on this device's row, walks and harvests bring theirs in their fixed loot. The forest bazaar spends them on this device's row: seeds (carrot 2 from level 1, strawberry 3 from 2, mushroom 4 from 3, sunflower 6 from 5, apple 12 from 7) and accessories (`acc_<id>`: bow 8 from level 2, scarf 15 from 4, hat 25 from 6, glasses 35 from 9, crown 50 from 12, bell 70 from 15); a bought accessory is worn at once. A fresh start sets `br` (days and the worn accessory go; the ledger, garden, nest and games reset as before). A join (`tests/petworld.test.js`).
- **SIMON v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{c4|r4|c6|r6:{n, ts, g}}}} }` (mode c/r × 4/6 pads): best score `n` reached at `ts`, games played `g`. Per row: larger epoch `b` wins; equal epochs take per setting the better best (higher `n`, then earlier `ts`) and the larger `g`; rows with `b < br` drop. A join (`tests/games.test.js`). The shown record is the best across rows; games are summed.
- **WHACK v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:{n, ts, g}}}} }`: best score `n` reached at `ts`, rounds played `g` (finished rounds only). Same join and reset as SIMON v1 (higher `n`, then earlier `ts`; max `g`). A join (`tests/games.test.js`).
- **SNAKE v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{sw|so|nw|no|fw|fo:{n, ts, g}}}} }`: key = speed (s/n/f) + walls (w) or open (o); best score `n` (fruit eaten) reached at `ts`, games played `g` (finished games only). Same join and reset as SIMON v1 (higher `n`, then earlier `ts`; max `g`). A join (`tests/games.test.js`).
- **G2048 v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{n3|n4|n5|t3|t4|t5:{s, ts, v, g, w}}}} }` (`t*` = timed mode, since 0.52.01): best score `s` reached at `ts`, best tile `v` (0 or a power of two), games played `g` (finished games only), games that reached the target `w`. Join per size: higher `s`, then earlier `ts`; max `v`, `g`, `w`. A game with an undo counts in `g`/`w` but sets no `s`/`v`. A join (`tests/games.test.js`).
- **WORDLE v1:** `{ ver, br, days{"en|el:<day>":{b, r}}, rows{deviceId:{b, s{en|el:{g, w, h[6]}}}} }`: `day` = days since 1 Jan 2026 (local calendar day); `r` = tries 1–6, 7 = lost; per day key the larger `b` wins, equal `b` keeps the lower `r`. Free play rows: games `g`, found `w` (≤ g), guesses histogram `h`; per row the larger epoch wins, equal epochs take the max of every counter. Entries with `b < br` drop. A join (`tests/wordle.test.js`). Wave 49: `Share` (was `Copy`) goes through `orosDaily.share` (share sheet on a phone, clipboard elsewhere); the result and statistics dialogs link to the Game Center.
- **SPOT v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{l1|l2|l3:{t, ts, w}}}} }`: best time `t` (ms incl. penalties, 1 to 100 h) reached at `ts`, wins `w` (≥ 1). Join per level: lower `t`, then earlier `ts`; max `w`. Rows with `b < br` drop; per row the larger `b` wins. A join (`tests/spot.test.js`).
- **HEXAGON v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:{g, t}}}} }`: puzzles solved `g` (≥ 1) and best time `t` in ms (0 = none yet: every solve so far used a hint). Join per row: the larger epoch `b` wins; equal epochs take max `g` and the lower non-zero `t`. Rows with `b < br` drop; bad cells drop. A join (`tests/hexagon.test.js`).
- **CHESS v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[w, d, l]}}} }`: games vs the computer won / drawn / lost per level, counted from the row's epoch `b`. Per row the larger epoch wins, equal epochs take the max of every counter; rows with `b < br` drop, bad rows drop. A join (`tests/chess.test.js`).
  - Wave 50 adds the puzzle history, both omitted while empty so older data loads unchanged: `pz{puzzleId: [at, ok 0|1, fix]}` = the first attempt per puzzle (time, solved first time) and `fix` = when it was solved later (0 = never; a first-time solve has fix = at), `pbr` = the puzzle reset stamp. Merge (train.js `mergeHistory`): per id the earlier attempt wins (equal times: the failure), `fix` takes the max; entries with `at < pbr` drop; bad ids / entries drop; ids sorted (canonical). A join. The puzzle rating is not stored: Glicko-1 (start 1500 / RD 350, RD floor 60, no time decay) is replayed from the first attempts in time order against the puzzles' ratings, so every device computes the same number (`tests/chess-train.test.js`).
- **SUDOKU v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h|x|k:{t, ts, n, c}}}}, days{"<day>":{b, t, h, m}} }` (`k` = Killer, Wave 49): best time `t` in ms (0 = none yet: every solve used a hint) reached at `ts`, puzzles solved `n` (≥ 1), solved without hints `c` (≤ n; `t` > 0 needs `c` ≥ 1). Join per row: the larger epoch `b` wins; equal epochs take, per level, the lower non-zero `t` (then the earlier `ts`) and max `n`, `c`. Rows with `b < br` drop; bad cells drop. **Daily (Wave 49):** `days{"<day>":{…}}`, `day` = days since 1 Jan 2026 (local calendar day, the numbering of `gamekit/daily.js`, key 0–100000); per day key the larger `b` wins, equal `b` keeps the better result (below); entries with `b < br` drop, so `Reset records` clears the dailies too. A client from before Wave 49 drops `days` when it normalises; the next newer client's join brings them back (the per-device rows were never at risk). Sudoku day: time `t` ms (≥ 1), hints `h` (0–81), `m` = 9-bit mask of the boxes a hint touched (share grid); better = no hint first, then lower `t`, `h`, `m`. The Daily puzzle is Medium, made by `generate("m", orosDaily.random("sudoku:<YYYY-MM-DD>"), 40, orosDaily.counter())` (a counting clock instead of a time budget, so every device makes the same grid). Killer: no stored puzzle format beyond the session; `makeKiller` builds cages of 2–5 cells over a random solution, proves uniqueness with a cage-sum solver (`solveKiller`, node cap 20000) and adds a given where two solutions differ or the cap is hit (≤ 6 givens). A join (`tests/sudoku.test.js`).
- **TETRIS v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{l1|l5|l10:{n, ts, l, g}}}} }`: per start level the best score `n` reached at `ts`, the most lines `l` in one game and games played `g` (finished games). Join per key: higher `n`, then earlier `ts`; max `l`, `g`. Rows with `b < br` drop; per row the larger epoch wins. A join (`tests/tetris.test.js`).
- **MINESWEEPER v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{b|i|e:{t, ts, w, g}}}}, days{"<day>":{b, w, t, f}} }`: best winning time `t` in ms (0 = no win yet; `t` > 0 exactly when `w` > 0) reached at `ts`, games won `w` (≤ g), games finished `g` (≥ 1). Join per row: the larger epoch `b` wins; equal epochs take, per level, the lower non-zero `t` (then the earlier `ts`) and max `w`, `g`. Rows with `b < br` drop; bad cells drop. **Daily (Wave 49):** `days{"<day>":{…}}`, `day` = days since 1 Jan 2026 (local calendar day, the numbering of `gamekit/daily.js`, key 0–100000); per day key the larger `b` wins, equal `b` keeps the better result (below); entries with `b < br` drop, so `Reset records` clears the dailies too. A client from before Wave 49 drops `days` when it normalises; the next newer client's join brings them back (the per-device rows were never at risk). Minesweeper day: won `w` 0|1, time `t` ms, mines found `f` (0–40); better = a win, then lower `t`, then more `f`. One try a day (the first result on a device is kept). The Daily board is Intermediate: `dailyBoard(day)` picks a start cell in the interior and lays the mines from the seed `minesweeper:<YYYY-MM-DD>`; the start area opens for everyone. A join (`tests/minesweeper.test.js`).
- **MAHJONG v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{turtle|pyramid|fortress:{t, ts, w}}}} }`: best time `t` (ms, 1 to 100 h) reached at `ts`, wins `w` (≥ 1). Join per layout: lower `t`, then earlier `ts`; max `w`. Rows with `b < br` drop; per row the larger `b` wins. A join (`tests/mahjong.test.js`).
- **GOMOKU v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[w, l, d]}}} }`: games vs the computer won / lost / drawn per level, counted from the row's epoch `b` (each device only grows its own row). Per row the larger epoch wins, equal epochs take the max of every counter; rows with `b < br` drop, bad rows drop. 2-player games are not synced (a device-local series score in the session). A join (`tests/gomoku.test.js`).
- **BUBBLE v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{l1|l2|l3:{s, ts, g, w}}}} }`: best score `s` reached at `ts`, games played `g` (finished games only, ≥ 1), boards cleared `w` (≤ g). Join per level: higher `s`, then earlier `ts`; max `g`, `w`. Rows with `b < br` drop; per row the larger `b` wins. A join (`tests/bubble.test.js`).
- **CHECKERS v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[w, l, d]}}} }`: games vs the computer won / lost / drawn per level, counted from the row's epoch `b` (each device only grows its own row). Per row the larger epoch wins, equal epochs take the max of every counter; rows with `b < br` drop, bad rows drop. 2-player games are not synced (a device-local series score in the session). A join (`tests/checkers.test.js`).
- **MASTERMIND v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:{g, w, bt, st}}}} }`: games `g` (finished games only), wins `w` (≤ g), fewest tries in a win `bt` (1–10, 0 = no win), tries of all wins summed `st` (w ≤ st ≤ 10·w; average = Σst / Σw). Per row the larger epoch wins, equal epochs take the max of `g`, `w`, `st` and the smallest `bt` above 0; totals add the rows, best = the smallest `bt`. Rows with `b < br` drop. A join (`tests/mastermind.test.js`).
- **BATTLESHIP v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:{w, l, bs}}}} }`: wins `w`, losses `l` (w + l ≥ 1), fewest shots in a win `bs` (17–100, 0 = no win). Per row the larger epoch wins, equal epochs take the max of `w`, `l` and the smallest `bs` above 0; totals add the rows, best = the smallest `bs`. Rows with `b < br` drop. A join (`tests/battleship.test.js`).
- **RPS v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[mw, ml, rw, rd, rl, bs]}}} }`: matches won / lost, rounds won / drawn / lost and the best win streak (≤ rw) per level, counted from the row's epoch `b`. Per row the larger epoch wins, equal epochs take the max of every cell; totals add the rows, the streak takes the best row; rows with `b < br` and bad cells drop. A join (`tests/rps.test.js`).
- **HANGMAN v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{en|el:{w, l, c, m, ts}}}} }`: won `w`, lost `l` (w + l ≥ 1), current streak `c` and best streak `m` (c ≤ m ≤ w), time of the last result `ts`. Per row the larger epoch wins; equal epochs keep, per language, the later state (more games, then later `ts`, then larger `w`, `c`, `m`: a total order, so the max is a join). Totals add `w`/`l`; the shown streak is the one of the row with the latest `ts`, the best streak the max `m`. Rows with `b < br` drop. A join (`tests/hangman.test.js`).
- **FLOW v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{"5"…"9":{g, t}}}}, days{"<day>":{b, t, h, m, k}} }`: puzzles solved `g` (≥ 1) and best time `t` in ms (0 = none yet: every solve so far used a hint). Join per row: the larger epoch `b` wins; equal epochs take max `g` and the lower non-zero `t`. Rows with `b < br` drop; bad cells drop. **Daily (Wave 49):** `days{"<day>":{…}}`, `day` = days since 1 Jan 2026 (local calendar day, the numbering of `gamekit/daily.js`, key 0–100000); per day key the larger `b` wins, equal `b` keeps the better result (below); entries with `b < br` drop, so `Reset records` clears the dailies too. A client from before Wave 49 drops `days` when it normalises; the next newer client's join brings them back (the per-device rows were never at risk). Flow day: time `t` ms, lines `k`, `m` = mask of the lines a hint drew, `h` = its bit count; better = no hint, then lower `t`, `h`, `m`, `k`; the first solve of a day counts. The Daily puzzle is 7×7 from `genJob(7, orosDaily.randInt("flow:<YYYY-MM-DD>"), 0)`, unique like every Flow puzzle. A join (`tests/flow.test.js`).
- **NONOGRAM v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{n5|n10|n15:{t, ts, n, c}}}}, days{"<day>":{b, t, h, m}} }`: best time `t` in ms (0 = none yet) reached at `ts`, puzzles solved `n` (≥ 1), solved without hints `c` (≤ n; `t` > 0 needs `c` ≥ 1). Join per row: the larger epoch `b` wins; equal epochs take, per size, the lower non-zero `t` (then the earlier `ts`) and max `n`, `c`. Rows with `b < br` drop; bad cells drop. **Daily (Wave 49):** `days{"<day>":{…}}`, `day` = days since 1 Jan 2026 (local calendar day, the numbering of `gamekit/daily.js`, key 0–100000); per day key the larger `b` wins, equal `b` keeps the better result (below); entries with `b < br` drop, so `Reset records` clears the dailies too. A client from before Wave 49 drops `days` when it normalises; the next newer client's join brings them back (the per-device rows were never at risk). Nonogram day: time `t` ms, hints `h` (0–225), `m` = mask of the rows a hint touched (≤ 32767); better as Sudoku. The Daily picture is 10×10 from `makePuzzle(10, orosDaily.random("nonogram:<YYYY-MM-DD>"), 300, orosDaily.counter())`, line-solvable and unique. A join (`tests/nonogram.test.js`).
- **BREAKOUT v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{p1|p0:{n, ts, v, g}}}} }`: per mode (p1 power-ups on, p0 off) the best score `n` reached at `ts`, the best level reached `v` (1-based) and games played `g`. Join per key: higher `n`, then earlier `ts`; max `v`, `g`. Rows with `b < br` drop; per row the larger epoch wins. A join (`tests/breakout.test.js`).
- **REVERSI v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[w, l, d]}}} }`: games vs the computer won / lost / drawn per level, counted from the row's epoch `b` (each device only grows its own row). Per row the larger epoch wins, equal epochs take the max of every counter; rows with `b < br` drop, bad rows drop. 2-player games are not synced (a device-local series score in the session). A join (`tests/reversi.test.js`).
- **MANCALA v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[won, lost, drawn]}}} }`: each device only grows its own row, counted from epoch `b`. Join per row: the newer `b` wins; equal `b`: per level the per-cell max. Rows older than `br` and bad cells drop. A join (`tests/mancala.test.js`).
- **PONG v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:{w, l, m, ts}, p2:{g}}}} }`: per computer level wins `w`, losses `l` and the best winning margin `m` (0–11, set at `ts`; 0 = no win yet); `p2.g` = 2-player games played. Join per key: max `w`, `l`, `g`; higher `m`, then earlier `ts`. A cell needs `w + l ≥ 1`, and `m > 0` only with a win. Rows with `b < br` drop; per row the larger epoch wins. A join (`tests/pong.test.js`).
- **BACKGAMMON v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[won, lost, ptsWon, ptsLost]}}} }`: each device only grows its own row, counted from epoch `b`. Join per row: the newer `b` wins; equal `b`: per level the cell with more games, then more wins, ties by the max of the point counts. A cell must hold `won ≤ ptsWon ≤ 3·won` and `lost ≤ ptsLost ≤ 3·lost` or it is dropped; rows older than `br` drop. A join (`tests/backgammon.test.js`).
- **LIGHTSOUT v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:{g, p, t}}}} }`: puzzles solved `g`, perfect solves `p` (presses = par, no hint; `p ≤ g`), best time `t` in ms (0 = none yet: hinted solves count in `g` only). Per row: larger epoch wins; equal epochs take max `g`, max `p`, min non-zero `t`; rows with `b < br` drop. A join (`tests/games.test.js`).
- **SLIDER v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{n3|n4|n5:{t, m, g}}}} }`: best time `t` (ms), fewest moves `m` (two separate records, possibly from different games), solved `g`. Per row: larger epoch wins; equal epochs take min `t`, min `m`, max `g`; rows with `b < br` drop. A join (`tests/games.test.js`).
- **PET v1 — three synced slices:**
  - `pet` (oros-pet-data): `{ ver, pet{id,name,palette,birthTs,fm{field:mtime}}, lastFed, lastPetted, wokeAt/awakeE?, asleepSince/asleepE?, tombs{} }`.
    - Stats are DERIVED from anchors at render time, never stored.
    - Identity merges per field via `fm`. Temporal anchors use max-value merge, and anchor pairs travel together.
  - `petEvents` (oros-pet-events):
    - Union by event id, sorted by (ts, id), rolling trim to 100.
    - Birthday ids are deterministic: `bday-<petId>-<ymd>`.
    - `clearLog` writes a `{clearedAt}` wipe tombstone.
  - `petSettings` (oros-pet-settings): calendar-feed toggle, per-field LWW via `calFeedTs`. The legacy key oros-pet-calendar-sync is kept in lock-step as a read-only mirror for `calendar.js`.
- **NOTIFICATIONS v1:** `{ ver, settings{position,style,sound,volume}, appToggles{}, items[{id,dedupKey,ns,type,title,body,deepLink,createdAt,firedAt,readAt,expiresAt}], meta{} }`.
- **SPREADSHEET:**
  - Cells: `{"<sid>|<r>|<c>":{v,mtime,f?,fm{v,f}}}`, sparse; value and format merge separately by the per-cell field stamps `fm`; shared tombstones. `f{b,i,u,al,co,nf,bg,bd,wr,va,mr,mc}` in that canonical order; `nf` ∈ "" | "0" | "2" | "%" | "€" | "d" (date, since Wave 1 2026-10-14). Wave 2 (2026-10-14) adds `bg` (fill, `#rrggbb`), `bd` (borders, a subset of "tblr" in that order), `wr:1` (wrap), `va` ∈ t | m | b (vertical align; default bottom), and `mr`/`mc` (merge span in rows / columns on the top-left cell, ≥ 2 when present; a merge is ≤ 500 rows). The new keys come last, so a format without them keeps its exact bytes. Covered cells keep their own records (a paste or an unmerge shows them again); two devices that merge overlapping areas: the merge whose top-left cell comes first (row, then column) wins in the view, the other is ignored until unmerged.
  - Sheets: `{id,name,rows,cols,pos,mtime,cw{colIdx:px},fz?{r,c},rh?{rowIdx:px}}`, whole-sheet LWW by `mtime` (tie: smaller canonical JSON). `rh` (Wave 2, custom row heights, 18–400 px, written after `fz` only when set) syncs like `cw` and is shifted by row inserts/deletes. `fz` (frozen panes: top `r` rows, left `c` columns; `normFz`: integers, r ≤ 50 and < rows, c ≤ 26 and < cols, at least one > 0) is written after `cw` only when set, so a sheet without frozen panes keeps its exact bytes; it syncs like column widths. Size caps (Wave 1): 10,000 rows × 104 columns (A…CZ) per sheet; was 500 × 64 (import the same). Import caps follow the new limits.
  - Device-local, never synced: `oros-spreadsheet-view` `{sid:{flt:{top,l,r,cols:{c:{q,ex[]}}}}}`: the filter of each sheet (heading row, column span, per column a "contains" text and the unticked values). Deleting a sheet drops its entry.
  - Formula engine: `spreadsheet/functions.js` (`OrosSheetFx`, pure UMD, Node-tested), own code, no third-party. Recursive-descent parser with Excel precedence (unary minus binds before `^`, `^` left-associative, `%` postfix, `&`, comparisons), refs `A1`, `$A$1`, `A:A`, `1:1`, `Sheet!A1`, `'My sheet'!A1:B5`; strings with `""` (old `\"` escapes still read); `_xlfn.`/`_xlws.` prefixes dropped; dotted names (`STDEV.S`, `PERCENTILE.INC`). 213 function names incl. aliases (maths, statistics, `*IF(S)` with criteria strings and `*`/`?`/`~` wildcards, lookup VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/XMATCH/LOOKUP/INDEX/MATCH/CHOOSE/OFFSET/INDIRECT/ADDRESS, logic IF/IFS/SWITCH/IFERROR/IFNA lazily evaluated, text, date, financial; not yet named ranges or spilled dynamic arrays). **Wave 4 functions (2026-10-31, `tests/spreadsheet-wave4.test.js`, expected values = Excel's documented results):** GCD LCM FACT COMBIN PERMUT MROUND EVEN ODD QUOTIENT, trigonometry + RADIANS/DEGREES, CEILING.MATH/FLOOR.MATH, SUBTOTAL (1–11 / 101–111; counts rows the device-local filter hides, since the engine does not see the filter); AVERAGEA MAXA MINA GEOMEAN HARMEAN CORREL/PEARSON RSQ SLOPE INTERCEPT FORECAST(.LINEAR), NORM.DIST/NORM.S.DIST/NORM.INV/NORM.S.INV (+ old names; West's double-precision CDF, Acklam's inverse + one Halley step) STANDARDIZE; WEEKNUM (types 1, 2, 11–17, 21) ISOWEEKNUM YEARFRAC (bases 0–4, basis 1 as Excel: one-year span → 365/366 by Feb 29, longer → average year) DAYS360 (US / European) TIMEVALUE (h:mm[:ss] [AM/PM/πμ/μμ] or a text date-time) NETWORKDAYS.INTL / WORKDAY.INTL (weekend 1–7, 11–17 or a 7-digit Monday-first mask); TEXTBEFORE/TEXTAFTER (instance ±n, several delimiters as an array, match_mode, match_end, if_not_found) CLEAN UNICHAR UNICODE NUMBERVALUE (default separators follow the app language: EL `,` decimal `.` group) FIXED T N; IPMT PPMT CUMIPMT CUMPRINC RATE IRR XNPV XIRR MIRR SLN SYD DDB DB EFFECT NOMINAL (RATE/IRR/XIRR: Newton with a numeric slope, 100 steps, `#NUM!` when it does not settle). OFFSET and INDIRECT are lazy and get the engine (`L[name].f(nodes, cx, ev, engine)`), building a range through `Engine.box(sid, r0, c0, r1, c1, cx)`; INDIRECT takes A1 text only (the text is tokenized, never run; R1C1 → `#REF!`). Both are naturally volatile because every recalculation resets the cache. Array constants `{1,2;3,4}` (tokens `T.LB`/`T.RB`, AST node `arr`): `,` next column, `;` next row, items number (leading sign), text, TRUE/FALSE, error literal; ragged rows or a reference inside → `#ERROR!`. Before wave 4 a brace was a bad token (`#ERROR!`), so an old device shows `#ERROR!` for such a formula; the stored text is the same, nothing in sync changes. Blank cells are 0 in arithmetic, "" in text, left out of AVERAGE/COUNT ranges. Errors are values (`#DIV/0!`, `#N/A`, `#NAME?`, `#REF!`, `#VALUE!`, `#NUM!`, `#CYC!`, `#ERROR!`) that functions such as IFERROR/ISERROR see. A deep dependency chain is warmed in row order, so long chains do not overflow the stack. Function help (EN/EL one-liners) for the fx box and the function list.
    - **[fixed 2026-10-10]** Binary operators (`=1+1`) and plain ranges (`=SUM(A1:A5)`) returned `#ERROR!`. **[fixed 2026-10-14, Wave 1]** unary minus (`=-A1`). `tests/spreadsheet-formula.test.js`, `tests/spreadsheet-functions.test.js`, `tests/spreadsheet-sync.test.js`.
  - Dates are Excel serial numbers (days since 1899-12-30, UTC arithmetic, so a time-zone change never shifts a date). Format `nf:"d"` shows EN `yyyy-mm-dd`, EL `dd/mm/yyyy`; a formula whose outermost function is TODAY/DATE/EDATE/EOMONTH/DATEVALUE/WORKDAY shows as a date without a format, NOW with the time. **Decision:** a typed date (`14/10/2026`, `2026-10-14`) stays text as typed (no silent conversion of stored data, nothing changes on old devices); date functions and comparisons read text dates (day first, ISO) when they need a number.
  - Sort (A→Z / Z→A) rewrites the selection's rows as one undo step; a first row that looks like a heading stays put; formulas in moved rows are shifted by their row offset. Insert/Delete rows and columns rewrite every reference in every sheet (`FX.adjustFormula`: refs into deleted cells → `#REF!`), shift `cw` and `fz`, one undo step. A structural edit is ordinary cell writes (new `fm` stamps), so a concurrent edit on another device to a moved cell lands at the old position (accepted; documented in help).
  - Charts and conditional formatting (Wave 2): top-level maps `charts{id:{id,sid,mtime,t,src,by?,ttl?,xl?,yl?,lg,co?[],at{r,c,x,y},w,h}}` (t ∈ col | bar | line | pie | donut | scatter; `src` an A1 range on sheet `sid`; anchored to cell `at` plus a pixel offset) and `cf{id:{id,sid,mtime,pos,rg,k,a?,b?,n?,st?{bg,co,b},cs?[2–3 colours],db?}}` (k ∈ gt | lt | bt | eq | tx | top | bot | dup | cs | db; lower `pos` = higher priority, first matching style rule wins; colour scale and data bar paint under it). Normalised by `OrosSheetKit.normChart` / `normCf` (fixed key order). Each record is LWW by its own `mtime` (tie: smaller canonical JSON); delete = tombstone `deleted["ch:"+id]` / `deleted["cf:"+id]`, delete wins a tie, a newer edit resurrects. `canonSS` drops records older than their tombstone or whose sheet is gone, and writes the `charts` / `cf` keys only when non-empty, so a workbook without them keeps its exact bytes. Structural inserts/deletes shift `src` / `rg` (`KIT.adjRange`: they grow with an insert inside, shrink with a delete; a rule whose whole range is deleted is deleted, a chart gets `#REF!`) and chart anchors, in the same undo step.
    - **Decision (charts as floating objects, records of their own):** charts float over the grid in `#ch-layer` (inside `#grid-wrap`, under the sticky headers and frozen panes), positioned from `COLLEFT` and the row offsets, so they move with scrolling and stay put independent of which rows are rendered; selected → move by drag, resize by the corner, edit / PNG / SVG / delete. Chosen over a side panel because it is what Excel and Sheets users expect and a panel costs a phone its grid. They (and the rules) are top-level records, not fields of the sheet, because the sheet is whole-entity LWW: an older device rewriting the sheet (rename, a column width) would otherwise wipe every chart; as separate records the old device simply doesn't know them and can't overwrite them.
    - Charts: own SVG (`KIT.chartSVG`, no library), data model `KIT.chartModel` (first text row / column = names / categories, series in columns when the range is taller than wide, ≤ 8 series × 1000 points; pie folds slices after the 8th into "Other"), theme palette read from the shell's tokens (categorical order of the dataviz reference palette, light and dark steps; bars ≤ 24 px with 4 px rounded ends, 2 px lines, hairline grid, legend only for 2+ series, `<title>` tooltips). Rows hidden by the device-local filter are left out. Re-rendered on every recalculation and palette change. PNG via canvas at 2×, SVG as the file; both through `orosDialog.saveFile` when in the shell.
  - **Wave 4.2 (2026-10-31, `tests/spreadsheet-wave4-2.test.js`).** Chart `t` gains `area`; chart options `cb:1` (combo: last series as a line over columns; col only), `ln:1` (dashed least-squares trend line, `KIT.trendFit`; col/line/area/scatter), `sk:1` (stacked; col/bar/area: positives up, negatives down, an area on the running total) are kept by `normChart` only where `KIT.CH_OPT` allows them and written right after `t`. Rule kinds `fx` (formula, `a` = a formula written for the top-left cell, shifted per cell with `FX.shiftFormula` and run by the sheet's own engine; TRUE or a non-zero number hits; blank cells count; cached per recalculation in `CFST`) and `ic` (icon set `is` ∈ ar | dt, thirds of min…max; the glyph is a `span.cfi` built with textContent). Top-level `calc {it, n, d, mtime}` (`KIT.normCalc`, n 1–1000 default 100, d > 0 default 0.001; LWW through `newerObj`, kept also when turned off so the off wins; written by canonSS only once set): the engine's `setIter` + `settle()` (run in `resetEval`) re-evaluate all formula cells while a cycle was met, each round reading a cell in a cycle from the last round (`prev`, which survives `reset()`, so the next recalculation starts from the settled values as in Excel); off → `#CYC!` as before. The Assistant's own engine copy (`commands.js`) does not iterate.
    - **Decision (mixed versions, checked against the real 4.73.00 `sheetkit.js` + `mergeState`):** a 4.73.00 device turns `area` into `col`, drops `cb`/`ln`/`sk`, drops `fx`/`ic` rules and `calc`. On an equal `mtime`, `newerObj` keeps the smaller canonical JSON: `"area"` < `"col"`, and every new chart key sorts before `"src"`, so the new copy is smaller and wins; dropped rules and `calc` are simply missing on the old side, so the union keeps them. The round trip new → old → merge on new is byte-identical in both orders. **Accepted loss:** editing such a chart on the old device (move, resize, rename) writes a newer copy without the new type/options. Documented in help Limits.
  - **Wave 4.3 print / PDF (2026-11-01, `tests/spreadsheet-wave4-3.test.js`).** No sync or data-model change: settings `{pa a4|a3|letter|legal, or p|l, fit w|p|n, hr 0–5 (max 50 in `normPrint`), gl, pn, ch, sel}` live only in the device key `oros-spreadsheet-print`. `KIT.printPages` (pure) plans pages in pt (1 px = 0.75 pt, margins 36 pt, footer 18 pt): fit `w` scales down to the page width only, `p` to one page, `n` 1:1; column bands × row bands, down then over; repeated rows 1…hr are taken out of the body and drawn on top of every page; an oversize column/row gets a page of its own. spreadsheet.js section 3j draws it with jsPDF and Noto Sans Regular/Bold/Italic/BoldItalic (precached vendor files, loaded on first use, text as Identity-H text so Greek is real text): fills, data bars, icon-set glyphs as vector shapes (Noto has no arrows), gridlines (not inside merges), left text running on over empty cells, wrap with the cell's vertical alignment, `#` for a number too wide, borders, merges (the visible part on each page), charts as PNG (light palette) on the page of their anchor cell (a chart anchored in a repeated row prints once, on the first page of its column band), footer sheet name + `Page n of t`. Used area = `sheetExtent` + merges + chart ends; filtered rows are skipped. Print = the same PDF in a hidden iframe → `print()` (new tab if refused). Ctrl+P on the grid opens the dialog.
  - **Wave 4.4 range selection on touch (2026-11-01, `tests/spreadsheet-wave4-4.test.js`).** No data change. With a touch or pen pointer (last `pointerdown`, else `(pointer: coarse)`) two round handles `.rg-h` sit on the selection's top-left and bottom-right corners (hidden while editing, with a chart selected, or off the visible grid); dragging one anchors the opposite corner (`KIT.handleGrab`) and moves the grabbed one under the finger (`KIT.handleMove`; a whole-column selection keeps its rows, a whole-row one its columns), with edge auto-scroll. On touch the fill handle moves just outside the bottom-right corner (16 px diagonally), so neither covers the cells. `Extend selection` (sheet menu, was the one-shot "Select a range…") is now a mode: each tap on a cell or header grows the selection from the anchor (handled in mousedown too, which on touch used to collapse the anchor first, so the old one-shot never worked on a phone); a floating `Extending ✕` chip above the sheet tabs, Esc or starting an edit ends it. Header taps already selected whole columns/rows. Mouse behaviour is unchanged.
  - Fill handle (`KIT.fillSeries`): numbers continue by linear trend (a single number copies; Ctrl counts), date-formatted numbers and text dates (ISO, d/m/y) by their step, weekday and month lists in EN and EL (full, short, Greek genitive months; the case of the first entry is kept), "text + number" (zero padding kept); formulas copy with shifted references; formats come along; merges are not copied. Mouse and touch (pointer events, autoscroll at the edges).
  - Clipboard: copy writes `text/plain` (TSV, values as shown; CRLF-free, quotes for tabs/newlines) and `text/html` (a `<table>` with inline styles for bold/italic/underline/colour/fill/alignment and colspan/rowspan) through the native copy event (toolbar: `execCommand("copy")`). Paste reads `text/html` first (`KIT.parseHTMLTable`: own regex tokenizer, never `innerHTML`, `<script>`/`<style>` content dropped except class rules from `<style>` for Excel's classes, entities decoded, white fill / black text ignored, `th` → bold, colspan/rowspan → merges), else TSV / plain text. A paste whose text equals the internal clipboard's TSV uses the internal clipboard (formulas shift, all formats). Values from outside go through `KIT.pasteValue` (trims, reads EN/EL thousands and decimal separators); a text starting with `=` becomes a formula of the app's own engine, as in Excel (never script, never HTML).
  - Touch: long-press (420 ms) then drag selects a range; long-press without moving opens the sheet menu; "Select a range…" in the sheet menu (tap the last cell); header edges (16 px hit zone) resize columns and rows.
  - Rendering: rows are virtual (variable row heights via a prefix-offset table `OFF`, binary search; ~30 rows buffer, spacer rows), frozen rows/columns are sticky; merges are drawn with rowSpan/colSpan on the rendered rows; turning wrap on measures the selected rows (the first 300) and sets each one that needs more than the default height to fit; a later text change does not refit.
  - Mixed versions (checked with the pre-Wave-1 merge code): a device still on the version before Wave 1 strips `fz` and `nf:"d"` (and shows at most 500 rows / 64 columns; cells beyond are kept). New devices keep both (on an equal stamp the copy with the field is the smaller JSON and wins), so nothing is lost, but while such a device syncs, a sheet with frozen panes or a cell with the date format is re-uploaded on each sync interval, the same transient as Timesheet Wave 6. It stops when that device updates; sheets without either field are byte-identical and quiet.
  - Mixed versions, Wave 2 (Wave 1 device = 1.98.00 code): it strips the top-level `charts` / `cf`, the sheet's `rh` and the cell `f` keys `bg bd wr va mr mc` (its `canonSS` keeps only what it knows). Merge on the new device unions the records and keeps the fields (`tests/spreadsheet-wave2.test.js`, "a copy stripped by an older version loses nothing"), so the same transient re-upload ping-pong as above runs while both sync, and ends when the old device updates. **Accepted losses** (documented in help Limits): setting a format on a cell on the old device writes a newer `fm.f` without the new keys (that cell loses fill/borders/wrap/merge); changing a sheet there (rename, column width, freeze) writes a newer sheet without `rh`. Charts and rules cannot be lost that way. The old device shows none of it (merged areas show as separate cells).
- **RADIO v1:** `{ ver, favorites[{stationuuid,…,mtime}], deleted{} }` — union by stationuuid (Dice pattern).
  - W42 (same `ver`, additive): optional `wake{alarmId: {m, st}}` = which station a Time alarm (`oros-time-data` alarm id) plays; `st` = `{stationuuid, name, url_resolved, favicon, codec, bitrate, country, countrycode}` or `null` (tombstone). Merge `OrosRadioTools.mergeWake`: per id LWW by `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON; ≤ 50 rows (newest kept); tombstones dropped 90 days after the newest row. Omitted when empty, so old data loads unchanged; an older client writes the slice without `wake`, and the next merge on a newer client takes the union back (`mergeWake(remote, local)`). `radio/tools.js` (pure helpers + engine, loaded by the app and injected into the shell window as `window.__orosRadioEngine`): ICY peek (`Icy-MetaData: 1`, first 64 KB, every 30 s while playing) then Icecast `status-json.xsl`, else no titles (radio-browser has no now-playing API); recording = a second `fetch` of the stream copied to `/internal/Radio/YYYY-MM-DD HH.MM <name>.<ext>` via `orosFS.write`, cap 200 MB / 4 h, HLS refused (captureStream is silent for cross-origin media, so not used); both need CORS. Sleep timer fades the volume out over the last minute (volume restored after the pause). Shell `alarmTick` → `alarmRadio(due)` (desktop only, beside `alarmNotify`): reads `oros-radio-data`.wake[id].st, plays it through the engine with a fade-in, else stages `oros-radio-wake` + `__orosOpenRadio(uuid)`. Tests `tests/radio-tools.test.js`.
  - RX-HTTPS (2026-10-14): streams are only ever loaded over https. `secureStreamUrl` (radio.js) picks an https candidate (`url_resolved`, then `url`) or upgrades `http://` to `https://`; `normalizeStation` and `host.api.play` both apply it, so stored favorites / recents / wake rows with http addresses are upgraded at play time (stored data is not rewritten, so sync is untouched). ICY, Icecast and recording read `host.current`, so they use the https address too. A station that only answers over http fails with `err.insecure`. Why: an http stream is mixed content, the page loses its secure state, and the installed app (PWA / Android TWA) then shows the browser's address bar. Tests `tests/radio-https.test.js`.
- **MINIMALISM:** day records + `prefs{remindHour}`. Reminder logic is shell-side (`minimalismCheckTick` reads the slice directly, so it works with the app closed).
- **MINDMAP v1:** `{ ver, maps[{id,m,sides:"both"|"right"}], nodes[{id,m,map,parent,ord,text,emoji,color,note,url,done}], links[{id,m,map,from,to,label}], pos[{id,m,map,dx,dy}], imgs[{id,m,map,src,w,h}], tombs{} }`. Central node id = `<mapId>-r` (parent ""), its text is the map title. `color` ∈ LABEL_COLORS keys or "" (auto per main branch). `url` http(s) only. Nodes of a deleted map are dropped by the merge. A node whose parent is missing, and the smallest id of a parent loop (two devices moving nodes at once), hang from the centre flagged "recovered" (dashed) — deterministic, nothing written. **Phase 2 (v1.1.0):** cross-links, free-placement offsets and pictures are NEW collections, never new node fields (older code rebuilds nodes from known fields and, on an equal-m tie, its shorter row would win the canonical comparison and drop new fields; unknown collections it just leaves out and newer devices keep them by union). `pos` / `imgs` rows use their node's id, so the node's tombstone removes them; they are never tombstoned themselves: a reset is `dx = dy = 0`, a removal is `src ""` (so it wins over the older row elsewhere). `pos` = offset in px (|v| ≤ 100000) from the automatic place, summed down the tree (a moved node carries its branch); never on the centre. `imgs.src` = `data:image/(jpeg|png|webp);base64,…` ≤ 40,000 chars, w/h ≤ 640, all pictures ≤ 1.4M chars (checked when added); the app re-encodes every picture as JPEG on a canvas. `links`: from ≠ to, both live nodes of the same map, label ≤ 200 chars, ≤ 5,000 per slice.
- **TIMESHEET v1:** `{ ver, clients[{id,name,rate,m}|tomb], projects[{id,name,client,color,rate,bill,arch,m}|tomb], entries[{id,p,desc,s,e,billed,m}|tomb], prefs{cur,rate,goal,round,rup}, pm }`. Rates are integer cents per hour, 0 = inherit (project → client → default). `s`/`e` are ms epoch; `e = 0` = running; days are derived in local time and an entry crossing midnight is split per day at render. Rounding (prefs.round minutes, rup up/nearest) is applied per day piece in reports and CSV only, never stored. Deleting a project with entries or a client with projects is refused (archive instead). No tombstone pruning.
  - Wave 6 (tasks, tags, budgets): entries may carry `task` (text ≤ 80) and `tags` (≤ 10 tags of ≤ 30 chars, "#" dropped, unique regardless of case, sorted), projects `budget` (minutes, 1…6 000 000); each is written only when set, so records without one stay byte-identical. **Forward compatibility:** a flat field this version does not know (name `[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}`, value string ≤ 500 / finite number / boolean, at most 16, sorted by name) rides along on clients, projects and entries, and in-place edits keep it. Devices still on a version before Wave 6 strip the new fields: until such a device updates itself, an entry with a task/tags is re-uploaded on its sync interval (no data loss; the newer record wins on equal m by the larger JSON). Reports: filter `tag` ("" all, "-" untagged), group `task` (per project + task, case-insensitive) and `tag` (an entry counts under each tag; the total once). CSV export adds Task and Tags columns after Description; the import fills `task`/`tags` from the Task/Tags columns (ids still hash the joined text, so Wave 5 imports match).
  - Wave 7 (BR-TS-POMO, Time Pomodoro → Timesheet): Time never writes `oros-timesheet-data`. When a Focus leg starts with "Log focus in Timesheet" set (device-local `oros-time-pmlog`: "" off, "-" no project, else a project id; archived/deleted → off), Time puts `{s, e (planned end), p}` in the device-local, never-synced inbox `oros-timesheet-inbox` (`core.INBOX_KEY`; ≤ 200 legs, ≤ 64 KB, one per start, ≤ 3 h); a stop by hand moves `e` to now, or drops a leg under a minute (`inboxEnd`); the start and a `logged` flag ride in `oros-time-pmrun`. Timesheet (boot, every 15 s while visible, visibility, `storage` event) turns legs whose `e` has passed into entries `{id: "pomo"+hash(s), task: "Pomodoro", p (cleared if the project is gone)}` via `mergeTimesheet`, re-reads the inbox and removes the logged legs. So a leg is logged even if Time is never reopened; ids make it once-only. time/index.html loads ../timesheet/core.js.
  - CSV import (0.60.06, #138, Toggl / Clockify / Harvest): imported records get deterministic ids from a hash of the row: entries `imp…` (Harvest: day + hours + text), new projects `impp…`, new clients `impc…` (existing ones matched by name, case-insensitive), so the same file imported on two devices converges and re-imports add nothing. Imported entries carry `m = 1`, so any later edit or tombstone wins. The import is one `mergeTimesheet(data, plan.add)`; no schema change.
  - Minimum charge, day rate, overtime and extra charges (Chris 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-24, thread "Ελάχιστη χρέωση και έξοδα στο Timesheet"): a client **or a project** may carry the billing fields `minH` (minimum hours, minutes 1…44 640), `minAmt` (minimum amount per period in cents, e.g. a day rate), `otH` (overtime after these hours, minutes; 0 = after `minH`, none without it), `minPer` (`d` day worked | `w` | `m`, default `d`) and `otRate` (cents per hour, 0 = the usual rate; kept only with `minH` or `otH`); all are written only when `minH`, `minAmt` or `otH` is set (`normBilling`), so records without them stay byte-identical, and older versions keep them as forward-compatible extras. A project's own fields make its periods its own; a client's cover all its projects without their own, together (`billingOf`). A project with its own `minAmt` charges time only at its own hourly rate (`chargeRate`: nothing inherited, so rate 0 = the day rate and overtime alone). New top-level list `extras[{id, d (YYYY-MM-DD), p, c, desc (≤ 200), amt (cents 1…100 000 000), billed, m}|tomb]` (fuel, work away, …): `p` a project (its client follows it) or `c` a client alone; merged like the other lists (per id LWW by `m`, tombstone wins ties, then the larger JSON) and **written only when it holds a record**, so data without extra charges serializes exactly as before (no re-upload on update). A device still on the version before this strips `extras` (like Wave 6's fields): it re-uploads without them, the new device's merge keeps them, bounded until that device updates. Nothing is stored about minimums or overtime: `core.chargedPieces` derives them at report time from the filtered, rounded billable pieces in time order, per billing owner and period (day = the piece's local day, week = Monday–Sunday, month); a period counts only when it lies wholly inside the report range (else `partial`, no minimum and no overtime), a period without work charges nothing; time past `otH` (else `minH`) is overtime at `otRate`; when the time up to that limit is charged less than the minimum (`minH` × the rate of the period's last piece, or `minAmt`, whichever is more) a top-up charges the difference (counted under the last piece's group; `ms` > 0 only when the hours decided it). `report` totals: `amount` = time (overtime included) + top-ups + extra charges, with `minMs/minAmount/minN`, `otMs/otAmount`, `exAmount/exN`, `exIds`, `tops`, `partial`. Extra charges have no tags and are always billable (a tag filter or "non-billable" leaves them out). CSV / sheet: piece rows (amount with overtime), then a "Minimum charge" row per top-up and an "Extra charge: …" row per extra (no times). Quote / invoice lines (`quoteLines`): hours per project at its rate, an "Overtime" line per project, a "Minimum charge · project or client" line per owner and rate (hours) or per owner and amount (quantity = periods), no zero-price hours line for a day-rate project, one line per extra charge (quantity 1). The `.oroshours` file carries `extras` too (`package.js`). Tests: `tests/timesheet-charges.test.js`.
- **SPLIT v1** (slice `split`, key `oros-split-data`):
  - `groups[]`: `{id, m, n, col 0–8, cur (16 ISO codes), arch 0|1}`.
  - `people[]`: `{id "<gid>.<own>", m, n}`.
  - `exp[]`: `{id "<gid>.<own>", m, t, a (cents), d, c ∈ food|groc|stay|trans|bills|fun|other, by {person: cents} (sum = a), mode eq|ex|sh|pc, w {person: weight} (eq 1; sh 1–1000; pc hundredths, sum 10000; ex cents, sum a), n}`.
  - `pay[]`: `{id "<gid>.<own>", m, f, to, a, d}`.
  - `mine[]`: `{id gid, m, v person|""}`: who I am per group. Travels in the user's own sync, NEVER in a group file.
  - `tombs`: `grp:<gid>`, `per:|exp:|pay:|rec:<gid>.<own>`.
  - Shares are derived (`sharesOf` → `allot`): floor(a·w/W), leftover cents to the largest remainders, ties by person id (BigInt past 2^53). Balances and settle-up suggestions are derived, never stored (R27).
  - **Wave 28 (multi-currency, items, repeating, receipt photos).** Optional expense fields, each written only when set (an old expense stays byte-identical and "equal split" stays `mode eq`):
    - `fx {c (ISO 3 letters), a (cents in c), r (1 c = r group currency, 6 significant digits), s "ecb"|"man", d? (ECB rate date), by? {person: cents in c} (several payers), w? {person: cents in c} (exact amounts)}`. `a = round(fx.a·r)`; `by` / `w` are `allot(fx.by / fx.w, a)`. `normFx` drops the whole `fx` (never the expense) when any of this does not hold, so the stored group-currency numbers are the only ones balances read and never change when rates move.
    - `it {l [{n ≤ 40, a cents, p [person…] sorted}] ≤ 60, x tax, tp tip}` on `mode ex` only. `itemShares`: each item shared equally by its people, the odd cents rotating from item to item (`allot(…, rot = item index)`); tax + tip allotted in proportion to the item subtotals. `w` must equal `itemShares(it)` (converted with `allot` when `fx`), else `it` is dropped. The dialog's "Items" mode is stored as `ex`, so older versions read the right shares.
    - `ph` receipt photo file name `yyyymmdd-<gid>-<own>-<rand>.jpg` (`PH_RE`) under `/internal/Split/Receipts` via `window.parent.orosFS` (Garage pattern: canvas re-encode ≤ 1600 px JPEG 0.8, no EXIF; written on pick, removed if the dialog is cancelled; removed 12 s after a delete (8 s Undo) or a group delete when no expense points at it). One per expense. Travels in group files as a name only (friends see "Not on this device").
    - `r` the rule that made the expense.
  - `rec[]` (written only when non-empty, so slices without repeating expenses stay byte-identical to v1.98): rule = an expense (no `ph` / `r`) + `f w|m|y` + `u?` (last date ≥ d). `nthDate`: weekly +7 days, monthly/yearly keep the first date's day clamped to the month's end (Budget's rule). `dueOccurrences(data, today)` (boot, day change, after a pull, after saving a series) adds occurrences up to today as ordinary expenses: id `<gid>.<first 15 of the rule's own id><yyyymmdd>`, `m` = the rule's `m`, so two devices (or two friends with the group file) make identical records. Any `exp:` tombstone for that id stops it from being made again, even after the rule is edited. Archived groups make none; ≤ 400 per rule per pass; ≤ 50 rules per group. Editing a rule changes later occurrences only; "Stop repeating" tombstones the rule, past expenses stay. Rules travel in group files with their `rec:` tombstones.
  - **Merge tie rule (wave 28):** on equal `m`, the record with MORE top-level fields wins, then the larger canonical JSON (old rule). An older version strips the new optional fields without a new stamp; its copy must never win the tie (lexically `"n":""}` beats `"n":"",…`). Records of one version have the same fields, so for them nothing changes. Known limit, as Timesheet Wave 6: a device still on an older version strips `fx` / `it` / `ph` / `r` / `rec` and re-uploads until it updates (no loss on newer devices); if it EDITS such an expense, the newer stamp wins and the expense becomes a plain group-currency one (balances unchanged).
  - Rates: Split reads Units' device-local cache `oros-units-rates` and fetches with the one shared helper `UnitsCore.fetchLatest(fetch)` (units/core.js, also used by Units; `crossRate`, `CURRENCY_ORDER` exported too); split/index.html loads `../units/core.js`. Fetched only when a foreign currency is picked and the cache is older than 6 h, or on "Update rates". Offline: the last cached rates, or a rate typed by hand. Latest rates, not the expense date's.
  - CSV adds Original amount / Original currency / Rate columns; the PDF list shows the original amount in brackets.
  - Group file `{app:"oros-split-group", ver:1, data}`: one group, its children and only the tombstones with its prefix. `unpackGroup` keeps only that prefix, so a file can never touch another group or `mine`. Import = merge (idempotent); importing a group you deleted brings it back (re-stamped). Backup `{app:"oros-split"}` = whole slice, restore = merge.
  - "From Contacts" / "From a trip" in the group dialog read `oros-contacts-data` and `oros-travel-data` read-only (`contactNames`, `tripChoices`): only names (and an empty group name) are copied into the draft; deleted contacts/trips are skipped; nothing is written to those apps. "Send my share to Budget" uses BR-B1 (`src:"split"`).
  - Receiver BR-SPLIT-NEW (wave 31): `__orosOpenAt("split", { newGroup: { name, cur, people[], from } })` opens the NEW group dialog prefilled (`newGroupFrom` → `groupDialog(null, pre)`): name and people pass `normText` with the usual lengths, duplicates (case-insensitive) dropped, at most MAX_PEOPLE, an unknown currency falls back to the usual default. A prefill, not data: nothing is written until Save; ignored while another dialog is open. Split's data rules are unchanged.
- **TRAVEL v1** (slice `travel`, key `oros-travel-data`): `{ ver: 1, trips: [{ id, name, dest, start, end, people, notes, cur, bplan, geo, f, pack: [{ id, name, qty, rule, grp, who, note, done, f }], plan: [{ id, kind, title, day, t1, day2, t2, place, from, to, ref, note, pos, num, prov, cost, ccur, geo, geo0, f }], docs: [{ id, of, file, name, f }], spend: [{ id, cat, amt, cur, day, what, who, f }], jrnl: [{ id, day, text, trk, f }] }], tpls: [{ id, m, name, items } | { id, m, seed: 1 }], tombs: { <id>: ms } }`. `mergeTravel`:
  - Trips, packing items, itinerary entries, attachments, expenses and journal days carry one stamp per field in `f` (the To-Do pattern): the newer stamp wins each field, equal stamps → larger JSON; the five lists (`LISTS` = pack, plan, docs, spend, jrnl) are unioned per trip.
  - Wave 31 fields (all optional; an old trip or entry loads with the defaults and is not re-stamped, so nothing uploads by itself): trip `cur` (one of 16 ISO codes, "" = EUR), `bplan` `{transport|stay|food|fun|shop|other: cents}` (planned budget, fixed key order), `geo` `{lat, lon}` (destination point, 6 decimals) or null. Entry `kind` adds `rental` and `ticket`; `num` ≤ 20, `prov` ≤ 60, `cost` cents (integer ≥ 0), `ccur` ("" = the trip's), `geo` (the place / arrival point) and `geo0` (the departure point of a journey), set only by "Find on the map" or kept from a saved point; editing the text the point came from clears it.
  - `docs`: one attachment `{of: <entry id | journal day id>, file: "<id>.pdf|jpg", name}`; the file is `/internal/Travel/<file>` on the orOS disk (`FILE_RE` checked; ≤ 300 per trip, ≤ 10 per entry, ≤ 24 photos per journal day). PDFs must start with `%PDF-`; photos are re-encoded on a canvas to JPEG (≤ 1600 px, quality 0.82), which drops EXIF/GPS. Deleting an entry tombstones its docs (Undo restores them); a file no doc refers to is removed from disk 12 s later (after the Undo window). A doc whose file has not arrived yet shows "Not on this device yet".
  - `spend`: `{cat ∈ BUD_CATS, amt cents > 0, cur, day, what ≤ 80, who}` (≤ 1000 per trip). Budget totals are derived (`budget(trip)`): planned per category vs expenses plus entries with a price (kind → category via `KIND_CAT`), in the trip's currency; other currencies are listed apart, never converted.
  - `jrnl`: one per day, id `"j" + yyyymmdd + "-" + tripId` (deterministic, so two devices writing the same day merge into one record), `text` ≤ 5000, `trk` = a Maps track id (`oros-maps-tracks-data`, read-only; a sketch from its `prev` polyline) or "".
  - Templates: whole-entity LWW by `m` (equal `m`: larger canonical JSON); a hidden ready template is `{ id, m, seed: 1 }`.
  - Tombstones max-merged; an entity is dropped when its tomb ≥ its newest field stamp (delete wins ties, a newer edit resurrects). Tombs older than 180 days before the newest stamp in the data are pruned, except those of ready templates (R26, R27).
- **CHORES v1:** (pure logic in `chores/core.js` since 0.57.04, also loaded by the shell and Calendar: `readPrefs`, `summary`, `feedRows`)
  - Slice `chores` (oros-chores-data): `{ ver, members[{id, m, name ≤ 30, color 0–7 (LABEL_COLORS), icon, away: null | [ymd, ymd], order, om}] by id, tasks[{id, m, name ≤ 50, icon, freq {k: d | n (n 2–30) | wd (d: 0–6, Monday = 0) | w | mo}, weight 1–3, mode rr | bal | spin, who[] (empty = everyone), start ymd, off}] by id, done{"<taskId>|<ymd>": [0 undone | 1 done | 2 skipped, by, m]}, set{"<taskId>|<ymd>": [memberId | "", m]}, tombs{} }`. ≤ 12 members, ≤ 40 chores (UI caps).
  - The assignment is COMPUTED, never stored: rr = pool[(k + off) mod n] skipping members away on the occurrence's first day; bal = fewest done points in the 28 days before the occurrence, chores of the same day in id order, ties follow the turn; spin = nobody until a `set` event. A `set` event (hand-over or spin result) wins over the mode for that one occurrence. `off` is fixed at creation (count of chores of the same kind) so chores made together spread over the members (`tests/chores.test.js`).
- **MEALS v1** (slice `meals`, key `oros-meals-data`): `{ ver: 1, rc: [{ id, m, t, e, c, sv, pt, ct, dt, tg, ig, st, no, src, fv }], pl: { "2026-10-09|<slot>": { m, it } }, ck: { "2026-10-09|<ing>": { v, m } }, mn: [{ id, m, w, t, d }], ai: { <ing>: { a, m } }, pn: { <ing>: { v, m, n? } }, set: { m, dt, sl, nm, ws }, tombs: { <id>: m } }`. Merge is `mergeMeals` in `meals/core.js`:
  - `rc` (recipes) and `mn` (manual shopping items): LWW per id by `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON; tombstones max-merged, a tomb at or after `m` wins (R17). Recipe tombstones are never pruned, so a deleted ready recipe stays deleted.
  - `pl` (plan cells), `ck` (ticks), `ai` (aisle), `pn` (pantry): LWW per key; a cleared cell or un-ticked box is a newer entry, not a removal. `set`: LWW as a whole.
  - Plan days, ticks, manual items and their tombs more than 400 days (`KEEP_DAYS`) before the newest day in the data are dropped inside the merge (data-relative, order-independent).
  - **Wave 2 (additive, `ver` stays 1):** a recipe may carry `img` (the picture's http(s) address from an import, ≤ 500; a link only, never loaded by the app) and an ingredient `q0` (lower end of a range, only when below `q`; `q` stays the upper end, so older code and the shopping list read the range as its upper end). Both keys are present only when set, so older recipes keep their exact canonical JSON. New units `oz`, `lb` (mass) and `floz` (vol) add up with g / ml in the shopping list; new aisle `household` (before `other`). An older client drops these on its own normalise but never uploads on a pull (R6), so they survive until it edits that recipe / choice.
  - **Units shown** (`convertQty`, `convertTemps`, `fmtIngQty(ing, lang, factor, sys)`, `buildShop(…, sys)`): `sys` "" as written, "metric" (oz/lb → g/kg, fl oz/cup → ml/l, spoons stay, °F → °C) or "us" (g/kg → oz/lb, ml/l → tsp/tbsp/cup, °C → °F); cup 240 ml, spoons 5 / 15 ml; temperatures rounded to 5°, a step that already gives both scales is left alone. Device-local (`oros-meals-prefs.un`), never synced. As written, a shopping amount made only of US units stays in US units.
  - **Sections:** `lookup` checks modifier words first ("frozen", "κατεψυγμένο…" → frozen; "canned", "κονσέρβα" → pantry), then known phrases anywhere in the name ("baking paper", "χαρτί κουζίνας"), then single words. The user's choice per ingredient key is `ai` (synced, as before).
  - **Import (`meals/import.js`, `OrosMealsImport`, loaded on demand):** web page → schema.org Recipe from `script[type=application/ld+json]` only (DOMParser into an inert document; nothing from the page is run, shown or loaded; a text scan in Node), also in `@graph`, arrays, nested nodes, `@type` arrays; HowToSection (its name prefixes its first step) / HowToStep / ItemList; ISO 8601 durations (cook = total − prep when only total is given); recipeYield in any shape; image/url as links; recipeCategory → course, cuisine + keywords → tags, suitableForDiet → diets; every string to plain text (tags dropped, entities decoded). Paprika (`.paprikarecipes` = ZIP of gzipped JSON; `.paprikarecipe` = one gzip; `DecompressionStream("gzip")`), Mealie (recipe JSON, structured ingredients via originalText / display / quantity + unit + food + note) and Tandoor (recipe.json, also one ZIP per recipe inside the export ZIP, one level) via the shared `atelier/zip.js`. Limits: 40 MB per file, 8 MB per inflated entry, 500 recipes. One draft opens in the editor (nothing saved before Save); several in a tick list (titles already present start unticked).
  - **Wave 3: pantry + nutrition (additive, `ver` stays 1).** Two new top-level keys, present (empty) in every canonical blob:
    - `pa: [{ id: "pa-<4–36 [a-z0-9]>", m, n ≤ 60, q: number | null ("some"), u: unit id | "" (only with q), l: "fridge"|"freezer"|"cupboard", bb: ymd | "", bc: 6–14 digits | "" }]` (≤ 1000): LWW per id by `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON; tombs in the shared `tombs` (a tomb at or after `m` wins, R17); pantry tombs more than 180 days before the newest pantry stamp (item `m` or pantry tomb) are pruned in the merge (data-relative, R26/R27). Undo re-writes the old copy with `m` = tomb + 1.
    - `nu: { <ingredient key>: { m, s: "tbl", t: row id } | { m, s: "off", c: barcode | "", nm ≤ 80, k ≤ 1000, p, cb, f ≤ 100 (per 100 g, one decimal) } | { m, s: "x" } , g?: grams in one piece }`: the user's confirmed nutrition match per ingredient key, LWW per key. A barcode-added product writes its values for its own name's key only when that key has no match yet.
    - A tick may carry `p: 1` and a manual item `p: 1` (only when set, so older blobs keep their canonical JSON): that shopping line was put in the pantry, so "Ticked to pantry" never adds it twice. An older client drops `pa`, `nu` and `p` on its own normalise but never uploads on a pull (R6); its next own edit uploads a blob without them, and the newer client's merge (union) keeps its own.
    - **`meals/pantry.js` (`OrosMealsPantry`, pure; also loaded by the shell):** `matches` (same key; or one name's words all inside the other's when the nutrition table does not put them on different rows: "feta" ↔ "Feta Dodoni", "milk" ≠ "coconut milk", "pepper" ≠ "green pepper"); `convert` (g/kg/oz/lb, ml/l/fl oz and spoons (5 ml) within a family, else through grams with the food's density / piece weight); `coverShop` → full / part / none for a `buildShop` line (lines now carry `am`, their raw amounts; a pantry item with no amount counts as covering; amounts that cannot be compared → part); `cookable` (recipes with ≥ 1 non-staple ingredient at home; order: fewest missing, highest share at home, fewest "not enough", uses an item within 3 days of its date, title; staples = `inPantry`); `cookPlan` (per ingredient key: take from matching items soonest best-before first, in each item's unit; `some` when the recipe or the item has no amount = offer "used up"; `short` = what the pantry lacked); `expiring`, `daysLeft`, `fromShop`, `addInto`, `guessLoc` (dairy/meat/fish → fridge, frozen → freezer, else cupboard), `niceAmount` (0.97 l shows 970 ml; the editor keeps the stored unit when the fields are untouched, R27).
    - **`meals/nutrition.js` (`OrosMealsNutrition`, pure):** a built-in table of 178 foods `[id, EN names, EL names, kcal, protein, carbs, fat per 100 g as bought, piece g, density g/ml]`, values rounded from USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy / Foundation, public domain); Greek cheeses without a USDA entry use the closest USDA food (kefalotyri → romano, graviera → gruyère, kasseri → provolone, myzithra / anthotyro / manouri → ricotta), named in a comment. A name finds the row whose phrase (any alias, as keys) appears in the ingredient key as whole words, longest phrase first. Unit → grams: mass exact; ml/l/fl oz/spoons (5 / 15 / 240 ml) × density (1 when unknown); pieces × piece weight (the user's `g` first); can 400 g, clove 4, pinch 0.4, slice 25, bunch 40; a pack only with the user's `g`. `recipeNutrition` → per serving (total / recipe servings), rows with `ok | noqty (not counted) | nomatch | nogram | x`; `dayNutrition` = one serving of each planned recipe of the day (per person), cached by `id@m` per render. An Open Food Facts match brings the values; the table row still gives density and piece weight.
    - **Open Food Facts** (world.openfoodfacts.org, no key, CORS, data ODbL; attribution in Settings, the nutrition dialogs and the help): `/api/v2/product/<code>.json?fields=…` (barcode) and `/cgi/search.pl?search_terms=…&json=1&page_size=12&fields=…` (search), fetched straight from the browser only when the user presses Look up / reads a code, 20 s timeout, `credentials: "omit"`, no referrer. Answers are read as data: names to plain text, numbers checked (kcal ≤ 1000, grams ≤ 100; kJ only → ÷ 4.184); products without the four values are not offered for nutrition. `validBarcode` checks the GTIN check digit (8, 12, 13, 14 digits); `parseQuantity` reads "400 g", "1,5 l", "6 x 125 g", "33 cl".
    - **Barcode:** the camera loop is Stock's (`stock/stock.js` §9b) inside the barcode dialog: `BarcodeDetector` (EAN-13/8, UPC-A/E) + `getUserMedia` (environment camera), stopped on a read, on close and on a typed look-up; without it the number is typed. A code already on a pantry item opens a new item from it without the network.
    - **UI:** fourth tab `Pantry` (key 4): quick add by `parseIngLine` (merges into a same-name item with no best-before when units add up), filter chips per place, "Use soon" (≤ 3 days or past), editor (name, amount, unit, place, best-before, barcode); shopping list: lines covered → "At home already" section (not counted, copied, sent to To-Do), part → "at home: …"; a tick offers "To pantry" (local action toast), "Ticked to pantry" adds every ticked line without `p`; recipe view and the last cooking step: "Cooked" → preview with ticks → one commit, Undo; recipe view "Per serving" box + "Check the ingredients" (per-row match: table row, Open Food Facts search, leave out, grams per piece); week day header "≈ N kcal" (per person; tooltip P/C/F). Settings: best-before reminder hour, "Show nutrition estimates", data sources.
  - **Fetching a page:** the Reader's network layer, read-only (`feeds/core.js` + `feeds/fetch.js`, `orosFeedsFetch.fetchOne`): straight from the browser when the site allows CORS, else the relay's existing `web` op (`relay/web.js`, unchanged) at the Reader's relay setting, else Mail's. No relay → a message suggesting Mail's relay or copy-paste. The page is fetched only when the user presses Fetch.
- Slice `layout` (oros-layout-data): `{ ver: 1, docs[], dt{docId: deletedAt} }`. Doc: `{ id doc-…, m, name ≤ 120, setup{w, h (pt), unit mm|pt|in, bleed, mt, mb, mi, mo, cols, gut, facing 0/1, preset}, pages[{id, m, pos (fractional order), ms}], masters[{id, m, name{en, el}, pre}], items[], stories[], pstyles[], cstyles[], swatches[{id, m, name, mode rgb|cmyk, v}], guides[{id, m, pg, o v|h, p}], rec[{id, m, sid, t}], tombs{} }`.
- Item common: `{id, m, t text|img|rect|ell|line, pg (page or master id), side ""|L|R (master items), x, y, w, h (pt, page-local), rot, z, fill, stroke (swatch ids), sw, dash, op 0–100, r, lock, hide, grp, wrap none|box|ell, wo}`; text adds `story, seq (fractional thread order), cols, gut, ins, va t|c|b`; image adds `a (^[0-9a-f]{64}\.(jpg|png)$ only), nm, iw, ih, fit fit|fill|custom, ix, iy, isc`.
- Story: `{id, m, h[≤ HIST previous m], paras[{ps, runs[{t | f pn|pc, cs, b, i, u}]}]}`; runs coalesced. Paragraph style keys: font sans|serif|mono, size, lead (0 = auto), align l|c|r|j, b, i, u, sb, sa, fi, li, ri, track, color, bul, caps, base. Character style: font, size, b, i, u, caps, track, color, base.
- Since 1.1.0 (0.58.00): an item may carry `ov` (id of a master item, never its own id): the page's own copy of that master item; the master item stops showing on that page (render, PDF, PNG, wrap); reset to master = delete the copy. Guides are made from the rulers and deleted by dragging back onto a ruler (tomb).
- Limits: 5000 items, 999 pages, 400 000 characters per run; a document above 400 KB warns once (R30).
- Since wave 45 (data merge): an image item may carry `mf` (≤ 60 chars, no braces or line breaks; stored only when set, so older documents canonicalise byte-identical): the CSV column that names its picture file. Text fields are typed in stories as `{{Field}}` (no schema). The merge itself (`layout/merge.js`, `window.LY_MERGE`, pure) never stores anything: it builds a transient, NOT normalized document per part (≤ 12 cards, or 4 sheets) — ids `pg-mN`, `it-r<row>c<card>k<i>p<page>`, `st-…`, so it can exceed the 999 / 5000 limits — and `designkit/pdf.js` appends each part to one jsPDF (`deps.pdf`, fonts embedded once via `pdf.orosFonts`) with an optional per-item clip box (`deps.clip`, N-up cards). Field names match the CSV header case- and accent-free (`fold`); a paragraph left empty by empty fields is dropped; an unknown field stays as typed. CSV: , ; or tab sniffed from the first line, RFC 4180 quotes, BOM, ≤ 1000 rows × 60 columns, cells ≤ 2000 chars, 5 MB. Pictures: looked up by file name (case/accent-free, path dropped) in a folder of the orOS disk (≤ 3 levels, ≤ 4000 entries) or device files picked in the dialog; decoded in memory (≤ 2400 px), never written to `/internal/Assets`; in the PDF one embedded copy per picture + crop (jsPDF alias). N-up: A4 / A3 / Letter, the orientation that holds more cards, 10 mm margin, user gap, cut marks as hairlines in the margin on every card edge; bleed is not printed in N-up. Tests: `tests/layout-merge.test.js`.
- **Since L0 (designkit model level 2, `designkit/model.js` 1.2.0; Layout and Atelier).** `setup`, pages, masters, items, stories, paragraphs (`paras[]`), runs, paragraph and character styles, swatches and guides may carry `ext`: a plain JSON object kept byte for byte (`normX`): keys `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]{0,23}$` sorted at every level, strings ≤ 4000 chars without control characters other than tab and line breaks, finite numbers, booleans, null, arrays ≤ 1000, depth ≤ 6, ≤ 8 KB of JSON per entity (`setup.ext` ≤ 64 KB); empty or invalid = dropped whole, never trimmed. Named `ext`, not `x`, because items and frames already use `x` for their position. Runs coalesce only with an identical `ext`. Not on `rec`. Atelier items: an `ax` whose kind this copy does not know (`setItemExt(fn, known)`) is kept as `axu` (same JSON rules, ≤ 16 KB); a copy that knows the kind turns it back into `ax`; Atelier draws it in the editor as a locked grey box "Needs a newer orOS" and never selects, edits or exports it. Equal-`m` tie (`better()`, also `mergeStory` and the doc meta): the copy that carries `ext`/`axu` (on the entity, in a story's paragraphs or runs, or in `setup`) wins, then the larger canonical JSON. `MODEL_LEVEL = 2`; `setup.ext.mv` (integer > 1, absent today) = the lowest level allowed to edit the document: `needsNewer(doc)` → both apps list it with "Needs a newer orOS" and refuse to open it, so they never write it; sync and merge go on. `unknownX(entity, known)` lists the keys a copy does not understand. `DATA_VER` stays 1; existing documents canonicalize byte-identical (tests/designkit-compat.test.js against the frozen pre-L0 model `tests/fixtures/designkit-model-2.56.js`). Residual risk: a device still on pre-L0 code keeps uploading its stripped copy until it updates; every L0+ device rejects it.
- **LY-FONT (fonts besides Noto, Layout 4.11.00, `designkit/fonts.js` 1.0.0).** A paragraph or character style names an extra family in `ext.fam` = `fs_<Fontsource slug, "-" → "_">` or `uf_<first 16 hex of the sha256 of the family's regular file>` (`text.FAM_RE`); its `font` (sans|serif|mono) stays the stand-in, so a copy without the family, or an older copy, lays it out with Noto. A style that sets a built-in `font` without `ext.fam` ends an inherited family (`famOf`); `runAttrs` takes `fam` from the character style when it sets `font` or `fam`. `setup.ext.fonts = [{id, name ≤ 60, fb sans|serif|mono, r?, b?, i?, bi?}]` (≤ 40, one per id, newest last; r/b/i/bi only for `uf_`: file names `<sha256>.ttf`) lists the document's families so every device knows their names and files. Own font files live once in `/internal/Fonts/<sha256>.ttf` (orOS disk, synced by Vault like any file); they are checked before they are kept (`fonts.check`: TrueType outlines (`glyf`) only, since jsPDF cannot embed CFF; OS/2 fsType "restricted licence embedding" refused; ≤ 15 MB; a WOFF 1.0 is unpacked to TTF first; WOFF2 not accepted). Fontsource files are fetched per subset (latin, latin-ext, greek, greek-ext) from jsDelivr and kept in Cache Storage `oros-atelier-fonts` (shared with Atelier; a 404/403 is cached as 204). The PDF embeds each face file in use (`pdf.orosFonts`, key `key` or `key~i` for the i-th subset file) and writes every character with the file that has it, else the stand-in's. `.oroslayout` packages carry the own font files the styles use as `media/<sha256>.ttf`; on open they are verified by hash (`fonts.put`), a missing one leaves the stand-in and says so (`imp.fontFail`). Ext styles may also carry `srcFont` (≤ 60, the font name in a Scribus file; kept for later matching). Line metrics (ascent, descent, leading) always come from the stand-in `font`, never from the family, which only draws: whoever places a frame from a known baseline (Rebuild, 4.38.01 `lineKey`) must use the stand-in's ascent too. Tests `tests/layout-fonts.test.js`.
- **LY-KERN (pair kerning, Layout 4.12.00, `designkit/text.js`).** `parseTTF` reads the GPOS `kern` feature's pair adjustments (lookup type 2, also inside type 9 extensions; formats 1 and 2; the first value's x advance) per script (`latn`, `grek`, `cyrl` by the left character, else `DFLT`, else all), else the old `kern` table (format 0); a damaged table means no kerning. A style turns it on with `ext.kern` 1 (0 = off; inherited through `base`; a character style may override); `runAttrs` gives the run `kern`, layout lines carry `kern: 1`, `measure(key, str, size, track, kern)` adds the pairs between neighbours of one face file (a character drawn by the fallback is not kerned), `render.js` draws such runs letter by letter, `pdf.js` starts a new text piece at every kerned pair. No GSUB (ligatures, decomposition): HarfBuzz can differ on a decomposed accented letter. Default off, so existing documents keep their line breaks; Layout's `createDoc`, Rebuild a print PDF and Scribus import set `ext.kern: 1` on `ps-base`. The bundled Noto subsets have no pairs. Checked against Chromium's own kerning (canvas `fontKerning`) on Noto Sans, FreeSerif and DejaVu Serif: equal on Latin, Greek and Cyrillic samples. Tests `tests/layout-kern.test.js`.
- **LY-SLA-LINK (Scribus linked pictures, Layout 4.13.00, `layout/sla.js` 1.3.0).** Every Scribus image frame keeps how its picture was placed in `ext.place` = `[mode, LOCALSCX, LOCALSCY, LOCALX, LOCALY]` (mode 0 free: `SCALETYPE` 0; 1 fit keeping proportions; 2 stretched to the frame: `SCALETYPE` 1 with `RATIO` 0; scale in pt per pixel, offset in pixels), and `convert` lists linked pictures as `links: [{ item, name }]`. `placePicture(it)` (once `iw`/`ih` are known) sets mode 1 → `fit`; mode 2 → `custom` with `isc = w / iw`, `ext.iscy = h / ih`; mode 0 → `custom` with `isc = sx`, `ix = LOCALX·sx`, `iy = LOCALY·sy`, and `ext.iscy = sy` when it differs from sx. `ext.iscy` (designkit, R39) is a custom placement's own height scale: `render.js` `imageRect` uses it, `effectivePpi` takes the lower resolution of the two sides, `R.uniform(it)` drops it and every edit of the fit or the scale, Place image / Replace and the data merge call it; a resize with the picture kept scales it too. `nameKey` matches names by the last path part, NFC, lower case. io.js: Open file with one `.sla` and pictures, or Open folder on a folder with a `.sla` and no `content.json` (Scribus Collect for Output), fills the frames from the pictures by name (embedded pictures are placed the same way); when some are still missing the message has `Find pictures…` (`sla.find`), which fills the empty frames of the open document that name the picked pictures in one undo step (`sla.relinked`). Tests `tests/layout-sla-links.test.js`.
- **LY-FIT (line breaks of a print PDF, Layout 4.14.00, `layout/linefit.js`, `designkit/text.js`).** text.js: a soft hyphen U+00AD and a zero-width space U+200B inside a word are break opportunities (token `h`, `hy` 1 / 0): unbroken they show nothing and add no width or justification gap; a line that breaks at a soft hyphen ends with a `-` run (offset of the U+00AD, n 1) that must fit too, else the line ends one opportunity earlier; layout lines carry `aw` (the first segment's available width). Only text with these characters lays out differently (IDML text with discretionary hyphens now hyphenates instead of drawing them). linefit.js: `fit(doc, targets, opts)` with targets `{ sid, p, br }` (offsets where the PDF's 2nd, 3rd… lines of paragraph p start): per paragraph, last line first, the tracking range (lo, hi] in which the line's words fit its `aw` and the next word does not (widths as text.js measures them, kerning included); a line whose own tracking is outside it gets a character style `cs-fit…` (ext.fit 1, `base` = the run's own character style, `track` = the chosen value: an existing fit value in range, else a whole number a little inside the range; never more than 60 from the style's tracking); up to 6 layout passes; unused fit styles are removed; the doc is normalized again. `align(doc, sid, texts)` lines a story up with the PDF's line texts (NFKC, accents and spaces ignored (4.35.01: some print PDFs give Greek text without its tonos when read), page-number fields match digits, a 400-character look-ahead), inserts U+00AD where a line ended in a hyphen the story does not have and U+200B where it broke after the story's own hyphen, and leaves out any paragraph with a line not found. rebuild.js: `para()` keeps the line starts (`br`), a joined hyphenated word keeps a U+00AD (before 4.14.00 the hyphen was dropped), a compound split at its hyphen gets U+200B (before: a forced break, which left the line unjustified), and `build` fits before its check (`report.fit`); `pdfText(buf)` reads only a PDF's text (`spansOf`, shared with `open`); `matchPdf(doc, pages, opts)` gives each unrotated text frame the PDF's spans inside it, by column, lines them up (`align`) and fits; when the page counts differ, PDF page = file page − `pageShift` (4.35.01, see Part XII), reported as `rep.shift`. io.js: a `.sla` picked with a PDF (Open file, or in a Collect for Output folder) is fitted to it before it opens (`sla.fitting`, `sla.fit`, `sla.fitBad`, style name `sla.fitStyle`). Tests `tests/layout-linefit.test.js`, `tests/layout-rebuild.test.js`.
- **LY-AF (an Affinity file helps a rebuild, Layout 4.16.00, `layout/afread.js`, experimental, Part IX 2026-10-17).** `LY_AF.read(bytes, {zstd: fzstd})` → `{text, fonts, styles, pictures: [{name "af-N.ext", type, bytes}], files, problems: ["zstd" | "doc"]}` or null (no magic `00 FF 4B 41`). Container as read from Affinity 3.3 files: the u64 at byte 16 is the newest file table `#FT4`; each table has the previous table's offset at +4 and its end at +20, and entries `u32 id, u8, u64 offset, u64 size, u64 stored size, 13 bytes, u16 name length, ASCII name` ("c/N" stored pictures, "d/…" data tiles); an entry counts only when its offset holds `#Fil` and its sizes fit the file, and the newest entry of an id wins (the older copies of the document are its history, never read). A `#Fil` is a zstd frame (decompressed into a buffer of the entry's size, at most 256 MB) or a stored block whose `Data` tag holds the bytes; stored JPEG/PNG/GIF/TIFF are the pictures (at most 400, passed on as pictures, decoded only as images by the caller). The document is the first compressed non-tile file whose output starts with `00 FF 4B 53`; its strings are `+`, a 4-letter tag stored backwards, u32 length, UTF-8 (invalid UTF-8 skipped): `Utf8` text, `Famy` families, style names = values of `Base`/`Foll`/`Next`/`PSty`/`BSty`/`TSty` and `Name`s whose object goes on with one of those. Never geometry. `rebuild.open` takes a `.af` among its sources (≤ 1 GB, the first one only): its pictures join the original-picture candidates, its words the hyphen dictionary, and `report.af = {pictures, styles ≤ 60, fonts ≤ 30, problems}` or `{failed: 1}`; the report dialog shows `rb.af`, `rb.afStyles`, `rb.afFonts`, `rb.afBad`. Rebuild's file picker accepts `.af`. Assistant: `rebuild_in_layout` sources take an attached `.af` (not with `sla`), and `rebuildReport` adds `affinity: {read, pictures, styles: count}` (counts only). Tests `tests/layout-afread.test.js` (a synthetic container built in the test: two tables, history, stored and zstd files, damaged frame, looping table), `tests/assistant-rebuild.test.js`.
