- **LY-PN (first page number, Layout 4.17.00, `designkit/model.js`, `designkit/render.js`).** `setup.ext.pnStart` (R39; integer 0-9999, absent = 1) is the number of the first page: `M.firstNumber(doc)` reads it (anything else gives 1) and `computeLayout` labels page i as `i + first`, so `{f: "pn"}` fields show it; `{f: "pc"}` stays the page count. A client without LY-PN keeps the key (ext is verbatim) and shows 1, 2, 3. `Document setup…` has `First page number` (`new.pnStart`; 1 removes the key, an empty ext is removed). Rebuild: when the PDF's page numbers follow the pages (`numberOffset`), each page-number frame holds one `{f: "pn"}` run and `pnStart` is the PDF's first number (not stored when it is 1); a number that does not follow stays text; `rb.numbers` says so. Tests `tests/layout-pagenum.test.js`, `tests/layout-rebuild.test.js`.
- **LY-THR (threaded rebuild, Layout 4.18.00, `layout/rebuild.js` `build` opts.thread, `layout/io.js` `framesDlg`).** Before a rebuild from the menu, `Text frames` asks `Per page` (default, the session keeps the choice) or `Going on across pages`. With `thread`, body frames (body size, no wrap, not display type, not a caption) are taken in reading order (page, then column by horizontal overlap, then top down); frame A goes on in the next one, B, when B is at most two pages on, A's last line runs to the column's end (`full`/`fulli`), B's first line starts at the column's edge (`full`/`l`), both have the same measure (±1.5 pt) and the same paragraph look (size, family, font, bold, italic, colour, leading ±0.5), and no display-type block sits above B within 8 pitches in its column. B's frame joins A's story (`seq` + 1) and A becomes as tall as its lines plus half a leading. The paragraph cut by the page becomes one (`join()`, the same joining as line ends, `br` offsets carried over for LF.fit) unless A's last line ends a sentence (`END`: . ; U+037E ! ? … : and closing quotes) and B's starts in upper case; then they stay two paragraphs, as on their pages. `report.threads = { stories, frames }` (`rb.threads`); Assistant `rebuild_in_layout` takes `thread: true` (only for a PDF, not with sla), carried by the card (`ui.thread`) to Layout (`rebuild.thread`), report `threaded: { articles, frames }`. Tests `tests/layout-rebuild.test.js` (LY-THR, full stop), `tests/assistant-rebuild.test.js`.
- **LY-BK (book typesetting, Layout 4.19.00, `designkit/text.js`, `designkit/render.js`, `layout/panels.js`).** Paragraph style ext keys (R39), inherited through `base` by `resolvePs` (`bookOf`): `hyph` 1/0 Greek hyphenation; `orph`, `wid` 1-9 the fewest lines of a paragraph before and after a column break; `kwn` 1/0 keep with next; `brk` `col` | `page` | `odd` | `even` (4.24.00) where the paragraph starts (anything else, e.g. `any`, is anywhere); `sink` 0-600 pt (4.24.00) how far below the top of a column the paragraph starts when it opens the column (a chapter's sunk opening; `sb` is ignored there as before, and `sink` is ignored inside a column). Old copies read `even` as anywhere and ignore `sink` (display only). Hyphenation: `hyphenGreek(word)` (exported) follows the school rules: one consonant between vowels goes on; two or more go on when a Greek word can start with their first two letters (`GR_ONSET`), else the first stays; a vowel group is never split unless its next vowel has a dialytika; two letters at least on each side; only words of Greek letters (leading/trailing punctuation kept aside), one-part words only. `tokenize` inserts `h` tokens with `auto: 1` (no character), and the hyphen run of such a break has no `o`/`n`, so the caret, line fit and offsets never count it. Layout (`layoutChain`): `brk` moves to the next column, past the page of the last line placed, then (odd / even) to a frame whose page number (`ctx.no`, render.js passes `pg` and `no`) is odd / even (a page without a number takes either); no page context (Atelier, the master view, Slides, Certificates) never moves pages. Each paragraph is laid out from a snapshot; orphans: fewer than `orph` lines before a break → restart in the next column (not when it began at a column top); widows (paragraph over two columns): fewer than `wid` lines after → the first column keeps `n − (wid − last)` lines when that is still ≥ `orph`, else the whole paragraph moves; `kwn`: when the next paragraph's first `orph` lines would not fit after it (by its leading, ignoring wraps), it starts in the next column. Pages are never added by the engine (automatic layout, wave H5, adds them). New documents (`LY.createDoc`, templates via `LY.hyphOn`) have `hyph` on in `ps-base`; existing, rebuilt, Scribus and IDML documents keep their breaks. Style dialog: `Book typesetting` (`sty.book`, `sty.hyph`, `sty.kwn`, `sty.orph`, `sty.wid`, `sty.brk*`). Tests `tests/layout-book.test.js`.
- **LY-WD (placing a Word document, Layout 4.20.00, `layout/wordin.js` `LY_WORDIN`, `layout/io.js` `importText`).** More › "Place text or a document (Word, .odt, .txt)…" reads .docx/.odt (`WriterIO.parseZipBuf`) and .rtf/.html/.htm/.md (`WriterIO.parseTextOf`) with Writer's own reader (`writer/io.js`, loaded on first use; .txt keeps the old path, one `ps-body` paragraph per line). `LY_WORDIN.parse(html)` gives each paragraph a role: `h1`, `h2`, `h3` (h3-h6), `p1` (first non-empty paragraph after a heading, an empty paragraph or the start), `p`, `center` (text-align center), `quote` (inside blockquote), `li`; runs keep b/i/u, `<br>` → "\n", empty paragraphs stay (`runs: []`), footnote marks (`sup.fn-ref`), comments, script/style/title are left out (footnote text is not placed). The mapping role → paragraph style id is `doc.setup.ext.wmap` (R39; `doc.m` stamped only when it changes; `mapOf` falls back to the seed style, then `ps-base`, when a mapped style is gone); a dialog shows one select per role present, with its count, before anything is placed. Placement as before: appended to the one selected text frame's story, else a new frame in the current page's margins; one undo step for the text and the mapping. Limit 64 MB per file. Tests `tests/layout-wordin.test.js`.
- **LY-HS (house style, Layout 4.21.00, `layout/house.js` `LY_HOUSE`, `layout/houseui.js`).** A house style is an ordinary Layout document with `setup.ext.house = {v: 1, from, roles: {body|first|title|subtitle|center|quote|note: ps id}, rules: [{id "r<n>", src "works"|"greek"|"own", on 1|0, code + p (text from strings `hr.<code>`) | t (own words, ≤ 400), a: {k "style", role, set {hyph|orph|wid|kwn|brk|fi}} | {k "fix", fix quotes|dash|ellipsis|spaces} | {k "info"} | {k "check"}}]}` (R39) and `setup.ext.wmap` from its roles (LY-WD), so it syncs and merges like any document. `learn(docs)`: per work, each paragraph's look = its style + its first run's character style (Scribus/InDesign books often set titles as body style + a bold, larger character style); body = the look with most characters; title = the most used short look larger than the body (≥ 1.05×) or bold where the body is not; subtitle only when at least half its uses follow a title; first = the body-size look after titles; center, quote, note by alignment, indents, size. A title "opens a page" when no non-empty line on its page is above it (empty lines above are its sink). Works rules: titles on a new page when ≥ 80 % of titles open one (odd page when all of them do, `brk` odd), first paragraph flush when body fi > 0 and first fi = 0 in half the works, the sink (info), body and page-size differences (info). The template is a copy (`M.copyDoc`) of the work whose page setup most works share (then the most pages): its masters, styles, colours, front matter (pages before the first title, where a look that differs from the title's only in spacing is a title too, since a rebuilt PDF gives each spacing its own style; never past the first page with ≥ 400 characters of body text, 4.23.01; ≤ 16) and back matter (after the last body paragraph, ≤ 16) with their whole stories, and one empty body page on the body master; pages carry `ext.hs` front|body|back. A role whose look is not its style's own gets `ps-hs<role>` based on it. The Greek set (`GREEK`): hyphenation, orphans 2, widows 2 (body), keep with next and no hyphenation (title, subtitle), quote, dash, ellipsis and double-space fixes. `apply(doc)` writes the "style" rules that are on into the role styles and takes a rule's value back out when it is off (own rules removed in the sheet are applied once as off). `fixText(paras, rules)`: Greek quotes by depth (« » outside, “ ” inside; straight and curly quotes, open after a space, bracket, dash or the start), a hyphen or en dash opening a paragraph → em dash, " - " → " – ", "..." → "…", double spaces → one; never a letter. Placing text (`importText`, .txt and LY-WD) into a document with house rules runs `fixText` and names the count in the toast; .txt lines take the mapping's body style. UI: More › "House style…" (learn from picked documents, report, rules sheet with role selects, rules on/off by source, own rules with an optional setting); a house style card on the home grid says "House style". Tests `tests/layout-house.test.js`.
- **LY-AUTO (automatic layout, Layout 4.22.00, `layout/autolay.js` `LY_AUTO`, dialogs in `layout/houseui.js`).** `build(house, list, meta, opts)` → `{doc, report}`: (1) `M.copyDoc` of the house style; (2) `fillFields`: `{title|τίτλος}` `{subtitle|υπότιτλος}` `{author|συγγραφέας}` `{isbn}` `{year|έτος}` `{publisher|εκδότης}` inside runs, from the typed details or a Publishing title (`oros-publish-data`, read only: t, sub, ppl r "a", the first format ISBN, rel year); learning (LY-HS `markFields`) already turned the template's ISBN into `{isbn}`, the largest text of the first front page into `{title}` (when that page is all one size, a colophon, the line that is only a quoted name, quotes kept as `«{title}»`; else no title field, 4.23.01), and a front/back story whose paragraphs mostly end in page numbers into the contents (story `ext.hs` "toc"); (3) `structure`: a short (≤ 80) paragraph with a letter or digit (a line of stars is never a title) all in bold after an empty one or at the start, or centred after ≥ 3 empty ones, is a guessed title (h1); the manuscript's own front matter (before the first title followed by more than 200 characters of text before the next title, 4.23.01) is left out unless `keepFront`, and only when it looks like front matter: ≤ 40 non-empty paragraphs, none over 400 characters (`FRONT_MAX`); empty paragraphs at the ends, next to titles and doubled go; p1 after each title; roles → styles by `H.wmapOf(roles)`, a role the house lacks takes the body (`noStyle`); `H.fixText` with the house rules; (4) `flow`: the body story from the house's body page (`ext.hs` "body") through n pages (one margin frame each, setup cols/gut, the body page's master), n from the characters placed (≤ 12 passes), then trimmed to the last page with lines; back matter after; pages renumbered `pos` 1024 apart; (5) `toc(doc, L)`: entries from title-style paragraphs and their first line's page (`firstNumber` + index), in the first entry's style and runs, with its separator (tab, dots, spaces); the paragraphs before the first entry stay (the heading); (6) report `{pages, body, titles, guessed, dropped, front, fixes, fields, toc (-1 none), noStyle, pictures (not placed), check: [{page, why overset|oversetOther, id}]}`, overset counted only where the house style itself was not. UI: More › "Automatic layout…" (house style, manuscript via `LY.io.readDoc`, details, keep the manuscript's front matter), report with page links; More › "Update contents" (`LY.house.updateToc`, one undo step). Tests `tests/layout-auto.test.js`, synthetic books `tests/layout-books.js`.
- **LY-IN (book intake: questions and the book sheet, Layout 4.24.00, `layout/intake.js` `LY_INTAKE`, dialog in `layout/houseui.js`).** Before an automatic layout from the dialog, Layout reads the manuscript and asks a fixed list of questions (`QUESTIONS`: `size` 120x190|140x210|148x210|170x240, `start` odd|even|page|run, `parts` own|chap (only when the manuscript has parts), `sink` top|third, `first` flush|indent, `sep` keep|`***`|`* * *`|`⁂`|blank (only with scene breaks), `pn` footC|footOut|headOut|headC|none, `pnHide` hide|show, `toc` start|end|none, `tocParts` parts|chap, `hyph`, `widows`, `fix` on|off; plus `marg {t,b,i,o}` mm, `pnStart`, `at<Section>` s|front|back|out per section found), each with "as in the series (…)" first (`s` or missing). Sheet `{v: 1, a, ty: {part: {fam, size, lead, align, b, i, caps, track}}, drop: [page id], ded, motto}`, normalized by `clean` (known keys and values only, so `setup.ext` never fails R39 normalization), kept in the new book as `setup.ext.book` (plus `house` id, `partPs`, `openMs`); "keep as the series' own" writes `{a (without pnStart), ty}` to the house style's `setup.ext.house.answers`, which `defaults(house)` returns next time (pages, dedication and motto are never series answers). `info(house, list, cut)`: parts (a title `Μέρος|Βιβλίο|Part|Book|Teil` + one word, ≤ 40 characters, accents and case ignored), scene breaks (`H.isSep`: a short line of stars, dots, ornaments, no letter), sections by their title (`SECTIONS`: ded, motto, prologue, thanks, notes, bio, links), the dedication and motto text (also from the manuscript's own front matter `cut`, which `structure` now returns), the house's front/back pages, and the series' answers for the labels. `mark(list, sheet, inf)`: part titles → `ps-hspart` (unless `chap`), the first title after a part → `ps-hsopen` when chapters run on, scene breaks → `ps-hssep` with the chosen text, thanks/links paragraphs → `ps-hsthanks`/`ps-hslinks`, sections moved before the first chapter, after the last, or left out; the dedication and motto sections leave the text. `prepare(house, sheet, inf, opts)` → a copy of the house style: pages dropped (front/back only); a new size scales every item (pages and masters) and guide; margins; title `brk` (`run` → `any`) and `sink` (`third` = h/3 − mt; as the series = the learned `w.sink`); the first paragraph's indent (a `ps-hsfirst` when the house has no first role); `ps-hspart` (title-based, centred, `brk` odd, sunk a third) and `ps-hsopen` (`brk` page when titles do not break); contents removed, moved (pages re-marked front/back), or made (`ps-hstochead`, `ps-hstoc`, on a new page) and entries restyled; the publisher's page (a story with `{isbn}` `{year}` `{publisher}`) restyled per style (`ps-hscol<n>`); dedication and motto each on a right-hand front page of its own (a blank page added before when needed), a third down, in `ps-hsded`; page numbers: the body page gets a master of its own (`ms-hsbody`, a copy) whose page-number frames are replaced (60 pt centred, or a narrow frame at the outer/inner text edge, head or foot margin middle, per side when facing; `ps-hspn` when the house has none) or removed; `pnStart` → `setup.ext.pnStart`; hidden numbers → `ms-hsopen` (the body master without its page-number frames); typography per part with `setLook` (body and first, title, part, toc, colophon, thanks, links, ded); `hyph`, `orph`/`wid` 2 or 1 on body and first; the fix rules on/off. `finish(doc, L)` after the flow: body pages that are empty or whose first line starts a title, part or chapter-after-part paragraph get `openMs`. `A.build(…, {sheet, names, tocHead})` runs info → mark → prepare → the usual steps → `finish`; a paragraph with its own `ps` keeps it; `toc` also lists `ps-hsopen` and `partPs`; report adds `sheet, moved, left, bare`. Without a sheet (the Assistant's `layout_book` until wave Q3) nothing changes. LY-HS learning adds: page-number frames (`pnOnly` stories, on pages or masters, `pnStudy`) set page by page go onto `ms-hsbody` (a copy of the body master) so every new page has them; `house.pn = {at, hide}` (`pnAt`: head/foot, centre/outer/inner of the right-hand page; hidden when fewer than half the opening pages show one); `house.sep` the most used scene break. `H.cloneMaster(d, from, to, name, pre, now, keep)` copies a master with its stories. UI: the questions dialog in groups (page and structure, front and back pages, typography of each part, text), `Everything as in the series`, `Keep these answers as the series' own`; More › `Book sheet…` (`LY.house.sheet`) opens the automatic layout with the book's house style and sheet for a new layout. Strings `in.*`, `au.f.editor`, `au.f.publisher`, `au.rep{Moved,Left,Bare}`, `more.sheet`, `sty.brkEven`, `sty.sink` (EN, EL, DE); `{editor|επιμέλεια}` field. Tests `tests/layout-intake.test.js`.
  - **Photos (4.25.00, wave Q2).** `W.parse(html, {pics: 1})` (and `LY.io.readDoc(f, ext, {pics: 1})`, used only by the questions path) gives each `<img>` as an entry `{role: "img", runs: [], src, alt}` instead of an empty paragraph; without the option nothing changed. `I.pictures(list)` → `{list, pics}`: each picture goes with the next paragraph that has text (`p.pics`: indexes; pictures at the very end go with the last paragraph), and a short paragraph right after it (≤ 300 characters, not a title) that is all italic, centred, or starts like "Photo/Φωτ…" (`CAP_RE`) is its caption (`pic.cap`, `p.capOf`). Questions (group `pics`, asked only when the manuscript has pictures or others were picked): `picAt` page|before|each|out, `picSize` text|page, `cap` below|above|none, `capSrc` para (series)|file|typed, `grey` no (series)|yes; `extraAt` end|after<n> for pictures picked besides the manuscript; `sheet.pics[k] = {at, cap}` per picture in order (the manuscript's, then the others), kept in `ext.book.pics` (no picture data in the sheet). `mark` drops the caption paragraphs (when the caption is taken from them) and carries their pictures on; `prepare` adds `ps-hscap` (from the house's note or body style, centred, italic, 2 pt smaller). `A.placePics` after the flow, in reading order: `page` inserts picture pages before the anchor paragraph's page (an empty page before it is reused; when the page that holds the anchor opens a chapter with `brk` odd/even in a facing book, the side is kept by an extra blank page), one picture per page, fitted within the margins (`text`) or the whole page to the bleed (`page`), caption below/above in its own frame; `before` puts the picture at the top of the anchor's page with `wrap: box` and the caption below; `out` leaves it out (counted). Pictures picked besides the manuscript always get pages of their own, before chapter n + 1 or at the end (the text is grown to fit first; `grow` adds body pages with chained frames from the last text page's master, `trimEnd` drops trailing empty ones). `finish` treats picture pages (`ext.pic`) as openings (no page number when hidden) and ignores caption frames. Report: `placed`, `pictures` (left out), `overset`. The dialog: a Photos group, `Photos besides the manuscript…` (`LY.io.pickFiles`, several at once), where they go, `Each photo…` (a thumbnail, its own place when `each`, its own caption). On go, each picture is imported with `LY.A.importFile` (a Word `data:` URL as a Blob), black and white first when `grey` is yes (luminance 0.299/0.587/0.114, JPEG 0.92, white under clear parts, at most 4000 px); one that cannot be read stays without an asset and is reported as left out. LY-HS learning adds `house.pics = {at, size, cap}` (`picStudy`, the most used answer over pictures of at least a sixth of the page: at most 200 body characters on its page → `page`, more → `before`; as wide as the page → `page` size, else `text`; a text frame of at most 300 characters within 40 pt under or over it → caption below/above). Tests `tests/layout-intake.test.js` (photos).
  - **Running heads and photos in the flow (4.28.00, wave Q4a; LY-RH).** Question `rh` (group page, after `pnHide`): `s` | `none` | `titleChap` (left: the book's title, right: the current chapter) | `authorTitle` (left: author, right: title); `info` reports the house's own heads as `own`, else none. **LY-RH** (`designkit/text.js`, `designkit/render.js`): a run `{t: fallback, ext: {fld: "sec"}}` is the running-head field and a paragraph style with `ext.sec = 1` (R39, inherited through `base` by `bookOf`) marks the titles it follows. `computeLayout` (render) lays out the page stories first, then `runningHeads` gives every page `secOf[page]` = the text of the first marked paragraph that opens on that page, else the last one before it, else ""; it is passed as `ctx.sec` to master frames only (page frames show the fallback). `tokenize` keeps a sec run as one part `{t: null, f: "sec", fb, n}` (never hyphenated or split) and `partText` shows `ctx.sec` when it is a string, else the fallback; an older orOS shows the fallback (the book's title), so the field never shows junk. `prepare` with heads: the body page gets its own master if needed, the house's heads (`rhItems`: master text above the top margin that is not a page-number frame, or marked `ext.rh`) are removed, `addHeads` puts left/right frames (`ext.rh`, centred vertically in the head margin, `ps-hsrh` 0.85 × body size, centred; inset 36 pt or `ps-hsrhl`/`ps-hsrhr` aligned out when the page number is in the head), and the title style gets `ext.sec = 1` for titleChap; the opening master (`openMs`) is made without them, so chapter openings carry no head. After `fillFields` the head stories keep only filled fields (a sec run keeps " "). Story editor: the § button inserts the field (atomic in the editor, never split by `cut`, runs with ext are never merged); the style dialog's `Running head title` (`sty.sec`) sets the flag. **Photos in the flow** (`picAt` value `flow`): after the text flows, each picture goes right below the line where its paragraph ends (`lineAt`), across the text width, `fit` scaling and a box wrap so the text moves below it; one that does not fit goes to the top of the next frame's page, else on a page of its own; several after one paragraph stack (`flowAt`). Pictures that push text into overset grow the flow first (`grow`) and are then placed, so none is dropped. Strings `in.q.rh`, `in.rh.*`, `in.n.{rh,rhL,rhR}`, `in.picAt.flow`, `sty.sec`, `story.sec` (EN, EL, DE); the Assistant's `BOOK_Q` gains `rh` and picAt `flow` (`lb.q.rh`, `lb.rh.*`, `lb.picAt.flow`). Tests `tests/layout-intake.test.js`.
  - **Word's notes (4.29.00, wave Q4b; LY-NT).** Writer's DOCX reader (`writer/io.js` `ioDxNotes`) reads `word/footnotes.xml` and `word/endnotes.xml` (Word's separator notes, `w:type`, left out; each note plain text, paragraphs joined by a line break, ≤ 20000 characters) and turns each `w:footnoteReference` / `w:endnoteReference` into Writer's `<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn>` with a payload footnote `{id, text}` in mark order (a mark with no note is left out), so Writer's Open also keeps Word's notes (endnotes become footnotes). Layout's `readDoc` with `pics` also passes `notes: 1`: `W.parse` gives each mark as a run `{t: "*", fn: id}` (never merged) and `readDoc` returns `notes` (the payload's footnotes; Markdown `[^n]` notes come the same way). Question `fnAt` (group text, only when the manuscript has marks, `info().notes`): `s` | `chap` | `book`; the series' answer is `book` (a house style learns no notes). `I.notes(list, notes, mode, head)` (after `mark`, in `A.build`; opts `notes`, `notesHead`): each mark becomes a raised number `{t: "1", ext: {sup: 1}}` (R39), numbered again in each chapter for `chap`, through the book for `book`; `chap` puts a heading in `ps-hsnotehead` (body, bold, keep with next) and one paragraph per note `N. text` in `ps-hsnote` (body − 1.5 pt, no indent) before the next top-level title; `book` puts a title of its own (the top title level, so it opens a page, enters the contents and the running head) and the notes after the last chapter, before the back sections. Without a sheet a mark is dropped (never "*"). Report `notes`, `notesLeft` (`au.repNotes`, `au.repNotesLeft`). **Raised run** (`designkit/text.js` `runAttrs`): a run with `ext.sup` is 0.65 of its size and its line run's `y` is raised by 0.33 of the size, in every renderer (canvas, PDF, SVG); an older orOS shows the number at the text's size. The story editor shows it as one `<sup>` piece (`data-f "sup"`, never split by `cut`, read back with its ext). Strings `in.q.fnAt`, `in.fnAt.*`, `in.n.{note,noteHead,notesHead}` (EN, EL, DE); the Assistant's `BOOK_Q` gains `fnAt` (`lb.q.fnAt`, `lb.fnAt.*`). Tests `tests/layout-intake.test.js`, `tests/convert-writer.test.js` (DOCX notes in Chromium).
- Package `.oroslayout`: an OBF bundle (see "orOS file format (OBF)"): content.json `{kind: "oros-layout-package", ver: 1, doc}` + `media/<sha256>.<jpg|png>` + thumbnail; older JSON packages `{…, assets{id: base64}}` still open. Opened as a NEW document (new id), every image checked against its sha256 name and decoded as an image before it is written.
- **Many packages at once (4.55.00, `io.js importMany` / `importDisk`, `designkit/zipin.js` `window.orosZipIn`, in `layout/` until 4.61.01).** Home › Open › A file takes several `.oroslayout` files and `.zip` files of them; A folder in Files browses the orOS disk (Trash and, since 4.57.01, `/internal/Layout` left out: Layout's own document files are never imported again as copies; `SKIP_DIRS`) and opens every `.oroslayout` in the chosen folder and its subfolders (depth ≤ 4, sorted by path). At most 500 packages per batch, one after another, each through `openFile` like one file (≤ `PKG_MAX`). A zip is never read whole: `LY_ZIPIN.list(blob)` (pure, app-neutral, no DOM) reads the end record and central directory by `slice`, and each entry is sliced (stored) or inflated with `DecompressionStream("deflate-raw")` (deflated), the size capped while it streams; ZIP64, encrypted entries, `__MACOSX/` and dot files are left out. While batching the per-file toasts are silenced (`say`) and `LY.addDocQuiet` adds without opening and writes storage at once; the first document that does not fit (R30) is taken back and the batch stops, so nothing is shown that a reload would lose. Home re-renders and one toast gives the counts (`imp.many`, `imp.manyBad`, `imp.full`). One package alone still opens as before. A picked file is told by its methods, never `instanceof Blob`: files from the shell's `orosDialog` belong to the parent window. Tests `tests/layout-import-many.test.js`.
- **LY-DISK · documents on the orOS disk (4.56.00, `designkit/docstore.js` `window.orosDocStore`, Layout section 3b).** With the orOS disk (Layout in the shell), `create({dir, ext, kind, ver, fs, M, core})` names files `<name ≤ 80, cleaned> · <id><ext>` (`parse` tells a FILES-V copy `… (conflict …)<ext>` apart), writes the JSON package `{kind, ver, doc}` (a rename moves the old file first; `verify` reads it back), and `trash` moves a file to `/internal/.trash` with the record Files reads (`files-core.js`). `open({store, M, fs, ls, keys{legacy, index, open}, rescue, entry})` is the app's side: `load()` reads every file (two files of one id and conflict copies merged), merges the old slice (`oros-layout-data`) and the journal (`oros-layout-open`), writes what the files lack (read back) and, the first time the old store has documents, writes its text to `/internal/Rescue/<rescue>-<ms>.json` first (index flag `rescued`; `sweepRescue` trashes copies older than 30 days); `save(data, openDoc)` journals the open document at once, then writes each document whose `maxM` moved or a merge marked, trashes the files of documents gone from data and rewrites the index (`oros-layout-index`: `{ver, rescued, dt, docs[{id, m, name, path, pages, setup{w, h, unit, ext.mv?}, tx ≤ 1000}]}`); `absorb(data, incoming)` takes a pull of the old slice (kept as the legacy copy, its documents merged); `sliceGet(data)` = the legacy copy + every deletion; `rescan(data)` after a Vault "stats" event with downloads, deletions or conflicts: changed files (size:mtime) merged, a file moved in Files adopted, a file that vanished dropped only when it is in the Trash and nothing here is newer. Without the disk (a page opened on its own, or the disk unreadable at start: toast `toast.diskOff`) everything stays in localStorage as before. A failed write keeps the document marked and says so once (`toast.diskSave`); unreadable files are left alone (`toast.diskRead`). Batch import (`addDocQuiet`) counts a document once its file is written and read back. Readers: `layout/search.js` (index first, the old key on a device that has not used the disk yet), the Assistant (`EDIT_SRC.layout` `disk`, `pkg`: picks on the index, reads the picked files, at most 64 MB each). Tests `tests/layout-disk.test.js`.
- **SLIDES v1** (slice `slides`, key `oros-slides-data`): `{ ver, decks{id: {id, m, t, as "16:9"|"4:3", th, ft{n, d, x, s1}, c, tm}}, slides{id: {id, m, d (deck), p (order key), ly, tr, hid, bg?, n (notes), nb, nm, tm}}, items{id: {id, m, s (slide), k text|image|shape|line, x, y, w, h, r, z, ph?, …}}, ghosts{decks, slides}, tombs{id: deletedAt} }`. Decks merge in parts (`m`: title, aspect, theme, footer; `tm`: "something inside changed", max) and slides too (`m`: order, layout, transition, hidden, background; `nm`: notes; `tm` max); items LWW by `m`; equal clocks → larger canonical JSON (`tests/slides.test.js`). **PowerPoint (.pptx), no schema change:** `slides/pptx.js` (`OrosSlidesPPTX`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/slides-pptx.test.js`; ZIP = `atelier/zip.js`, loaded read-only). `write(data, deckId, media, {prompts})` → `{bytes, out:{slides, pictures, missing}}`: 1 slide unit = 6858 EMU (16:9 = 12192000 × 6858000, 4:3 = 9144000 × 6858000); one slide layout per Slides layout (cSld name = the English layout name) with real placeholders (title → `type=title`; sub → `subTitle idx 1`; body/body2/cap/cap2/quote → `body idx 2–6`; img → `pic idx 7`); theme1 = the deck theme as `name="orOS <id>"` (dk1 fg, lt1 bg, dk2 mu, lt2 sf, accent1–3 a1–a3, major/minor font = tf/ff), role colours as `schemeClr` (fg tx1, bg bg1, mu tx2, sf bg2, a1–a3 accent1–3) and theme fonts as `+mj-lt`/`+mn-lt`, so Slides' own files reopen with roles intact (docProps/app.xml `Application` = "orOS Slides" + that theme name are the marker); per paragraph `sz` = levelSize(fs, l) × 0.54 pt, bullets `buChar •` / `buAutoNum arabicPeriod` with marL/indent as dk.js draws them, spcAft = 0.35 × size, insets = dk.js INS; title runs written bold, quote italic (dk.js draws them so; dropped again on read); fit → `normAutofit`, fit false → `noAutofit`; pictures as the visible part (frame ∩ drawn picture, turned round the frame centre) + `srcRect`, rad → `roundRect` adj; notes slides + a notes master (theme2); hidden → `show="0"`; tr none/fade/slide/push/zoom → none/fade/cover/push/zoom. The deck footer is not written. `read(zip, {labels, parseXml})` → plan (DOMParser; any `<!DOCTYPE`/`<!ENTITY` refused before parsing; external relationships never followed; ≤ 300 slides, ≤ 80 items per slide, media ≤ 60 MB each): placeholder positions and text styles inherited slide → layout (idx first, then type) → master → txStyles/defaultTextStyle, clrMap + lumMod/lumOff/tint/shade, normAutofit fontScale, `a:br` splits a paragraph, groups flattened, master/layout decoration as locked items, a background picture as a locked full-slide picture, roles from ph type/idx (two bodies → body/body2), the Slides layout = the smallest whose roles hold them (none → blank, items stay free), the layout's missing placeholders added empty; dt/ftr/sldNum/hdr placeholders dropped; charts/tables/SmartArt/OLE/video/audio → a dashed text box with the localised name (a table keeps its rows as text); other presets → nearest rect/ellipse; custGeom without text skipped. Foreign `noAutofit` is ignored (Slides clips overflow, PowerPoint does not). `build(plan, assets, now, newId)` → a NEW deck through `normDeck/normSlide/normItem`; a crop becomes fill + zm/ox/oy (one scale, never stretched). io.js stores every picture with `designkit/assets.js importFile`, toast counts what was lost.
- **SLIDES v1, wave 24 fields (no version bump; all optional, absent = old behaviour, so old decks load and canonicalise byte-identical, `tests/slides-wave24.test.js`).** Slide `td` (transition length ms, 100–5000, stored only when set; default 450; part of the slide's `m` part). `tr` adds `wipe`. Item kinds add `table` (`tb {rows [[cell ≤ 400 chars, multiline]] ≤ 20 × 10, hd (header row, default true; false stored as absence), bd (banded), ln all|h|none, ac (header colour, default t:a1), fs 8–200 (default 28)}`, plus `ff`, `fc` (default t:fg), `fill`, `st` (default t:mu) / `sw` 2; `r` always 0) and `chart` (`ch {t col|bar|line|pie|donut|scatter, rows [[≤ 60 chars]] ≤ 31 × 9 (first row series names, first column categories), ttl?, lg false?, by r|c?}`; `r` 0). Any item: `g` (group id: the items of ONE slide sharing it form a group; one level; a lone `g` is no group; copies get fresh ids via `freshGroups`) and `an` (entrance: `{e appear|fade|fly|zoom, o (order key, POS_RE), d b|l|r|t (fly only), w w|a (absent = on click), du ms 100–5000 (absent = 500; never on appear), dl ms ≤ 10000, p true (text only: bullets one by one)}`; group members carry the same `an`). Everything new lives inside the item / slide, so it merges by the existing clocks (LWW by `m`; slide `m` part): no new merge path, no new tombstones, no idle uploads. `normItem` drops anything else.
- **Slides wave 24 decisions.** Animation order = `an.o` key (posBetween), ties broken by group, then id; moving a unit rewrites only that unit's key unless two keys are equal (two devices), then the slide is renumbered (`moveAnim`). Playback (`slides/anim.js` `OrosSlidesAnim`, pure): PowerPoint semantics — step 0 = effects "with / after the previous" before the first click (they wait for the transition to end), "with" joins the current group, "after" starts when it ends, delays count from there; bullets one by one = one effect per non-empty paragraph (first keeps the start, the rest on click). Frames: `objects.js` `SL.renderFrame` draws item by item through designkit `render.drawItem` (hidden items skipped, hidden / moving paragraphs filtered by run `p`), fade / zoom through an offscreen canvas, fly as a translation; plan + layout cached per data object. `designkit/show.js` 1.2.0 (backwards compatible for Atelier): `steps(i)`, `renderSlide(i, c, w, h, t, step)`, `live(i, t, step)`, `duration(i)`, `wipe`, `onChange(state)`, `tools`; Previous goes back one build, from the first build to the previous slide fully built; state adds `step, steps, blank, el, paused`; a dialog open over the show keeps its keys. prefers-reduced-motion: builds and transitions show at once. Charts: dk.js `chartSpec` (theme colours, slide background, ×0.45 of the frame, 3× raster) → sheetkit `chartModel` + `chartSVG` (the Spreadsheet engine, read-only) → canvas, keyed `hash64(spec).png` so designkit treats it as an image (`SL.getImage` / `SL.loadImage`; PDF, PNG and PowerPoint use the same picture). Tables: one shrink factor for the whole table (`tableFit`), cells as designkit text boxes. PowerPoint: tables ↔ `a:tbl`, groups ↔ `p:grpSp` (placeholders stay out of groups; read: the outermost group, and a shape's own fill + text pair, become `g`), charts → a picture (one way), `td` ↔ `spd` fast ≤ 350 / slow ≥ 800 (read also `p14:dur`), wipe ↔ `p:wipe` (split / strips read as wipe), entrances ↔ `p:timing` (presets 1 Appear, 2 Fly In subtype 1/2/4/8, 10 Fade, 53 Zoom; other entrances read as fade; exit / emphasis / paths dropped; paragraph targets ↔ `an.p` + `bldP build="p"`). Phone remote (`slides/remote.js`): `remote-link.js` ns `oros-slides-remote`, one phone, Allow on the host, join link `?open=slides#slides-remote=<code>`; host → phone `{t:"st", on, end, n, c, left, blank, title, notes ≤ 5000, next, el, paused}` (snapshot), phone → host only `hi`, `leave` and `a` ∈ next|prev|first|black|white (`cmd`); both sides validate (`adopt`). Video recording of the show was not built.
  - Deep link (0.58.01): one receiver `__orosOpenAt("slides", target)` in `slides/app.js`: `{outline, title}` (another app, e.g. Mind Map; plain text in the Outline view's format) opens the "new presentation from an outline" theme picker, nothing is created until a theme is picked; `{deck, slide}` (universal search) opens that deck/slide. Targets wait until the fonts are loaded.
  - Deletes (R17): tombs max-merged; a deck lives while one of its clocks is after its tomb, a slide also needs to be after its deck's tomb, an item after its own, its slide's and its deck's tombs. Deleted decks and slides stay as small `ghosts` (no notes, no items) so the merge stays associative.
  - Pictures are not in the slice: designkit assets `/internal/Assets/<sha256>.<jpg|png>` on the orOS disk, synced per file by Vault Drive.
- **PUBDOMAIN v1** (no slice, no synced key): nothing is synced. The rules table lives in code (`pubdomain/rules.js`, `window.orosPD`, `VERSION: "1.0.0"`): 21 `COUNTRIES` rows `{ id, n: { en, el }, term, anon, old?, us?, law, src, v, notes }`, every rule "life + N" (public domain on 1 January of death year + N + 1); rows with `v: 0` are shown as "check the source".
- **PIXEL v1** (slice `pixel`, key `oros-pixel-data`): `{ ver, items[{id, m, name (≤ 40, default the seed), f{s (seed), n 8|12|16, p (palette id), b 0|1 (colour background), px ("" = unedited, else n×n digits 0–7)}}] sorted by id, tombs{id: deletedAt} sorted }`. Faces are stored as recipes, not pictures: the same seed gives the same face; `px` equal to the generated face is stored as "". Merge: LWW per item (newer `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON); tombs max; a tomb ≥ `m` hides the item, a newer edit resurrects (`tests/pixel.test.js`).
- **ATELIER v1:** a designkit DOC (units are points; screen designs 1 px = 1 pt, print designs `setup.unit: "mm"`, bleed 3 mm). Item base types: text/shape/icon → `rect`, photo → `img`, line → `line`. Extras in `ax` (defaults omitted, canonical key order): `k` text|shape|icon|photo|line; `bg` (locked page background item, z −1e9); `fc`/`sc` fill/stroke colours (stroke width is the base `sw`); `g` gradient; `shp`/`rd` shape and roundness (photos use `shp` as mask); `ico` Tabler id; text `tx` (≤5000), `font`, `size`, `b`, `i`, `u`, `caps`, `al`, `lh`, `tr`, `tfx` (effect), `cv` (curve); photo `adj`, `flt`, `flh`, `flv`; line heads `as`/`ae`; `cr` credit. A model without the extension drops `ax` (Layout unaffected). Package `.orosdesign` = an OBF bundle: content.json `{kind:"oros-atelier-package", ver:1, doc}` + `media/<asset or clip id>` + thumbnail (older JSON `{…, assets}` still opens); import always makes a NEW doc with fresh stamps and verifies each asset hash.
- **ATELIER v1, wave 45 fields (no version bump; absent = old behaviour).** `ax.k` adds `table` and `chart` (base type `rect`). Table: `ax.tb {rows [[cell ≤ 400, multiline]] ≤ 30 × 10 (rectangular, padded), hd 0 (only when the header row is off), hc 1 (bold first column), bd 1 (banded), ln all|h|none|box (default all, omitted), ac header colour (default #2b4c7e), bf band colour (default #eef2f7), cf cell fill, cw [int 1–100] (only when not all equal)}`, plus `ax.font` (≠ sans), `ax.size` (≠ 24), `ax.al` l|c|r (≠ l), `ax.fc` text colour, `ax.sc` + base `sw` lines. Chart: `ax.ch {t col|bar|line|pie|donut|scatter, rows [[cell ≤ 60, single line]] ≤ 31 × 9, ttl ≤ 100, lg 0 (legend off), by r|c (absent = auto), tc text colour (≠ #1f2328), co [≤ 8 hex] (all valid or none)}`, plus `ax.fc` background (absent = see-through) and `ax.size` label size (absent = auto). Normalisers in `atelier/objects.js` (pure, shared by ax.js and the UI). Old clients drop items whose `ax.k` they don't know (normAx → null), so tables/charts are invisible on a device that has not updated, and if that device saves the design before updating, its stripped copy (same `m`, canonically larger) can win the merge and remove them — accepted while the PWA updates itself; documented in Help Limits.
- **ATELIER v1, AC3 fields (Canva PowerPoint fidelity, 4.32.00; R39, absent = old behaviour).** Text item `ext.fam` = `uf_<16 hex>`: an own font file (designkit/fonts.js, `/internal/Fonts/<sha256>.ttf`) drawn instead of `ax.font`, which stays the stand-in (Fontsource match or sans/serif/mono) for older copies and devices without the file; it counts only when this device registered it from the design's list (`AX.famOf`), so a missing file falls back to `ax.font`. The list is `setup.ext.fonts = [{id, name ≤ 60, fb sans|serif|mono, r, b?, i?, bi?}]` as in LY-FONT (`AX.docFonts` keeps valid entries, `AX.useDocFonts` registers them with `asset:<file>` URLs; `AT.draw.fontKeys(doc)` calls it before every draw / export). Every font change goes through `AX.setFont(it, id)`: an own id sets `ext.fam` (text only; tables keep `ax.font`), any other id sets `ax.font` and drops `ext.fam` (and an empty `ext`); `fonts.js`, `recipesteps.js` (`font`) and `magicdesign.js` use it; `commands.js` (`textstyle`, which only takes built-in and Fontsource ids, and `brand`, `dropOwnFont`) drops `ext.fam` the same way. `AX.fontOf(it)`, `AX.fontKeyOf(ax, it)` and `textStyle(ax, it)` resolve the drawn family. Text item `ext.kern` = 1: pair kerning (LY-KERN) in layout (style `ext.kern`), on the canvas (letter by letter, `draw.js paintRun`), in the PDF (a kerned pair starts a piece shifted by the kerning, `pdfout.js run`) and on a web page (`dx` per letter, `webout.js tspan`); set on every text the PowerPoint import makes, new text keeps the old behaviour. PDF: a face whose file has PostScript outlines (`text.faceParts(key)[i].cff`, "OTTO") is never embedded (`faceFor` → null, the element becomes a picture at the export dpi). Web page: text in an own font is always a picture (`kindOf` → `raster`), because the font's licence may not allow handing out its file. `.orosdesign` packages carry the design's own font files as `media/<sha256>.ttf` (`ownFontFiles`) and import them with `fonts.put(name, blob, {cff: true})` (hash checked); older Atelier copies ignore them. `designkit/fonts.js`: `check`, `importFile` and `put` take `{cff: true}` (Atelier only) to keep PostScript-outline fonts; such a file is never listed by `library()` (Layout's library stays TrueType only).
- **ATELIER v1, AC3b import rules (Canva PowerPoint fidelity, no new fields).** `pptx.js textOf` returns blocks: paragraphs in one look (font, face, size, b, i, u, caps, al, lh, tr, fc, op; the first non-empty run of each paragraph counts) stay one text item, a paragraph in another look starts the next item. Blank paragraphs stay in their block, except those that close a block before a change of look: they become the next block's `gap` (points, the block's own line spacing each). `build` stacks one box's items baseline to baseline: the next item's first baseline = the last baseline above + `gap` + one line at the next item's spacing (`size · lh / 100`), as PowerPoint sets exact spacing, then anchors the whole stack (`anchorTo`). A rotated box stays one item in its first look (the stack is laid out upright). A design past PowerPoint's largest slide (`p:sldSz` side ≥ 51117500 EMU, Canva's cap) comes scaled into that slide and centred: `unbox` takes the largest unrotated non-text element that spans the slide's width (or height) and that the margins centre as the design's page, moving every item with it; without such an element the slide stays as it is.
- **ATELIER v1, AC3b fields (Canva PowerPoint fidelity, second part; R39, absent = old behaviour).** Text item `ext.runs = [{n, b?, i?, fam?}]` (at most 400): pieces of `ax.tx` in order (the line breaks count) in another weight, slant or own font (`fam` a registered `uf_` id); they count only when their lengths add up to the text (`AX.runsOf`), so an older edit that changed the text leaves them out. `AX.textLayout` turns them into designkit/text.js character styles (`storyOf(ax, it, cs)`), so the canvas, the PDF (per piece font) and layout all follow them; `AX.textWidth` lays them out on one line. The in-place editor keeps them in step with typing (`AX.editRuns`: the changed stretch is cut from the runs it covered, what is typed joins the run it was typed in); `AX.setFont` and the Assistant's `textstyle` / `brand` drop the runs' `fam` (and runs left with nothing). A web page draws text with an own-font run as a picture. The PowerPoint import makes runs from pieces of a paragraph that differ from the box's look only in weight, slant or typeface (another size or colour keeps the box's look). Shape and page background `ext.gs = {st: [[pos 0..1, "#rrggbb"] ×2-10, in order], r?: 1, c?: [x, y]}`: a gradient's own stops, radial (`r`, centred at `c` as parts of the box, reaching the farthest corner) or linear along `ax.g.ang`, over `ax.g`, which stays the two-colour stand-in; it counts only while its end colours are `ax.g`'s (`AX.gradOf`), so a gradient changed with Atelier's own controls shows as changed. Drawn on the canvas (`draw.js gradient`), web page (`radialGradient` / every stop) and PowerPoint (`a:path circle` + `fillToRect`, every stop); the PDF draws gradients as pictures as before. The import keeps `ext.gs` for more than two stops or a `path` gradient.
- **ATELIER v1, My style (AC4, `atelier/style.js`, `window.AtelierStyle`, pure).** What the person's designs have in common, per kind of design told apart by page shape (`kindOf(w, h)` on width / height: < 0.42 bookmark, < 0.6 9:16, < 0.72 A portrait, < 0.88 4:5, < 1.15 square, < 1.9 16:9, else banner; `commands.js styleKind` is a copy, kept equal by a test). `profile(docs, now, nameOf) → {v: 1, at, kinds: {kind: {n, pages, fonts: {title|subtitle|body: [{id, fb, name?, share}] ≤ 3}, colours ≤ 6, backgrounds ≤ 4, sizes: {role: % of the short side, median}, align, caps 0..1, lh, sum}}}`: on each page a text's role comes from its size against the page's largest text (≥ 75 % title, ≥ 40 % subtitle, else body), fonts and text colours are weighted by characters, an own font (`ext.fam`, `uf_` id) counts under its id with its stand-in (`fb`) and the name the design gives it; `sum` (`summary()`) is the short object the Assistant reads (font names, never asset ids or text). Worked out on the device from the library (`brand.js`, 3 s after `open` / `change`, only when the count or newest change differs) and kept only in localStorage `oros-atelier-style`, never synced. `AtelierCommands.outline(doc, style)` adds `style` (the summary for the design's kind) when given a profile; `add` of a text without `font` / `size` / `c` takes `env.look(doc, role)` (≤ 40 characters title, else body: font with `ext.fam` for an own font, size from the share of the short side, the main text colour; the box height follows the size). Shown in the Brand kit panel as "My style" (colours tap into the brand kit).
- **AT-DISK · Atelier designs on the orOS disk (4.57.00, wave 2 of the documents-on-disk plan; core.js section 3b on `designkit/docstore.js`, as LY-DISK).** With the orOS disk, every design is `/internal/Atelier/<name> · <doc id>.orosdesign`, its text the JSON package `{kind: "oros-atelier-package", ver: 1, doc}` (the same that Import reads; no `assets`: pictures stay once in `/internal/Assets`). Old slice `atelier` (`oros-atelier-data`) = legacy copy (pulls merged in, never grown, carries deletions); first load writes `/internal/Rescue/atelier-data-<ms>.json`; journal `oros-atelier-open`; index `oros-atelier-index` (`tx` = the text boxes' words in page order, ≤ 1000). Folders (`atelier-folders`), brand kit, Canva map, My style and the Assistant's undo records keep naming designs by id and are unchanged (every design is still in memory). `AT.keepStored(ids)` keeps the designs of an import batch only once stored (on the disk written and read back, else saved in localStorage; a full storage stops the batch and drops the design that did not fit); `AT.openStored` opens a design's own file instead of importing a copy; Import › From a folder in Files leaves `Files › Atelier` out. **Not-used check:** a picture, video or sound counts as used while localStorage (apart from Vault/disk/sync bookkeeping and Atelier's index/journal), any design in memory, or any document file names it: `/internal/Layout`, `/internal/Atelier`, `/internal/Rescue` and everything of theirs in `/internal/.trash` (depth ≤ 3). A file that cannot be read or is over 64 MB means "cannot tell": nothing is offered or deleted. When designs are deleted with their pictures, those designs (in memory, their files here or in the Trash, and inside rescue copies) do not count; the delete dialog waits at most 15 s for the check. Readers: `atelier/search.js` and the Assistant (`EDIT_SRC.atelier` `disk`, `pkg`, `list: "docs"`, keeping its folders and brand kit). Tests `tests/atelier-disk.test.js`.
- **ATELIER v1, many files at once (AC5, 4.47.00, `io.js importMany` / `importDisk`).** Home › Import › From files takes several files (`orosDialog.openFiles`, else a `multiple` input) and `.zip` files whose `.orosdesign` / `.pptx` entries are imported (`__MACOSX/` and dot files left out; since 4.61.01 the zip is read piece by piece with the shared `designkit/zipin.js`, so no size cap beyond the zip format's 4 GB without ZIP64). From a folder in Files browses the orOS disk's folders (Trash left out) and imports every `.orosdesign` / `.pptx` in the chosen folder and its subfolders (depth ≤ 4, sorted by path). At most 500 files per batch, one after another, each through the same import as one file. While batching, `AT.addDoc(d, true)` adds without opening and the per-file toasts are silenced (`say`); Home re-renders and one toast gives the count of new designs and of files that brought none. One file alone still opens its design as before. Files picked through the shell's dialog are made in the shell window, so a picked file is told from a Files-folder entry by what it can do (`arrayBuffer` + `slice`), never by `instanceof Blob`/`File` against the app frame (the AC5 release checked `instanceof Blob`: every multi-file pick through the shell failed as one "can't be opened").
- **Atelier wave 45 decisions.** Charts are drawn by the Spreadsheet engine (`spreadsheet/sheetkit.js` chartModel/chartSVG, the same one Slides wave 24 uses); an empty top-left cell makes the first row series names even when they look like numbers. The SVG becomes a cached bitmap per chart + resolution step (`atelier/objui.js`, async; exports, film and Present await `AT.charts.prepare`). Tables lay out with ONE shrink factor for the whole table (binary search, `AX.tableLayout`). PDF (`atelier/pdfout.js`, pure): text is real PDF text in the embedded Noto / Fontsource faces (Identity-H, one font per face part, runs split by part), shapes/lines/tables are vector paths, everything else is a picture of that element only (photos, icons, charts, gradients); a text whose blur passes (glow, soft shadow) can't be vector is a picture of the blurred passes under real text; a text with a glyph no face covers (emoji) is a picture; `Whole pages as pictures` keeps the old raster PDF. PPTX: tables and charts are pictures. Template library: 50 templates (`atelier/templates.js` 14 + `atelier/templates-more.js` 36), each with `cat` (13 categories) and EN/EL `tags`; search folds case/accents/final sigma; previews are drawn lazily (IntersectionObserver, a few per frame) and cached as PNG data URLs for the session; home shows a 12-card sampler (one per category first) with `Show all`.
- **HEALTH v1** (slice `health`, key `oros-health-data`; logic in `health/core.js`):
  - `{ ver: 1, en: [entry] by id, ty: [kind] by id, set: settings | null, tombs: { "en:<id>" | "ty:<id>": ts } }`
  - entry `{ id, m, t, at, v: [int], c, a, p, n, g: [tag] }`: t = kind (bp, wt, gl, sl, hr, tp, o2 or an own `c…` id); at = ms; v in storage units (grams, tenths of mg/dL, hundredths of °C, minutes asleep + quality 0–5, own kinds × 1000); c glucose context 0–4; a arm; p position; n note ≤ 500; g ≤ 6 tags.
  - kind `{ id, m, n, u, dc, h, lo, hi, lo2, hi2, r }`: built-in rows exist only once edited; own target in storage units or null; r ≤ 4 reminder minutes.
  - settings `{ m, h (mm), wu kg|lb, gu mgdl|mmol, tu c|f, nm, fw }`.
  - Deleting an own kind tombstones the kind and its readings (Undo restores both). A reading of an own kind deleted on another device stays stored but is not shown.
  - **Wave 2 (medicines and symptoms)**, five more collections, same LWW + tombstones (`"md:" | "dl:" | "rf:" | "sy:" | "sk:"`); older data loads with them empty. `{ …, md: [medicine], dl: [dose log], rf: [refill], sy: [symptom], sk: [symptom kind] }`:
    - medicine `{ id ([a-z0-9]{1,20}, no dash), m, n ≤ 60, s strength ≤ 30, f tab|cap|liq|drop|inh|spray|inj|cream|patch|supp|sach|other, q dose (hundredths of the form's unit), k d|w|n|p (every day / weekdays `wd` bit 0 = Monday / every `ev` 2–90 days from `sd` / as needed, no times), tm ≤ 8 minutes, wd, ev, sd, ed ("" = open), rm 0|1, sk stock (hundredths at `sa` ms; −1 = not counted), sa, pk pack (hundredths, default 30 units), rw warn days 0–60 (default 7), ar stopped 0|1, ca created ms, nt ≤ 500, ps [{u, k, tm, wd, ev}] ≤ 12 }`. `ps` = earlier schedules, each in force up to its last day `u`: editing times / days of a medicine that started before today pushes the old schedule with `u` = yesterday (once per day), so past days keep their times (`withHistory`). Stop = `ar` 1 + `ed` today; again = `ar` 0, a past `ed` cleared.
    - dose log `{ id, m, md, d, tm, s t|s|z, ta ms, q (taken only), zu (snooze only) }`. Scheduled: id = `doseKey` = `<md>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM` (enforced by the normalizer); as needed: `tm` −1, id `<md>-YYYYMMDD-p<random>`, taken only. States (`doseState`): taken, skipped, snoozed, upcoming, due, late (30 min past, today), missed (earlier day). A dose before `ca` is never late, reminded or counted unless marked. Marks at a time no longer in the schedule still show (`extra`).
    - refill `{ id, m, md, at, a }`; stock = `sk` + refills since `sa` − taken doses (`ta` ≥ `sa`); typing a new count sets `sk`/`sa`. Days left = stock / average use per day (`perDay`); low when ≤ `rw` days (as needed: less than one dose).
    - adherence = taken / counted, counted = marked or at least 30 min past (`adherence(d, md, from, to, now)`).
    - symptom `{ id, m, k, at, i 1–10, n, g }`; symptom kind `{ id, m, n, h }`: built-ins `ha na dz ft pn cg br pl` (rows only once hidden), own ids `s…` with a name; deleting an own kind tombstones its entries (Undo).
    - Shared: Today rows (open doses as tasks, low stock as top lines, `__orosOpenHealth("meds")`), Calendar opt-in feed `lbl-feed-meds` (`calendarOn`), search hits `{med}` / `{sym}`, report + CSV sections. Tests: `tests/health-meds.test.js`.
  - **Wave 3 (Record: Medical ID, appointments, vaccinations, documents)**, six more collections with the same LWW + tombstones (`"al:" | "cn:" | "ec:" | "vx:" | "ap:" | "dc:"`) and `pf` (profile, LWW as a whole like `set`); older data loads with them empty / null:
    - allergy `{ id, m, n ≤ 60, sv 0–3 (unknown / mild / moderate / severe), r reaction ≤ 120, nt }`; condition `{ id, m, n ≤ 60, sd (date or ""), nt }`; emergency contact `{ id, m, n ≤ 60, rl relation ≤ 30, ph ≤ 40 (digits, spaces, + ( ) - . /, must hold a digit), ci (Contacts id it was picked from, or "") }`. A contact is copied when picked (no live link: the Medical ID must still work if the contact is later deleted).
    - profile `pf { m, nm, bd (birth date or ""), bt "" | A+ … O-, od 0|1|2 (not set / yes / no organ donor), nt ≤ 500, sm 0|1 (show current medicines, default 1) }`.
    - vaccination `{ id, m, n ≤ 60, d given, nx next dose ("" or after d), rm 0|1 (0 when no nx), lt lot ≤ 30, nt }`. Only the newest entry per name (case-insensitive) with an `nx` is open (`vaxOpen`), so "Given again" (a new entry with the same name) silences the old one without editing it.
    - appointment `{ id, m, dr doctor ≤ 60, sp specialty ≤ 40 (one of dr / sp required), pl place ≤ 120 (Maps link via `__orosOpenMapsQuery`), at ms, du minutes 0–720, rm −1 (off) | minutes before 0–10080, nt }`.
    - document `{ id ("d" + [a-z0-9], 6–40), m, k lab|rx|img|ltr|oth, n ≤ 80, d, nt, sc? }`: `sc` = up to 6 file NAMES `YYYYMMDD-<docId>-<random>.(jpg|pdf)` (`AT_RE`), sorted, key absent when none. Files on the orOS disk at `/internal/Health/<name>` (Vault Drive syncs them, not the slice), same rules as Garage receipts: photos redrawn on a canvas (≤ 1600 px, JPEG 0.8, white background, so no EXIF / location), PDFs must start with `%PDF-` and be ≤ 10 MB; files of a cancelled editor, removed from a row, or of a deleted row (after the Undo window, when no row names them) are removed. Files are only shown as blobs in a viewer or downloaded, never run.
    - Medical ID (`medicalId(d, now)`): profile, age, allergies (severe first), conditions, contacts and current medicines (`currentMeds`: not stopped, in course today) when `sm`. Full-screen view (big text, `tel:` buttons, screen wake lock where allowed) and a printable wallet card (front / back, print window → PDF). Optional QR (shared `qr/qr-encode.js`, ECL M) holds `idText`: plain text ≤ 700 UTF-8 bytes; when longer it drops notes, then medicines, conditions, contacts, allergies from the end (at least one allergy and one contact kept), marking cuts with "+n". Nothing in the QR is a link.
    - Shared: Today rows (appointments `ap@<id>` as events today … horizon; vaccines due within −30 … horizon days as tasks `vx@<id>`), Calendar opt-in feed `lbl-feed-appts` (`recordOn`), search hits `{appt}` / `{vax}` / `{doc}` / `{al}` / `{cn}`, deep links `health:appts` / `health:vax` / `health:record`. Phone reminders: `alarmsBetween(d, from, to)` (doses, appointments, vaccines; keys equal to the shell's). Decisions: no doctor directory, no lock-screen Medical ID (a web app cannot reach it), allergies and documents stay out of the doctor report for now. Tests: `tests/health-record.test.js`.
- **BUDGET v1** (slice `budget`, key `oros-budget-data`): `{ ver, tx[{id, m, d "2026-10-09", a (integer cents > 0), k "o"|"i", c (category id | ""), n (note)}], cats[{id, m, k, name ("" = ready name), col 0–8}], bud[{id (expense category id | "all"), m, a (cents, 0 = no limit)}], rec[{id, m, k, a, c, n, f "w"|"m"|"y", s (first date), e (last date | "")}], acc[{id, m, n (name), o (starting balance, cents, may be < 0), col 0–8}], xfer[{id, m, d, a, f (from account), t (to account ≠ f), n}], set{m, cur}, tombs{"tx:<id>"|"cat:<id>"|"rec:<id>"|"acc:<id>"|"xfer:<id>": deletedAt} }`; `tx` and `rec` carry an optional `ac` (account id), written only when set (accounts + transfers since phase 2; a deleted account leaves its entries without one; transfers are never income or expense, only balances: `accBalances()`), each list sorted by id. Merge: per collection LWW by id (newer `m`, equal `m` → larger canonical JSON); tombs max-merged, a tomb ≥ `m` hides the record (delete wins ties, a newer edit resurrects); limits have no tombs; `set` LWW by `m` (default `{m: 0, cur: "EUR"}`) (`tests/budget.test.js`).
  - **Forward compatibility (since 0.48.x):** a field this version does not know rides along on its item and on `set` (name `[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}`, value string ≤ 500 / finite number / boolean, at most 16 per item, sorted by name), and a top-level array this version does not know (name `[a-z]{2,8}`) is merged as a collection of `{id, m, …}` with the same LWW and tombstones `"<name>:<id>"`. In-place edits keep these fields. So a newer Budget can add accounts or transfers without an older device stripping them. Rule for later versions: a new collection's tombstone prefix is its own key; new item fields stay flat.
  - Ready categories have language-free ids (`o-groc` … `o-other`, `i-salary` … `i-other`); a recurring occurrence gets a fixed id, so two devices that create the same occurrence create the same entry.
  - **Linked entries (BR-B3, Invoices Novus wave 2).** An entry another app keeps here has id `l-<src>-<key>` (`budget/links.js` `txId`) and the flat extra `src` (e.g. `"invoices"`); its `m` is the source record's `m`, so two devices write the same entry. Nothing else in the format changes; an older Budget carries `src` along as an unknown field.
  - **Bank statements and rules (since the bank-import wave, after 1.97.00).** Two new collections, both LWW by id with their own tombstones: `prof[{id, m, ac (Budget account | ""), ca, ccr, cd, cdb, cm, cp, cs (0-based CSV columns: amount, credit, date, debit, extra text, description, debit/credit marker; -1 = none), dec ("," | "."), df ("dmy" | "mdy" | "ymd"), enc ("auto" | "utf-8" | "windows-1253" | "iso-8859-7" | "windows-1252"), inv (bool, reverse signs), n (name ≤ 30), sep (";" "," tab "|"), sig (folded CSV header joined by "|", or "ofx:<ACCTID>" / "camt:<IBAN>", ≤ 400)}]` (`prof:<id>`) and `rule[{id, m, c (category), hi, k ("o"|"i", the category's kind), lo (amount range in cents, 0 = open), nt (note ≤ 80), py (rename to ≤ 60), q (description contains ≤ 60)}]` (`rule:<id>`; a rule needs `q` or a range). Both write their fields in name order after `id, m`, exactly what an older Budget's carry-forward of an unknown collection writes, and `prof`/`rule` sit after `xfer` in name order (where an older version puts unknown collections), so old and new devices produce the same canonical JSON (tested). Entries get three optional flat fields, written only when set and kept in name order with any other extra: `fit` (bank transaction id ≤ 80: OFX FITID, CAMT AcctSvcrRef / NtryRef / EndToEndId), `ot` (the bank's own text ≤ 140, what rules match and duplicates compare), `src` (`"bank"`, the source marker). An imported entry is a normal entry otherwise (category, note, account, totals, limits, export).
  - **Envelopes, goals, subscriptions, currencies, receipts (wave 10, after the bank-import wave).** Two new collections, LWW by id with their own tombstones, keys in name order after `id, m` (what an older Budget's carry-forward of an unknown collection writes); all new collections sit after `xfer` in name order: `asg, goal, prof, rule`. `asg[{id "<yyyymm>-<category id | none>", m, a (signed cents), c (category id, "" = uncategorised), mk "YYYY-MM"}]` (`asg:<id>`): one assignment per envelope and month; the id is fixed by `mk` + `c` (checked), so two devices that assign the same envelope converge on one value by LWW, never a sum; a move between envelopes rewrites both cells. `goal[{id, m, ac (account id | ""), col 0–8, d (target date | ""), n (≤ 40), sv (cents put aside by hand), t (target cents > 0)}]` (`goal:<id>`). New optional flat fields, written only when set and kept in name order with any other extra (an older version carries them untouched, same canonical JSON, tested): entry `oc` (3-letter currency ≠ main) + `oa` (cents as typed; dropped unless both are valid; `a` stays the main-currency amount every total, limit and envelope reads, so an older device sees correct totals) and `rc` (receipt file names, ONE string of ≤ 3 space-separated names `YYYYMMDD-<entry id>-<random>.jpg|pdf`, flat on purpose: an older version strips arrays); recurring `nd` (reminder lead 0–30 days, 0 = on the day); account `cur` (its own currency; starting balance in it); transfer `ta` (cents that reached the to-account, in its currency, when the currencies differ); `set.env` (true = envelope budgeting on) and `set.envs` ("YYYY-MM", the month it started; kept when switched off).
    - Envelope math (`budget/plan.js` `envMonth`, pure): per expense category and month, available = carry + assigned − spent; leftovers AND overspending roll into the same envelope next month (Actual Budget style). To be assigned (month M) = start cash + income from `envs` through M − assignments from `envs` through M, start cash = net worth at the end of the month before `envs`, floored at 0. Entries of a deleted category (or none) count under "Uncategorised"; a deleted category's assignments go back to To be assigned. Limits (`bud`) stay independent and are shown on each envelope.
    - Currencies: rates are Unit Converter's (shared fetcher `UnitsCore.fetchLatest` / `crossRate`, ONE device-local cache `oros-units-rates`), fetched only when Budget has something in another currency, at most every 6 h; offline the last cached rates are used and the dialog says so ("offline, the last saved"). The converted amount is stored at save time (editable, e.g. the bank's real charge), so totals never move with later rates; account balances are kept in each account's currency (`balancesFx`), net worth converts them at the current rates, also for past months (a stated limit). Bank / Stripe / Invoice Ninja imports still take the main currency only.
    - Receipts: files on the orOS disk under `/internal/Budget/Receipts` (Vault Drive moves them, never the slice); photos re-encoded on a canvas (long side 1600 px, JPEG 0.8: no EXIF), PDFs ≤ 10 MB kept only when they start with `%PDF-`; a deleted entry's files leave the disk after the Undo window if no entry names them. "Read the total from text" (`amountFromText`): the last total / ΣΥΝΟΛΟ / ΠΛΗΡΩΤΕΟ line, never a VAT line, else the largest amount; no OCR.
    - Subscriptions: recurring expenses with monthly / yearly cost and next charge (`subscriptions`). Reminders: shell engine `budgetCheckTick` (60 s throttle) reads `oros-budget-data` with Budget closed through `budget/plan.js` (loaded by the shell's index.html), `subsDue`: a recurring expense with `nd` whose next charge is `nd` days away or closer; dedup key `sub-<recId>-<yyyymmdd>`, from the device-local hour `oros-budget-prefs.nh` (default 9, −1 = off on this device); deep link `budget:sub:<recId>` → `__orosOpenAt("budget", {sub})` (Recurring › Subscriptions, the entry open).
    - Reports: `yearReport` (expenses per category per month of a year, chart + table) and `netWorthSeries` (sum of account balances at each month end, the current month ends today). Tests `tests/budget-plan.test.js`.
  - **Import ids.** `"b" + 2 × FNV-1a(key)` in base 36, key = `f|<account>|<FITID>` or `t|<account>|<date>|<signed cents>|<folded text>` plus the n-th occurrence of that key in the file: the same file into the same Budget account gives the same ids on every device (a second import adds nothing; sync never doubles), two identical purchases on one day stay two. A deleted imported entry's tombstone makes the row "Deleted here earlier" (unticked; ticking it re-adds it with a newer stamp).
  - **Core** `budget/bank.js` (`OrosBudgetBank`, pure, Node-loadable; `tests/budget-bank.test.js`): decode (BOM, strict UTF-8, XML/OFX charset, then a Greek-vs-Western single-byte sniff: Greek letters are runs of high bytes), CSV (quote-aware, separator by consistency, header row = first row as wide as most rows unless it already looks like data, column guess from EN/EL/DE/FR/ES header words and the cell types, balance columns never), amounts (`1.234,56`, `1,234.56`, `12,50-`, `(12.50)`, `DR`/`CR`, currency marks; the decimal mark is decided per column), dates (`dd/mm/yyyy`, `mm/dd/yyyy`, ISO, `yyyymmdd`, 2-digit years, QIF `'`, EN/EL month names; order guessed from values > 12), OFX 1.x SGML and 2.x XML, QIF, CAMT.052/053/054 by regex (namespace prefixes allowed; DBIT negative; a status other than BOOK is skipped). Plan statuses: `new`, `same` (that id is here), `dup` (FITID twin in the same account, or same account + date + kind + amount with similar text: equal, contained (≥ 4 chars), word Jaccard ≥ 0.5, or one side empty; each existing entry matches at most one row), `gone` (tombstoned), `skip` (no date / amount / zero / another currency / pending). Rules: `fold()` (lowercase, no accents, final ς → σ) contains, kind equal, `lo ≤ a ≤ hi`; the match with the longest `q` wins, then newer `m`, then id. A rule sets the category and the note `py || text` (+ " · " + `nt`). Re-run touches only uncategorised entries and rewrites the note only on an imported entry whose note is still its `ot`.
  - **More statement files and "already here another way" (BK-1, thread "Σύνδεσε το Budget με τράπεζες", Chris 2026-11-01 20:44 "Ναι σε όλα"; tests `tests/budget-bank-bk1.test.js`).** `parseMt940` (MT940/MT942: `:25:` account, `:60F:`/`:60M:` currency, `:61:` date + `C`/`D`/`RC`/`RD` (RD = a debit taken back: money in) + amount with decimal comma + bank reference after `//` (else the customer reference unless `NONREF`) as FITID, a reference seen twice in one file is dropped as FITID; `:86:` text: German `?20..?29`/`?32 ?33`, SWIFT `/NAME/ /REMI/`, else free text); `detectFormat` → `"mt940"` on `:20:` + `:61:<6 digits>`. PayPal activity CSV: `paypalMap(header)` (EN/EL/DE/ES column names, folded; needs date, currency, net, transaction id and gross or fee) turns the CSV path into format `"paypal"` (profile signature `"paypal"`, no column UI); `paypalItems(rows, start, map, home)`: amount = Net (income after PayPal's fee), FITID = Transaction ID, text = Name · Item Title; "General Currency Conversion" rows are folded into the payment they reference (Reference Txn ID) and the payment takes the converted amount in the Budget currency; skipped: Balance Impact Memo / holds and authorisations (`memo`), a status other than Completed (`pending`), card/bank deposits, withdrawals and bank transfers (`xfer`: money between PayPal and the person's own card or bank). Rows written from a PayPal file carry the flat extra `pp: 1` (budget.js `txBank` keeps it only as `1`). Plan `crossTwin` (after the plain duplicate check, each existing item matches at most one row, the row is `dup` + `dk`, unticked): `inv` = an income entry with `src "invoices"` (BR-B3) of the same amount within 10 days; `pp` = the same kind and amount within 4 days between a `pp: 1` entry and a bank row (any Budget accounts, also none) whose text has `paypal` / `pp *` / `pypl` (both orders: `ctx.pp` is set while a PayPal file is planned); `xfer` = with a Budget account chosen, a transfer (`xfer`) within 3 days that left it (expense, `a`) or reached it (income, `ta || a`). Viva: its monthly account statement is an .xls, read by the existing sheet → CSV path.
  - **UI** `budget/bankui.js` (`OrosBudgetBankUI`): More › Import bank statement (file picker via `orosDialog.openFile`, ≤ 8 MB, ≤ 5,000 rows, preview list capped at 300 rows), More › Rules. Writes only through budget.js (`addEntries` = one write + Undo with tombstones; `saveRule`, `deleteRule` + Undo, `saveProf` (by id, else same name; no write when nothing changed), `applyChanges` + Undo that skips entries changed again since). The uncategorised inbox is the list filter `inbox` (device-session only, like every filter): `src === "bank"` and no category, every month, an inline category select per row; a bar over the list links to it.
- **FITNESS v1** (slice `fitness`, key `oros-fitness-data`): `{ ver: 1, ex: [{ id, m, n, g, k, h }], pg: [{ id, m, n, days }], wo: [{ id, m, d, st, en, ti, p, pd, n, x: [{ e, tr, tr2, rest, s: [...] }] }], bm: [{ id: "2026-10-09", m, w, wa, ch, ar }], set: { m, wu, du, incU, incL, rest, hb } | null, tombs: { "<coll>:<id>": m } }`; all quantities are integers (grams, metres, millimetres, seconds). `mergeFit`: per collection LWW by `m` (equal `m`: larger canonical JSON), tombstones max-merged and a tomb ≥ `m` wins; `set` LWW as a whole.
  - **Wave 29 (supersets, progression programs, outdoor GPS):** optional fields, written only when set so older rows keep their canonical JSON: program item / workout entry `ln: 1` (linked to the next one: superset of 2, circuit of 3+; the last entry's link is ignored); workout entry `pk` (`"m|a|t1|t2|t3|l:<exercise>"`, the plan slot), `pr` (prescribed reps per working set), `am: 1` (last working set is "+"); workout `pl` (plan id) + `pp` (plan position it was started at), `g: { a: "walk"|"run"|"ride", ps: 0|1, sg: ["<segment>"] }`. New collection `pl: [{ id, m, n, tp: "531"|"gzclp"|"lin", rd (plate step, g), bb: 0|1, k (sessions done), tm{lift: g}, sl{"t1:x-squat": {w, lv 0–2, b, f}}, fl{lift: 1} }]`, LWW + `pl:<id>` tombs like the others; the `pl` key is left out of the slice while empty (data without programs keeps its old canonical form).
  - Shared pure cores (Node-tested in `tests/fitness-wave29.test.js`): `fitness/plan-core.js` (`OrosFitnessPlan`: templates 5/3/1 (TM %, warm-ups, "+" sets, deload, +1 step per 4-week cycle or −10% for a lift whose "+" set missed, optional BBB 5×10 @ 50%), GZCLP (T1 5×3+ → 6×2+ → 10×1+ → 85% reset; T2 3×10 → 3×8 → 3×6 → last 3×10 weight + 3 upper steps; T3 3×15+, +1 upper step at 25 reps), Linear 5×5 (A/B, +step on success, −10% after 3 misses in a row); `advance` only when `wo.pl === plan.id && wo.pp === plan.k`, so a workout counts once; rounding to `rd`; superset flow `groupsOf / flowOrder / nextAfter / restAfter / groupRest`: a group is run round by round and rests after the round with the last exercise's rest); `fitness/gps-core.js` (`OrosFitnessGps`: segments as delta-coded integer triples lat×1e6, lon×1e6, s since start in the polyline varint alphabet; distance and time summed per segment so pauses count in neither; splits per km / mile by interpolation; reuses Maps' `maps/tracks-core.js` unchanged for `distM`, the recording filter `accept`, Douglas-Peucker (finished tracks thinned to 2 m) and `writeGpx`); `fitness/wger.js` (`OrosFitnessWger`, see below).
  - Outdoor session: `watchPosition` (high accuracy) runs only on the device whose `oros-fitness-prefs.gps` is that workout; the live segment is written into the row every 10 s and on hide (sync paced as for any running workout); `Finish` puts distance and moving time into the single `x-run` / `x-walk` / `x-bike` set, so records, charts, CSV and Health Connect use them unchanged. GPX export = Maps' writer with `creator="orOS Workouts"`. Decision: no map tiles under the route preview (offline, no third-party request); the help says plainly that browsers may stop GPS when the screen is off.
  - Exercise pictures (wger.de, CC BY-SA): only on "Show picture"; search `/api/v2/exercise/search/?language=en&term=` (ready exercises by their English name) then `/api/v2/exerciseinfo/<id>/` for author and licence, shown next to the image with links. JSON direct from the browser, then (CORS refused) the Reader's `feeds/fetch.js` relay "web" op loaded by path (no relay change); images are plain `<img>` (the relay refuses images) and kept in Cache Storage `oros-fitness-pics` when the server allows CORS. Per-exercise result (or "none", asked again after 30 days) in device-local `oros-fitness-pics`, never synced.
- **BABY v1** (slice `baby`, key `oros-baby-data`, since 0.47.00): `{ ver, kids[{id, n, b, s, c, m}], ev[{id, k, t, ts, e?, ls?, rs?, cur?, cs?, sd?, ml?, x?, v?, tx?, m}], gr[{id, k, d, g?, l?, h?, m}], mk[{id, k, t, key?, tx?, d, nt?, m}], prefs{wu, tu, vu}, pm }`. Arrays sorted by id; a tombstone is `{id, m, del:1}` (delete wins equal m; a newer edit resurrects). Event types: feed, bottle, solid, sleep, diaper, pump, med, temp, bath, tummy, note. A running timer (feed, sleep) is an event without `e`; a running breast feed also has `cur` (side) and `cs` (segment start); `ls`/`rs` are banked seconds per side, `sd` the last side. Units stored metric (ml, g, mm, tenths of °C); `prefs` are display units only. Deleting a child tombstones the child and all its records. Restore from a JSON backup goes through `mergeBaby` (never removes). Core 1.1.0 (0.57.03) adds `readRem`, `reminderDue`, `reminderText`, `calendarRows`; slice unchanged.
  - Wave 34: a pump's length (1–180 min) is its end `e` (older builds already keep `e` on a non-timer event with e > ts, so nothing is lost; the CSV "minutes" column shows it). New list `st` = the family's milk stash (no kid): `{id, ml 1–1000, d pumped, w "f" fridge | "z" freezer, u use-by, s? "u" used | "x" thrown away, sd? that day, th? thawed day, tx?, m}`, per bag LWW + `{id, m, del: 1}` tombstones like every list (`core.normSt`, `mergeBaby`); the key sits between `mk` and `prefs` and is LEFT OUT while the merged list is empty, so a slice that never had a bag keeps its bytes (no upload at update). Use-by defaults (`core.useBy`, CDC guidance): fridge 4 days, freezer 6 months; `thaw` = to the fridge, use-by today + 1 (never later than before). Order (`stashBags`): fridge first, then earliest use-by, then oldest pumped; expired bags flagged, "soon" = use-by ≤ tomorrow. "Use" can log a breast-milk bottle (Undo toast with an extra action). Tests: `tests/baby-stash.test.js`.
- **FAMTREE v1:** `{ ver, trees[{id,m,name,home}], people[{id,m,tree,given,family,birthName,sex f|m|x|u,birth{d,q,place},death{d,q,place},dead,note,photo,contact,parents[{u,kind birth|adopted|foster|step}]}], unions[{id,m,tree,a,b,kind married|partner|divorced|unknown,start{d,q},end{d,q}}], tombs{} }`. Dates `YYYY | YYYY-MM | 2026-10-09` (year 1–2200), q `"" | abt | bef | aft`. Photos: canvas-re-encoded JPEG data URI ≤ 28,000 chars, all photos ≤ 1.4M chars. JSON file `{ app:"familytree", format:1, exported, trees, people, unions, tombs }`; import = allow-list rebuild + merge (restore is a merge).
  - GEDCOM (`.ged`, since 0.53.02): import = GEDCOM 5.5.1 / 7.0 (UTF-8, UTF-16, ANSEL, ANSI/Windows-1252), ≤ 15 MB, always into ONE NEW tree named after the file; reads INDI NAME (TYPE birth/maiden → birthName), SEX, BIRT, DEAT/BURI/CREM (→ dead), NOTE (inline or record), FAMC+PEDI; FAM HUSB/WIFE/CHIL (+_FREL/_MREL), MARR (→ married), DIV (→ divorced), else kind unknown; dates ABT/CAL/EST/BET/FROM → abt, BEF/TO → bef, AFT → aft, dual years → new-style year, non-Gregorian/Julian and day-month-only dates dropped; same checks as JSON import (refs, loops, caps). Export = GEDCOM 5.5.1 UTF-8 CRLF of one tree, optional "hide details of the living"; sex x → U, step parent → `_FREL/_MREL Step`, partner union → FAM without MARR.

Every row has `id` (`[a-z0-9]{1,40}`) and `m` (mtime, R27: only bumped on a real change); child rows carry `v` (vehicle id). Dates are `2026-10-09`; money is integer cents; km are integers.
  - Since 0.52.01, fuel / service / cost rows may carry `rc`: up to 6 receipt file NAMES (`YYYYMMDD-<rowId>-<random>.jpg`, `core.RC_RE`), sorted and unique. The key is absent when there are none, so older rows keep their canonical form. Files live on the orOS disk at `/internal/Garage/Receipts/<name>` (Files; synced by Vault Drive when the user runs it). The row is LWW as a whole. Photos are re-drawn on a canvas (long side ≤ 1600 px, JPEG 0.8, white background), so no EXIF or location data and no foreign bytes are kept. A photo added in an editor that is then cancelled is removed. A photo taken off a row leaves the disk on save. A deleted row's photos leave the disk after the Undo window when no row points at them. A photo missing on a device shows "Not on this device".
  - vehicle `{name, type (car|moto|scooter|van|truck|camper|tractor|boat|bike|ebike|escooter|other), fuel (petrol|diesel|lpg|cng|hybrid|phev|ev|none), make, model, year, plate, tank (L), col 0–7, arch 0|1, notes}` (max 30).

  - tyre `{label, season s|w|a, size, brand, dot WWYY, tread, km (earlier mounted periods), on, okm}`.
  - renewal `{kind (kteo|ins|tax|kek|road|lic|other), exp, every (months, 0 = once), label, c, prov, ref, warn[] (days, max 4, default [30,7,1]), n}`. Renewing writes a cost with a FIXED id `(renewalId + "x" + exp digits).slice(-40)` and moves `exp` by `every`, so the same renewal done on two offline devices merges into one cost.
  - cost `{d, cat, c ≥ 1, km|null, n, bud}`; odo `{d, km}`.

Two of quantity / price / total give the third; when all three disagree, quantity and total win. Nothing is saved before Save. Photo OCR is not wired here: `vendor/tesseract/` (Contacts wave 26) is not in this branch; the receipt dialog is the place a recognised text would go.

Every data text is escaped there; print goes through `#print-area` (only it prints, emptied on `afterprint`), "Save as HTML" through `orosDialog.saveFile` (a self-contained page with inline CSS and no script). Tests: `tests/garage-receipt.test.js`.
