- **ATELIER-FOLDERS v1** (slice `atelier-folders`, key `oros-atelier-folders`, owner `atelier/folders.js`, UI `atelier/homefolders.js`, since 0.80.00): `{ver:1, folders[{id "af-…", m, nm, pos}] ≤ 200, place{docId:{f, m}} ≤ 20000, dt{folderId:m}}`. Merge per folder and per place by m, ties by canonical JSON; a tombstone removes a folder not newer than it; a place naming a missing folder counts as no folder. Which folder is open stays per device.
- **RECIPES v1** (slice `recipes`, key `oros-recipes`, owner `recipes/core.js`, Atelier catalog `atelier/recipesteps.js`, UI `atelier/recipes.js`, since 3.22.00): automations without code. A recipe is a named list of steps `{op, …args}`, DATA only; each app has a catalog (op → argument specs + kind doc/async/out) and a step whose op or arguments the catalog does not accept never runs (`check()` / `normStep()`). The slice keeps unknown steps byte for byte (plain JSON, sorted keys, ≤ 40 steps, ≤ 20 KB a recipe) so an older device never strips a newer device's steps (lesson of K1). Atelier steps: `text` (find/repl, cs, word), `color` (from/to on fc, sc, gradient ends, table colours), `font` (from "" = any), `size` (pct), `filter`, `center` (text/all), `cutout` (on-device background removal), `resize` (sizes; copies = the next steps work on the copies), `export` (png/jpg ×1-3 or pdf 150/300 dpi; several files = one ZIP). Edit steps stamp only what they change (R27), so a recipe run twice changes nothing more. Record: snapshot of the open design, then `learn(before, after)` turns changed words (widened to whole words), colours, fonts, one shared text-size ratio and photo filters into steps, plus notes (`rc-note` events) from Resize, Background removal and Download. A run first previews the counts; designs change through `AT.putDoc` (the open design keeps an undo step) and one Undo restores every design (`AT.restoreDoc`, as new edits) and drops the copies.
  - **Wave A2: Layout and Photo Lab.** Both mount the shared panel `recipes/ui.js` (`orosRecipesUI.mount(adapter)`: list, editor drawn from the catalog's argument specs, run preview, progress with Stop, one Undo toast; strings in its own table, pack `recipes`). It registers the same slice (the getter always returns the whole record, so whichever app registered last carries every app's recipes). No catalog may name an argument `op` (it would overwrite the step's op; `tests/photolab-recipes.test.js`). **Layout** (`layout/recipesteps.js` catalog + pure `apply`, `layout/recipes.js` runner): `text` (find/repl, cs, word; a match may span text runs and takes the first run's formatting, a field run splits the search), `pstyle` (from "" = any → to), `master` (ms "" = none, on all/odd/even), `margins` (t/b/i/o mm), `preflight` (stop: a document with errors is not exported), `export` (bleed, marks, spreads, print 300 / screen 150 ppi). Since 4.10.00 also `style` (name* → size 0–400, lead 0–500, font ""/serif/sans/mono, align ""/l/c/r/j, track −500–2000; 0 or "" leaves a field as it is; the style is found by `resolve`, stamped only when a field changes, so the step is idempotent). Since 4.27.00 (LY-IN wave Q5, the Layout command catalog) also: `style` adds bold/ital/caps ""/on/off (into `b`/`i`/`caps`; named bold/ital so they never clash with the margins' numeric `b`/`i` in the Assistant's tool), sb/sa/fi pt (−1 = as it is), brk ""/any/col/page/odd/even and hyph ""/on/off (into the style's ext, LY-BK; any clears the break); `pages` (n 1–500 at end/before/after position `page`; flow: the overflowing story ending before them chains a margin-sized frame on each new page), `delpages` (positions first–last, 0 = only first; pages, their items, emptied stories and their guides become tombstones; a document keeps one page; named first/last, not from/to, which pstyle uses for names), `numbering` (set n or shift by n, into `setup.ext.pnStart`, LY-PN), `bleed` (mm 0–25), `fit` (overflowing text gets pages after its last frame in batches estimated from what fit, trailing empty ones taken back; ≤ 40 rounds, `M.MAX_PAGES`), `imgfit` (fit/fill on the picture frames of `pages`) and `grey` (kind async: the runner first makes greyscale copies of the pictures those pages hold, found on a trial copy so earlier page steps count, with `LY.io.greyBlob` into the disk, then `apply(doc, st, now, ctx)` swaps `it.a` to `ctx.grey[a]`; a picture that cannot be read keeps its colour). `pages` everywhere: "" (all), odd, even or positions like `3-10,12` (`pageTest`; anything else changes nothing). Styles and masters are matched by id, else by name in any language and case (`resolve`), so one recipe fits documents with their own style ids; a document without them is skipped. Targets: the open document (one `LY.op`, normal undo) or all documents (copies put back with `LY.putDoc`); the Undo toast puts every changed document back with `LY.restoreDoc` (snapshot re-applied as new edits, like undo). One PDF uses the Save dialog; several go to `/internal/Layout/` with names that never overwrite (`LY.io.pdfBlob(doc, opts)` builds a PDF of any document). **Photo Lab** (`photolab/recipesteps.js` catalog + pure `cropRect`, `resizeTo`, `job`, `wmOf`; `photolab/recipes.js` runner): `tone` (fx sliders), `look` (fx FILTERS), `gray`, `blur` (gauss), `sharpen` (unsharp), `noise`, `crop` (largest centred ratio), `resize` (batchcore targetSize), `watermark` (text, size %, colour, place, opacity), `export` (jpg/png/webp + quality, into Pictures). On the open picture each step is the editor's own command on the active layer and selection (one undo step each; the watermark is a layer of its own; the toast's Undo takes them all back). Batch process offers every Photo Lab automation under Adjustments (`onCanvas`: after the batch resize, before its watermark; an export step only presets format and quality).
  - **Wave A3: sharing and the Assistant** (`recipes/share.js`, `orosRecipeShare`). An automation travels as DATA only and is checked where it lands. **File** `.orosrecipe` (MIME `application/x-oros-recipe`): plain JSON `{format:"orosrecipe", ver:1, app, name, steps}` (no id, stamp or place), at most 64 KB; `unpack()` refuses junk (`big`, `json`, `format`, `app` = an app this orOS has no automations for, `empty`) and keeps steps through `normRecipe` (plain JSON; an op must be a string), so a newer orOS's steps stay and are skipped. Automations › `Share` saves it (`orosDialog.saveFile`), `Import` reads one. **Deep link** `__orosOpenAt(app, { newRecipe: { app, nm, steps } })` in Atelier, Layout and Photo Lab opens the editor with the steps filled in (`prepare()`: numbers written as text become numbers, a field that is there but wrong is left empty so the editor marks it, unknown steps are kept); nothing is saved before Save and nothing runs before Run. A draft for another app offers `Open in <app>`. `CATALOGS` holds copies of the three catalogs (so the Assistant checks without loading editing code); `tests/recipes-share.test.js` keeps them equal to the apps' and checks that the model guide names every op and field. **Assistant** tool `propose_automation` `{app, name, steps}` (offered when one of the three apps is installed and the model takes tools; every step field declared, so Gemini keeps them): `normAutomation` runs `problems()` (unknown op, missing or wrong field, an enum value that is not allowed is never silently defaulted) and the error goes back to the model; a valid draft is a card with the steps in plain words (`words()`, EN/EL + pack `recipes`) and `Open in <app>` (the deep link), `Save as file`, `Dismiss`. The card is rebuilt with the same check whenever it is drawn.
- **Atelier links + web page (wave B1, `atelier/webout.js`).** An element's link lives in the item's extension bag, `ext.lnk` (R39; kept by older copies through `normX`), written only through `AX.setLink` and read only through `AX.linkOf`, which re-checks it with `AX.normLink`: https / http (no user:password; "example.com" gets https://), `mailto:` with one address, `tel:` digits, or `#p<n>` = page n of the same design; everything else (javascript:, data:, file:, //host, …) is "". Download › Web page: a ZIP (`AtelierZip.write`) with `index.html`, `style.css`, `img/`, `fonts/` (+ README with the licences, OFL.txt when the device has it). Each page is a `<section id="p<n>">` with one inline SVG drawn from the same layout as the canvas and the PDF: texts are `<text>`/`<tspan>` per run at the layout's positions in the design's fonts (`@font-face` per face file with its unicode-range, `font-kerning:none`, `white-space:pre`), a space added after each word and wrapped line so the text reads and copies as typed; effect copies are `aria-hidden`, curved text is one `role="img"` group with the text as its label; shapes, gradients, lines, icons and tables are vectors; photos (filter, crop, flip) are pictures cut to their shape by a clipPath, charts and blurred effect passes are pictures (drawn by io.js `pictureOf` at 144 dpi). A link wraps its element in `<a>` (with a transparent hit area); `#p<n>` links to pages left out are dropped. No JavaScript, no inline styles or handlers, CSP `default-src 'none'; img-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`, no outside requests; works from file:// and any static host. The PDF (`pdfout.js`) adds a link annotation over each linked element (`linkBox`: the box around a turned element; `#p<n>` → that page). Tests `tests/atelier-web.test.js`.
- **Blend (wave C1, Atelier + Layout).** `designkit/blend.js` (`orosDK.blend`, pure): two outlines in unit space become closed runs of cubic segments (L → straight cubic flagged as a line, drawn back as `L`); the run with fewer segments splits its longest segment until both have the same count (at least 16, at most 600), B turns the same way as A (signed area) and starts at the rotation with the least squared anchor distance, a subpath with no partner grows from its middle; `at(plan, t)` moves every control point on a straight line (4 decimals); `steps(n)` = i/(n+1); `angle` takes the short way round; `hex` / `mixVals` blend colours. Atelier (`atelier/blend.js`, AtelierBlend): two non-background shapes on one page → n (1..50, default 5) ordinary shape items: box, rotation, opacity, stroke width, fill or gradient (a plain fill meets a gradient as a two-colour gradient), stroke colour and roundness in even steps; z strictly between the ends (when the gap is too small, the higher end and everything above it move up); a different shape on each end keeps the step's outline in item `ext.pth` (unit path text, chunks ≤ 4000 chars, dropped to 3 decimals or left out to stay within normX's 8192) and `shp` = the nearer end's shape, which older copies draw; `ext.bl = {g, a, b, n, i}`. Every renderer draws `AX.shapeCmds(it)` (canvas, PDF, web page, .pptx custom geometry). Context bar `Blend` (two shapes, a step, or an end alone): steps slider (live), Update (re-make from the ends as they are now, keeping the step ids in order so other devices see the same steps change; extra steps get a tombstone), Release (removes `ext.bl`, keeps `ext.pth`); a copy of a step is a plain shape. Layout (`layout/blend.js`, LayoutBlend): rect+rect stay rects (corner radius blended), ell+ell stay ellipses, any other pair of rect/ell/path becomes `path` items; colours are swatches: the same swatch on both ends is reused, else a swatch per step (CMYK when both ends are CMYK, else RGB; an existing swatch with the same values is reused) named by its values and marked `ext.bl = g`; Update removes marked swatches nothing uses any more, Release unmarks them; a gradient fill is the nearer end's. Properties panel section `Blend`. Tests `tests/blend.test.js`.
- **Morph (wave C2, Atelier).** `atelier/morph.js` (AtelierMorph, pure): a page whose background has `ext.mph = 1` morphs in from the page before it (Animate › transition `Morph`; `ax.ptr` is left as is, so older copies show it, default fade; choosing another transition removes `mph`; Magic animation's plan replaces it). Pairs, old page → new page: the two backgrounds (same kind), then the same content (text with the same `tx`, photo/video with the same picture and clip, the same icon), then the rest kind by kind in z order (shape, line, text, icon, photo); tables, charts, hidden items and template guides never pair; an item with its own entrance (`ax.an`) on the new page does not pair and enters after the morph. A pair moves box, rotation, opacity, stroke width, z, fill / gradient / stroke colour, roundness, text size / line height / tracking, custom photo crop; different outlines morph through `orosDK.blend` (plan cached per pair, drawn copy gets `ext.pth`), different words or icons crossfade at the moving box; unpaired items fade out / in. Frames are drawn copies only (`drawPage` opts.morph `{from, p}`), never stored. Timing (`anim.js`): `pageTransition` = "morph", `MORPH` = 1 s with ease in-out, the page lasts at least MORPH + its intro, `at()` gives `pt` = page time for entrances (local − MORPH); the first page (or a page exported alone) never morphs. Plays in the editor's Play, video, GIF and Present (drawn by Atelier through show.js `live` + `renderSlide`; only when the show came forward from the page before, tracked through `transition(i)` + `onChange`, otherwise the fallback `ptr`; reduced motion shows none). Tests `tests/atelier-morph.test.js`.
- **ATELIER-BRAND v1** (slice `atelier-brand`, key `oros-atelier-brand`, owner `atelier/brandkit.js`): `{ver:1, colors[{id,m,c,pos}] ≤ 40, fonts{h|s|t:{f,b,m}}, logos[{id,m,a,w,h,nm,pos}] ≤ 20, dt{id:m}}`. Own slice because the design slice's merge drops unknown top-level fields. Merge per entry / font slot by m, ties by canonical JSON, tombstones remove entries not newer. Video / sound clips are Vault files at `/internal/Assets/<sha256>.<ext>` (type sniffed from bytes; ≤ 100 MB video, 30 MB sound, 30 min); design items reference them via `ax.vid/vs/ve/mu/vol/nl`, page sound `ax.au/av/ao`, validated in `normAx`.
- **MUSEUM v1** (slice `museum`, key `oros-museum-data`): `{ver:1, items[{id ("en"|"el" + page id, or "pf" + hash for a picture of the day), m, kind, lang, title, …}], tombs{id: ts}}`, kept exhibits only; LWW per item by m + tombstones (R17), delete wins ties, Undo restores past the tombstone with a newer m; canonical (R26); a pull never marks the slice dirty (R6). Prefs and thumbnails are device-local (`oros-museum-prefs`, IDB `oros-museum`). Network: `{en,el}.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1` only, images only from `upload.wikimedia.org`, all text via textContent (listed under external services).
- **ASSISTANT v1** (slice `assistant`, key `oros-assistant-data`): `{ ver, set{m, chat 0|1, prov ""|pid}, provs{pid: {m, base, model}}, perm{appId: {m, v ask|always|never}}, ks{m, on 0|1}, keys{pid: {m, d 0|1, s}} }`. Every entry LWW by `m`, tie → larger canonical JSON; maps sorted by key; unknown providers / bad app ids / non-http(s) base URLs dropped. Symmetric, idempotent, associative (fuzz in `tests/assistant.test.js`).
  - New top-level entry `cs {m, on}` (LWW like `ks`): "Sync conversations" switch, off by default. Older 0.63–0.6x devices drop the unknown key on their own merge, which costs nothing (a pull never marks dirty, the newer device keeps `cs`).
  - **AS-CS (conversation sync, opt-in, Chris 2026-10-10):** a chat file is `core.chatFile(c)` = canonical `{id, m, title, msgs, refs, refN}`; a deleted chat leaves a tombstone `{id, m, del: 1}`, so a missing file never means "deleted" (it is written again). `reconcile()` (app open, tab visible, Vault "done", switch turned on, slice pull turning it on) folds every `*.json` in the folder (Vault conflict copies included, then removed) into the device's chats with `core.mergeChat`: newer `m` wins; if one history starts the other, the longer one is kept with the newer stamp; a fork keeps the older side as a copy with the fixed id `<id>x<m base36>`, the same on every device; a tombstone wins only when it is newer. Only files whose text differs are written, so idle rounds upload nothing (tested). A chat being answered is skipped until the next round. "Delete all" with the switch on writes tombstones (asks "on all your devices"). Turning the switch off stops reading and writing; the files stay in Files. Needs "Keep conversations on this device".
  - **Key sync (AS-K, opt-in, Chris 2026-10-10):** off by default. While `ks.on`, each device puts its keys in `keys[pid].s` sealed with the sync passphrase (`orosSync.vaultCrypto.encryptJson({p, k})`), only when sync is connected and unlocked (`hasPassphrase()`; never seal with a null passphrase). Newer `m` wins; `d: 1` = the user removed the key → every device drops its copy. Turning the switch off blanks `s` everywhere (`d: 0`), devices keep their own keys. A sealed key that no longer opens (passphrase changed) is re-sealed by a device that still has it. localStorage never holds a key in clear.
- **TYPEWRITER v1** (slice `typewriter`, key `oros-typewriter-data`): `{ ver: 1, pages[{id (p + 6–20 [a-z0-9]), m, title (≤ 80, one line), text (≤ 200,000), goal (words, 0 = none, ≤ 100,000)}], tombs{id: deletedAt} }`. LWW per page (newer m wins; equal m → larger canonical JSON), tombstones max-merged, delete wins ties, a newer edit resurrects (R17); canonical (R26), tested in `tests/typewriter.test.js`. A struck letter is stored as the letter + U+0336 (combining long stroke overlay), so copied text still reads as crossed out in any editor.
  - Phase 2 (PR #91, shipped in 0.56.00): `tags[]` and `rules[]` collections, `feed.full` (full-text extraction, `feeds/extract.js`), `item.tags`, tombstones `t:`/`r:`, settings `view` / `dedup`; device pref `width`.
  - Phase 3 (PR #118, 0.56.00): `feed.notify` and `rule.notify` (0|1; new articles under 2 days old, unread, not muted, never on a feed's first fetch, at most 5 per fetch; key = article id, so two devices merge into one inbox entry). Deep-link targets via `__orosOpenAt`: notes `{add:{title,text}}`, feeds `{add:{url}}` and `{item:id}`; bookmarks `{add:{url,title}}` (since #83); To-Do through BR-TD-ADD. Mail compose contract `__orosOpenAt("mail", {compose:{subject, body}})` live since 0.67.01 (#156; Mail phase 2 0.66.00), replacing mailto:.
  - **Wave 36 (other sources; no new fields, same version):** (a) **Mail folders as feeds:** a feed's `url` may be `oros-mail:<mail account id>/<IMAP folder name, encodeURIComponent>` (`core.mailUrl` / `parseMailUrl`, one spelling; id = `"f" + hash(whole address)`, never equal to an http feed's id, which hashes `host/path`). `normFeed` keeps it with `site: ""`; `buildOpml` leaves it out; Newsletter's `readerFeeds()` (already) and `feeds/search.js` skip non-http addresses. Its articles never come from the network: `refreshMail()` reads Mail's cache through the read-only bridge `mail/feed.js` (BR-MAIL-FEED, Part VI) and `sources.mailParsed()` turns it into the parsed-feed shape, so storing, read state, stars, tags, rules, search and notifications work unchanged. Item key = `mid:<Message-ID>` (else `uid:<uidvalidity>:<uid>`); device-local head fields `mt {acct, folder, uid}` ("Open in Mail" → `__orosOpenAt("mail", mt)`, Mail's search receiver) and `nobody: 1` (body not on the device yet; a later read without the body never overwrites the copy Reader already stored). Pictures default to off for a Mail feed (`imagesFor`, img −1); body base "" (no relative URLs). A device on an older Reader drops the unknown address on its own merge (harmless: a pull never marks dirty; the feed stays on newer devices). (b) **Import from FreshRSS (Google Reader API: `accounts/ClientLogin`, `subscription/list`, `stream/contents` starred and reading-list `xt=read`) and Miniflux (REST: `/v1/feeds`, `/v1/entries?starred=true|status=unread`, `X-Auth-Token`)**, `feeds/sources.js`: fetch straight from the page (mode cors, credentials omit, no referrer, 30 s); the relay's `web` op takes no auth headers and relay/ is not changed, so a server without CORS (or http from the https page) gets the file path instead: OPML + "Import starred articles (JSON)" (Google Reader JSON as FreshRSS / Inoreader export it, or Miniflux entries). Credentials are never stored. Order: new feeds (folders by name) → `refresh(ids)` → stars `starredRecords()` (matched to the device's article by `dupKey(link)` so the id is the same; else `itemId(feed, link)`; `m` above any tomb) → read marks `readMarks()` (articles of the imported feeds whose address is not in the server's unread list; nothing is ever marked unread; skipped when the unread list was cut at 10 000). Stars and read marks are ordinary FEEDS v1 records (`items[]`, `read.ids`). (c) **Summarise:** `feeds/ai.js` = Atelier's pattern (atelier/ai.js): reads `oros-assistant-data` (merged with `../assistant/core.js`, loaded on first use) and the sealed key (IndexedDB `oros-assistant`, opened without a version, never written), asks the user's provider straight from the device with `sources.summaryPrompt()` (title + ≤ 12 000 characters of text, the article labelled as data, answer in the UI language); not set up → a dialog that opens the Assistant. The answer is plain text (textContent), kept in memory only (≤ 30), never synced. No orOS key. Tests `tests/feeds-sources.test.js`.
- **SCORES v1:** `{ ver, matches[], rounds[], tpls[], players[], tombs{id: at} }`, each list sorted by id. match `{id, m, c, name, tpl, seats[2..8], target (0 = none), low 0|1, quick[≤4], done (0 | ms)}`; round `{id, m, g (match id), c (order), s[int per seat]}`; tpl `{id, m, name, target, low, quick, seats, base ("" | ready id it replaces)}`; player `{id, m, name, col 0..7}`. Totals, leader, winner and stats are DERIVED (ties count as a win for everyone in the lead). Ready templates (tavli, prefa, xeri, biriba, poker, free) are code, not data. Tests `tests/scores.test.js`.
- **PODCASTS v1** (slice `podcasts`, key `oros-podcasts-data`): `{ ver, shows[{id, m, url, title, by, img, spd, skA, skB, auto, ntf}], eps[{id, m, s (show), p (position s), d (duration s), x (played 0/1), pd (played at)}], floors{showId: stamp}, queue{m, ids[], sh{epId: showId}}, prefs{key: [value, mtime]}, tombs{showId: deletedAt} }`. Shows and episodes LWW by `m` (equal `m` → larger canonical JSON); tombs max-merged and a tomb ≥ `m` hides the show and drops its episodes, floors and queue rows (a newer resubscription resurrects); floors max, played rows under the floor are dropped; queue LWW as a whole; prefs (`spd, back, fwd, autoNext, delPlayed, search, ntf`; since W42 also `sil` skip silence and `vb` voice boost, 0|1, off by default) LWW per field; unknown pref keys (`/^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]{0,15}$/`, number / string ≤ 100 / boolean) are kept and merged, up to 20 in name order, so a newer client's settings survive an older one; tombs older than a year are dropped (`tests/podcasts.test.js`). **PODCASTS 1.2** (0.57.00, same format): `show.ntf` = "tell me about new episodes" (off by default); notices `orosNotifs.emit` ns `podcasts`, key `e:<episodeId>`, deep link `podcasts:ep:<id>` (DL_BRIDGES); receiver `__orosOpenAt("podcasts", {ep} | {add:{url}} | {show, ep?})`.
  - The slice is registered by `podcasts/host.js` in the shell window, not by the app, so it syncs while the app is closed; positions are written to it only by the `shouldCommit` throttle (about 12 uploads per listening hour, none while paused).
  - W42 audio effects (`host.js`, pure parts in `core.js` §14, `tests/podcasts-fx.test.js`): Web Audio graph `MediaElementSource → highpass 80 Hz → peaking 2.8 kHz +5 dB → compressor (−30 dB, ratio 4) → gain 1.7` (voice boost) plus an AnalyserNode; skip silence = `playbackRate` raised to `silenceRate(base)` (3×, clamped 2.5–4) after 250 ms under RMS 0.012 (back above 0.02). Only for media the page may read: blob downloads, same origin, or an origin a plain CORS GET probe accepted (cached a day in `oros-podcasts-local.cors`, ≤ 60); then `crossOrigin = "anonymous"` before `src`. Anything else plays on a fresh plain `<audio>` (a MediaElementSource can never be undone) with `fx.state = "blocked"`; a media error or 10 s of exact-zero samples falls back the same way. Saved seconds go to the third column of the device-local `stats` rows. `getState().fx = {state, sil, vb, saved, fast}`.
  - Browse like Radio (2026-10-16, Chris: "Προβολή podcasts όπως στο Radio"): Discover shows Popular · Genres · Countries · Surprise me. Lists = Apple's iTunes chart `itunes.apple.com/{cc}/rss/toppodcasts/limit=100[/genre={id}]/json` (no key), feeds via `lookup` in batches of 50 with `&country=` (shows sold only in that storefront); fallbacks: no genre → `rss.applemarketingtools.com` top 50, a genre → catalog search `genreId` + the genre's English name, kept to that genre. 19 Apple genres and 171 storefronts in `core.js` §15 (`GENRES`, `COUNTRIES`, names via `Intl.DisplayNames`); sub-genre chips from the shows' `genres`. **Preview:** tapping a show not followed opens it from its feed in memory only (never IndexedDB, never the slice); its episodes play, and the host writes no position to the slice for a show that is not in `shows` (device-local position only). Surprise me picks a random show from the list on screen, preferring ones not followed, and plays its newest non-trailer episode. Spotify exclusives have no public RSS and cannot appear.
  - Browse wave 2 (shuffle + index): `core.js` §16. **Shuffle** (`shufflePlan`): a show's unplayed, playable, non-trailer episodes in a random order, or for `Shuffle all` one random unplayed episode per followed show; the first plays, the rest go to the front of Up next (`queueFront`: front ids then the old queue, no duplicates, one queue write). **Index** (`letterOf`, `indexLetters`, `indexSort`): A–Z and Α–Ω (accents and final sigma folded, leading punctuation skipped, digits and other scripts = "#"), Greek letters first when the app is in Greek; Library is sorted in that order and shows the letter bar from 8 podcasts, Countries always. Adding a podcast by address now returns Discover to browsing (the address no longer stays as a search with "Nothing found").
  - W42 gpodder sync (`podcasts/gpodder.js`, `window.OrosPodcastsGpodder`, `tests/podcasts-gpodder.test.js`): gpodder.net API v2 or Nextcloud GPodder Sync, straight from the browser (`fetch` mode cors, Basic auth UTF-8); a server without CORS gives error code `cors` and the dialog points to the files (OPML + episode actions JSON `{actions:[…]}`). The mail relay is not used (GET only, no auth). Config `oros-podcasts-gpodder` (localStorage, device: `{kind, server, user, device, subsTs, actTs, mark, known[] (≤ 2000 feed URLs last agreed with the server), last, err}`), password sealed with a non-extractable AES-GCM key in IndexedDB `oros-podcasts-sync` (never synced, never exported; in the factory-reset list). Subscriptions: `subsPlan` against the last known set (local add over a remote remove uploads). Episode actions: newest per episode wins; applied as position/played rows with `m` = the action time (≤ now), ≥ 95 % = played. Runs on open, hourly while open, and on `Sync now`.
- **WORDSEARCH v1:** `{ ver, br, days{"en|el:<day>":{b, t, h}}, rows{deviceId:{b, s{"<lang>:<e|m|h>":{n, t, d}}}}, themes[{id, m, name, lang, words[]}], tombs{id: ts} }`: `day` = days since 1 Jan 2026 (local calendar day); daily `t` = seconds (1–360000), `h` = 1 when a hint was used; per day key the larger `b` wins, equal `b` keeps the better result (`h` 0 first, then the lower `t`). Free play rows: solved `n` ≥ 1 (max), best time `t` in seconds with its date `d` (ms; 0/0 = none yet, a hinted solve never sets it; the lower `t` wins, then the earlier `d`); per row the larger epoch wins. Entries with `b < br` drop; a reset leaves the themes alone. Own themes (≤ 30; 3–60 words of 3–15 letters of the theme's alphabet; name ≤ 40): LWW per id by `m` (tie → the larger canonical JSON), tombstones max-merged, delete wins ties, a newer edit resurrects (R17); sorted by id. A join (`tests/wordsearch.test.js`).
- **SOLITAIRE v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{<key>:{p, w, k, t?, tt?, m?, mt?, s?, st?}}}} }`, key = variant + setting (`k1c` Klondike draw 1 classic score, `k1n`, `k3c`, `k3n`, `f` FreeCell, `s1` `s2` `s4` Spider suits, `p` Pyramid (Wave 49)): played `p` (counted at a deal's first move), won `w` (w ≤ p), best streak `k` (k ≤ w), best time `t` (ms) with date `tt`, fewest moves `m`/`mt`, best score `s`/`st` (scored settings only); bests only once w ≥ 1. Per row the larger epoch wins; equal epochs take the max of p, w, k and the better of each best (earlier stamp on a tie): a join. Totals add p/w and take the best k and bests. Rows with `b < br` drop (`tests/solitaire.test.js`). **cardkit** (`cardkit/cardkit.js` + `cardkit.css`) is a shared module, not an app: no slice, no storage, `window.orosCards` (cards as ids suit·13 + rank − 1, decks, crypto and seeded shuffles, EN/EL names, DOM/SVG and canvas faces, pointer drag/tap helper); loaded by Solitaire, planned for Xeri. **Pyramid** (Wave 49): 28 places (`tab[0..27]`, row r place k), 24 cards in the stock; pairs of open cards (no card on the two places below) summing to 13 go to `fd[0]`, a King alone; the waste top pairs too; 3 passes through the stock (`ps`); won when the 28 places are empty. `validPyramid` checks every stored position (each removed card was open when it left, pairs sum to 13, 52 cards exactly once) (`tests/solitaire.test.js`).
- **JIGSAW v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{12|24|48|96|150:{n, t, ts}}}} }`: puzzles solved `n` (≥ 1), best time `t` in ms (1 … 10 days) and when it was made `ts`. Per row the larger epoch wins; equal epochs keep, per count, the larger `n` and the better best (lower `t`, then the earlier `ts`): a join. Totals add `n` over devices; the best time is the lowest `t` of any row. Rows with `b < br`, bad ids, bad cells and unknown counts drop. Symmetric, associative, idempotent (`tests/jigsaw.test.js`).
- **CROSSWORD v1:** `{ ver, br, days{"en|el:<day>":{b, t, h}}, rows{deviceId:{b, s{"<lang>:<e|m|h>":{n, t, d}}}} }`: `day` = days since 1 Jan 2026 (local calendar day); daily `t` = seconds (1–360000), `h` = 1 when a letter was revealed; per day key the larger `b` wins, equal `b` keeps the better result (`h` 0 first, then the lower `t`). Free play rows: solved `n` ≥ 1 (max), best time `t` in seconds with its date `d` (ms; 0/0 = none yet, a solve with a revealed letter never sets it; the lower `t` wins, then the earlier `d`); per row the larger epoch wins. Entries with `b < br` drop. A join (`tests/crossword.test.js`). Wave 49: the daily result dialog shares a spoiler-free line (one square per word, yellow = a revealed letter) through `orosDaily.share`.
- **GAMECENTER (no data):** no slice and no keys of its own. `gamecenter/core.js` (`window.orosGameCore`) reads `oros-<game>-data` for 37 games read-only (an adapter per schema above; rows / days with `b < br` skipped, Memory games with `ts ≤ br`) and returns per game `{p played, w won|solved (-1 = no win), t best ms, sc best score, cur/best streak, dn dailies, today 0|1|2}` plus the overall daily streak (days with any of the six dailies solved). 15 achievements (first win, first daily, 7- and 30-day streak in one game, all six dailies on one day, a daily without hints, Wordle in ≤ 2, Killer solved, all four Solitaire variants won, beat the computer on Hard, Minesweeper Expert won, Sudoku under 5 minutes, 10 different games won, 100 played, 250 won) are computed from that summary on every render and never stored, so there is nothing to sync or to get out of step; resetting a game's records takes its achievements away (help says so). **All games** (Chris 2026-10-22, so the orOS Games app is more than the Dailies): every game as a tile (shell icon via `orosTodayEnv.icon`, name, "Played n" or "New") in `GROUPS` from `core.js` (puzzles, word games, cards and tiles, board and two-player, arcade; each of the 37 once, tested against apps.json's Games category, so a new game must be added there), a name filter (accents ignored; matches the shown name, the English name and the id); a tap opens the game (Back returns in the single app). Deep links: `__orosOpenAt("gamecenter", {game})` scrolls to that game, `{all: true}` to All games; Daily cards call `__orosOpenAt(<game>, {daily: true})`. Games show an `All games` link only when `orosDaily.hasHub()` (the app is installed). (`tests/gamecenter.test.js`, `tests/gamekit.test.js`)
- **XERI v1:** `{ ver, br, rows{deviceId:{b, s{e|m|h:[m, w, x, j, d]}}} }`: matches finished `m`, won `w` (w ≤ m), xeri `x` (10 points, incl. Jack on a lone card when that option is on), Jack-on-Jack xeri `j`, best deal `d` (your points in one deal, ≤ 999); a deal adds x, j and the best, a match end adds m and w. Each device writes only its own row (id in `oros-xeri-device`). Per row the larger epoch `b` wins, equal epochs take the max of each field: a join (symmetric, associative, idempotent). Totals add m/w/x/j, the best deal is the max. Rows with `b < br` drop; bad ids, cells and unknown levels drop in `normRow` (`tests/xeri.test.js`). Uses `window.orosCards` from `cardkit/` (deck, crypto shuffle, EN/EL card names, DOM faces, drag/tap helper).

**WRITER v1** (verified 2026-10-01):

```
{ ver:1,
  docs[ { id, title, author, tags[], category, html,
          footnotes[{id,text}], comments[{id,quote,text,ts}],
          versions[{ts,html,manual,footnotes?,comments?}],
          pageSize, margins{top,bottom,left,right}, header, footer,
          goal{type,target,lock,startTs,startWords}|null,
          mtime, del, fm{c,m,p,g},
          lang?: "en"|"el"|"none",        // wave 22; absent = automatic
          track?: true } ],               // wave 22; absent = off
                                          // SORTED BY id (R26)
  tabOrder[],      // COMPAT ONLY = alive doc ids sorted; NOT the open tabs
  settings{smartTypography,spell?,typewriterSound (default false: a soft Web Audio key click per typed or deleted character and a carriage return on Enter, never on paste or IME; made on the spot like Typewriter, no files),_mtime}, autocorrect{rules[{find,repl,def}],mtime}|null,
  templates[{id,name,desc,html,mtime}] (sorted, tombstoned ones filtered),
  tplTombs[{id,ts}] (deduped max-ts, sorted), seeded,
  userDict?: { word: ±stamp } }   // wave 22; absent when empty
```

- **Device-local** `oros-writer-prefs = { open[], active, seen{}, view{focus, unit, tw, wc}, who }` (`who` = the author name for tracked changes, wave 22; empty = the device name from `WriterTrack.deviceName`). Docs never seen on this device auto-open once. At boot with no open tab, the most recent doc opens. `view` (focus mode, `unit` "p" paragraph / "s" sentence, typewriter scrolling, word count chip) is read before the first `savePrefs()` of the boot and never enters the slice.
- **Pure core** `writer/core.js` (`window.WriterCore`, loaded before `writer.js`; tests `tests/writer-core.test.js`): `textStats` (words as in the goal bar, characters with/without spaces in code points, paragraphs = blocks with a letter or digit, sentences, reading 230 wpm / speaking 130 wpm), `sentenceRanges` / `sentenceAt` (ends at . ! ? … and, in Greek, ; and U+037E, only before a space or the end; a line break ends one too), `breakLines` / `alignLine` (PDF line breaking: tokens without a leading space stay glued to the previous one; justify leaves the last line and lines before a break alone), `colWidths`, `fitBox` (96 dpi, never enlarged), `centerDelta`.
- **Insert menu / table tools (wave 6):** the toolbar `Insert` menu opens the same link / image / table dialogs as Alt+right-click, plus rule, page break, footnote, special characters. A table strip (`.table-bar`) shows while the selection is in a `td`/`th`: rows and columns are plain DOM edits (not in the browser's undo stack, said in Limits), new cells copy the neighbour's inline style without the old header background; the header row is real `<th>` cells now (new tables too; older tables with a background-styled first row still export as a header in the PDF).
- **View (wave 6):** focus mode adds `.focus-mode` to `#w-app` (bars hidden, text colour dimmed through `color-mix`) and lights the caret's block with ONE generated `<style>` rule (`#rich-editor > :nth-child(i) …`); sentence focus uses the CSS Custom Highlight API (`::highlight(w-focus)`; falls back to the paragraph). Nothing is written into the document, so the saved html and mtime never move. Typewriter scrolling pads the editor by half its height (`--tw-pad`) and scrolls by `centerDelta` on selection change / input.
- **Undoable replace (wave 6):** `Replace` / `Replace all` select each hit by text offset (after the find marks are unwrapped) and go through `execCommand('insertText' | 'delete')`, last hit first, so every change is in the native undo stack. A `Replace all` records `{n, before, after}`; Undo (button, Ctrl/Cmd+Z, `beforeinput historyUndo`) while the editor still equals `after` runs native undo up to n times until it equals `before` (Redo the same way back). Smart typography ignores these inserts (`frBusy`).
- **Dictation (wave 6), removed.** Voice input removed 2026-10-14 at Chris's request: Web Speech recognition sends audio to Google. `#btn-dictate`, the `dict.*` strings, the listening pill and `WriterCore.joinDictation` are gone; Writer has no speech recognition.
- **PDF (wave 6):** jsPDF (vendor) with NotoSans-Regular (full) + the `vendor/noto/` Bold / Italic / BoldItalic / Mono subsets (Latin + Greek); per word, a face that lacks a glyph falls back to Regular (bold drawn `fillThenStroke`), checked through the font's cmap. Paragraph runs keep b / i / u / s / sup / sub / code / links (`pdf.link`, http(s)/mailto only) and inline-style bold/italic/underline; blocks keep alignment, hanging list markers, quote bar, shaded code, tables as a grid (`colWidths`, header shading), images through `addImage` (data: JPEG/PNG as is, others via canvas, a cross-site image without CORS becomes a placeholder), figure captions; page size, margins, header, footer and `n / N` page numbers from Page settings; document metadata as PDF properties.
- **Spelling (wave 22, §26):** own Hunspell-compatible checker `writer/spell.js` (`window.WriterSpell`, tests `tests/writer-spell.test.js`): reads `.aff`/`.dic` as DATA (SET, FLAG char/long/num/UTF-8, PFX/SFX with conditions and cross product, REP, MAP, TRY, ICONV, NEEDAFFIX, FORBIDDENWORD, ONLYINCOMPOUND, NOSUGGEST; no compounding). Words live in one string + an FNV-1a open-addressing `Int32Array` table (el_GR: ~830k entries, ~350 ms parse). Case: initial capital → lower form; all caps → lower / Capitalized, and for Greek the tonos-less capitals match accented words. Suggestions rank by kind of fix (capital, Greek accent, REP/MAP, swap, one edit, split in two) then by likeness. It runs in `writer/spell-worker.js` (ops `load` / `check` / `suggest`). Dictionaries `vendor/hunspell/en_US.{aff,dic.gz}` (SCOWL, permissive) and `el_GR.{aff,dic.gz}` (MPL 1.1/GPL 2.0/LGPL 2.1; ISO-8859-7, decoded by the aff `SET`), from LibreOffice/dictionaries. They are **NOT precached**: loaded on first need (`DecompressionStream('gzip')` after a magic-byte check) and cached in IndexedDB `oros-writer-spell` under `name@DICT_VER` (bump `DICT_VER` when the files change). Not in the SW caches, because sw.js purges caches outside its keep list on every release. Underlines are the CSS Custom Highlight API `::highlight(w-spell)` (fallback: an `aria-hidden` `.spell-layer` of absolutely placed lines); nothing is written into the document. The word under the caret is skipped while typing. `doc.lang` "" = each word by its script (Greek / Latin), "en", "el" or "none". The browser's own `spellcheck` is on whenever our checker is off or a needed dictionary isn't ready. Right-click (touch: tap) on a marked word → `openMenuAt` suggestions, Add to my dictionary, Ignore (per doc, session only). `userDict` = `{word: ±stamp}` merged by larger |stamp| (tie → removal), canonical (sorted, ≤ 3000, removals dropped first).
- **Track changes (wave 22, §27; pure ops `writer/track.js`, tests `tests/writer-track.test.js`):** `doc.track` (clock group m). Marks are `<ins|del class="tc" data-tc data-au data-ts>`, kept by the sanitiser with cleaned attributes (`cleanAttrs`: author ≤ 60 chars without `<>"`, ts integer, id `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`). Deletions are cancelled in `beforeinput` and wrapped in `del.tc` (deleting your own still-tracked insertion really removes it). Typed text goes through and is wrapped from MutationObserver `characterData` diffs (`diffEdit`, caret-aware; NBSP ↔ space swaps are no edit). Paste/drop insert plain text as one insertion. Undo/Redo while tracking use editor snapshots (`tcSnapshot` / `tcTryUndo`). Paragraph split/join and formatting are not tracked. `resolveHtml(html, accept|reject, id?)` resolves one change or all (Undo toast). Panel `#tc-panel` (`.side-panel`), author colours from `colorIndex` via one generated `<style>`. Export: DOCX writes `w:ins` / `w:del` + `w:delText` (`docxOpen`, ids per export); DOCX import turns them back into marks; every other format and the mail merge use the accepted text (`ioExportClone` accepts unless `keepTracked`, toast `tc.exportNote`). Spelling skips `del.tc` text.
- **Mail merge (wave 22, §28; pure `writer/merge.js`, tests `tests/writer-merge.test.js`):** `{{Field}}` placeholders, found in text segments only (never inside tags or attributes), matched to columns ignoring case, accents, spaces, `_`, `-`, `.`, plus EN/EL aliases of the Contacts columns. Data: Contacts (`oros-contacts-data` read-only from localStorage, live contacts only, optional label; columns FullName … Birthday) or a CSV/TSV (`,` `;` tab sniffed, quotes, BOM, ≤ 5000 rows, ≤ 100 columns). Every value is HTML-escaped (`\n` → `<br>`) and the result goes through `ioSanitizeHtml` again. Preview record by record. Output: one PDF, a ZIP of PDFs (≤ 500 records; names `001 Name.pdf`, UTF-8 name flag in `ioZipStore`), or one new document (page breaks between records; footnote refs and comment marks dropped).
- **Merge:** per-doc field groups (`fm{c,m,p,g}`, WR-6: content / meta incl. `lang` + `track` / page / goal), each group's newer stamp wins; template LWW vs tombstones; settings LWW on `_mtime`; autocorrect LWW on `mtime`; `userDict` per word (above).
- **mtime (R27):** moves only when the editor html changes (`flushSave`) or through `markDoc(doc)` for field edits (meta, page, footnotes, comments, goal, versions).
- **Versions:**
  - Auto: at most 1 per 5 minutes, riding the save pipeline (no timers); keeps the newest 8 within 400k chars per doc.
  - Manual: never dropped.
  - Restore brings back footnotes and comments when the version carries them.
- **Delete:** tombstone with content stripped + 8s Undo (fresh mtime resurrects).
- **DB import (.json):** MERGES and restamps the imported entities "now". Backup tombstones are ignored.

**CALCULATOR** (verified against `calculator.js` `canonCalc` at v2.0.0; the slice did not change in 2.0.0):

```
oros-calculator-data = { ver:1, troll, trollIntensity (0|1|2), mem (number|null), sciOn,
  sm{ mem, sciOn, troll, trollIntensity },              // ms stamps, LWW per setting
  history[{ id, expr, res, ts, lied? }] (ts DESC, cap 50),  // lied: only old entries (TR-1), never written now
  deleted{ id: ts } }                                    // tombstones, pruned 30 days of data time
```

- **Merge:** `registerSlice("calculator", sliceGet, sliceSet, LS_KEY, mergeCalc)`: settings per field by stamp (tie → greater JSON), history union by id, tombstones max-ts union and always win. The old v1.1.0 note (no `mergeFn`, "remote wins") is superseded (A2 fixed by CA-1/CA-2).
- **History entries from Scientific (2.0.0):** `expr` is the typed line (`sin(30)+1`, `3 ft to cm`), `res` the plain result (`1.5`, `1.5e20`, or `91.44 cm` for a unit conversion). Same shape as Standard's entries, so older bundles read them; reuse takes the number before the first space.
- **Device-local `oros-calculator-prefs`** (R10, never synced): `{ panelWidth, ui: { mode: std|sci|graph|prog|fin, angle: deg|rad|grad, second, graph: { fns[4] (≤200 chars), angle, view: { cx, cy, ppu } | null }, prog: { base: 2|8|10|16, bits: 8|16|32|64, view: keys|bits }, fin: { tool: vat|pct|loan|save, vatMode: add|remove, vals: { "<field id>": text ≤40 } } } }`. `normUi()` validates every field on load; anything unknown falls back to the default (Standard, DEG, graph `sin(x)` in RAD, DEC / QWORD, VAT add).
- **Pure logic `calculator/core.js` (CalcCore, UMD, tests `tests/calculator-core.test.js`):** own tokenizer + recursive-descent parser (no eval/Function): `+ −` < `× ÷ mod` and implicit multiplication (left to right) < unary minus < `^` (right-assoc, `-2^2 = -4`) < postfix `! % ² ³`; `a ± b%` = a·(1 ± b/100) like the Standard key. Decimal mark `.` or `,`, argument separator `;`, "1 000" thousands groups, `E` exponent (`2e3` is 2000, a bare `2e` is 2·e). Unknown words are split into known names (`2pix`, `sinx`). Sums are rounded to the precision of the larger operand (`0.1+0.2−0.3 = 0`), `floor/ceil/mod/!` round to 15 digits first, exact trig zeros at multiples of 90° (100 grad), `tan(90°)` is a domain error. `formatNum`: 15 significant digits, `1.5e20` style outside 1e-9…1e16. Errors are codes (`syntax paren name char domain div0 big end args digit empty` + unit codes), translated by the app.
- **Units in expressions:** `CalcCore.unitConvert(text, UnitsCore, { rates, env })` splits at the last `to|in|into|as|σε|→|->` whose right side is a unit alias, takes the longest alias at the end of the left side and evaluates what precedes it (empty = 1). It builds its alias index from `UnitsCore.CATS / unitsOf / aliasesOf` and converts with `UnitsCore.convert`: no unit data is copied (a test checks that no factors appear in core.js). Category preference = Unit Converter's table order with Cooking last. Currency uses Unit Converter's device-local `oros-units-rates`; when missing, the app fetches with `UnitsCore.RATES_URLS` + `readRates` and stores into the same key (≈15 lines of fetch code duplicate `units.js fetchRates`; a shared `UnitsCore.fetchRates(fetch)` would remove them — proposal).
- **Programmer:** BigInt, every operation wrapped with `BigInt.asIntN(bits)`; precedence `| NOR` < `^` < `& NAND` < `<< >>` < `+ −` < `× ÷ mod` < unary `− ~ NOT`; `/` truncates; `>>` arithmetic. Display: DEC signed, HEX/OCT/BIN two's complement of the word.
- **Finance:** VAT add/remove (cents), percentage change / % of / what %, loan with bank rounding (instalment to cents, the last one absorbs the rest, ≤1200 months), savings monthly or yearly compounding (yearly: deposits earn simple interest within the year), CSV with formula-injection guard.
- **Graph:** canvas, equal x/y scale, pan (drag), zoom (wheel, pinch, buttons), trace (tap/hover), points of interest from 300 samples of the visible range (bisection roots, golden-section extrema with a pole guard, pairwise intersections), recomputed 180 ms after the view settles.

**SHELL slice v2** (SH-D1, verified 2026-10-06):

```
shell = { lang, theme, skin, wallpaper, syncInterval, autoexport,
          alarms[{ id, at, label, repeat: once|daily, state:"pending", mtime }],
          weather{ on, auto, lat, lon, label },
          wpart: recipe | null,                                                    // since 0.45.04
          ver: 2,
          sm{ lang, theme, skin, wallpaper, syncInterval, autoexport, weather, wpart },   // ms stamps
          alarmTombs{ <id>: { t, x } } }                                           // t = deletion ms, x = the once-alarm's time, 0 for daily
```

- **Stamps:** 0 = still the default, 1 = customized before stamps existed, otherwise the ms of the change. A side WITHOUT `sm` (old bundle, old backup file) counts as 1 for every valid setting it carries. An invalid or missing setting is "default at 0".
- **Merge (`shellMerge`):** per setting, higher stamp wins, tie → greater JSON. Alarms: union by id, higher `mtime` wins (tie → greater JSON), alive only if `mtime` > tombstone `t`; a once-alarm whose time has passed is dropped. Tombstones: expired ones (`x > 0` and `x` + 1 day ≤ now) are dropped per side BEFORE the union; then `t` = max, `x` = 0 if either is 0, else max.
- Fuzz 2026-10-06: 20,000 random triples (legacy and v2 sides, invalid values, tombstones): symmetric, idempotent, associative, fixed point, every output setting comes from an input, no live alarm lost, no deleted alarm back. 0 violations.
- **`wpart` (0.45.04):** the "Mine" wallpaper recipe of the Wallpaper Generator (WALLPAPER v1 recipe), validated by `OrosWallArt.normRecipe`; a field like the others (own stamp, LWW). `wallpaper: "custom"` selects it. An older bundle has no such field: it treats "custom" as invalid (default at stamp 0), so the newer side wins without ping-pong.
- Storage: the scalar settings stay in their own keys (`wpart` in `oros-wallpaper-art`); `oros-shell-stamps`, `oros-alarms`, `oros-alarm-tombs` (all travel inside this slice).

**MAPS v1** [log — Doses 1–3, 2026-10-04]:

```
oros-maps-data = { ver:1, places[{ id, name, sub, lat, lon, mtime }], deleted{ <id>: <ts> } }
```

- `id` is deterministic: `"p" + lat.toFixed(6) + "," + lon.toFixed(6)`. The same place starred on two devices is one entity. Legacy random ids are re-derived by `normalize()` on load; duplicates collapse to the newer mtime.
- `normalize()` is the single funnel (load, save, merge output, `sliceGet`, `sliceSet`): places sorted by id, tombstone keys sorted, fixed field order.
- **Merge:** union by id, LWW by mtime (tie: lexicographic JSON); tombstones max-ts union; a place survives only if `mtime > tombstone` (delete wins ties, a newer star resurrects). No tombstone pruning.
- The places list keeps its visible order (oldest first) although storage is id-sorted.
- A fresh install persists nothing until the first real change. Unreadable data is copied to `oros-maps-rescue`, never overwritten silently.
- **Device-local route snapshot** `oros-maps-route`: `{ ver:1, from, to, vias[], profile, geometry, steps, distance, duration }`. `from` / `to` / `vias[]` are `{ lat, lon, name, sub }`; "My location" carries `me: true` (its lat/lon are re-measured whenever a route is calculated). `vias` (stops, at most 3) is additive since 0.43.00: an older snapshot without it restores with no stops. Steps are stored slim, `{ maneuver:{ type, modifier, exit?, location? }, name, ref?, distance, duration, via? }`; `via: n` marks the "arrive" step that ends leg n (stop n), so the panel, the HUD and a re-route know the stops. Since 1.55.00 a step may carry `lanes: [{ i: [indication…], v: 0|1 }]` (the maneuver's turn lanes, indications from OSRM's fixed list, at most 16; additive, older snapshots have none). OSRM per-step `geometry` and `intersections` are never stored. Only the route in use is stored, never the alternatives. Cap 600,000 characters; over the cap, or on a quota failure, the key is REMOVED with one toast per session.

**MAPSOSM v1** (slice `mapsosm`, key `oros-maps-osm-data`, `maps/osm.js` normalize / merge, since 1.43.00):

```
{ ver: 1,
  set:    { m, comment },          // "" = default "Uploaded using orOS Maps"; ≤ 255 chars
  drafts: { <id>: { id, m, dev, kind: note|comment|close|reopen, srv: live|dev,
                    lat?, lon? (note), note? (OSM note id), text, err? } },
  tombs:  { <id>: ts } }
```

- A draft = an OSM note action not sent yet (offline, or OSM answered 5xx / 429). Only the device in `dev` sends it automatically; "Send from here" rewrites `dev` with a newer m. A sent draft becomes a tomb (ts > m), so an older copy on another device never comes back and nothing is sent twice.
- Text: control characters removed, ≤ 2000 (OSM's limit). ≤ 500 drafts, ≤ 2000 tombs (oldest dropped, deterministic). Symmetric, idempotent, associative (fuzz in `tests/maps-osm.test.js`).
- Device-local (never synced; factory reset sweeps `oros-*`): `oros-maps-osm` (server choice + per-server access token, user name, uid), `oros-maps-osm-pkce` (one sign-in in flight, 15 min), `oros-maps-osm-cb` (callback hand-off, one-shot), `oros-maps-osm-dev` (device id for drafts), `oros-maps-osm-mine` (last reply seen per note), `oros-maps-osm-rescue`.

**MAPSEDITS v1** (slice `mapsedits`, key `oros-maps-edits-data`, `maps/poi-core.js` normalizeEdits / mergeEdits, since 1.45.00):

```
{ ver: 1,
  edits: { <id>: { id, m, dev, srv: live|dev, op: create|modify|delete, t: n|w|r,
                   oid (0 for create), lat?, lon? (create, or a moved node),
                   set: { k: v | "" },     // "" = remove the key
                   was: { k: v | "" },     // modify only: the value the user saw
                   name, pre (preset id), err? } },
  tombs: { <id>: ts } }
```

- An edit = a place change not uploaded yet. Only the device in `dev` uploads it ("Upload from here" takes it over with a newer m); after the upload it becomes a tomb (ts > m), so nothing is uploaded twice. A failed upload keeps the edit with `err` (409 conflict, element gone, node used by a way).
- Upload: one changeset per tap (comment = MAPSOSM `set.comment`, `created_by` "orOS Maps <ver>", `source=survey`); each modify is rebased on the element's current tags: keys the user didn't touch follow the server; a key both sides changed keeps the server value and is reported.
- Keys ≤ 255 chars without "=" or control characters, values cleaned ≤ 255; ≤ 120 keys per edit, ≤ 500 edits, ≤ 2000 tombs. Symmetric, idempotent, associative (fuzz in `tests/maps-poi.test.js`).
- The places themselves (Overpass result, ≤ 600, at zoom ≥ 17, reused 30 minutes) live only in memory.

**MAPSQUESTS v1** (slice `mapsquests`, key `oros-maps-quests-data`, `maps/quests-core.js` normalize / merge, since 1.53.00):

```
{ ver: 1,
  answers: { <id>: { id, m, dev, srv: live|dev, q (quest id), t: n|w|r, oid, lat, lon,
                     set{k: v}, was{k: v|""}, name, err? } },   // ≤ 500, newest m kept
  tombs:   { <id>: ts },                                       // ≤ 2000
  hide:    { "<t><oid>:<quest>": ts },                         // ≤ 3000, max wins
  set:     { m, off: [quest ids] },                            // LWW by m
  done:    { <dev>: { "YYYY-MM-DD": n } } }                    // per device and day, max wins (≤ 20 devices, 400 days)
```

Only the device in `dev` uploads an answer; the answer counter is a G-counter per device, so two devices never double count. Elements from Overpass stay in memory only. Since 1.67.00 `q` may also be an overlay-only quest (`OVERLAY_ONLY` in quests-core.js: `sidewalk`); overlay changes for lights, surface and house numbers use `way_lit`, `way_surface` and `housenumber`.

**MAPSQSTATS v1** (slice `mapsqstats`, key `oros-maps-qstats-data`, `maps/quests-core.js` normStats / mergeStats, since 1.65.00):

```
{ ver: 1,
  cnt:  { <dev>: { <quest id>: n } },   // answers uploaded per device and quest, max wins (≤ 20 devices); unknown quest ids kept
  team: { m, size: 1-12, idx: 0..size-1 } }   // LWW by m; size 1 = solo
```

Achievements are computed, not stored: the sum of `cnt` per quest category (`CATS`) against `LEVELS` [1, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000]. Team mapping keeps an element when FNV-1a("<t><id>") mod size = idx (`teamOf` / `teamKeeps`), so every member sees a disjoint share without a server. Own slice because an older version's `mapsquests` normalizer would drop new top-level fields.

**MAPSENTR v1** (slice `mapsentr`, key `oros-maps-entr-data`, `maps/everydoor-core.js` normalize / merge, since 1.69.00):

```
{ ver: 1,
  items: { <id>: { id, m, dev, srv: live|dev, op: create|modify, lat, lon,
                   wid, a, b,          // create: building way + the two nodes of the edge
                   oid,                // modify: node id (an entrance or a building corner)
                   set{k: v}, was{k: v|""}, name, err? } },   // ≤ 300, newest m kept; modify may set "" (remove)
  tombs: { <id>: ts } }                                    // ≤ 2000
```

Only the device in `dev` uploads. A create is inserted between `a` and `b` in the way's current node list (either order); if that edge is gone the item keeps an error. Building outlines and entrance nodes from Overpass stay in memory only.

**MAPSFAV v1** (slice `mapsfav`, key `oros-maps-fav-data`, `maps/fav-core.js` normalize / merge, since 1.75.00):

```
{ ver: 1,
  groups: { <gid>: { name, color, m } },   // gid g[a-z0-9]{4,24}; name ≤ 60, no control chars or <>; color from COLORS; ≤ 100, newest m kept
  pins:   { <place id>: { g, m } },        // place id = slice maps id (p<lat6>,<lon6>); g "" = no group; ≤ 5000
  tombs:  { <gid>: ts } }                  // ≤ 300; a tomb ≥ m drops the group
```

Groups and pins are LWW by m (equal m → larger canonical JSON); tombs max-union. A pin whose group is gone reads as "no group". Pins are their own records, not a field of the places in slice `maps`, so a device on an older version that rewrites `maps` cannot drop them. Which groups are hidden from the map or folded in the list is device-local (`oros-maps-fav-prefs`: `{ hide: [gid], fold: [gid | "_none"] }`).

**MAPSTRACKS v1** (slice `mapstracks`, key `oros-maps-tracks-data`, `maps/tracks-core.js` normalizeTracks / mergeTracks, since 1.47.00):

```
{ ver: 1,
  tracks: { <id>: { id, m, name, color (#rrggbb), folder, hidden: 0|1,
                    start (ms), dur, moving (ms), dist, up, down (m), n (points),
                    bbox: [s, w, n, e] | null,
                    prev,                 // Google polyline, ≤ 300 points, ≤ 8000 chars
                    src: rec|import } },
  tombs:  { <id>: ts } }
```

Since 1.48.00 an uploaded track's OSM trace page URL lives in its GPX file (`<metadata><link href="https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/<u>/traces/<n>">`), not in the entry: the entry shape is unchanged, so 1.47.00 devices merge it without loss.

- The points live in the GPX 1.1 file `/internal/Maps/Tracks/<id>.gpx` (orOS disk; Files and Vault Drive see it). The entry carries what the list, the search and another device need before the file arrives (`prev` is drawn instead of the file). Deleting a track writes a tomb and removes the file.
- A recording in progress is device-only: IndexedDB `oros-maps-rec` (store `rec`, key `cur`: `{ id, started, segs, paused }`), saved every 10 s and on pagehide / hidden; next boot offers Continue / Save / Discard. Factory reset deletes the database. The GPX file is written only on Save.
- Reading files (`parseAny`): strict string scanner for GPX (trk / rte / wpt), KML (LineString, gx:Track, Point) and GeoJSON (LineString, MultiLineString, Point); ≤ 20 MB, ≤ 500,000 points, ≤ 2000 waypoints, coordinates only as numbers in range, names as plain text (≤ 120). No DOM, no entities beyond the XML five and numeric references.
- ≤ 2000 tracks, ≤ 4000 tombs. Symmetric, idempotent, associative (fuzz in `tests/maps-tracks.test.js`).

**MAPS OFFLINE PACKS** (wave 51, `maps/offline-core.js` pure + Node-tested in `tests/maps-offline.test.js`, `maps/offline.js` UI / storage / drawing; device-only, never synced):

- **Source.** Default: the newest daily Protomaps build of OpenStreetMap, `https://build.protomaps.com/<yyyymmdd>.pmtiles` (newest date from `https://build-metadata.protomaps.dev/builds.json` `[{ key: "<yyyymmdd>.pmtiles" }]`; if that list is down, the last 10 days' names are probed with a 127-byte range). PMTiles v3, vector (MVT) tiles, gzip, zoom 0–15, Protomaps basemap layers (earth, water, landuse, landcover, roads, transit, buildings, boundaries, places, pois; `kind` or v3 `pmap:kind`). Data ODbL (© OpenStreetMap contributors), attribution "© OpenStreetMap contributors, Protomaps" on the layer. Nothing needs a key. A pack is cut out of the planet file the way `pmtiles extract` does: header + root directory (first 16 KB), only the leaf directories the box needs (≤ 4 in parallel, cached per check), then the tiles' byte ranges. OSMF tiles (tile.openstreetmap.org) are never bulk-downloaded (tile usage policy). Device-local `oros-maps-packs` `{ src }` may name another http(s) PMTiles file (vector, gzip or none, Protomaps layout); anything else (raster, brotli, zstd, v2) is refused with a message.
- **Planning.** The box = the map area the sheet does not cover. Tile ids z0..N of the box (Hilbert, as the spec; checked against the reference pmtiles 3.2.1); N = the highest zoom ≤ 15 with ≤ 600,000 tiles (`MAX_TILES`); below z10 the box is "too big". `resolve` walks root → leaves (depth ≤ 4, run lengths honoured, absent tiles dropped). `sizesByZoom` gives the bytes per level (unique blobs, so equal sea tiles count once) for the four choices z10 / z12 / z14 / z15 (capped at the source's max zoom). `makePack(res, z)` keeps tiles ≤ z, dedups blobs by source offset, sorts them and merges neighbours into download chunks (gap ≤ 32 KB, chunk ≤ 4 MB; a bigger tile is its own chunk). Free space (`navigator.storage.estimate`) must exceed the size + 5 %; `navigator.storage.persist()` is asked on the first download.
- **Storage (OPFS).** `maps-packs/<id>/` (id `p` + base36 time + random): `meta.json` = `{ v:1, id, name ≤ 80, bbox [w,s,e,n], maxz, src, build (yyyymmdd or ""), created, bytes, tiles, chunks, tc 1|2 (tile compression), state dl|index|ready, paused, sig (header offsets/lengths of the source), words, replaces (id of the pack an Update replaces) }`, normalised by `normMeta` (unknown state → dl, non-http src → ""). `plan.bin` = `packToBin`: Float64 header [1, nTiles, nChunks, maxz], Float64 tile ids (sorted), Uint32 chunk index / offset in chunk / length per tile, pad to 8, Float64 chunk source start / length; `binToPack` rejects a wrong size, unsorted ids or a tile outside its chunk. `c<k>` = chunk k's bytes exactly as on the server (still gzip). `search.json` = `[[name, alt names joined by "|", "<layer>:<kind>", lat, lon]]`.
- **Download.** One pack at a time, 3 parallel range requests, 3 tries each; each chunk is written whole with `createWritable` (no partial files), so a chunk is done iff its file has its length: resume (after Pause, a reload or a lost connection) only fetches the rest. Before resuming, the source's header must still give the same `sig` (else "replaced on the server", delete and redo). A 200 instead of 206 for a range not at 0 = "no partial downloads". Lost connection → paused without error and resumed on `online`; a pack in dl/index state that was not paused resumes when Maps opens. Then `index`: the top zoom's tiles give every named feature (points; middle of a line's middle segment; average of an outer ring), lower zooms only `places`; features whose position is in the tile buffer are skipped; `addr:housenumber` + `addr:street` without a name become "street number" (kind `address`); same folded name + kind within 1/50° merge (`buildIndex`, ≤ 250,000 entries). Then `ready`. Update = a new pack with the same box / zoom / name and `replaces`; the old one is deleted when the new one is ready. Cancel / Delete remove the folder.
- **Drawing.** `L.GridLayer` ("Offline map (downloaded)", `orosId` "offline", added through `__orosMapsHost.addBaseLayer`; the choice is kept in `oros-maps-prefs.layer` like the others). Per tile: the ready pack with the highest maxz containing it; above its maxz the parent tile is drawn scaled (overzoom, sharp). Canvas at devicePixelRatio ≤ 2; order: water background, earth, landcover / landuse fills, water, buildings (z ≥ 14), road casings then fills (minor < major < highway; paths dashed z ≥ 14; service z ≥ 14), rail, country / region borders, labels (places by population_rank, road names along the longest piece z ≥ 14/15, POIs z ≥ 16) with a halo and per-tile collision; a label that would cross the tile edge is not drawn. No pack → a hatched tile. Decoded tiles LRU 96, chunk `File`s 48 per pack. When the device goes offline over a pack, the layer switches to it (toast) and back on `online`.
- **Search.** `__orosMapsHost.offlineSearch(q, [lat, lon], limit)` → Promise of hits `{ name, sub: "<kind> · <pack> (offline)", lat, lon, kind: "place" }`, or null when there is no ready pack. maps.js uses it offline, and online when Photon fails (search bar, route planner, `?q=` deep links). Matching: NFD without accents, lower case, ς → σ, then Greek letters to Latin (`latin`) on both sides; whole-name prefix > every word starts a word > contained; places before POIs; nearer first.

**TELEVISION v1** [log]:

```
oros-television-data = { ver, favorites[], deleted{}, sources[]?, srcDel{}? }
  sources[] = { id, kind: "m3u" | "xmltv", url, name, mtime }   (since wave 43)
```

- **Merge:** mirror of the Radio merge (union by channel id, LWW by mtime, JSON tie-break; delete wins ties, a newer edit resurrects).
- **Sources (wave 43):** the synced list of the user's playlist (M3U) and programme-guide (XMLTV) addresses, never their contents. `id` = `m`/`x` + 16-hex hash of the URL (`orosTvCore.sourceId`), so the same address added on two devices is one entry. Merge `mergeSources` (television/core.js): union by id, LWW by `mtime` (tie: larger JSON), `srcDel` tombs max-union, a tomb wins ties, a newer add resurrects; fuzz-tested symmetric / idempotent / associative. `sources` / `srcDel` are written only when non-empty and sorted (id / key), so old data stays byte-identical and loads unchanged. URLs http(s) only (≤ 2048), ≤ 100 sources. A device on an older build drops the two keys in its own merge; the next new-build device brings them back only from its own copy (decision: accepted, every device runs the same PWA build within a day).
- **Device-local (wave 43):** `oros-television-files` (files opened on this device: `{ id: "f"+hash, kind, name, mtime }`, never synced). Contents live in Cache Storage `oros-television-api`: `pl-<id>.json` (parsed playlist; addresses refresh after 24 h, stale copy kept on failure), `epg-<id>-<ymd>.json` (a guide address, today's window −3 h … +30 h, one per day; older days deleted), `epgf-<id>.json` (a guide file, −1 day … +7 days).
- **Guides:** iptv-org publishes no guide files (its epg repository ships only the grabber since GitHub Actions were disabled; `api/guides.json` maps channels to grabber sites, no programmes). So guides are user XMLTV addresses / files only. Network: `feeds/fetch.js` `fetchOne` (direct, then the Mail relay `web` op, 5 MB per response), `.gz` unpacked with `DecompressionStream`. A playlist that names `url-tvg` / `x-tvg-url` adds that guide on Add (not if the user removed it before: tomb present).
- **Parsing (television/core.js, no DOM):** M3U `#EXTM3U` / `#EXTINF` attributes (`tvg-id`, `tvg-name`, `tvg-logo`, `group-title`, `tvg-chno`), `#EXTGRP`; stream URLs http(s) only, ≤ 50,000 channels, channel id `m3u:` + hash(stream URL). XMLTV: string scanner, entities = XML five + numeric, CDATA kept as text, preferred title language = UI language, times `YYYYMMDDhhmmss ±zzzz` (no zone = UTC), open-ended programmes closed at the next start, ≤ 300,000 programmes. Logos and icons https only. Every string is text; the app escapes it.
- **Matching:** guide channel id lowercased without `@feed` against the channel's `tvg-id`, then its id (iptv-org ids), then a normalised name (accents, case, `HD`/`1080p`/bracket tags dropped) against the guide's display names.
- Recents (`oros-television-recents`, cap 20) and volume are device-local. One note says the proxy slice carries "favorites + recents"; that contradicts the rest (A11).
- Deep-link payload `{ channelId }`; notification deep link `television:channel:<id>`.

---

**SEASONAL v1** (`seasonal.js`, slice `seasonal`, key `oros-seasonal`, since 2.23.00):

```
oros-seasonal = { ver:1, f:{ <field>: { v, t } } }   fields sorted
fields: on (bool, default true) · motion auto|still · amount low|mid|high · xmas tree|boat · easter orthodox|western (2.25.00) · bday "MM-DD"|"" (2.25.00) · ev.<id> (bool, default per event)
oros-seasonal-local (device, never synced) = { keep: { id, until: YYYY-MM-DD } | null, hide: YYYY-MM-DD | null }
```

- Per-field LWW: `t` moves only at the user's change, always forward (`max(now, t + 1)`); merge = higher `t`, tie → greater JSON; symmetric, idempotent, associative (fuzz in tests/seasonal.test.js). Unknown fields from a newer bundle (small primitives, `/^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}(\.[a-z0-9]{1,24})?$/`, max 120) are kept. A fresh device stores nothing; nothing is written because of the date.

**LAUNCHER v1** (`launcher.js`, slice `launcher`, key `oros-launcher-data`, since 0.49.00):

```
oros-launcher-data = { ver:1, items[{ id, desk: number|null, dock: number|null, mtime }] }
```

- One item per app id (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$/`), sorted by id, fixed field order; `normalize()` is the single funnel (load, save, merge output, slice get / set). At most 500 items.
- `desk` / `dock` are fractional order keys; shown order = key, then id. Pin = end of the place (max + 1); moving one shortcut writes only that item (midpoint of its new neighbours); when keys get closer than 1e-6 the place is renumbered 1..n (every item stamped, rare). A drag is `moveTo` (a chain of moves).
- `mtime` moves only at the mutation site, always forward (`max(now, mtime + 1)`). A removal keeps the item with both places null: it is its own tombstone.
- **Merge:** union by id, higher `mtime` wins, tie → greater canonical JSON. Fuzz (20,000 triples): symmetric, idempotent, associative, fixed point, canonical, every output item from an input, inputs not mutated.
- A fresh device writes nothing until the first real change (`get()` returns null). Unreadable data is copied to `oros-launcher-data-broken`.
- Device-local (never synced): `oros-launcher-prefs` = `{ on, size: s|m|l, hover, magnify, autohide, over: true|false|null, style }` (over null = never chosen = off; a stored true / false is the user's choice and is kept; style unknown = classic; hover never chosen = magnify, or none when the old `magnify` was false; `magnify` is still written as hover === "magnify" for older bundles). A phone and a PC want different docks; only the pins travel. The factory reset sweeps both (`oros-*`).

**MENU APPS v1** (`launcher.js` 1.3.0 section 1b, slice `menu`, key `oros-menu-apps`; Chris 2026-10-11 "Απόκρυψη όλων, εμφάνιση όλων, επιλογή"):

```
oros-menu-apps = { ver:1, apps[{ id, hidden: boolean, mtime }] }
```

- Which apps the menu lists. An app with no item is shown, so a new app always appears. Showing an app again keeps its item (`hidden:false`, new mtime): it is its own tombstone. Same id rule, 500 cap, sorting and `mtime` discipline as LAUNCHER v1; `menuSetHidden(data, ids, hidden, now)` stamps only the apps whose state really changes (Hide all / Show all = one change, one push).
- **Merge:** union by id, higher `mtime` wins, tie → greater canonical JSON (hidden wins). Its own slice, not a field of `launcher`: an older bundle's `normalize()` would drop an unknown field, while an unknown slice is carried untouched.
- A fresh device writes nothing until the first real change. Unreadable data is copied to `oros-menu-apps-broken`. Factory reset sweeps it (`oros-*`).
- First-run profiles write through `menuPreset` (`mtime: 1`, only apps without an item): a real choice on any device always wins. Known limit: an app nobody ever touched on the other devices stays hidden there too after a fresh device picked a profile before connecting sync; the screen offers "I already use orOS on another device" and is skipped once sync is connected or menu data exists.
- Hidden means "not in the menu list" only: the menu search still lists it (while a query is typed), universal search hits, deep links (`__orosOpenAt`, `openAppById`), desktop shortcuts and the Dock still open it.

**PHOTOLAB v1** (`photolab/`, Photo Lab / Εργαστήριο εικόνας, 0.97.00)
- Doc / Layer: see the header of `photolab/core.js`.
- Disk: `/internal/Photo Lab/<id>/doc.json`, `t-<28 hex>.plt` (tile files "PLT1" + deflate-raw RGBA 256×256, content-named, never rewritten), `thumb.jpg`. Vault Drive syncs them per file.
- Slice `photolab` (`oros-photolab-data`): project index only, LWW per project + tombstones.
- **Wave 44 (subject, RAW, batch):** no change to Doc, Layer, the disk layout or the slice; old projects load unchanged.
  - Select subject / Remove background (`photolab/subject.js`): loads `atelier/cutout.js` on first use (script tag, same `?v=`) and calls its public API only (`ready`, `cut`, `alphaFor`, `S`, `LO`); the model files stay in Atelier's IndexedDB `oros-atelier-ai` (same origin, shared by both apps). Input: the flattened visible picture at ≤1024 px. Output: `alphaFor(mask, S, doc.w, doc.h, lo, lo + 0.76)` → `PL.setSel` (Select › Subject) or a new `L.mk` `{bg: 0, on: 1}` written only over its non-zero box, replacing an existing mask, one `docChange` step (Layer › Remove background).
  - Camera RAW (`photolab/raw.js`, pure part Node-tested): `PL.RAW.decode(blob, {half, signal})` first develops with LibRaw (`vendor/libraw/`, unmodified libraw-wasm 1.6.0 = LibRaw 0.22.1, LGPL-2.1/CDDL-1.0; dynamic `import()` only when a RAW is opened, its module worker disposed after every file; settings: camera WB, AHD, sRGB, 8 bit; phones always half size). Its memory is a shared WebAssembly.Memory: Chromium allows it without cross-origin isolation as long as no thread starts; where it fails, `previews(bytes)` gives the embedded JPEGs (TIFF IFD chain + SubIFDs + Exif IFD: 0x201/0x202, JPEG strips with compression 6/7/99, RW2 0x2E; RAF header 84/88; then a bounded scan for SOI in anything else, e.g. CR3/ORF/X3F), only whole baseline/progressive frames (lossless SOF3 raw data dropped), biggest first; orientation = the JPEG's own Exif if any (the browser applies it), else IFD0 0x112. ≤300 MB per RAW.
  - Batch (`photolab/batch.js` UI + runner, `photolab/batchcore.js` pure + worker op `stack`): items `{name, file}` or `{name, path}` (orOS disk picker), ≤2000; per photo: decode (browser, or `PL.RAW.decode` with half size when the output is ≤ half: `rawHalf`) → `targetSize` (none | long | w | h | pct, `up` = may enlarge, ≤8192 and the device limit) with halving steps → adjustment stack in the worker (`stackOf(doc.layers)`: visible adj layers with op, masks ignored; or `stackFromXmp(xmp.parse(...).layers)`) → watermark (text: % of short side, shadowed; picture: % of width; 9 places, 3% margin, opacity) → JPG (white below) / PNG / WebP (PNG when no WebP encoder) → `fileName(pattern)` tokens `{name} {n} {nn…} {date} {w} {h}`, `uniqueName` against the folder's existing files → `/internal/Pictures/<folder>/` or an in-memory stored ZIP (`AtelierZip.write`, ≤1 GB) saved from a button on the end screen (a user gesture for the save picker). Stop aborts after the current photo. Device-local `prefs.batch` (`norm`), never synced; the item list and the watermark picture are not kept.

- **CRM (`oros-crm-data`, slice `crm`, `crm/core.js` UMD `OrosCrmCore`)**: `{ ver:1, cust[], deals[], acts[], fups[], tags[], prefs{pm,cur,forget}, tombs{id:ms} }`.
  - cust `{id,m,name,kind:"co"|"person",st:"lead"|"active"|"past",alias?,afm?,doy?,job?,addr?,country?,phone?,email?,web?,src?,note?,star?,ct,tags[],people[{c?,n,role?,phone?,email?}]}`; a person with `c` is a Contacts id (read live, never copied); phone/email stored only for unlinked people.
  - deal `{id,m,cust,title,val (cents),stage:new|contact|proposal|nego|won|lost,prob?,close?,cd?,why?,note?,ct}`; default probabilities 10/25/50/75/100/0.
  - act `{id,m,cust,k:call|mail|meet|msg|note,at (ms),text,deal?,who?}`; fup `{id,m,cust,d (ymd),text,t? (HH:MM),deal?,done? (ymd)}`; tag `{id,m,name,col 0-7}`.
  - Limits: 2000 customers, 5000 deals, 20000 history, 10000 follow-ups, 50 tags.
- Device-local: `oros-crm-wf` `{ dev, last }` (this device's id for `wf.dev` and its last web-form check), `oros-crm-prefs` (tab, sort, filters, last stage on phones), `oros-crm-notified` (follow-up reminder keys already sent, pruned; since 1.14.00 written by the shell `crmCheckTick`, not the app: `{ "<fupId>|<day><time>": 1 }`, only keys still due are kept).
- (v1.2.0, 1.22.00) `stg[]` (LWW by m, tombstones for own stages): `{ id, m, name?, prob?, pos?, off? }`. id `new` | `contact` | `proposal` | `nego` = an override of a built-in open stage (name "" → built-in label; `off: 1` hides it; never tombstoned); any other id (ID_RE) = an own open stage (name required, prob default 50). `pos` orders the open stages (built-ins 10/20/30/40). Won and Lost are fixed. At most 8 open stages on the board; all hidden → New comes back. `deal.stage` may now be an own stage id. Derived: `OrosCrmCore.stages(data)`, `stageOf(data, deal)` (unknown → first open stage), `dealProb(d, data)`.
- Known limit: while a device still runs CRM 1.1 (before its update), its normalizer turns an own-stage id into "new" if it re-saves that deal; the newer app keeps the stage list itself.
- **Web form (`wf`, crm/webform.js, approved by Chris; relay side approved by the relay owner):** one top-level record, absent until a form is made (older data keeps its bytes). On: `{ m, k [a-z0-9]{16}, sec [A-Za-z0-9]{32}, priv (RSA-OAEP-256 private JWK: kty, alg, n, e, d, p, q, dp, dq, qi), back? (https ≤ 300, no userinfo), dev? (the collecting device, [a-z0-9]{6,20}), at? }`; off: `{ m, off: 1 }` (so "off" reaches the other devices). `normWf`; merge = last writer wins by m, equal m → larger canonical JSON; wf.m counts for the tomb pruning clock. In a backup like the rest.
  - **Why the keys sync (Newsletter's decision for list forms, followed):** k, sec and the private key guard only the messages that become this CRM's own synced data, so syncing them exposes nothing more than the data already exposes; kept device-local, losing the device would orphan the form and other devices could not show the HTML or take over the collecting. One device collects (`dev`, "Collect on this device"), so two devices never pull at the same time.
  - **Pick-up:** relay op `crmf` `pull` (after 0, ≤ 100 rows, ≤ 10 pages a check) → open each row on the device (RSA-OAEP unwraps the AES-GCM key, as `relay/newsletter.js seal`) → `apply` → commit → `ack upto` (delete at the relay only once saved; a commit failure leaves them there). Manual "Check for new leads" and a quiet check on boot / visibility, at most every 10 minutes (`AUTO_EVERY`), only on the collecting device and online.
  - **A message → data (`OrosCrmWebForm.apply`, pure):** `{e, n?, p?, c?, m?, l, t}`; e via `mailLog` (lower-cased). E-mail already known (`custByEmail`: the customer's own, a person's, a Contacts-linked person's live address) → only an act `{k: "msg", at: t, text: message (or "Sent the web form without a message."), who: name}`, with "Name / Phone / Company: …" lines under it for details the record does not show; the record itself never changes. New → a customer `st "lead"`, `src` "Web form" / «Φόρμα ιστότοπου» (app language), `ct` = t: with a company → kind co named after it with the person as a `people` line (n, email, phone); else kind person (name or the e-mail, email, phone); plus the act. The same act (customer, at, text) twice is skipped, so a pull repeated after a failed ack adds nothing. Customer / history limits → counted as "didn't fit", never stored. A time later than now + 1 day → now.
  - Snippet (`OrosCrmWebForm.snippet(wf, relay, lang)`): plain `<form method="post" action="<relay>/crm/f/<k>" accept-charset="utf-8">` with name, email (required), phone, company, message (≤ 2000), hidden `lang` en|el, the off-screen honeypot `website`, one button; labels EN/EL; no script; every value escaped. Relay address = Mail's relay setting, else orOS's (`relayOf`, same as Newsletter).
