  - Mixed versions: an older CRM drops `wf` in its own merge; the newer devices' merge keeps it (absent never beats present), so the same transient re-upload as other new fields runs until that device updates. Tests: `tests/crm-webform.test.js`, `tests/crm-form-relay.test.js`.

- **STOCK v1** (slice `stock`, key `oros-stock-data`, since 1.04.00): `{ ver: 1, items[], cats[], units[], sups[], moves[], settings{m, cur, vat, neg}, tombs{id: ms} }`. Every row has `id` (`[a-z0-9]{6,40}`) and `m` (R27: bumped only on a real change). Quantities are integer thousandths (1 piece = 1000, 1 kg = 1000); money is integer cents; dates `YYYY-MM-DD`.
  - item `{name ≤ 80, sku ≤ 40, bc (barcode, no spaces) ≤ 40, cat, unit (ready id pcs|box|pack|pair|set|kg|g|l|ml|m|m2 or an own unit id), min, rq (reorder qty), sup, ssku (supplier's code), cost, price, vat 0–100 (default 24), loc ≤ 60, note ≤ 500, arch 0|1}` (max 20 000).
  - cat `{name}`; unit `{name ≤ 16, dec 0–3}` (an own unit; a ready id is refused); sup `{name, person, tel, email, vatno, lead (days 0–365), note}`.
  - move `{d, t, ref ≤ 60, sup (in / rts only), note ≤ 300, lines[1..500], src?, v?}`. Types and line signs: `in` + (unit cost `c`), `out` − (unit price `p`), `ret` + (customer return), `rts` − (return to supplier), `loss` −, `count` any or 0 with `n` = counted quantity (q = counted − computed at that moment), `fix` ≠ 0. A movement is never edited or deleted: `v: 1` voids it (final, wins the merge whatever its m). `src` (`app:ref`, reserved for BR-ST-OUT) passes through untouched.
  - settings `{m, cur (16 currencies), vat (default for new products), neg (1 = a sale below zero is allowed after a confirm; 0 = refused on this device)}`.
  - Derived, never stored: quantity (`qtyMap`), weighted average cost (`costMap`: receipts with a cost blend in time order; stock that came in without a cost counts at the item's own `cost`), value, low list (`min > 0 && q ≤ min`), suggested order (`rq`, else 2 × min − q, rounded up to the unit), days left (out rate over 30 days).
  - Join: `stock/core.js` `merge` (own keys only, prototype-free maps, strict normalizers drop anything malformed). Tests: `tests/stock.test.js`.
  - **1.1 (1.15.00):** new top-level list `pos[]` (purchase orders) `{id, m, no ≤ 60, sup, d, exp ("" or YYYY-MM-DD), st: draft|sent|closed|cancel, note ≤ 300, lines[1..500] {i, q > 0, c?}}` (one line per item). LWW per id + tombs like suppliers. What arrived is NOT stored on the order: it is the sum of live `in` movements with `src = "po:<id>"` (`receivedMap`), so a receipt voided later un-receives by itself and two devices receiving parts at once both count. Derived state: `partial` (something arrived), `received` (nothing left), else the stored st; `open` = sent or partial. `onOrder` (what open orders still expect) lowers the Reorder suggestion. A 1.0 device drops `pos` on its own merge (costs nothing: a pull never marks dirty; `src` was already carried in 1.0).
  - Reports are derived only (`valueByCat`, `periodSummary`, `deadStock` = stock with no sale / return to supplier / loss for 90 days, `reportRange`).
  - **1.2 (1.24.00):** new top-level list `pics[]` `{id = the item's id, m, f: file name (core.PIC_RE) | ""}`, LWW per id; "" = removed (an edit, no tombstone); a tombstone of the item hides its row too. A separate list, not an item field, so a 1.0 / 1.1 device that edits the item never drops the photo (its own merge drops only the whole list, which costs nothing).
- **1.3 (1.36.00):** lists gain `form: {k:[a-z0-9]{16}, sec:[A-Za-z0-9]{32}, priv:{kty,alg,n,e,d,p,q,dp,dq,qi}, back:https|"", dev, at}|null`. subs.src adds "form".
- **1.4 (1.38.00):** chans (kind smtp) gain `via: "smtp"|"api"` (api only for brevo, postmark, sendgrid, mailgun, mailgun-eu) and `dom` (Mailgun sending domain, else ""). Device state `oros-newsletter-dev` gains `papi: {chanId: last read ms}`.
  - Barcodes are derived only (`barcodeFor`: a 13-digit barcode with a valid check digit → EAN-13, 12 digits get their check digit; otherwise Code 128 set B of the barcode or the SKU, printable ASCII, ≤ 40 chars; `barSvg` writes rects only, no item text in the SVG). Encodings checked against python-barcode for 5 EAN-13 and 4 Code 128 values.
  - **1.4 (1.30.00):** new top-level list `whs[]` `{id, m, name ≤ 80, arch 0|1}`, LWW + tombs; the reserved row id `whmain` only names the main warehouse (never archived). Movement field `w` = warehouse id (absent = main; `whmain` is normalized away). New type `xfer` (transfer): lines q > 0, from `w` to `w2` (must differ); it changes no total: `qtyMap`, `costMap`, `periodSummary`, `deadStock`, `lowList` skip it (`live()`), `whQty` / `qtyIn` count it (−q at w, +q at w2), `itemMoves` lists it with the running total unchanged. A 1.3 device drops `xfer` rows and the `whs` list on its own merge (its totals stay right; the union keeps them on 1.4 devices).
  - Device-local prefs: `wh` (this device's warehouse for new movements and the counter, the last used), `wf` (Products filter, "*" = all), `pos` (1.7: `{pl, head ≤ 300, foot ≤ 200, paper 58|80, dev /^[A-Z2-9]{2}$/}` — the till's price list, receipt header / footer, roll width and register code; made on first use).
  - **1.5 (1.33.00):** line fields `lot` (≤ 40 chars; not on count / fix / xfer) and `exp` (YYYY-MM-DD, only with a lot, only on in / ret). What is left per lot is derived (`lotsOf`, `allLots`): ledger in time order, transfers skipped (lots are business-wide); incoming lines fill their lot (expiry = the earliest given) or "none"; outgoing lines take the lot they name, then the lots that expire first (no expiry last), then "none" (may go below zero). `expiring(data, today, days)` = lots with stock whose exp ≤ today + days (expired included), archived products left out. A 1.4 device strips lot / exp; the richer copy wins the tie on m.
  - **1.6 (1.34.00):** top-level `close` `{id, m, d, at, bal: [{i, q ≠ 0, w?, lot?, exp?}], avg: {itemId: cents}, ls: {itemId: last sale day}, fs: {itemId: first day}, rcv: {poId: {itemId: q}}, ids: "id,id,…", f: archive file name}`. `bal` is read as a pseudo movement `{id: "!open", t: "open", d}` (never stored, never voided) that every walk takes FIRST (`ledger`, `byTime`): qtyMap / whQty (line w) / lots (minus lines go straight to "without a lot") / itemMoves / hasMoves; costMap starts from bal quantities + avg; deadStock from ls / fs; receivedMap adds rcv; periodSummary and outRate see only real movements. `closePeriod(data, d, now, id, file)` is pure and keeps every derived number (tested: quantities, warehouse split, lots, averages, value, low list, dead stock, PO receipts; also a second close on top). Items and warehouses in bal can't be tombstoned away. A 1.5 device keeps full history until it updates.
  - **1.7 (wave 46, point of sale):** three new top-level lists, written only when non-empty (data without a sale stays byte-identical; a 1.6 device drops them on its own merge without marking dirty, like `pos` / `pics`). `sales[]` `{id, m, d, at, no ≤ 24 ("<dev>-<YYMMDD>-<NNN>", per device and day), pay cash|card|other, pl?, given? (cents), mv? (its movement id), w?, v?, lines[1..500] {i, q > 0, p (net cents), vat 0–100, n (name as printed)}}`: union by id, a void wins whatever its m (`mergeSales`, cap 50 000 newest ids). The stock leaves through an ordinary `out` movement `{src: "pos:<sale id>", ref: no, lines q = −q}`, so quantity keeps its one rule; voiding a sale voids its movement and voiding that movement voids the sale. `pls[]` price lists `{id, m, name, pct −90…500, p: {itemId: net cents}}`, LWW + tombs (cap 50); price = own `p`, else sale price × (100 + pct)/100, else the sale price; "Retail" ("" id) is built in. `zs[]` closed days `{id "z"+YYYYMMDD (must match d), m, d, at, no, n, g, net, vat, cash, card, other}`, LWW (cap 4000). Pure rules in `stock/pos-core.js` (`OrosStockPosCore`: priceOf, totals with VAT per rate, nextNo, makeSale, zReport, zRow, nextZ, receiptRows); the UI in `stock/pos.js` (`OrosStockPos.open(api)`, textContent everywhere; the 58/80 mm receipt and Z printouts escape every text). Receipts and Z reports are not fiscal documents. Tests: `tests/stock-pos.test.js`.

- **UNITS v1** `oros-units-data = { ver:1, favs: { "c:f>t": { c, f, t, m } }, recent: { "c:f>t=v[@i]": { c, f, t, v, i?, m } }, prec: { v: 2-12, m } | null, tombs: { id: ms } }`. Merge `UnitsCore.mergeData` (symmetric; ids are deterministic so two devices starring the same pair converge, R16; recent capped at 20 newest by m then id; tombstones capped at 300 newest; junk dropped).

- **TYPING v1** (Typing Tutor, slice `typing`, key `oros-typing-data`, `typing/core.js` `TypingCore`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/typing.test.js`): `{ ver:1, set{m, lay ""|el|en|de|elp|dv|cm (elp/dv/cm wave 4; devices on 4.84.00 or older drop rows of the new layouts when they save), goal 1-120 min, hint auto|on|off, err stop|go, kid 0|1 (wave 3), fs 1-3, rs reset stamp}, prog{"<lay>|<lesson id>": {s stars 0-3, w best wpm ≤ 400, a best accuracy %, m}}, days{"<yyyymmdd>|<dev>": {ms, ch right chars, er wrong presses, n runs, m}}, keys{"<lay>|<dev>": {m, k{<char>: [right, wrong, ms]}}}, best{"<lay>|1|2|5": {w, a, t, m}} }`. `<dev>` = device-local `oros-typing-dev` (a-z0-9, ≤ 12): `days` and `keys` rows are written only by their device (LWW by m, tie larger canonical JSON) and add up across devices; `set` LWW by m; `prog` takes the max of each number (progress never lost); `best` the higher wpm (then accuracy, newer t). The settings merge first and `set.rs` (Reset progress) drops every row with m < rs BEFORE rows are combined, so a pre-reset row never lifts a newer one; `days` keep the 400 newest dates inside the merge. Symmetric, idempotent, associative (tests); bad rows dropped. Lesson ids (`typing/course.js` LESSONS: h1-h6 home row, t1-t6 top, b1-b6 bottom, s1 Shift, s2 quotes/brackets/minus (ä ü ß in German), n1 n2 digits, p1 signs, f1 final text) are stored and NEVER change meaning. Nothing typed is stored, only counts. Device-local `oros-typing-prefs` {snd, osk}.
- **TYPINGTEXTS v1** (Typing Tutor My texts, slice `typingtexts`, key `oros-typing-texts`, `typing/texts.js` `TypingTexts`, Node-tested in `tests/typing-wave2.test.js`): `{ ver:1, items:[{id "t…" (a-z0-9 4-20), m, n title ≤ 80, t text ≤ 20 000}], tombs{id: m} }`. LWW per text by m (tie: larger canonical JSON); a tombstone ≥ the text's m deletes, a newer edit comes back; ≤ 50 texts (the newest m stay, same cut on every device); sorted by id; bad rows dropped. Symmetric, idempotent, associative (R5, R17, R26). A separate slice because TYPING v1 is rebuilt from known fields by wave-1 devices.

- **Invoices (`oros-invoices-data`, slice `invoices`, `invoices/core.js` UMD `OrosInvoicesCore`)**: `{ ver:1, prof{}, series[], clients[], docs[], pays[], tpls[] }`; money in integer cents, ISO currency per document.
  - prof `{name,trade,job,addr,country,afm,doy,phone,email,web,iban,logo (png/jpeg data URL ≤200000 chars),cur,vat,days,wht,plang,terms,footer,m}`.
  - series `{id,kind:inv|rcpt|pro|cred,prefix,year 0|1,digits,m}`; implicit defaults ser-inv INV, ser-rcpt RCT, ser-pro PRO, ser-cred CN. The series used on a device is a device pref.
  - client `{id,m,name,afm,doy,job,addr,country,email,phone,note,crm?}`.
  - doc `{id,m,kind:inv|rcpt|pro|cred|ext,st:draft|issued|void,ser,seq,num,date,due,cur,cli,c{party snapshot},s{seller snapshot, issued only},lines[{code,d,q,unit,p,disc,vat}],gDisc,wht,exempt,terms,notes,ref (credit note → invoice, invoice → proforma),crm,mark,file,sent,plang,xnet?,xvat? (ext)}`.
    - PDF import (`invoices/pdfin.js`): an imported record is an ordinary `ext` doc (no lines: the PDF's lines go into `notes`, so older devices strip nothing), plus flat extras `mdu` (UID) and `mda` (authentication code) as mydata-ui.js names them, never `mds`. Ids are deterministic from the ΜΑΡΚ, else issuer ΑΦΜ + number + date: doc `x…`, new client `c…` (from ΑΦΜ), cash/card payment `p…`, received invoice `b…` (`hashId`), so one PDF imported on two devices is one record after sync.
  - pay `{id,m,doc,date,amt,how,note}`; tpl `{id,m,name,kind,cli,cur,lines,gDisc,wht,exempt,terms,notes,rep:""|m|q|y,next,dom}`; recurring drafts get id `rec-<hash(tpl|date)>` so two devices make the same draft.
  - Payments to Budget (Novus wave 2): flat extra `ab: 1` on a pay made while the setting is on (Budget then keeps an income entry for it, BR-B3); `bud: 1` when sent by hand with BR-B1 (Budget never derives those). Setting: `prof.ab` (`0` = off; absent = on, the default).
  - Limits: 200 lines per document, amounts ≤ 1.000.000.000,00.
  - **Pay online (wave 46):** flat extra `paylink` on `prof` and on each `profs[]` row (an https URL ≤ 500, `payLinkOk`; older devices carry it along). `payLinkFor(link, doc)`: for a stripe.com host adds `client_reference_id` (= doc number, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) and `prefilled_email` (the client's) unless already present; any other https page is used as it is. The PDF of an invoice / proforma that still owes something gets "Pay online" with the link and a QR (`orosQR`); the email body gets a line. The user's own Payment Link only: orOS never stores or asks for a payment key and never learns about the payment. Tests: `tests/invoices-paylink.test.js`.
  - **v1.3 (1.42.00, wave 3):** new top-level `profs[]` `{id,m,name,trade,job,addr,country,afm,doy,phone,email,web,iban,logo,terms,footer}` plus tombs, LWW by m; the key is left out while empty. An older device drops it in its own merge, which costs nothing because the union keeps it on newer devices (same pattern as Stock pics). Flat extras that ride along on older versions: `doc.pid`, `tpl.pid`, `series.pid` (the profile; none = the main `prof`), `prof.qr = 0` (payment QR off).
- Device-local: `oros-invoices-prefs` (tab, filters, dashboard range/currency, series per kind), `oros-invoices-draft` (the editor's unsaved work).

**NEWSLETTER v1** (`newsletter/`, slice `newsletter`, key `oros-newsletter-data`, 1.21.00): `{ ver:1, chans:[{id,m,name,kind:"mail"|"smtp",acct,preset,host,port,sec,user,inbox,rate,cap}], lists:[{id,m,name,chan,from,fromName,reply,lang,addr,why,theme,color,salt}], subs:[{id:"s"+cyrb53(list|email),m,list,email,name,lang,tags[],src,basis,at,conf,off,offSt,inv,bnc,c}], issues:[{id,m,list,subj,pre,fmt:"blocks"|"md",blocks[],md,tags[],st:"draft"|"sending"|"paused"|"sent",lock:{dev,at},start,done,n,err,fail{subId:reason}}], sent:{issueId:[subId]}, supp:["x"+cyrb53("supp|"+email)] }`. Tokens: unsubscribe/confirm "nl-"+cyrb53(salt|subId) (14 chars), subscribe code "nl-"+salt[0..6] (9 chars).
- **1.1 (1.31.00):** issues gain `seg`, `l2:{lang:"en"|"el",subj,pre,fmt,blocks,md}|null`, `when` (ms, st "sched"), st adds "sched" (lock kept for "sched" = scheduling device). New collections: `segs:[{id,m,list,name,tags[],match:"any"|"all",lang:""|"en"|"el"}]` (≤50), `tpls:[{id,m,name,subj,pre,fmt,blocks,md,l2}]` (≤50). Subscriber src adds "crm".
- **1.3 (1.59.00):** `plinks:[{id:"pl"+cyrb53("plink|"+list+"|"+acct+"|"+grp),m,list,acct,p:"mlite"|"mchimp"|"brevo",grp,gname,last}]` (a list ↔ an email-platform group; LWW per id; left out while empty; an older device drops it in its own copy, the union restores it). Subscriber src adds "platform".
- **1.2 (1.35.00):** `rss:[{id,m,list,url,name,every:"day"|"week"|"month",wd:0-6,hour:0-23,mode:"draft"|"send",max:1-20,seg,last,ran,dev,on}]` (≤20 live). Merge: LWW per id, like segs. Issues gain `imp: 1` (only with st "sent").
- **1.4 (editor wave E1):** block kinds add `quote{t,by}`, `sp{h:4-120}`, `list{t,ord?:1}`; `h` may carry `lv:1|3` (2 is left out); `hr` may carry `st:"dashed"|"dotted"`, `w:2-8`, `c:#rrggbb`, `wd:10-99` (%); `btn` may carry `st:"line"`, `full:1` (one button only) and `more:[{t,href}]` (≤ 2 more buttons in the row). Any known block may carry `al:"center"|"right"`, `pad:1-48` (px), `bg:#rrggbb`; defaults are always left out. Lists may carry `sty:{font:"serif"|"mono", hs:"s"|"l", btn:"square"|"pill", link, bg}` (left out while all default). FORWARD COMPATIBILITY (NL-FC): a block of an unknown kind (`k` = `[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,11}`, ≤ 20 000 chars of JSON) is kept whole and never drawn; unknown short scalar fields (≤ 16, names `[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,15}`, strings ≤ 2000) on known blocks and on lists are kept too, so a device a version behind never strips what a newer one wrote. Preflight refuses to send an issue holding an unknown block (`newerBlock`). Devices from before E1 still drop new blocks if they edit the issue; the editor shows such a block as "Newer block" (move/remove only). Editor: drag by the handle (pointer events; arrow keys on the handle), duplicate, per-block settings, undo/redo per open issue (≤ 60 snapshots of the written part, typing snapshots once per pause; Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z outside text fields; the toast Undo keeps priority).
- **1.5 (editor wave E2):** block kinds add `head{f?,w,h,b,lw:40-300 (default 140),t≤120,sub≤200,links≤4 [{t,href}]}` (logo optional, an issue picture like `img`), `social{items,st:"c"|"d"|"l" (default c),sz:24|32|40 (default 32)}` and `foot{t≤2000,items,st}`. `items` = one `{n,href}` per network in `OrosNewsletterSocial.ORDER` (facebook, instagram, x, linkedin, youtube, tiktok, mastodon, bluesky, threads, pinterest, whatsapp, telegram, website, email); href http(s), `mailto:` only for email (a bare address becomes `mailto:`). `head`, `social`, `foot` are centred by default (`alignOf`; `al:"left"` is stored, `al:"center"` left out); they never count as body for preflight, and an item or header link without an href is `badBlock`. Icons are drawn on a canvas at send time (`newsletter/social.js`, Simple Icons paths, 2x PNG) and attached inline like any picture: picture name `icon:<n>:<st>:<sz>` (`picsOf`), footer icons always 24 px. The unsubscribe line and the list address stay below the footer and cannot be removed. Lists may carry `hf:{head?,foot?}` (normalised blocks): a new blank issue starts with `hf.head` and ends with `hf.foot`.
- **1.6 (editor wave E3):** block kinds add `imgtxt{f,w,h,b,alt,href,hd≤200,t≤4000,bt,bh,side?:"r"}` (picture beside text; a button needs both bt and bh), `cols3{a,b,c}`, `gallery{items≤9 [{f,w,h,b,alt,href}],per?:3}`, `video{f?,w,h,b,url (http(s) only),alt,t≤300}` (picture name `play:<f>`: the play mark is drawn on a canvas at send time, cid `play-<file>`; without a picture a button opens the link; nothing is fetched from the video site), `table{rows≤20 × ≤6 cells ≤200, rectangular,hd?:1}`, `event{t≤200,d YYYY-MM-DD,tm?,te? HH:MM (te only with tm),loc,sub≤1000,bt,bh,ics?:1}`. `picRefs(b)` lists a block's picture holders (img, head, imgtxt, video, gallery items) for `picsOf`, the bundle (`imgPaths`, media import) and the picker. Preflight `badBlock` also for: imgtxt without picture or half a button, gallery empty or with an empty item, video without url, event without title or day. An event with `ics:1` is sent with an attachment `<slug>.ics` (`icsOf`: RFC 5545, floating local times, 1 h when no end, all-day otherwise, escaped and folded to 75 octets; UID `<issue>-<index>@oros`), in MIME and in the Postmark/SendGrid/Brevo API payloads. New top-level collection `blks:[{id,m,name,b}]` (saved blocks, ≤ 100 live, any list; left out while empty; LWW per id, tombstones; an older device drops it in its own copy and the union restores it; included in `.orosnewsletter` bundles). Built-in layouts (weekly, announce, offer) are code, not data: the list's own header/footer around blocks in the app's language. Editor: "More blocks…" dialog (header, picture+text, gallery, video, 3 columns, table, event, social, footer + saved blocks), "Save block" in block settings; the alignment select now shows the real default of centred blocks.
- **1.7 (editor wave E4):** block kind `prod{items≤9 [{id (shop product id ≤80 of [A-Za-z0-9:/._-]), name≤200, t≤300, href (http(s)), src (the shop's picture address), alt, price, was (cents; -1 = not known; was only above price), cur (ISO 4217, default EUR), out?:1, f,w,h,b}], per?:1|3 (default 2), bt≤40, sh?:"woo"|"shopify", acct? (links/ account id), at? (ms of the last price read)}`. Products are read from a connected shop (`newsletter/shop.js`, read only) and their pictures copied into the issue (`/internal/Newsletter/img-*.jpg`, `picRefs` includes the items); cards render 2 per row (262 px) by default, 3 (170 px) or 1 (picture beside text), with the old price struck through, "Sold out", and a button (`bt`, default "Buy now"/"Αγορά"); plain text "name — price (old price)\nurl". Preflight: `badBlock` for an empty product block or a product without name or page; `warn oldPrices` when a shop block's prices were read more than 24 h ago (`PRICE_AGE`). Subscriber `src` adds `"shop"` (WooCommerce customers, basis `customer`; an older device shows them as added by hand). A Shopify customer export (CSV with Accepts Email Marketing / Accepts Marketing) is read by `import2.js` as source `shopify`, only those who accept, basis `consent`.
- **1.8 (clean-up of inactive subscribers, wave 1, Chris 2026-10-24 approved /mnt/project-files/newsletter/inactive-subscribers-plan.md):** lists may carry `clnPend` (7|14|30|60 days, 0 = never; default 30 left out), `clnGone` (30|90|180|365, 0 = never; default 90 left out) and `clnDev` (the one device that cleans the list). They are short scalars, so an older device keeps them (NL-FC). `C.cleanPlan(d, list, now, set?)`: `pend` = still unconfirmed `clnPend` days after their confirmation request (`inv >= at`; never before it went out), `gone` = off/bounce/spam for `clnGone` days; active people never; a record changed in the last 24 h waits a day. `ok` = n ≤ 200 and n ≤ max(10, a fifth of the list), else it waits for the user. `C.cleanApply` re-checks on the data it changes: tombstones (`{id, m, del:1}`); `gone` also adds `supp` (import never brings them back; their own form / e-mail sign-up does), `pend` does not (they never agreed and may be invited again). The engine's `runClean` (shell runner, every hour, first after 2 min, Web Lock "oros-newsletter-clean") cleans each list whose `clnDev` is this device once a day (device state `oros-newsletter-dev.cln`, list id → day); no `clnDev` = nothing deleted. The first device that sends a list's issue or confirmation request takes `clnDev` (it reads that list's Inbox, so a confirmation that just came in is applied where deletions happen); Subscribers › Clean up… changes the days, picks this device, previews, exports the people (CSV) and cleans by hand after a confirm (no cap). Notices "cleaned up" / "waits for your OK" (once a day). Open tracking stays off (decision 2026-10-12, reconfirmed 2026-10-24). Tests: `tests/newsletter-clean.test.js`.
- **1.9 (clean-up wave 2, "Do you still want it?", on for every list: Chris 2026-10-24):** lists may carry `clnIdle` (6|12|24 months of 30 days, 0 = never; default 12 left out). Subscribers may carry `ask` (ms the "Stay?" e-mail went out; left out while never; merge = max; an older device drops it, the asking device keeps its own). Last sign of life `C.lastSeen(s)` = max(at, conf): no opens are counted. `C.asksDue(d, list, now)`: active, silent `clnIdle` months, not asked since (`ask > lastSeen` = waiting), oldest first, at most max(20, ceil(5% of the active)) per list a day counting those asked in the last 24 h. The engine sends them only on the list's `clnDev`, after this device's issues (job kind `ask`, the same account, pace and daily cap; SMTP and API; `R.askEmail`, reply "confirm <token>"); a failure stops them for the window (notice `askfail`). The confirm request of an asked subscriber sets `conf` (a fresh sign of life; tally `k` "chose to stay"), also when they were already unsubscribed for not answering (`off >= ask`); an unasked active one or someone who left on their own is unchanged. `C.askTimeouts` (in the daily `runClean`, before the plan): asked ≥ 30 days ago (`ASK_WAIT`) and still waiting → off (offSt "off"); the clean-up deletes them `clnGone` days later. Subscribers › Clean up… adds the months and a count of who would be asked. Tests: `tests/newsletter-clean.test.js`.
- **1.10 (blocks from the Assistant, chat compose N1, 2026-10-25):** deep link `{ asAdd: { blocks, subj?, issue? } }`. `C.asAdd(v)` keeps at most `AS_MAX` (20) blocks of the kinds `AS_KINDS` (`h p quote btn list hr sp`: nothing that needs a picture or a shop), each through `normBlock`, and drops empty ones (no text; a button without text or a safe link); nothing left → toast "Nothing to add". The receiver writes only after the user's choice: an `issue` that is a blocks draft, else the draft open in the editor, takes the blocks at once; otherwise a dialog lists the blocks drafts (newest 8) and "Or a new draft" (list, subject prefilled; the list's saved header and footer around it); no list → "New list". An open dialog is left alone: the blocks wait for its `close`. Blocks go at `C.insertAt(blocks)` (before a closing `foot`, and a `social` row right above it) of the version being edited, up to the 60-block limit (the toast says how many did not fit); one undo snapshot, and the toast's Undo puts the earlier blocks back. Tests: `tests/newsletter-asadd.test.js` (the Assistant's output is kept by `asAdd` unchanged).
- **1.11 (pictures from the Assistant, chat compose N2, 2026-10-25):** `AS_KINDS` adds `img` and `imgtxt`. A picture never arrives as a file: the raw block may carry `src`, an https address (`picSrc`, ≤ 2000 chars), which `asAdd` moves to `pics: [{ i, src }]`; the block itself starts with `f: ""` (any `f` given is dropped) and no `src`; an `imgtxt` needs `hd` or `t`. After the blocks are added, `asPics` copies the pictures one after another: `fetch(src, {mode: "cors", credentials: "omit", referrerPolicy: "no-referrer"})`, 15 s, `image/jpeg|png|webp|gif` up to 15 MB, then `storeImage` (shrunk, `/internal/Newsletter/img-*.jpg`). It fills only the block that is still there unchanged and without a picture (matched by its JSON at insertion); sites that refuse (CORS, error) leave the block empty and one toast says how many to pick. No relay: the relay `web` op refuses images and stays the Reader's.
- **1.12 (products from the Assistant, chat compose N3, 2026-10-25):** `AS_KINDS` adds `prod`. Items from other sites go through `normProd` (prices in cents, `cur`), lose any `f`/`id` and keep `src: ""`; their https `src` becomes `pics: [{ i, j, src }]` (j = the item), copied by `asPics` like N2 pictures (the block's JSON is re-read after each copy, so several items of one block fill one by one). A bridge block never brings `sh`/`acct`/`at` (no shop refresh for web items). An empty `prod` with `shop: { n 1-9, q? }` (`shops: [{ i, n, q }]`) is filled when added by `shop.js auto(o, done, fail)`: the FIRST connected shop (Settings › Connected services), its newest products (WooCommerce `orderby=date desc`, Shopify the fixed query's `UPDATED_AT reverse`), or the newest whose folded name + line has every folded word of q (Shopify also sends q as its search variable), at most 3 pages; pictures through `copyPics` (relay `ext` only for the shop's own uploads, as E4). It fills only the still unchanged empty block and sets `sh`, `acct`, `at` like the picker; no shop, refusal or no match → toast, block stays for `Choose products…`. Nothing is written to the shop.
- **1.13 (sections and ready to send, chat compose N4, 2026-10-25):** a block may carry `sec` (`SECTIONS`: top, news, prod, promo, end; `BLOCK_KEYS` keeps it, `normBlock` drops any other value and never puts it on `head`/`foot`). `addAsBlocks` inserts the bridge blocks one by one at `insertAt(blocks, sec)`: after the last block of the same or an earlier section and before the first block of a later one, never past the footer and its social row; blocks without `sec` (placed by hand) never move and a new block goes after them unless a later section follows. Undo still restores the whole issue as it was. `{ check: { issue? } }` (`asCheck`) waits for an open dialog, picks the named draft, else the open one, else the newest draft (none → toast `as.noDraft`), opens it in the editor and runs `checkDialog(x, true)`: the pre-send check, and only when nothing must be fixed the send screen; sending stays the user's own confirm there.

**LIBRARY v1** (`library/`, Library / Βιβλιοθήκη, 1.08.00)
- `library`: Library / Βιβλιοθήκη, category **Personal**, right after Media Shelf (Chris 2026-10-12 11:38 "Ναι σε όλα"). EPUB and PDF reader for books on the orOS disk. Universal search provider `library/search.js` (books, highlights and noted bookmarks; target `{ book, loc? }`).
- Slice `library` (`oros-library-data`): `{ ver:1, books:[], pos:{}, marks:[], tombs:{} }`. Books, positions and marks are LWW by `m` (tie: larger canonical JSON), tombstones keep the max and hide records with `m <= tomb`. Merge symmetric, associative, idempotent, output canonical (tests/library.test.js).
- Device-local: `oros-library-prefs` (reading settings, view, sort, filter, side panel), `oros-library-paths` (path → size, mtime, book id; avoids re-hashing), IndexedDB `oros-library-cache` (cover thumbnails).
- File handler: `.epub` and `.pdf` open in Library ("Open with"; PDF was not taken by any app before).
- Book id = "b" + first 16 hex of the file's SHA-256: the same file on two devices is the same book, wherever it sits. `path` is a synced hint only; each device maps ids to its own paths.
- Locations: EPUB `e:<spine>:<offset in the chapter's text-node string>`; PDF `p:<page>:<offset in the page text>` (items + "\n" at EOL, same as the text layer DOM) or `p:<page>:y<per-mille>` for a place on the page. Highlights keep quote + 32-char context and re-anchor by quote when the offset no longer matches.
- Books the disk scan finds by itself get `m = 1`, so a record from another device (edits, finished date) always wins; a new device scanning before its first pull never overwrites them. The saved place is not rewritten while it is still on screen (other screen sizes start pages elsewhere).
- **Phase 2–3 (1.20.00):** read aloud (`library/speak.js`, `speechSynthesis` one sentence at a time, `core.speechParts`; pause = cancel keeping the sentence; key S; **local voices only since 2026-10-14**, Chris: "Remove Google, we don't want any logging on their part": `core.localVoice(voices, lang)` picks only `localService === true` voices of the book's language (exact tag, then default), every utterance gets that explicit `voice` (never the browser default, which can be a network voice such as "Google ελληνικά"); an empty list is waited for once (voiceschanged or 2 s); no local voice → toast `speak.noVoice` and no reading); reading stats (`library/stats.js`) in the synced slice as `stats: { d: {day: {device: secs}}, b: {book: {device: secs}} }`, each device only adds to its own counter, merge = max per counter, 400 days kept, device id `oros-library-dev` device-local; Send to Notes (`__orosOpenAt("notes", { add })`, ≤ 20,000 chars); Today provider `library/today.js` (apps.json `"today": ["core.js", "today.js"]`, read-only, one line: current book, progress, today's time, streak).
- FB2 (incl. `.fb2.zip`, any declared encoding) and CBZ (≤ 200 MB, ComicInfo.xml) become a small in-memory EPUB (`core` §12, `store.memZip`, `fb2Zip`, `cbzZip`) through the same sanitizer; records keep `fmt: "epub"` + `kind: "fb2" | "cbz"`. `.fb2` / `.cbz` added to BR-FILE-OPEN (TWA / MSIX packages need regenerating).
- Look-up (`library/lookup.js`, `core` §13): Wiktionary REST definitions, text only, after a one-time opt-in per device, only the word is sent. Ask the Assistant (word in its sentence via engine hook `sentenceAt`, a passage, or the whole book without spoilers) through `__orosOpenAt("assistant", { ask })` ≤ 2000 chars; nothing is sent until the user sends it.
- **Wave 33 — online catalogues, CBR, Markdown export:**
  - Slice gains `cats:[{id "c"+[0-9a-z]{6,24}, m, url (http/https, ≤ 500; the add form also refuses user:password@), name ≤ 80}]` (the user's own OPDS catalogues, ≤ 50, LWW by m, removal = tombstone under the same `tombs`; the key is left out while empty, so older devices' bytes are unchanged; an older device drops `cats` in its own copy and the union restores it on the next merge). Built-ins are code, never stored: Project Gutenberg (`https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks.opds/`, search `ebooks/search.opds/?query={searchTerms}`) and Standard Ebooks' free new-releases Atom feed (`https://standardebooks.org/feeds/atom/new-releases`, EPUB `rel="enclosure"` links); SE's full OPDS feed needs a Patrons Circle login, so it is not used. Device-local `oros-library-prefs`.opds = true after the one-time note.
  - `library/opds.js` (`window.LibOpds`, pure, Node-testable: `parseFeed` Atom OPDS 1.x + OPDS 2 JSON incl. groups, acquisition / enclosure / thumbnail links, OpenSearch `parseOsd`, `searchUrl` for `{searchTerms}` and `{?query}` templates, `sniffOk` by magic bytes, `absUrl` http(s) only — images https only, `fileName`). All feed text is plain text (inline tags stripped, then `textContent`); no markup or script from a feed reaches the DOM. `library/catalog.js` is the UI (`LIB.catalog.open`), loading `../feeds/core.js` + `../feeds/fetch.js` lazily: direct GET first, then the Mail relay's `web` op (≤ 5 MB a response) when CORS blocks; without a relay → "norelay" message. Downloads are checked (size, magic bytes) and go through `LIB.store.addFile` like a local import (to `/internal/Books`).
  - CBR (RAR comics): `kind: "cbr"` (fmt stays "epub"; a record with no `kind` but a `.cbr` path is read as cbr). `store.cbrZip` lazy-imports the vendored libarchive.js 2.0.2 (`vendor/libarchive/`: `libarchive.js` ES module, `worker-bundle.js` module worker, `libarchive.wasm`; loaded only when a .cbr is opened), refuses encrypted archives ("drm"), reads a ZIP-in-disguise as CBZ, then the CBZ path (`C.cbzBook` → `packBook` → `memZip`). ≤ 200 MB like CBZ. `.cbr` is not yet in BR-FILE-OPEN (shell-owned).
  - Markdown export: `core.exportMarkdown(book, marks, lang, labels, opts)` — with `opts.date` a Readwise / Obsidian-style header (`- Author:`, `- Highlights: N · Notes: M`, `- Exported: <date> from orOS Library`), chapter `##` sections, `>` quotes, colour · place %, note below; without `opts` the old output is unchanged. `core.notesMarkdown(book, marks, lang, {max, date, labels})` → `{text, left}` is what Send to Notes now sends (Markdown, ≤ 20,000 chars, "… and N more"). No change in Notes (`__orosOpenAt("notes", { add })` already existed).
  - Tests: `tests/library-opds.test.js` (OPDS 1/2 parsing, OpenSearch, URL safety, sniffing, cats merge/tombs, Markdown export).

**MONTAGE v1** (`montage/core.js`, slice `montage`, key `oros-montage`; video editor, plan `/mnt/project-files/video-editor/video-editor-plan.md`, Chris 2026-10-12 "Ναι σε όλα"; registered at 1.10.00):

```
oros-montage = { ver:1, projects{ <pid>: project }, tombs{ <pid>: ms } }
project = { id, name, ar: "16:9"|"9:16"|"1:1"|"4:5", fps: 30|60, bg:"#rrggbb", vs: bool, dk?: 1-90, m, items{ <iid>: item }, tombs{ <iid>: ms } }
item    = { id, k: video|image|audio|title, tr: main|ov|tt|a1|a2, m, … }
```

- Tracks: `main` is magnetic (order key `o`, clips follow each other, a transition `tx{k: fade|black|slide|wipe|push|zoom|circle, d}` overlaps the clip before, at most half of either clip); `ov` (picture in picture), `tt` (titles), `a1`/`a2` (sound) use a start `at`. Which kinds go on which track: `TRACK_KINDS`.
- video/audio: `src`, `len` (file length), `in`/`out` (seconds in the file), `sp` 0.25-4, `vol` 0-200, `mu`; image: `src`, `d`; title: `d`, `text{t,f,sz,col,ol,bx,al,an}` (+ `bg` on main = a title card). Pictures also `op`, `fit` fit|fill, `rot`, `fl`, `lk{b,c,s,t}`, `flt`; off-main pictures `box{x,y,w,h}`; all `fi`/`fo` fades.
- Media are never in the slice: `src` is an orOS disk id `/internal/Assets/<sha256>.<ext>` in the forms Atelier's `clips.js` and `designkit/assets.js` use (jpg|png, webm|mp4, mp3|m4a|ogg|wav|weba), so Atelier's "unused files" check sees them as in use. `vs` = this project's media travel through Vault Drive (off by default: device only).
- **Merge:** projects and items are separate entities, LWW by their own `m` (tie → greater canonical JSON); tombstones max-union, per project and per item; a project survives its tombstone when any edit in it is newer (R17). Strict normalizer drops invalid rows; output canonical (keys sorted). Edits stamp `m` at the mutation site, always forward (R27). Tests: `tests/montage.test.js`.
- Rendering: `framePlan(project, t)` (layers on screen) and `soundPlan(project)` (sound segments) are the single source for preview and export; `montage/gl.js` draws a plan (WebGL2), `montage/export.js` encodes frame by frame with WebCodecs via `vendor/mediabunny.min.js`.
- Phase 2 wave 1 (no new item fields): `dk` = ducking, % the Music row (`a1`) drops while anything sounds on Voice (`a2`), 0.25 s ramps, applied in `gainAt` so preview and export match. It is written only when on (absent = off), so a project without ducking is byte-identical on copies that predate it. Subtitles are ordinary `tt` titles (`SUB_BOX` style); `parseSrt`/`toSrt` read SRT and WebVTT (markup dropped, at most 1500 cues) and write SRT. Freeze frame = the video splits at the playhead and a full-size PNG of that frame (`MontageMedia.frameAt`, imported like any picture) goes between as a 2 s image (`freezeAt`). Filters added: vintage, chrome, dusk, golden. Sound-only export: M4A (AAC), else Ogg (Opus), else WAV; "keep a copy" goes to `/internal/Music/`.
- Phase 2 wave 2, keyframes: optional item field `kf = [{ t, x, y, s, o, v }]` (t seconds into the clip, sorted, one key per t, at most 60; pictures and titles take x/y −2..2 (fraction of the frame), s 0.1–5, o 0–100; video and sound take v 0–200; values r3). Written only when the clip has keys. Linear between keys (so a split at any time keeps the motion exactly; `split` adds a key at the cut on both halves), held before the first and after the last. `framePlan` turns them into the layer box (main clips get a box around the full frame) and alpha; `soundPlan` passes volume keys as `kv` to `gainAt`. Keys are relative to the clip start, so trimming the start shifts them.
- Phase 2 wave 3A: `rv: true` (video only) plays a clip backwards from its out point, silent (left out of `soundPlan`); `split` cuts a reversed clip from the out side. Export decodes reversed clips in forward runs of 15 frames handed out backwards (decoders only run forwards). `lut` (picture id) = a colour look from a `.cube` 3D LUT (2-64 points a side, DOMAIN_MIN/MAX honoured), stored as an n²×n PNG (blue slices side by side, red along x, green down y) through the normal picture import, so it lives on the device or syncs with the project's media like any picture; `mediaOf` and relink include it; MontageGL samples it on texture unit 1 after the filter. GIF export: 12 fps, long side 320 or 480 px, at most 30 s, silent, one popularity palette (5 bits a channel) per frame, LZW in `export.js` (`GifWriter`, no library); kept copies go to `/internal/Pictures/`.
- Phase 2 wave 3B: kind `shape` (Overlay row only) with `sh` {k, col, ol, ow} written only for shapes; `k` one of rect, round, ellipse, triangle, star, heart, arrow, bubble; `col` "" = no fill, `ow` 0-20, and normalize forces an outline when there is no fill and no outline width, so a shape is never invisible. Fit, rotate, flip, look, filter and LUT stay video/picture only. MontageGL draws shapes on a 2D canvas through the titles cache, so they take box, opacity, keyframes and transitions like any layer. Stickers are plain titles (emoji, size 18, `pop` entrance) on the Text row, no new field. Light copies (proxies): `Make light copies` in Project settings converts videos whose short side is over 540 px to 540 px copies (`proxy-<id>.webm|mp4`, Mediabunny `Conversion`, no sound) in the device media store; device-only, never synced, never in `mediaOf`; the player prefers them, export and `Grab frame` (now `MontageExport.still`, rendered from the originals at the project size) never use them; `Free space` keeps a proxy only while its original is still used.
- Wave 41 (parity with CapCut / Clipchamp / Shotcut). Five optional item fields, each written only when in use, so older projects stay byte-identical; invalid values are dropped or clamped by the normalizer; merge is unchanged (LWW per item, so a field travels with its item's `m`):
  - `sr` (video/audio) = speed curve `[{s, v}]`: `s` seconds in the file (sorted, inside `in..out`), `v` 0.1-10; 2-20 keys; linear in file time between keys, held outside. While `sr` exists `sp` is ignored. Clip time is ∫ds/v (per piece `L·ln(v1/v0)/(v1−v0)`), inverted in closed form (`fwdPos`/`fwdLocal`), cached per item (WeakMap). Keys live in file time, so `split` (cut at `fwdPos`) and trims never move them; reverse reads `fwdPos(dur − t)`. Presets (`RAMPS`: hero, bullet, montage, jump, flashin, flashout) are shapes scaled onto `in..out`. Preview: media element `playbackRate = rateAt(t)`, updated as it changes. Export sound: `srcPieces` cuts each window into 50 ms pieces of one rate each, every piece an `AudioBufferSourceNode` at that `playbackRate` (pitch follows speed, as with `sp`).
  - `ck` (video/image) = chroma key `{col, tol 0-100, soft 0-100, sp 0-100}`: distance in the CbCr plane (OBS-style), similarity `tol/100·0.3`, smoothness `soft/100·0.2`, spill `sp/100·0.3` (desaturates towards the key); in the MontageGL shader right after the texture fetch, so preview and export match. `Pick from the picture` averages 5×5 pixels of the stage canvas.
  - `bd` (video/image) = picture-in-picture frame `{w 0-10 (% of the frame's short side), col, r 0-50 (% of the box's short side)}`: rounded corners and border drawn by an SDF in the shader (`borderPx`), inside the box.
  - `fc` (video/image) = reframe focus keys `[{t, x, y}]` (≤ 60): `t` file seconds for video (clip seconds for pictures), `x`/`y` 0-1 in source coordinates before rotate/mirror (`shownPoint`/`uvOf` map them); used only when `fit` = fill (`placeIn` clamps the focus so the picture still covers the box). Auto reframe (`montage/reframe.js`): Mediabunny CanvasSink at 480 px, 3 samples/s (≤ 180); `FaceDetector` where the browser has it, else a centre-weighted motion centroid (frame difference) with a detail fallback; then smoothing and Ramer-Douglas-Peucker down to few keys. `Reframe all clips` (Project settings) = one undo step.
  - `na` (video/audio) = id of a cleaned sound file (noise removed), a normal sound media id: `soundPlan` plays it instead of `src` (same timing), `mediaOf`/relink/`replaceSrc` include it, relinking `src` to a different file drops it, `detachSound` carries `sr` and `na`. Clips of the same `src` reuse one `na`. Made by `montage/denoise.js`: RNNoise v0.1.1 (BSD-3, Xiph.Org / Mozilla / Amazon, original model) compiled to `vendor/rnnoise/rnnoise.wasm` (118 KB) with clang + wasm-ld and a tiny own libc shim (no Emscripten, no imports; build script and shim in `vendor/rnnoise/build/`), fetched on first use, not precached. Mediabunny `Conversion` with `audio.process` at 48 kHz, ≤ 2 channels, 480-sample frames, int16 scale, the 480-sample delay compensated → M4A (AAC), else Ogg (Opus), else WAV, imported like any sound.
  - Automatic subtitles (`montage/asr.js`, no new field: the result is ordinary `tt` subtitle titles via `addSubtitles`): OpenAI Whisper tiny (MIT; ONNX q8 export by Xenova, Apache-2.0) on the vendored ONNX Runtime Web (`vendor/ort/`, one thread), the same way Atelier runs u2netp, with no library around it: log-mel (Slaney mel table, checked against Whisper's `mel_filters.npz`), greedy decoding with Whisper's timestamp rules and KV cache (merged decoder), byte-level BPE text. Nothing is fetched until the user presses `Make subtitles` under a size notice; then the runtime (≈ 11 MB, same origin) and the model (≈ 42 MB: encoder, merged decoder, vocab.json, generation_config.json from `huggingface.co/Xenova/whisper-tiny`, the only third-party host) go into IndexedDB `oros-montage-ai` (version `ort1.22.0-whisper-tiny-q8`); `Remove the speech model` clears it. Input = the export sound mix (`MontageExport.speech16k`: mono, decimated 48 → 16 kHz per 10 s window), at most the first 30 minutes; 30 s windows, silent windows skipped, language `auto`/`en`/`el` (device-local pref `asr`), lines over 84 characters split by words. Sound never leaves the device.
  - Tests: `tests/montage-effects.test.js` (time remapping, keys, crop maths, chroma, border, subject finder, RNNoise stream with the real wasm, Whisper's pure steps and decoding loop with a scripted model).

## Part V — Sync + data-safety essentials

### Security model (absolute)

- Zero tracking. Zero-knowledge passphrase (AES-GCM + PBKDF2, client-side): 600,000 rounds for new writes since A70 (2026-10-07), 100,000 for blobs without `iter`. A passphrase being SET (empty cloud, change) needs at least 10 characters.
- Dropbox tokens are used only for file I/O (PKCE). Vault: sealed passphrase + IndexedDB NON-EXTRACTABLE key, opt-in per device.
- All third-party-cloud data MUST be E2EE, for any future provider too.
- **One cloud owner (R34):** `sync.js` holds the only OAuth handler and the only token state. Slice data and Vault Drive are separate channels in the same app folder (Part II).
- App frames are same-origin with the shell. **XSS in any app = full access to tokens and data.** Treat every import as hostile:
  - Sanitize in an INERT document (`document.implementation.createHTMLDocument`). `innerHTML` on a live-document element fires `<img onerror>` even when detached.
  - `esc()` does not escape quotes; use `escAttr()` in attributes and quote-escape URL captures.

### Data-safety supremacy (zero-loss guarantee)

- **Sync:** bidirectional push-pull, deterministic merges.
- **Automatic backup = folder backup [log, v0.38.25–26]:**
  - The localStorage auto-snapshot subsystem is RETIRED (it filled the shared quota, R30). The line that stood here ("rolling 5 full-DB auto-snapshots, oros-auto-snapshots, Restore picker") described it.
  - What remains: export to a user-chosen folder through the File System Access API. **Chromium desktop only**, progressive enhancement.
  - `maybeAutoExport`: daily / weekly / monthly, checked at boot and on tab-visible, no timers. The body is captured live by `exportBodyNow()` (inside try/catch).
  - Files `orOS-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.json` (`writeBackupFile`). Sealed when `oros-backup-enc` is on (BK-E): `{format:"oros-backup", v:1, enc}`; import asks for the passphrase and still reads plain files. `wipeFolderMirror` also cleans legacy `orOS-snapshot-*.json`.
  - Permission-lapse detection with one-click Reconnect. `state.autoexport` travels in the shell slice.
  - Firefox and mobile have no automatic local export (no File System Access API). Accepted (decision 2026-10-05): there the safety net is cloud sync (Dropbox or WebDAV/Nextcloud) + manual export.
- **Manual export:** full DB, every parameter; import restores zero-loss (through `applyPayload`, merge-aware). **[log]** The shell buttons and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+X go through `shellSaveJson` / `shellPickJson` (R33).
- **Close safety net:** on-close sync + `beforeunload` warning when dirty and online.
- **Factory reset:** double confirm → cloud → folder → localStorage prefix sweep → OrosFS wipe → **[log]** Cache Storage `oros-map-tiles` → reload. Everything is tombstoned and seeds are reborn.
- **Corruption:** rescue backup before any reseed. **Compatibility:** additive migrations; unknown fields carried forward.
- **Quota (R30):** one shared ~5 MB `localStorage`. A failed `setItem` means edits will not survive a reload, so warn the user.
- **No re-upload of what the cloud holds (SY-L1, 0.48.02):** after a pull applies a slice, the engine compares what the slice STORES (`get()` after `set()`) with the cloud copy, not the merge output. An app whose store normalizes the merge result differently no longer re-uploads at every reconcile. Apps should still keep `merge(x, null)` idempotent (store == merge output).
- **Visible failure reason (SY-L2, 0.48.02):** a failed background sync logs `orOS sync: auto sync (<reason>) failed:` in the console and shows the reason in the sync dot tooltip and the menu's sync section (generic errors carry the technical text, e.g. `upload failed: 429`) until the next successful sync. No toast, no inbox entry for network errors; since quality gate Q4 a failure only the person can fix (storage full, sign-in expired, newer orOS needed) adds one bell line a day (A72).

### Files-disk glue (`shell.js` §9f)

- `files.js` mutates → `__orosFilesDiskTouched()` (engine dirty + 1s-debounced cache refresh).
- Remote data while the app is closed sets a pending flag, consumed at the next open.
- `fdSliceGet` is PURE. `fdRefreshForExport()` guarantees a live snapshot before manual exports.

---

## Part VI — Canonical patterns (verbatim contracts)

Status per pattern: **[re-verified 2026-10-01]**, **[carried]** (from earlier revisions) or **[log]** (from session notes after 2026-10-01). Check the last two against the file before relying on them.

### Boot sequence [carried]

`load()` → `applyI18n()` → paint static aria/icons → `wire()` → `registerSync()` → `inheritPalette()` → `watchPalette()` → reset view state → first render (single pass) → consume staged deep link AFTER first paint.

**Invoke `boot()` at the END of the IIFE** (after every `let`/`const`): a boot triggered early hits TDZ errors on later declarations.

### Three things every sync slice must get right (2026-10-06)

1. The merge function is the FIFTH ARGUMENT of `registerSlice`. A union written inside the setter never runs: for a slice without `mergeFn` the engine decides "local or remote" by itself and may never call the setter.
2. The getter returns a canonical COPY of the data that travels, and nothing else: no device-local or volatile fields (sweep stamps, caches, timers). One field that moves by itself makes the slice "always changed" and every sync cycle uploads.
3. Whatever prunes locally by the clock must also prune inside the merge with the same rule, or the pruned entry returns with every pull.

### Boot marker [re-verified in Writer]

```js
var SCRIPT_V = "";
(function () {
  var m = (document.currentScript && document.currentScript.src || "").match(/[?&]v=([^&#]+)/);
  SCRIPT_V = m ? m[1] : "";
  console.log("<app>.js v" + (SCRIPT_V || "?") + " boot");
})();
```

### Shell API + language resolution in an app frame (R8) [re-verified]

```js
function syncApi() {
  try { return (window.parent && window.parent.orosSync) || window.orosSync || null; }
  catch (e) { return window.orosSync || null; }
}
// Language: shell writes localStorage "oros-lang" and reopens apps on toggle.
function appLang() {
  try {
    var l = localStorage.getItem("oros-lang") ||
            (window.parent && window.parent.orosLang) || "en";
    return l === "el" ? "el" : "en";
  } catch (e) { return "en"; }
}
```

### Sync registration + dirty funnel [carried; canonical rule re-verified]

```js
function registerSync() {
  // LOCAL FIRST: load() MUST have run before this (boot order). Live
  // registration does NOT hydrate the app — registering an empty state
  // lets the first get()/save() persist and push an empty slice.
  var api = syncApi();
  window.__orosSyncApi = { _suppress:false, dirty:function(){
    if (this._suppress) return;
    if (api && typeof api.markDirty === "function") api.markDirty(); } };
  if (!api || typeof api.registerSlice !== "function") return;
  api.registerSlice("<id>", sliceGet, sliceSet, STORAGE_KEY, mergeFn);   // 5 args, always
}
```

- `save()`: `localStorage.setItem` + `__orosSyncApi.dirty()`.
- `sliceSet(data, info)`:
  - if the user has pending edits, fold them in first (`mergeFn(serialize(), data)`);
  - write + persist the storage key, with NO `markDirty` (R6);
  - normalize, sanitize view state, re-render (keep the caret when the content is unchanged);
  - no toast (sync feedback is the taskbar dot).
- `serialize()` must be canonical (R26): arrays sorted by id, tombstones canonical, no device-local fields.

### Notification trigger [re-verified against notifications.js 0.38.12]

```js
function notifyDue(key, title, body, deepLink) {
  var n = null;
  try { n = window.parent && window.parent.orosNotifs; } catch (e) {}
  if (n && typeof n.emit === "function") {
    return n.emit({ ns: "<appid>", key: key, title: title, body: body,
                    deepLink: deepLink /* "<appid>:<payload>" */ }) !== null;
  }
  return false;   // caller falls back to its legacy local alert
}
```

### Transient note / toasts [re-verified]

```js
function showToast(msg) {            // informational → shell transient
  try {
    var n = (window.parent && window.parent.orosNotifs) || window.orosNotifs;
    if (n && typeof n.transient === "function" &&
        n.transient({ ns: "<appid>", title: String(msg) })) return;
  } catch (e) {}
  localToast(msg);                   // stale bundle / standalone fallback
}
```

- **Undo-bearing toasts stay LOCAL** (closure never leaves the frame), 8s.
- **A modal `<dialog>` makes the rest of the page inert:** host the local toast inside the top-most `dialog[open]`, and move it back to `<body>` when that dialog closes.
- **[log]** `transient` bypasses app toggles, accepts any `ns`, and returns the item id, or `null` when not ready. An app that only uses transient toasts does not need a `KNOWN_APPS` entry (Maps).

### Deep-link receiver [carried]

```js
window.__oros<App>Open = function (id, ymd) { /* navigate; guard deleted ids */ };
// Boot: read sessionStorage "oros-<app>-open", remove it, invoke the receiver.
```

### Universal search provider (2026-10-09)

The menu's search field (A74) also searches the apps' own data. `search.js` (root, shell core, unit-tested in node) finds and ranks; `shell.js` draws ("In your data" under the app list, groups per app, 3 hits then "All (n)", at most 50 per app). Every app with user text ships a provider:

```js
// <app>/search.js — declared in apps.json as "search": "search.js";
// the shell loads it on the FIRST search, never at boot.
(function (root) {
  var PROVIDER = {
    id: "<app id>", keys: ["oros-<app>-data"],
    // ctx = { q, words, fold, lang, limit, readJSON(key) }
    search: function (ctx) { return [{ id, title, text, when, target }]; },  // or a Promise
    open: function (target, win) { /* optional: an existing bridge */ }
  };
  if (typeof module !== "undefined" && module.exports) module.exports = PROVIDER;
  if (root && root.document) {
    var list = root.orosSearchProviders = root.orosSearchProviders || [];
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) if (list[i] && list[i].id === PROVIDER.id) return;
    list.push(PROVIDER);
  }
})(typeof window !== "undefined" ? window : globalThis);
```

- READ-ONLY: never `setItem`, never sync, never `innerHTML`; skip tombstones, trash, archived and hidden items. `title` and `text` are plain text (HTML bodies → text in an inert document, as Writer's provider does). `when` = ms, shown as a date and used for ties: give it only when the date means something to the user (due date, event day, last edit).
- `ctx.readJSON` parses once per stored string; ranking and matching are the shell's (fold: case/accents/ς; every word must match; title prefix > title word > title > text; ties → newest). A provider that throws or answers after 1 s is skipped for that search.
- Opening: without `open`, the shell calls the generic deep link `window.__orosOpenAt(appId, target)`. App running → `contentWindow.__orosOpenAt(target)`; closed → sessionStorage `oros-open-at` = `{ app, target }`, and the app takes it at boot with `window.parent.__orosTakeTarget("<id>")`. A receiver ignores unknown ids and does nothing while one of its dialogs is open (unsaved edits win).
- Per-app on/off switches: menu → Search → "Search in", device-local `oros-search-prefs` `{ off: {id: true}, on: {id: true} }`. An app whose data is sensitive sets `"searchOff": true` in `apps.json`: it starts switched off (opt-in).
- Providers (phase 1, 2026-10-09): Notes (pages), Contacts (name; company, phones, e-mails, addresses, note), To-Do (lists + tasks), Calendar (events; next occurrence of a series, walk mirrors `eachOccurrence`), Kanban (cards; archived boards skipped), Bookmarks, Writer (documents), Files (names only, walked through `orosFS.ls`, capped at 3,000 entries / depth 12, refreshed at most every 10 s). Contacts, Calendar and Kanban open through their existing bridges; Notes, To-Do (now down to the task), Bookmarks, Writer and Files gained `__orosOpenAt` receivers.
- Shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F opens the menu with the cursor in the field (from inside an app too).

### Assistant shell bridges (0.63.00, shell.js next to `openSearchHit`)
- `window.orosAssistApps()` → `[{id, name, sensitive}]`: apps with a search provider.
- `window.orosAssistSearch(q, ids)` → Promise of search groups for exactly those ids (the menu's own on/off switches don't apply; the assistant has its own permissions). Read-only, same loader and ranking as the menu.
- `window.orosAssistOpen(appId, target)` → the menu's `openSearchHit` (provider `open` first, else `__orosOpenAt`).

- (0.67.00) `window.orosAssistInstalled()` → `[{id, name}]` of every installed internal app (the assistant offers entry cards only for those).
- `openAssistant(q?)`, `SC_DEFS` key `a` → `sc.desc.assistant` "Open the Assistant" / «Άνοιγμα του Βοηθού». Help topic Shortcuts lists it.
- Menu search: `appendAsk()` adds `.menu-ask` under the data results (`search.ask` EN/EL).
- (WR-FMT, 2026-10-27) `window.orosAssistAtt = { mem, text, pages }`: the Assistant's attachments for this tab (AS-ATT-MEM). `orosFileOpen.openIn(app, file)` (`fileopen.js`): opens one `File` in that app if the app is in `HANDLERS` and the file is within its `maxFor` size, through the same `openWith(app, ownFile(file))` as BR-FO; returns `false` otherwise.
- (AS-RB, 2026-10-28) `window.orosAssistAtt` also holds `blob: {}` (AS-DEV files, `File` objects in the shell realm) and `rb: {}` (rebuild reports by card key, written by Layout); `onRb` is set by the live Assistant frame. `orosFileOpen.hand(file)` (`fileopen.js`): copies a `File` into the shell realm and returns a one-shot token (`hold`, 10 min) that an app takes with `__orosTakeFile(token)`; `""` for anything that is not a file. Layout's `__orosOpenAt` targets: `{rebuild: {pdf, src, folder, key, chat}}` (each file a token or an `/internal/` path; from 4.15.00 also `sla`, see AS-RB-SLA) and `{page: n}`. Atelier's targets (AS-EDIT, 4.30.00): `{edit: {key, chat, docs, steps}}` and `{editUndo: {key, tok}}`, answered in `rb[key]`. Layout takes the same two targets from 4.33.00 (`LY.assist`).
- (AS-HS, 2026-10-28) Layout's `__orosOpenAt` also takes `{house: {op: "learn"|"book"|"rule", house, key, chat, …}}` (see AS-HS); its report goes to `orosAssistAtt.rb[key]` like a rebuild's.
### Moon & Sky bridges (0.68.00)
- Time → Moon & Sky: `__orosOpenAt("sky", {})` from the "More in Moon & Sky" button on Time's Sun & Moon card (`time/astro.js`).
- Moon & Sky → Time: `__orosOpenAt("time", { astro: "location" })` opens Time's location dialog. It is Time's only `window.__orosOpenAt` receiver (in `time/astro.js`), which also reads `__orosTakeTarget("time")` at boot.
- Deep link: `__orosOpenAt("sky", { date: "YYYY-MM-DD", tab?: "tonight"|"map"|"month" })`.
- `orosToday.agenda(appId, days)` → Promise<[clean row]> one app's Today provider over the next 1–31 days, whatever Today's own on/off says; `orosToday.agendaApps()` → ids of apps with a provider. Read-only, used by the Assistant.

### Mail integrations (0.77.00)
- Contacts receiver: `__orosOpenAt("contacts", { add: { email, name? } })` opens the card that already has that address, else a prefilled new-contact dialog (saved only on Save). Contacts also takes `__orosTakeTarget("contacts")` at boot.
- Contacts → Mail: an email on a card opens Mail compose (`__orosOpenAt("mail", {compose})`) when Mail has an account on the device, else mailto:.
- Calendar → Mail: a saved event's "Email" button (`#ev-mail`) opens Mail compose (To = addresses in the event, subject = title, body = date, time, place, note).
- Mail → To-Do (BR-TD-ADD), Notes, Bookmarks, Contacts, Assistant (`{ask}` ≤ 2000 chars) from "Other apps" under a message; prefill only, Notes creates the page. Recipient suggestions read `oros-contacts-data` read-only (`mail/people.js`).
- BR-MAIL-FEED (Mail side `mail/feed.js`, Reader side: wave 36): `window.orosMailFeed` loaded by path (`../mail/feed.js`, it loads `mail/mime.js` next to it). Read-only like `mail/search.js`: `oros-mail-data` (accounts, tombs) + IndexedDB `oros-mail` stores `folders`, `heads`, `bodies`, opened without a version (no database → nothing created), closed after each call; never `keys` / `creds`, never the relay, never `\Seen`. `folders()` → `[{acct, acctName, email, folder, label, role}]` (live accounts; Sent, Drafts, Trash, Spam and `\Noselect` left out; labels decoded from modified UTF-7, "INBOX." dropped); `messages(acct, folder, max ≤ 200)` → `{acct, folder, uidv, at, msgs:[{uid, mid, subj, from{name, addr}, date, seen, cached, html, text}]}` newest first, `\Deleted` left out, bodies decoded only for messages Mail already downloaded (Mail keeps the last 200), null when the account or the folder cache is not on the device. The caller sanitises the HTML.

### Label Maker bridge (0.70.00)
- Deep link (receiver in `labels/`): `__orosOpenAt("labels", { text })` opens the Label Maker with the text on the tape.
- Storage → Label Maker: the "Make a label" tag button on space / room / furniture / position cards sends the card's name.

### One-Sentence Diary bridge (0.86.00)
- Deep link (receiver in `diary/`): `__orosOpenAt("diary", { day: "YYYY-MM-DD" })` opens that day's line.
- Shell evening reminder: `diaryCheckTick` (shell.js, in `tickSafe` after `todayTick`) reads `diary/core.js` (loaded by `index.html` after `shelf/feed.js`) and posts notifications ns `diary` (deep link `diary:day:<ymd>`) only when the device-local reminder (`oros-diary-prefs`, off by default) is on and the day has no line; silent without DiaryCore.
- Wave 30: photos go through `window.parent.orosFS` (writeBlob / readBlob / rm) under `/internal/Diary/Photos`, picked with `orosDialog.openFile("image/*")`; a photo taken off an entry is removed from the disk 12 s later (after the Undo window) only when no entry points at it. Weather reads the Weather app's `oros-weatherapp-data` (units, active city as a fallback place) read-only. A deep link into a locked diary opens the day behind the lock screen. The PIN lock (`oros-diary-lock`) is device-local and never in the slice; relock after 60 s hidden; `inert` on the content while locked.

### Aura Painter bridge (0.82.00)
- Deep link (receiver in `aura/`): `__orosOpenAt("aura", { id })` opens a saved work; `{ surprise: true }` makes a random one.
- Shell API `window.orosWallpaper.setImage(blob, {bg})`: shows a finished picture as THIS device's wallpaper ("Mine" in Settings), stored device-local (`oros-wallpaper-pic` + IndexedDB `oros-wallpaper` "picture"). It never syncs and never changes the synced wallpaper choice; picking another wallpaper or making a Generator recipe removes it. Used by Aura's "As wallpaper".

### Shortcut forwarding (Contract Β, capture phase) [re-verified]

```js
document.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) {
  if (!(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) || !e.altKey || !e.shiftKey) return;
  var p = null; try { p = window.parent; } catch (err) { return; }
  if (!(p && p !== window && p.orosShortcuts &&
        typeof p.orosShortcuts.handle === "function")) return;
  if (p.orosShortcuts.handle(e)) e.stopPropagation();
}, true);
```

App-local shortcuts match `e.code` (`KeyS`, `KeyF`, …), never `e.key`, and skip Ctrl+Alt+Shift (shell territory).

### Merge engine shape [re-verified in Writer]

```js
function newer(a, b, key) {              // symmetric pick (R5)
  var k = key || "mtime";
  var ma = (a && Number(a[k])) || 0, mb = (b && Number(b[k])) || 0;
  if (ma !== mb) return ma > mb ? a : b;
  return String(JSON.stringify(a)) >= String(JSON.stringify(b)) ? a : b;
}
```

- Union by id with sorted output.
- Tombstones: max-ts union, deduped and sorted.
- An entity is alive if its mtime > the tombstone ts.
- Column/order values: the side with the larger om donates positions.
- Strict normalizers DROP invalid rows.

### Lazy entity materialization (R28) [Writer]

```js
function ensureDoc() {
  var cur = activeDoc();
  if (cur && !cur.del) return cur;
  var d = createDoc({ silent: true, keepEditor: true });  // no re-render, caret kept
  dirty = true; flushSave();                              // capture what is on the page
  return d;
}
```

### mtime discipline (R27) [Writer]

```js
// flushSave(): stamp ONLY if the content really changed
var html = editorHTMLForSave();
if (html !== doc.html) { doc.html = html; doc.mtime = Date.now(); }
// field edits stamp at the mutation site:
function markDoc(doc) { if (doc) doc.mtime = Date.now(); scheduleSave(); }
```

### Import sanitizer (inert document) [Writer]

Allow-list thinking; remove these elements:

- `script`, `style`, `iframe`, `frame`, `frameset`, `object`, `embed`
- `noscript`, `link`, `meta`, `base`, `template`
- `form`, `input`, `button`, `textarea`, `select`
- `svg`, `math`

Remove these attributes:

- every `on*` handler, plus `srcdoc` and `formaction`;
- `href`/`src`/`action`/`data` whose control-char-stripped value starts with `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:text/html`.

Parse with `document.implementation.createHTMLDocument('')`; never with a live element.

### Writer import with formatting (WR-FMT, 2026-10-27) [Writer]

Chris 2026-10-27: "Πρέπει να μπορούν να εισαχθούν στο Writer με πλήρη μορφοποίηση από οποιοδήποτε αρχείο." Every format below keeps headings, bold/italic/underline/strike, alignment (`style="text-align:center|right|justify"`) and numbered/bulleted lists with their `start` and nesting; everything still goes through the Import sanitizer above.

- **PDF** (`writer/pdfin.js`, `WriterPdfIn`; new): PDF.js from `vendor/pdfjs` with `isEvalSupported:false`, `enableXfa:false`, ≤ `MAX_PAGES` = 500. Pure part (`fromPages`, `markerOf`, `toLines`, Node-tested): pieces on one baseline → lines; repeated text in the top 12% / bottom 10% of ≥ 60% of pages and page numbers dropped; lines join into a paragraph when the size matches, the step is near and the line before was full or the next word would not have fitted; a first-line indent starts a paragraph (not a list item's hanging line); alignment from the line edges; headings H1–H3 by size ≥ 1.12 × body, a short bold-only paragraph one level down (max H4) unless > 40% of paragraphs are bold; list markers 1. 1) a) α) iv. • – and the Symbol-font bullets (U+F000–F0FF); a Greek capital or "A. Smith" is an initial, not a list; a word hyphenated at a line end is rejoined; text is escaped, rotated text skipped. No text layer (a scan) → `{code:"notext"}`, toast `io.pdfNoText` (points to Scanner & PDF). Tables come as text, pictures are not kept.
- **DOCX** (`io.js`): `word/styles.xml` read; paragraph and run styles resolved through `basedOn` (and the default paragraph style); headings from the style name (`heading N`, also Greek Word's numeric ids), outline level or Title; numbering from the paragraph or its style (`numbering.xml`, `lvlOverride`/`startOverride`), a list resumed after other paragraphs continues with `start`.
- **ODT** (`io.js`): automatic and `styles.xml` styles with inheritance; alignment, text formatting, list styles (number/bullet, format, start), `continue-numbering` and `start-value`.
- **RTF** (`io.js ioParseRtf`, pure, no DOM; replaces the text-only parser): b/i/ul/strike/super, `\qc \qr \qj`, `\s` styles from the stylesheet, `\outlinelevel`, `\ls`/`\ilvl` through the list and list-override tables, `\listtext`/`\pntext` markers dropped.
- **Markdown** (`io.js`): headings to h6, `***x***`, `_x_`, nested lists by indent with `start`, lazy continuation lines, and a trailing `{.center}` / `{.right}` / `{.justify}` / `{.left}` (also `{.centre}`) for alignment.
- Writer's Open, drag and drop, the converter (`writer/convert.js`, `converter/registry.js` `from` + `.pdf`, warnings for PDF and RTF) and the Assistant (AS-OPENFILE) all use the same code. Tests `tests/writer-pdfin.test.js`, `tests/convert-writer.test.js` (real PDF.js in Chromium, LibreOffice-made fixtures).

### Dismissable menus (per-instance listeners)

- Never leave `{once:true}` document listeners behind for a reusable menu: a stale one closes the NEXT menu instantly ("works every other time").
- Use one `AbortController` per menu instance; `close()` calls `abort()`.

### Dialogs [carried + Writer]

- Native `<dialog>` + `showModal()`; outside-click + Esc; null-guarded `close` listeners; remove the node on close.
- Themed confirm/prompt return Promises (`wConfirm(msg, {danger, ok})`, `wPrompt(title, value)`).
- A zero-edit close must not stamp mtime.

### i18n in an app [carried + Writer]

```js
const STRINGS = { en: { ... }, el: { ... } };          // same key set in both packs
function t(key) { return (STRINGS[appLang()] || STRINGS.en)[key] || STRINGS.en[key] || key; }
```

Escape user text with `esc()` before `innerHTML`, and use `escAttr()` in attributes. Keep key parity EN↔EL; a quick script that diffs the key sets and greps `t('…')` / `data-i18n` usages catches missing keys (Writer had one).

**Greek coverage (2026-10-14, Chris: "some users speak no English at all").** `tests/i18n.test.js` scans every `{ en: {…}, el: {…} }` table (and keys added later as `X.en["k"] = …`) in the shell and the apps: every English key must have a Greek string, and a Greek string may not be a copy of an English sentence; every `help.en.txt` / help topic needs a Greek page. Word lists and `maps/presets-data.js` are skipped. Accessible names count as text: an `aria-label`, `title` or `placeholder` written in the HTML is a placeholder that JS must translate (`data-i18n-aria="key"` / `data-i18n-title` / `data-i18n-ph`), and so are labels set by a library (Leaflet zoom and layer controls take `t()` strings). Prefer a plain Greek word over an English loanword when one exists (πίνακας, not board; έργο, not project; επίπεδο, not layer, with Levels «Στάθμες»); product and brand names stay as they are. The shell sets `#app-frame`'s `title` to the running app's name and relabels the sync button on every language change (`applyLang`).

**Languages beyond English and Greek (2026-10-17, Chris approved strategy item 12; first language German).** English and Greek stay inline and complete, with the checks above. Any other language is a folder `i18n/<code>/` of translator packs, `orosPack("<code>", "<app>", { "key": "text" })`, plus `help/<app>.txt` and `help/topics/<id>.txt`. `i18n.js` (root, precached) holds the language list (`LANGS`: code, own name, locale, dir, status full / partial / hidden; a hidden language is tried with `?lang=<code>`), reads the language (`orosI18n.lang()`: the shell's, then `?lang=` on the top window, then `oros-lang`), and, for a pack language, `document.write`s the pack named by `data-app` on its own script tag before the app's scripts. `orosI18n.table(STRINGS, "<app>")` adds `STRINGS[<code>]` = English overlaid with the pack values that keep the English `{placeholders}` and HTML tags (anything else shows English, so a pack cannot add markup to an `innerHTML`). `orosI18n.locale()` replaces `el ? "el-GR" : "en-GB"`; `orosI18n.plural()` reads `key.one/.few/.many/.other`. The shell keeps `state.lang` as the full code and passes `langBase()` ("el"/"en") to modules that still pick between two inline strings; `lang` syncs as any known code. `sw.js` serves `i18n/<code>/` from `oros-lang-packs`, a cache that outlives releases (cached copy first, network refresh behind it); the shell fetches the files of `i18n/<code>/manifest.json` once per release through the worker, so a chosen language works offline.
