- BR-CRM-INV (CRM side live, 1.25.00): CRM → Invoices `__orosOpenAt("invoices", { new: OrosCrmCore.invoicePrefill(cust, deal?, cur) })`; Invoices → CRM read-only `OrosInvoicesCore.byCrm(OrosInvoicesCore.parse(raw), crmId, today)`.
- BR-CRM-Q (new, read-only, 1.25.00): `OrosQuoteCore.forClient(quoteData, { name, afm })` → `[{ id, num, date, due, status, cur, total }]` (total in currency units); CRM opens a row with `__orosOpenQuote(id)` and creates with `__orosOpenQuoteNew(OrosCrmCore.quotePrefill(cust, deal?, cur))`.
- **Relay route BR-CRM-FORM (CRM web form; relay/crmform.js, approved by the relay owner):** public `POST /crm/f/<k>` (k = 16 a-z0-9), early branch in `relay/core.js` next to `/nl/`, same `limited(IP)`, no Origin check, no CORS. Body ≤ 20 KB urlencoded (2,000 Greek characters ≈ 12 KB encoded): email (required, ≤ 200, Newsletter's `validEmail`), name / phone / company (≤ 200, one line), message (≤ 2000, line breaks kept), lang en|el, honeypot `website`; control characters stripped. Sealed with the form's public key before INSERT (`seal` from relay/newsletter.js); in clear only k and the time. D1 = Newsletter's binding `NL_DB` (no new binding, no wrangler change), own tables `crm_form` (k, pub, sha256(sec), back, at, day, n) and `crm_q` (id, k, v, at), `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`. Limits: 500 waiting per form, 100 stored per form per UTC day, 5,000 forms; rows older than 30 days deleted on every POST and op call. Answer: a fixed EN/EL thank-you page or 303 to the form's registered https `back` (never from the request); input never echoed; GET → 405, bad shape → 404, too big → 413, bad e-mail → 400. Every D1 call inside a try: storage trouble → 503 "not available" page; without `NL_DB` the same. App op `POST /v1 {op: "crmf", act: reg {pub, back} | pull {after} → {rows[{id, v, at}] ≤ 100, more} | ack {upto} → {n} | drop, k, sec}`, origin-gated; errors nostore (503, also any D1 failure, its text never sent), auth (403), gone (404), full, bad-request. Shared helpers exported from relay/newsletter.js: `seal`, `sha256Hex`, `sameHex`, `validEmail`, `validBack`, `validPub`, `importPub`, `readSmall(request, max)`, `langOf`, `renderPage`, `isBot`, `oneLine`, `K_RE`, `SEC_RE` (Newsletter's own behaviour unchanged).
- BR-CRM-MAIL (receiver live in CRM since 1.29.00; sender live in Mail since 1.29.01, a "Log in CRM" button under a message): `__orosOpenAt("crm", { log: { email, name?, subject?, text?, at? } })`. email required (lower-cased, else ignored); subject ≤ 200, text ≤ 1800 chars, at = message time in ms. Prefill only.
- **BR-CRM-LINK (partners across apps, CRM core 1.5, partner card wave W1):** CRM keeps roles and links in its own top-level list `pt: [{ id = customer id, m, roles?, ln? }]` (LWW by m per id, the customer's tombstone hides it, dropped when its customer is gone; written only when it has rows; a 1.4 device drops the list on its own merge and the next union brings it back, so editing a customer there never strips it). `roles` ⊂ `cust|sup|shop|auth|assoc`, stored only when not "customer only". `ln` ≤ 30 keys `sup:<Stock supplier id>`, `wh:<Stock consignment warehouse id>`, `tsc:<Timesheet client id>`, `inv:<Invoices client id>` (only clients without their own `crm`), `pub:<folded name>` (a person on Publishing titles; people that carry `crm` in Publishing count without a link). One foreign record belongs to one partner (`linkMove`; two devices at once → the first pt row by id owns it). CRM reads the other apps only through their cores (`OrosStockCore.merge`, `orosTimesheetCore.parse`, `OrosInvoicesCore.parse`, `OrosPublishCore.normalize`) and never writes them. `crm/links.js` (`OrosCrmLinks`): `candidates`, `suggest` (ΑΦΜ → email → name, ambiguous names left loose), `forCust`, `linked`, `pubTitles`, `newCust`. `OrosInvoicesCore.byCrm(data, crmId, day, also?)`: `also` = linked Invoices client ids (a client with its own `crm` is never taken from another customer).
- **Partner card Overview (W2a, `crm/overview.js`, `OrosCrmOverview.build`):** pure, derived, never stored. Money in = `OrosInvoicesCore.byCrm(…, also)` open / overdue per currency; money out = unpaid, not voided Publishing statements (`stmts`, `!paid && due > 0`) of the names this partner goes by (pub links + people carrying its crm id); consignment = `OrosStockCore.whQty` of each linked `wh` at the products' sale price, `lastSettle`, `consDue`; supplier = open `poViews` of each linked `sup` (pieces left × line cost); work = `orosTimesheetCore.report(…, {client, bill: "bill", billed: "open"})` over all time; advance still to earn back = `rec[].left` of the latest statement per term. Opens Stock `{view:"cons"}` / `{sup}`, Timesheet `{client}`, Publishing `{view:"roy"}`.
- **CT-CRM (linked contacts ↔ CRM customers, both ways, CRM core 1.8):** Chris 2026-10-26 asked to keep all contacts in sync: a change in Contacts reaches the linked CRM record and back. `crm/contactsync.js` (`OrosCrmContactSync`, pure; tests `tests/crm-contactsync.test.js`). **Pairs:** a customer of kind person whose first `people` row with a contact id points to a live contact IS that contact. Fields: name ↔ given + middle + family; phone, email, web ↔ the first phone, e-mail, website; job ↔ job title; addr ↔ the first address (street, zip city, region); country ↔ its country. Nothing else is touched (tax number, notes, tags, birthdays, the other phones and e-mails). A company's linked people are its staff: only when the company is renamed in CRM, a linked contact whose company field still holds an earlier name (kept in the row, `o`, ≤ 5) takes the new one. **CRM side:** top-level list `cs: [{ id = customer id, m, c?, t?, f?: { field: [value, stamp] }, n?, o? }]` (c = the contact, t = when the pair started, stamp -1 = a difference left to the user), merged FIELD by field (newer stamp wins, ties larger JSON; another contact → the newer row whole), the customer's tombstone hides it, written only when it has rows (a 1.7 device drops it on its own merge, the next union brings it back). Because the row keeps the value, a whole-record customer merge that loses a synced value (another device's later edit of the same customer) can't lose it: the next pass puts it back. Every CRM write path stamps its own changes of these fields into the row (`crm.js commit` → `stampEdits` against a JSON copy of the last stored data; `assistant/edits.js crmStampCs`, also on Undo); an unstamped difference reads as a stale copy. **The rule per field:** equal → nothing; both stamps known → the newer change wins (tie → Contacts); CRM's stamp unknown (a pair that existed before) → a contact changed after the pair started wins, an empty side is filled from the other, two different values become a difference shown on the CRM card ("Different in Contacts" / "Διαφορές με τις Επαφές") with Keep this / Keep the contact's; nothing is overwritten until the user picks (Chris 2026-10-26). A copy is written only when it changes the other side and only when that side can hold it exactly (Contacts' 60-character name parts, 120-character street, …), so after one pass both sides are equal: no loop, no endless uploads. A customer's name never becomes empty. Emptying phone / e-mail / website in CRM removes the contact's first entry (the next one then flows back as the first). **Who writes:** the shell (`contactCrmSync`) reads both stored copies and writes each with that app's own rules (CRM `norm`, `m = max(m + 1, the contact's stamp)`; Contacts `merge.js restamp`), marks sync dirty and calls `__orosDataReload` in an app that is open (both apps adopt the stored copy at once). It runs after each sync (with a cloud, not before this session's first sync has ended, at most 2 minutes after the boot), on the 60 s tick and 1.5 s after either app writes; it does nothing when neither copy changed since its last pass. A single app (`?standalone`) only stamps; the pass runs in orOS.
- **Received invoices (W2b, Invoices wave 7, BR-CRM-LINK):** Invoices keeps invoices you RECEIVED in two new top-level lists, `bills: [{ id, num, date, due, cur, sup{name, afm}, crm?, net, vat, note, m } | tomb]` and `bpays: [{ id, bill, date, amt, how, note, m } | tomb]` (LWW by m per id, tombstone wins ties, flat extras ride along; written only when they have rows, so an older Invoices drops them on its own merge and the next union brings them back). Totals, paid, balance and status (`paid|overdue|partial|unpaid`) are computed, never stored. They never count in revenue, VAT, the dashboard, CSV or myDATA. Tab `Received` / `Λαμβανόμενα`; New › Record a received invoice. Read-only for CRM: `OrosInvoicesCore.billsByCrm(data, crmId, day, afm?)` → `{rows:[{id,num,sup,date,due,total,paid,bal,status,cur}], totals:{CUR:{billed,paid,open,overdue}}}` (a bill with `crm` belongs to that partner only; one without matches the partner's ΑΦΜ, `EL`/`GR` and spaces ignored). Overview `bills {n, last, open}`; money out = open bills + royalties due. Deep links `__orosOpenAt("invoices", {bills:{crm?, afm?, name?}})` (the tab, filtered to one partner) and `{bill:id}`.
- **Where an invoice came from, and partners on Budget entries (W2b):** Invoices docs keep `src = "<app>:<id>"` from the `ref` of a BR-INV-NEW prefill (written only when set; an older Invoices keeps it as a flat extra); `OrosInvoicesCore.bySrc(data, src)` → the non-cancelled docs made from it (drafts count). The Overview's consignment rows add `unbilled {n, value, moves}`: Stock settlements (`out` moves with `src "cons:<wh>"`, not voided, stamped on or after 2026-10-26, when sources started being kept) with no doc of `src "stock:cons-<move>"`, valued at sale price less the shop's discount; each opens Invoices with `OrosStockCore.consInvoice` + the partner's crm id (a prefill, saved only in Invoices). Budget entries (`tx`) carry an optional `crm` (validated `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,60}`, written only when set, a flat extra for older Budgets); the entry form shows `Partner in CRM` when CRM has records; BR-B1 (`__orosOpenBudgetNew`) passes `crm` through (Invoices "Add to Budget" sends the doc's or client's crm). Overview `budget {n, last, cur, year{i,o}, all{i,o}}` reads Budget's stored data as is (tombstoned entries skipped).
- **One timeline (W3, `crm/timeline.js`, `OrosCrmTimeline.build`):** pure, never stored; the record's `History` tab. Events newest first (day, then a contact's time, then key; at most 2000): CRM `act` and closed deals (`won`/`lost` on `cd`); Invoices issued docs (`inv`/`cred`), `pays`, `bills`, `bpays` of the partner (`byCrm(…, also)`, `billsByCrm`); Stock `po` of linked suppliers, `in` moves from them (`recv`), transfers to / from linked consignment shops (`ship`/`back`), settlements (`settle`, valued at the moves' prices); Timesheet hours per local day per linked client (`work`); Publishing statements of the partner's names (`stmt` on `to`, `roy` on `paid`, voided skipped); Budget `tx` with its `crm` (`bin`/`bout`). Groups `crm|money|stock|work|pub` as filter chips. Each event opens its app (`{invoice}`, `{bill}`, `{sup}`, `{view:"cons"}`, `{client}`, `{view:"roy"}`, Budget `{tx}`); contacts open the log editor, deals the deal.
- **Contracts, folder, actions (W4, core 1.6):** `ctr` is a top-level CRM list like `pt`, written only when it has rows (an older CRM drops it on its own merge; the next union brings it back): `{ id, m, cust, t, from?, to?, rem 0-365 (default 30), val?, note, file? (/internal/…), fup? }`; it follows its customer (gone customer, gone contracts; Undo of a customer delete brings them back) and is left out of `.oroscrm`. The end is remembered by an ordinary follow-up (`ctrRemindDay = to − rem`, never before today) written in the same commit: moved with the end while open, a new one when the end changes after it was done, tombed when the end day is removed or the contract deleted (Undo restores both). `ctrState` on / soon (reminder day reached) / ended; `contractsOf` lists running by end, open-ended, then ended. A contract file is written to `/internal/CRM/<partner name>/` only on Save, at a free name (`name (2).ext`, never replacing), and opens through Files `{path}`; `Detach` only drops the link. `Folder` makes and opens `/internal/CRM/<partner name>` (`{path, dir:true}`). Actions on the Overview open the other app only: Invoices `{newBill:{crm,name,afm}}` (a new received invoice prefilled, saved only there), Stock `{sup}` / `{view:"cons"}`, Timesheet `{client}`, Publishing `{view:"roy"}`. Tests `tests/crm-contracts.test.js`.
- **The partner outside CRM (W5):** `OrosCrmCore.balance(data, c, I, inv, today)` = what a partner owes you (`byCrm` with its `inv:` links) and you owe them (`billsByCrm`) in Invoices, per currency; used by the CRM search provider (a matching customer's text starts with it, worked out only for customers whose fields match every word; contracts are hits too, opening the customer) and by Contacts (`Customer:` button). CRM's Today provider (apps.json `today: [links.js, overview.js, today.js]`, shell cores) adds, for partners with links, royalties to pay and hours not billed (≥ 1 h) as info lines, each `{cust}` (a settlement due is Stock's own Today row since 3.81.00, not repeated). Invoices' Today adds received invoices still to pay due within the horizon (`{bill}`). Assistant `app_summary` takes `partner` for crm (`summary.crmPartner`: one match → the Overview in units, contracts, next follow-up and a ref to the card; several → their names; none → not found), loading `../crm/core.js`, `links.js`, `overview.js` and using the shell's cores; shown on the consent card first. Read-only everywhere. Tests `tests/crm-everywhere.test.js`.
- **Revenue Splitter on the partner card (W6):** a partner can be linked to beneficiaries of a WooCommerce shop's Noxpress Revenue Splitter (1.11+). CRM core 1.7 keeps the link in its own top-level list `rsl` `[{ id = customer id, m, a?: Connected services account id, n?: [the beneficiary's exact name, ≤ 5] }]` (like `ctr`: a 1.6 device drops the list on its own merge and the next union brings it back; inside `pt.ln` a 1.6 `normLinks` would strip an unknown `rs:` key). Names are trimmed and capped, never folded (the shop's splits match them exactly). A row without `n` is kept, and since 1.7 so is an emptied `pt` row `{ id, m }`: dropping it let another device's older copy bring an unlinked link back. The Overview's `Revenue Splitter` section (`crm/rs.js`, pure) calls through Connected services two read-only routes of the plugin, `GET /wp-json/wc/v3/rs/balances` and `GET /wp-json/wc/v3/rs/report?date_start=<year>-01-01&date_end=<today>` (allowlist `links/core.js` and `relay/ext.js`, no names in the URL: the card picks its own from the answers), and shows what is still to pay out (sales share + other income − payments), this year's titles with the beneficiary's share and each title's stock. Kept 5 minutes in memory, never stored, outside `Money` (Chris 2026-10-26: separate, so royalties kept in Publishing for the same person are not counted twice); offline it does not show. `Link beneficiary` lists the shop's beneficiaries (the partner's own name, then its people's names first; names linked to another partner of the same shop are left out), a tap links or unlinks with Undo. A customer's delete Undo restores its `rsl` row. Tests `tests/crm-rs.test.js`.
- BR-MAIL-SIG (sender Email Signature, receiver Mail, both 1.77.00): `__orosOpenAt("mail", { signature: { html, text, name } })`. Mail opens a dialog: pick the account, preview, Use. Only Use changes the account (`sig` = text ≤ 1000, `sigHtml` = `RT.clean(html,{cid:false}).html` when rich and ≤ 60,000; m moves forward). The sender builds the HTML with `SignatureCore.build(sig, {target:"mail"})` (lines, no tables, so clean() keeps it). No accounts → toast only.

### "Send to someone" share links (BR-SHARE) — phase 1
- **What.** One item from an app becomes a link `https://<orOS>/share/#<code>`. The item lives only in the URL fragment, which browsers never send to a server; `share/index.html` opens it locally, so the other person needs no account and no orOS. Chris 2026-10-12 chose this instead of a Messages chat (Part IX).
- **Code.** Envelope `{v:1,k,d}` (k = kind, d = normalized data). Plain: `1.` + base64url(deflate-raw(JSON)), or `0.` + base64url(JSON) when `CompressionStream` is missing. Locked: `p1.` + base64url(salt16 | iv12 | AES-GCM ciphertext), key = PBKDF2-SHA256 600,000 rounds; the first plaintext byte says deflated (1) or raw (0). Password optional, off by default, at least 6 characters.
- **Limits.** Send side refuses codes over `MAX_LINK` 32,768 characters (the link buttons go off; "Save as file" still works). Decode refuses codes over MAX_LINK+8 and stops inflating past `MAX_JSON` 262,144 bytes (decompression bomb). Every field is normalized with caps in `share/kinds.js` (`norm(kind, data)`), on send and again on receive; URLs http(s) only, emails must look like emails. The page renders with `textContent` only (`view.js` has no innerHTML; `send.js` only sets the eye icon constant).
- **Kinds (phase 1).** `list` (To-Do list: title + items with note/done), `note` (Notes page title + plain text), `contact` (Contacts card without photo, labels, star, relations), `event` (Calendar event or one occurrence, UID `<id>@share.oros`), `recipe` (Meal Planner recipe), `links` (one or many Bookmarks).
- **Kind `slots` (Calendar wave 8, "Share free times").** `{ t ≤ 120, n ≤ 80 (sender name), m? (email), len 5–480 min, tz? (IANA, regex), l? ≤ 200, x? ≤ 500, s[{ d: YYYY-MM-DD, m: [minutes after midnight, sorted, unique] }] }`, ≤ 62 days, ≤ 96 per day, ≤ 1500 in all; the sender's wall times in `tz`. `target()` is null (deliver says "could not be read"): the receiving page shows the times in the receiver's own zone (`slotWhen`, Intl), hides past ones, and after a pick offers a `mailto:` back to the sender with subject/body prefilled (`slotMail`, the sender's own wall time added when the zones differ), "Add to calendar (.ics)" and "Add to my orOS" (both as kind `event` from `slotEvent`, id `slot<hash>`). Nothing is booked or stored anywhere.
- **Sender API.** `window.orosShare.open({kind, data, text?})` in the shell (apps call `parent.orosShare`). The shell lazy-loads `share/kinds.js` + `share/send.js` on first use, so they are not in index.html. Window: Share… (navigator.share), Copy link, QR code (`qr/qr-encode.js`), Email (only with a Mail account, `__orosOpenAt("mail",{compose})`), Save as file (`<name> (orOS).txt` with the link), Send as text (old behaviour, when `text` is given). Senders: To-Do `#list-share`, Notes `#btn-share-page` + page menu, Contacts card Share, Calendar `#ev-share`, Meals recipe Share, Bookmarks context menu + `#sel-share` in the selection bar.
- **Receiving.** "Add to my orOS" writes `sessionStorage["oros-share-in"] = {at,k,d}` and goes to `../?share-in=1`; the shell strips the flag and calls the module's `deliver`, which runs `__orosOpenAt(app, target)` (30 min validity). Targets from `OrosShareKinds.target(env, lang)`: list → `todo {addItems:{newList, from, items}}` (BR-TD-ADD); note → `notes {add:{title,text}}`; contact → `contacts {importVcf}` and event → `calendar {importIcs}` (BR-FILE-IMPORT, they ask before saving); recipe → `meals {addRecipe: recipe}` (new, below); links → `bookmarks {add}` for one, `{addMany}` for several (new, below). Nothing is written without the user's own Save / Import / Add, except Notes (makes a page, as its `add` always did) and Bookmarks addMany (adds, toast says how many).
- **Kind `wiki` (Wiki wave 3, 2.07.00).** `{ t ≤ 200, x ≤ 60000 }`, target `{app:"wiki", target:{addArticle:{t,x}}}` (Wiki opens its editor prefilled, nothing saved until Save), file `.md`; the receiving page loads `../wiki/core.js` to render it; pictures are stripped by the sender (`WikiIO.shareText`).
- **Links with an expiry (BR-SHARE-RELAY, wave 1 = relay only).** Plan /mnt/project-files/sharing/share-relay-plan.md (Chris 2026-10-16, phase 1 only). Items too big for a link, or shared with an expiry (1/7/30 days) and a way to revoke, go to the relay as AES-256-GCM pieces (≤ 256 KiB each, key only in the link's `#fragment`, codes `r1.<id>.<key>` / `q1.` with a password, client side from wave 2). Relay `relay/share.js`: op `shr` (`new` → upload token, `fin`, `del` with the sender's revoke secret), `PUT`/`GET /s/<id>/<i>`; own D1 `oros-share` (binding `SHR_DB`), 25 MB per item, 400 MB in all, hourly cron purge. In clear only id, expiry, size, piece count, time and SHA-256 of the two secrets. Details in `relay/README.md`; tests `tests/share-relay.test.js`.
- **Links with an expiry, wave 2 (client).** `share/relay.js` (pure, UMD, `OrosShareRelay`): codes `r1.<id>.<key>.<n>` and `q1.<id>.<key>.<n>.<salt>` (id 16 B, key 32 B, salt 16 B, base64url; n = pieces ≤ 200). Plain text = flag byte + JSON `{v:1, x: expiry, e: BR-SHARE envelope}`, deflate-raw when flag 1, inflate capped at 4 MB; cut into pieces of ≤ 256 KiB, each `iv12 ‖ AES-256-GCM` with AAD `"orOS share|<id>|<i>|<n>"`. Password: key = HKDF-SHA-256(key ‖ PBKDF2-SHA-256(password, salt, 600,000), info "orOS share q1"). Revoke secret 32 B, relay gets SHA-256 hex of its base64url text. Send window (`share/send.js`): "With an expiry" + 1 / 7 (default) / 30 days; a plain code over `MAX_LINK` turns it on and locks it (message `forced`); the relay item is made once per (days, password) choice. "My shared links" (`links()`, also Settings › System row → shell act `shareLinks` → `orosShare.links()`): Copy link, Take back (two taps; relay `del`, then a tombstone). `share/out.js` (`OrosShareOut`, loaded at boot by `index.html`) = sync slice **`shareOut`** (`oros-share-out`, registered in `initSyncIntegration` with `merge`): `{v:1, items:{id:{c,d,k,t,x,a,p?} | {k,t,x,a,g:1}}}`; merge = union by id, revoke wins and drops the secrets, entries with `x` < newest `a` leave (deterministic, associative; ≤ 500). Receiving page: `relay.js` loaded, `#r1./#q1.` fetched from the relay and decrypted, rendered by the same `view.js` paths, "Available until …", one message for expired/revoked; meta CSP (`default-src 'self'`, `connect-src` the relay only, no inline). Tests `tests/share-expiry.test.js` (client against the real relay code on an in-memory D1, merge laws).
- **Kind `cal`, share wave 3 (a whole calendar or a date range).** Calendar › More › `Send calendar to someone…` (`#scal-dlg`): the person's OWN events (no subscriptions, no feed labels) of all labels or one, whole or only those with an occurrence in a range (this month / next 3 months / this year / chosen dates, via `OrosCalOccur.instancesBetween`); over 5,000 the newest go. Data `{ t ≤ 120, tz? (sender's zone), f?/u? (range), lb? [{n ≤ 60, c #rrggbb}] ≤ 50, ev [event] ≤ 5,000 and ≈ 3 MB JSON }`; event = the `event` kind's fields (wall times as stored, `r` short form + `r.x` RRULE when richer) + `id` (always; a stable hash when missing) + `xd` excluded dates (series only, ≤ 400) + `z` own zone (timed only) + `b` label index. File / target: one `.ics` (`calIcs`: TZID = IANA name, RRULE, EXDATE, CATEGORIES = label name, UID `<id>@share.oros` so a second import updates) → `{app:"calendar", target:{importIcs}}` (the Calendar's own import preview asks first). `encode` refuses JSON over `MAX_JSON` ("big"), so the send window turns `With an expiry` on (`tooBig`). Receiving page loads `../calendar/occur.js`: month grid (Monday first, dots in label colours, tap a day) or month list, ‹ › bounded by the range, timed events converted to the viewer's zone with a hint. Tests `tests/share-cal.test.js`, 5,000-event relay round trip in `tests/share-expiry.test.js`.
- **Kind `album`, share wave 4 (photo albums).** Relay only (`K.RELAY_ONLY`; `encode` refuses it, the send window starts with `With an expiry` on and locked). Senders: Files (context menu `Send photos to someone…`: selected pictures + pictures right inside selected folders, ≤ 200; `Send to an app…` on pictures also offers it through BR-SEND-5) and Photo Lab (`File › Send to someone…`, the flattened picture as JPEG ≤ 2048 px). They call `orosShare.open({kind:"album", data:{t}, photos:[{blob|path, name?, c?}]})`; `share/album.js` (`OrosShareAlbum`, lazy with send.js) draws every photo again on a canvas (EXIF orientation applied, long side ≤ 2048, JPEG q 0.85, so no EXIF/GPS leaves), caption = given or the file name unless it is a camera name, ≤ 200 photos, ≤ 25,000,000 bytes, unreadable ones (HEIC…) counted and left out. Data `{ t ≤ 120, p: [{ o, n ≤ 8 MiB, m jpeg|png|webp, w?, h?, c? ≤ 300 }] }`; the photos ride beside the JSON in the relay plain text: flag 2 = `[2] + u32 BE L + L bytes deflated JSON + photo bytes` (`relay.js` `pack(env, exp, bin)`, `unpack` → `bin`). Receiving page: each slice shown only when its first bytes are JPEG/PNG/WebP (`K.photoType`), from a `blob:` URL; grid + full-screen viewer (‹ ›, arrows, Esc) with `Save photo`; no Add to my orOS. Tests `tests/share-album.test.js`, relay round trip with a password in `tests/share-expiry.test.js`.
- **BR-SHARE-RECIPE.** `__orosOpenAt("meals", {addRecipe: r})` — `r` goes through `OrosMealsCore.normRecipe`, loses id/m/fv, and opens in the recipe editor as a new unsaved recipe.
- **BR-BM-MANY.** `__orosOpenAt("bookmarks", {addMany:{folder, items:[{url,title}]}})` — finds the folder by name or makes it, skips URLs already in it, removes a folder it made when nothing was added, toast with the count.
- **Files.** `share/kinds.js` (pure, UMD, Node-testable), `share/send.js` (shell window), `share/index.html` + `view.js` + `share.css` (page, has inheritPalette/watchPalette for G3), help topic `help/topics/share.*.txt`, tests `tests/share.test.js`.

### "Send to an app" (BR-SEND, app interop wave 1)
Decided by Chris 2026-10-16 23:35 (thread "Συνεργασία εφαρμογών orOS", all six waves of /mnt/project-files/app-interop/app-interop-report.md, in order). One orOS-wide sheet instead of a button per pair of apps.
- **BR-SEND-1 · API.** `window.parent.orosSend.open({ kind, data, share? })` in the shell. Senders show their entry only when `parent.orosSend` exists. The shell loads `send/core.js` (`OrosSendCore`, pure, Node-tested in `tests/send.test.js`) and `send/sheet.js` (`__orosSendImpl`) on first use, never at boot, and passes the installed internal apps (names from `orosAssistInstalled`), the sender (`state.running`, never offered to itself), its icons (shell constants) and `__orosOpenAt`.
- **BR-SEND-2 · Kinds.** `text {title?, text}` (≤ 200 000), `link {url http(s) only, title?, note?}`, `items {title?, items:[{text ≤ 300, note ≤ 1000}] ≤ 200}`, `table {name?, rows ≤ 500 × 64, sum?}`. Control characters out, CRLF → LF; numbers stay numbers, strings stay strings (Spreadsheet escapes `= + - @` itself, BR-S1-3).
- **BR-SEND-3 · Receivers = `RECEIVERS` in `send/core.js`**, each building that app's EXISTING deep-link target, capped to the app's own limit: Notes `{add}`, To-Do `{addItems}` (a text becomes one task per line, list markers stripped; `items` with a title → `newList`), Writer `{newDoc}`, Mail `{compose}`, Assistant `{ask}`, Bookmarks `{add}` (link only), Wiki `{addArticle}`, Spreadsheet `{newSheet}`, Text Tools / Case Converter `{text}`, Label Maker `{text}` (one line ≤ 40 characters only). Typing Tutor `{addText: {title, text ≤ 20 000}}` (text only; the Add dialog of My texts, Typing Tutor wave 2). `ORDER` fixes the sheet's order. A new receiver = one entry there + a line in the test that checks the app's code reads that target.
- **BR-SEND-4 · A prefill, not data (BR-W8-6).** The receiving app opens its own form / dialog / new draft; nothing is stored or synced by the sheet. All text through `textContent`; `sheet.js` has no innerHTML (test-checked).
- **BR-SEND-5 · Send to someone stays share/.** A sender may pass `share: { kind, data }` (its BR-SHARE item); the sheet then shows `Send to someone…`, which calls `orosShare.open(share)` unchanged. The existing "Send to someone…" entries in apps stay as they are.
- **BR-SEND-6 · Senders (wave 1).** Writer toolbar `#btn-send-app` (selection, else the whole document, before Settings), Notes page menu `Send to an app…` (page or selected text; share = kind note), Wiki article menu (plain text; share = kind wiki), Mail's "to an app" dialog `Another app…`, Bookmarks item menu (link; share = kind links), Reader's send dialog `Another app…` (link + article text).
- **BR-SEND-7 · Office apps (wave 3, 2026-10-17).** New receivers: Slides `{ outline, title }` (Mind map's contract; Markdown headings start slides, otherwise the title heads them, ≤ 8 bullets a slide, ≤ 300 slides), Mind map `{ pasteText: { text } }` (the paste dialog; "# title" root added when the text has no heading), Kanban `{ addCards: { title, cards: [{ title, notes }] ≤ 100 } }` (one card per line / item; a dialog picks board and column, cards go to the top, Undo; `kanban/tools.js` `asCards` cleans it), Prompter `{ newPrompt: { text ≤ 8000 } }` (the New prompt editor, same text in both language fields), Writer `{ newDoc: { title, rows } }` (a table, row 1 = heading, escaped cells), Mail takes `table` (tab-separated body). Senders: Spreadsheet sheet menu (selection, or the used area when one cell is selected; shown values, ≤ 500 × 64) → `table`; Slides More → `text` (its outline); Mind map idea menu → `text` (`M.toOutline` of the branch); Kanban card dialog `#c-send` (subtasks under the notes) and column dialog `#col-send` → `items`.
- **BR-SEND-8 · Pictures and sound (wave 5, 2026-10-17).** Layout receives `files` when it is exactly one picture (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp/.gif): `{ placeImage: { path, name } }` — path under `/internal/`, no `..`; read with `orosFS.read`, placed by `LY.io.placeFromBlob` as one image frame fitted to the margin box of the current page (one Undo step), or in a new document with the New document defaults when none is open. Senders save a PNG to `/internal/Pictures` (unique name " (2)"…) and open `files` (+ the album item when `orosShare` exists): Pixel `#send-btn` (512 px), Photo Lab File menu (flattened, long side ≤ 4096; `saveToPictures` resolves with the path), Atelier More menu (current page, ≤ 4096). Pixel `#wall-btn` → `orosWallpaper.setImage` (a screen-shaped canvas, face crisp at ~60 % of the short side, bg = the face background). Studio Export dialog: `#export-music` writes the mix (chosen format) to `/internal/Music` and opens Music `{ playPath }`; `#export-ring` turns the instrument notes of the export range (no drum, muted or non-soloed tracks) into one voice (`core.toRtttl`: highest note wins, 32nd grid, octaves 4–7, ≤ 255 notes) and opens Ringtone Composer `{ importText: { text ≤ 64 KB } }`, which only fills the Import dialog. Melodies as sounds: `window.orosMelodies { list, play(id, fallback, maxS), stop }` (stickies/host.js, read only); value `"rt:<id>"` in Settings › Notifications › Sound (every notification incl. Habits/Health reminders, ≤ 8 s, gone → chime) and in Time timers (`clock-core` accepts it; the shell rings it ≤ 15 s every 17 s until dismissed, gone → beep). Tests `interop-pictures`, `interop-picsend`, `interop-sound`, `interop-melodies`.
- **BR-SEND-9 · Everyday links (wave 6, 2026-10-17).** Meals shopping list `#sh-bud` → a "How much did you pay?" dialog (`core.parseAmount`, Budget's rules, cents) → BR-B1 `{ k:"o", a, c:"o-groc", d: today, n: "Shopping: N items · …" (ticked items, else all), src:"meals" }`. Calendar event dialog `#ev-track` (saved events, when the shell lists Timesheet via `orosAssistInstalled`) → Timesheet `{ startTimer: { title ≤ 200, note? } }`: starts a timer (project = first non-archived one with the same name, else none); a running timer is never stopped (toast). Diary shows that day's feelings from Mood (`OrosMoodCore.dayMoods(raw, ymd, lang)`, read only, tombstones honoured) as a button → Mood `{ day }` (Entries tab filtered to that day); Mood entry rows "Write about it" → Diary `{ write: { date, text } }`: the text goes into the longer entry as an unsaved draft with Keep / Discard (no autosave until the user acts; waits behind the PIN lock). Weather on days: `weather/days.js` (`OrosWeatherDays.forDates(dates, {lat,lon}?)`, reads oros-weatherapp-data/-cache, never fetches, cache ≤ 36 h, nearest city ≤ 0.5° or the shell place rule of today.js) → Calendar month cells (icon), week and day heads (icon + high/low), Travel itinerary days (trip.geo, else the destination point Travel already cached in oros-travel-wx). Calculator and Unit Converter "Send to…" → `text` kind ("expression = result", "5 km = 3.107 mi"). Tests `interop-everyday-a/b/c`.
- **BR-SEND-10 · Flashcards (Flashcards wave 4, 2026-10-17).** Receiver `flashcards` takes `text` → `{ make: { title, text ≤ 200 000 } }`, `items` → `{ make: { title, text } }` (one line per item, `text :: note` when it has a note), `link` only with a note (Reader's article text) → `{ make: { title, text: note } }`, `table` when a row after the heading row has two cells → `{ make: { title: name, rows } }`. Flashcards finds the cards with `flashcards/make.js` (FlashcardsMake, pure): `Q :: A` → Basic, `Q ::: A` → Basic and reversed (the colons need a space on one side), a line with `==highlights==` → Fill in the gap (one gap per highlight; the heading above it in Extra), a line with `{{cN::…}}` → Fill in the gap, a heading + the lines no rule took → Basic (heading on the front), table rows after row 1 → first two non-empty cells; nothing found → one Basic card (title / whole text) to shape; ≤ 500 cards, ≤ 20 000 chars a field. The preview dialog (untick, edit, deck: last used or a new deck named after the title; cards already here start unticked) saves nothing until `Make cards` (BR-W8-6). Senders unchanged: Notes, Writer, Wiki, Reader, Spreadsheet, Mail, Kanban… all reach it through their existing `Send to an app…`. Tests `tests/send.test.js`, `tests/flashcards-make.test.js`.

### Connected services contract (orosLinks, integrations wave 1)
- Apps reach another platform only through `parent.orosLinks.call(acctId, reqs)`; requests outside `OrosLinksCore.checkReq` are refused before any network call. Keys never pass through an app frame.
- Relay op `ext` (relay/ext.js): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p, host, base, ck, cs, reqs ≤ 10}` → `{ok, data:{res:[{status, body}|{status, err:"too-big"}|{err:"timeout"|"network"}]}}`. Host checked like a mail server (public DNS, https, default port), same allowlist as the app, bodies with listed keys only, redirects not followed, writes one at a time, 2 MB per answer / 8 MB per call, 20 s per request / 28 s per call; keys never stored, logged or echoed. Owned by the Mail thread (relay/).
- Relay op `ext` WooCommerce product pictures (Newsletter editor wave E4): a request `{m:"GET", path:"/wp-content/uploads/…", img:1}` is fetched from `https://<host><base><path>` (no API root, no Authorization, redirects not followed), only `image/jpeg|png|gif|webp`, ≤ 512 KB, one picture per call and nothing else in it (base64 on the relay costs CPU: ~25 ms for 2 MB against the Free plan's ~10 ms; Mail thread review); answer `{status, type, b64}` or `{status, err:"type"|"too-big"}`. The WooCommerce allowlist also gains GET `/customers` and `/data/currencies/current` (same as links/core.js).
- Relay op `ext` for Odoo (wave 4D): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"odoo", host, base, db?, key, reqs}`; host checked like WooCommerce's, `db` only for Odoo, Bearer + `X-Odoo-Database`, only the three search_read POSTs with fixed bodies (run side by side: `reads: true`).
- Relay op `ext` for Invoice Ninja (1.62.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"ininja", host, base, key, reqs}`; host checked like WooCommerce's, `X-API-TOKEN` + `X-Requested-With`, GETs only, same allowlist as `links/core.js`.
- Relay op `ext` for Stripe (1.61.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"stripe", key, reqs}`; restricted keys only, fixed host, GETs only, same allowlist as `links/core.js`.
- Relay op `ext` for CRMs (1.60.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"hubspot"|"pdrive", key, reqs}`; `host`/`base`/`env` refused (fixed hosts), GETs only, same allowlist as `links/core.js`.
- Relay op `ext` for email platforms (1.59.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"mlite"|"mchimp"|"brevo", key, reqs}`; `host`/`base`/`env` refused (fixed hosts; Mailchimp's from the key's data centre), same allowlist and body rules as `links/core.js` (incl. the Mailchimp `update_existing` rule), 64 KB per request body.
- Relay op `ext` for timologisi.online (1.58.00): `POST /v1 {op:"ext", p:"tol", env:"test"|"live", key, reqs}`; `host`/`base` refused (fixed hosts per env), header `API-KEY`, same allowlist and `okInvoice` as `links/core.js`, a write travels alone (`reqs` of 1, the app refuses more too), 64 KB request body, 65 s per request / 70 s per call (SendInvoices waits for AADE). The app gives a tol write 75 s. Any platform: a request never sent because the call's budget ran out returns `{err:"skipped"}`; `timeout`/`network` mean it may have arrived.
- Stock deep link `{view: "shop"}` opens the shop panel.

### Household sharing (BR-HH) — wave 1 at 3.48.00, wave 2 at 3.49.00, wave 3 at 3.50.00, wave 4 at 3.51.00, wave 5 at 3.52.00, wave 6 at 3.53.00 and 3.54.00, wave 7a at 3.55.00, wave 7b at 3.56.00, wave 7c at 3.57.00, wave 7d at 3.58.00, wave 7e at 3.59.00, wave 7f at 3.60.00, wave 7g at 3.61.00, wave 8 at 3.62.00
- **What it is.** People who live together share documents between their own orOS, each with their own sync and no account. A household is a box on the relay (`relay/house.js`, Durable Object `HouseBox`, binding `HOUSE`, SQLite, migration `house-v1`) that holds only ciphertext; the key `K` (AES-256, per epoch) never leaves the members' devices and their own sync (slice `household`). Plan: `/mnt/project-files/household/household-plan.md` (P1–P10, waves W1–W7).
- **Relay (`/h/<box22>/…`, own CORS, per-IP rate limit, 10 new boxes per IP and day):** write token `W = HMAC-SHA256(K, "oros-household/write")` (the box keeps sha256 of the current token and the last 20), admin token `A` (header `X-HH-Admin`), invite secret `I` (`Authorization: Invite`). Documents `PUT /d/<id>` with `If-Match` revisions (stale → 412 + current rev). Limits (`HOUSE_LIMITS`): 64 documents, 300 KB each, 5 MB per box, 12 envelopes (members), 5 invites, 10 waiting requests (7 days), invites ≤ 30 days and ≤ 20 uses, 120 writes/min per box, a box idle 180 days wipes itself (alarm). Key rotation `rot` swaps the token and leaves one envelope per member (`ECDH ephemeral → HKDF(salt "oros-household/"+box, info "wrap") → AES-GCM`). A hibernating WebSocket per open device (`["hh1","w.<W>"]`) sends notices only: `{k,r}` a document changed, `{q:1}` a join request, `{e}` new epoch, `{x:1}` box gone.
- **Bytes:** `"h", 0x01, flags (deflate-raw), epoch u32, iv12, AES-GCM(AAD "hh1|box|doc|epoch")`. Invite code `h1.<box>.<I>` or with a password `h2.<box>.<salt>.<sealed>` (PBKDF2-SHA-256 600 000). The link is `https://useoros.online/share/#<code>`: `share/view.js` keeps the code in localStorage `oros-household-invite` and opens `../?open=household` (never in a query string, DL-1 would copy it into `app-at`). A join request is sealed with `HKDF(I, info "invite")`; a member accepts → envelope for the new member; nothing is shared before that.
- **Engine (`household/engine.js`, shell, `window.orosHousehold`):** `ready, sync, syncAll, list, pending, member, me, create, invite, withdraw, join, checkJoins, dismissJoin, requests, accept, refuse, setMe, rename, removeMember, makeAdmin, leave, remove, rotate, forget, docs(kind), get, view, share(box, kind, title, changes, fromDoc), change(box, id, {set, del, m}), retitle, unshare, archived(kind), dropArchived, restore, liveOn, liveOff, on(fn)`. A pass: GET info → pull changed documents and merge → push dirty ones (roster first, 3 tries on 412). Removing a member rotates the key at once (auto-rotate also when `km` names someone not on the roster). A late `change` for a document that is gone does nothing (never recreates it). Sync every 10 minutes while visible, on online and on return; sockets close 60 s after the page is hidden.
- **Archive:** a document of a household left, removed or deleted, or one this person stopped sharing, is kept 30 days with `take: true`: apps make a private copy themselves (To-Do: `tdc-<doc>`, same task ids, every device of the person makes the same copy, stamped newer than the share's tombstones). A document someone else stopped sharing is kept with `take: false`: Household › "Removed lately" › Share again.
- **To-Do (`todo/house.js`, `OrosTodoHouse`):** a shared list is the document kind `todo`, shown as list `tdh-<doc>`; it is never in `oros-todo-data` nor in the person's slice (`personal()`), and `.orostasks` files hold only own lists. Task fields shared: text, done, due, notes, info, recurrence, prio, subs, o (place); list fields m: t, rec, last, next. Labels and todo.js's own stamps stay personal. Every edit leaves as the changed fields only (`save()` → `hhPush()` → `diffItems`), every document change rebuilds the list (`hhInject()`), and a built list projects back to exactly its document, so the two merges never answer each other (no endless uploads). Moving a task from an own list into a shared one tombstones it in the own lists. A shared list cannot be dragged among the tabs (it sits at the end).
- **Calendar (`calendar/house.js`, `OrosCalHouse`, wave 2):** a label becomes a shared calendar, document kind `cal`, shown as the label `hh-<doc>` (kept in `hhLabels`, never in `state.labels`) with its events in `state.events` in memory only: `writeStore()` writes `personal(state)` to `oros-calendar-data`, so they are never in the person's slice, `.oroscal` files or the phone bridge (BR-PHONE); `saveState()` marks the slice dirty only when the own copy changed. Event fields shared: date, dateEnd, start, end, title, note, location, recur, tz; m: t (name), c (colour, one of calendar.js `VALID_COLORS`, otherwise the default). Reminders stay personal: device-local `oros-calendar-hhrem` (`{event id: minutes}`). Every edit leaves as the changed fields (`saveState()` → `hhPush()`), every document change rebuilds them (`hhInject()`), and a built calendar projects back to exactly its document. Sharing tombstones the label and its events in the own calendar (ids the household does not take get a new id first); an event moved from an own label into a shared one is tombstoned in the own calendar (`hhTombMoved`, using the ids last written). Stop sharing → own copy `lbc-<doc>` with the same event ids, stamped now (archive `take`). The own events with no label (none, or a label not among the person's: `OrosCalHouse.loose(events, labels)`, the same set as the No label chip) can go in one step: Label manager › `No label` row (shown only with a household and such events) › house icon asks a name (default Home) and a household, puts them into a new own label `lbl-<uid>` (event `mtime` stamped now) and shares that label through the same path; when the household refuses, the label is dropped and the events get their old label and `mtime` back (nothing saved meanwhile). Label manager › "Shared with a household": name and colour for everyone, Stop sharing, Delete (no own copy). The initials of whoever changed an event last show on its row. A deep link (`__orosOpenCalendar`) to a shared event waits for the first build. The shell keeps the device-local mirror `oros-calendar-hh` (`{ver:1, labels, events}`, own reminders, written only on a change) for readers that only see localStorage: the reminder tick (`calRemTick`), the Today provider (`calendar/today.js`) and search (`calendar/search.js`).
- **Split (`split/house.js`, `OrosSplitHouse`, wave 3):** a group becomes a shared group, document kind `split` that keeps the group's own id (`m.g`; m also t, col, cur, arch), so group files and backups of it still join up. One item per record, `p:` person, `e:` expense, `y:` payment, `r:` repeating expense (`<kind>:<own id>`), each `{ v: the record without id and m, it: the itemised receipt or null }`: a record is whole in `v`, so two edits of one expense never mix into one that does not add up (split.js's normalisers check every record again). Who each member is: item `me:<member id>` `{ v: person id }`, set by that member only (Split's `mine` for a shared group lives there, never in the person's slice). In split.js the records sit in `data` like any other, in memory only: `commit()` stores and syncs `own(data)` (dirty only when it changed), sends the changed records (`hhPush`), and `hhInject()` rebuilds them from the household; the group record's `m` is lifted above the person's own `grp:` tombstone so a whole-data merge (import, restore) never drops it. Sharing tombstones `grp:<id>` in the own data. A copy of the same group the person already had (a group file, a second device that had not heard of the share) joins only with records the document lacks or that are newer than its copy and its deletion (`adopt`, reading the document's `dt`). Stop sharing → own copy with the same ids stamped now; Delete on a shared group = remove for everyone, no own copy. A group that leaves the household leaves the screen at once. Initials of who changed a record last on its row; a small house on the group card. Not yet: shared groups in universal search.
- **Chore Wheel (`chores/house.js`, `OrosChoresHouse`, wave 4):** the whole wheel is shared, document kind `chores` (m.t = the household's name at share time). Items: `mb:<id>` a member `{ c: {name, color, icon, away}, o: order }` (content and order merge apart, as in `mergeChores`), `tk:<id>` a chore `{ v: the task without id and m }`, `dn:<task>:<day>` a done/skipped mark `{ v: [state, by] }`, `st:<task>:<day>` a hand-over or spin `{ v: member id or "" }`, `me:<member id>` `{ v: wheel member id }` (who each household member is, set by that member only). The record stamps are the items' last change, so the turn, balanced mode and stats come out the same on every device. Only marks of the last 92 days (and later ones) travel, newest first, at most 1500 (a document holds 3000 items); older marks leave the document with the next change. Sharing moves the own wheel in (members and chores tombstoned in the own data, the marks stay there and age out after 13 months); the app shows one wheel at a time: `data` is the household wheel in memory only, the own wheel stays `pdata` (stored and synced, `sliceGet` = own only), chips at the top switch when there is more than one (device-local pref `wh`). "Who am I" in a household wheel lives in the document, never in `oros-chores-prefs` (whose `me` stays the own wheel's). Every change sends the items that changed against what was last read (`fromDoc`). Stop sharing → own copy with the same ids stamped now, merged into the own wheel; others get `take: false` (Household › Removed lately). The shell keeps the device-local mirror `oros-chores-hh` `{ ver: 1, wheels: [{ id, t, hh, me, data }] }` (written only when it changed): the daily reminder adds each wheel with this person's own `me`, and Today, universal search (target `{ task \| member, wheel }`) and the Calendar "Chores" feed read it too.
- **Plant Care (`plants/house.js`, `OrosPlantsHouse`, wave 4):** the person's plants are shared as one garden, document kind `plants`. Items: `p:<id>` a plant `{ v: the plant without id and m }`, `l:<id>` a log entry `{ v: the entry without id and m }`, `wh:<plant id>` `{ v: household member id }` (whose daily reminder the plant is; absent = everyone). The due day is still never stored: "Done" on one phone adds an entry and the next due day moves for everyone. Only entries of the last 180 days travel, plus always the newest of each plant and kind (the base of its schedule), newest first, at most 2400. Same shape as the Chore Wheel: sharing tombstones the plants in the own data, `data` is the garden on screen (in memory), `pdata` the own plants (`sliceGet`), chips (`#gardens`, pref `wh`) switch, deep links to a plant id find its garden (`hhFind`). Settings › Household shares or stops; the plant editor has "Reminder for" in a household garden, and the initials of that member show on the plant's tasks. Stop sharing → own copy with the same ids stamped now. Device-local mirror `oros-plants-hh` `{ ver: 1, gardens: [{ id, t, hh, mine, data }] }` (`mine` = plants whose reminder is for this person): the shell's daily reminder and Today use only `mine`; universal search and the Calendar "Plants" feed show every shared plant (each garden merged on its own, never with the own data, whose tombstones would hide them).
- **Maps places (`maps/hh-core.js` `OrosMapsHH` + `maps/hh.js`, wave 5):** each household has one folder of places, document kind `places` (title "Places"). Items: `p:<lat E6>_<lon E6>` `{ v: { name ≤120, sub ≤200, note ≤500, lat, lon } }`, at most 2500; the id comes from the coordinates (like the own saved places), so the same place added by two people at once is one place, and the whole place is one value (a rename and a note at the same time keep the newer whole place). "Household" in a place's popup adds it (the first place makes the folder; a second add while the folder is being made waits for it, so a household never gets two folders from one person); a place already in a folder shows "In" plus the household name. The folders show after the own saved places in the list and as orange pins (`#e5a03b`) in their own layer; the popup shows the note and the member who changed it last, with Route, Edit, Remove (Undo puts it back). "Stop sharing" on the folder → unshare; the stopper gets its places as own saved places through `importPlaces` (the note after the name in `sub`; a saved place stays as it is). No live location: a place is only ever where someone put it. The own saved places (`oros-maps-data`) never change while a folder is shared.
- **What the others changed (`household/recent.js`, `OrosHouseRecent`, wave 6):** the engine calls `opts.changed(box, doc, before, after)` when a pull changed a shared document this device already had (never on the first sight of a document, never for the roster). `summarize` counts items added (+), changed (~) and removed (−), per member of the newest changed field; the person's own member id and `me:` items are left out; a removal carries no member (the document keeps only when an item went), so removals show without a name. The shell keeps them device-local (never synced) in `oros-household-recent` `{ v: 1, b: { <box>: { hh, ev: [[t, mid, name, doc, title, a, c, d]], from, last } } }`, 36 h and at most 300 events per household. The bell: a burst rings once, as one line per household (title = household name, body "Shopping: Nikos +3 ~1, −1 · Calendar: Anna ~2", deep link `household:<box>`, key `chg:<box>:<from>`), when nothing new came for 10 minutes or an hour after the burst began (checked every minute while orOS runs). Today: `household/today.js` (apps.json `today: ["recent.js", "today.js"]`) shows one info row per household with what reached this device since midnight ("Today at home").
- **Wakes with orOS closed (wave 6b, optional, off by default, per device):** the Household app's "Tell me about changes when orOS is closed" (needs Settings › Notifications › "Notifications with orOS closed" on this device). The shell (`household/engine.js` `wake`, device-local `oros-household-push` `{ on, b: { <box>: { pid, wt, e } } }`) registers every household at its current key epoch: `POST /h/<box>/p { pid, wt, ct }` where pid = this device's push box id, wt = a wake token from `webpush.js wakeToken()` (relay `wtok`; it can only `wake`, never set/del/sub; revoked with `wdel`), ct = one packet encrypted on the device for itself (payload `ns: "household"`, k `household:wake:<box>`, title = household name, "Something changed. Open orOS to see it.", link `household:<box>`). Document writes carry `X-HH-Dev: <pid>`, so the writer is not woken. The relay box wakes every other registered device 2 minutes after a change, at most once per device per 15 minutes (`relay/house.js` alarm, which also keeps the idle deadline; `relay/push.js` `wake`, `Urgency: normal`); a key rotation clears the rows, so devices register again with the new token (a removed member's devices stop hearing of changes). Turning it off unpings every box and revokes the wake tokens. Only "something changed" travels; no names, counts or content reach the relay. Mail thread OK 2026-10-24 (separate wake token, one alarm, clear on rotation).
- **Whole apps (`household/whole.js` `OrosHouseWhole`, `household/share.js` `OrosHouseShare`, wave 7):** the apps that share all their data with a household (Meal Planner first) describe it as parts: `list` (`[{ id, m, … }]`), `map` (`{ key: { m, … } }`), `one` (`{ m, … }`). One item per record: `<p>:<id>` `{ v: record without id and m }`; an id or key the item id cannot hold (spaces, accents, `|`, longer than 60) is `<p>::<hash>` `{ k, v }` (FNV-1a ×2, 64 bits base 36); a `one` part is the item `<p>`. A value whose JSON is longer than 7800 characters travels in chunks: `v = { z: n, h }`, fields `z0…z21 = { h, s }`; every write of such a record rewrites all its chunks (each carries the hash), so all its fields share one stamp and the household merge (stamp, then member id) never mixes two versions; chunks that do not add up are `raw`: not shown, never deleted (`push` sends them back as they were). Record stamps are the items' last change (`_t`), an own copy is stamped now. `share.js` keeps the books in the app frame (copies, the one on screen, `last` so only changed records leave, own copies of copies that left) and never touches the page. Sharing COPIES the own data into the household; the own data stays under "Only mine" (chips at the top switch, device-local pref `wh`), `sliceGet` = own only. Stop sharing → the stopper's own data gets the household copy merged in (stamped now); the others get `take: false` (Household › Removed lately).
- **Meal Planner (`meals/house.js` `OrosMealsHouse`, wave 7a):** document kind `meals`. Parts: `r` recipes, `n` own shopping items, `pa` pantry, `pl` plan cells, `ck` ticks, `ai` aisle choices, `pn` "always at home", `nu` nutrition matches, `set` settings. Deleted ready recipes travel as the item `sd` `{ v: { recipe id: stamp } }`. Plan cells, ticks and own shopping items older than 120 days do not travel (they leave the document with the next change; the own plan keeps them). A plan cell shows the initials of the member who changed it last. The shell writes the device-local mirror `oros-meals-hh` `{ ver: 1, plans: [{ id, t, hh, data }] }` (only on a change; `index.html` loads `household/whole.js`, `meals/core.js`, `meals/house.js`); `meals/today.js` adds each household plan's meals of the day as "<household> · Dinner: …". The pantry best-before reminder, universal search and the Calendar "Meals" feed read the own data only.
- **Baby (`baby/house.js` `orosBabyHouse`, wave 7b):** document kind `baby`. Parts: `k` children, `e` events, `g` growth, `mk` milestones / vaccines / visits, `s` milk stash. Travels: live records only (a deletion removes the item), events of the last 90 days newest first, at most 2400, and every running feed or sleep timer. Prefs (units) never travel and the reminders stay device-local: the copy on screen always carries the own `prefs`/`pm`. Sharing MOVES what travels (`moved(d, now)`): after the household accepted it, the own copies get tombstones (stamp + 1), so a child is never on screen twice and older events stay on the device that shared; stop sharing merges the household copy back, stamped now (newer than the tombstones). Chips "Only mine" / the shared Baby at the top (device-local view `hh`), initials on events someone else logged; a search or Today target for a child in another Baby switches to it. Mirror `oros-baby-hh` (`{ ver: 1, sets }`, written by the shell only on a change); the shell's feed and medicine reminders and Baby's Today rows read `union(own, sets)` (own tombstones left out, same ids merge), so a shared child reminds once.
- **Pet Health Book (`petcare/house.js` `OrosPetcareHouse`, wave 7c):** document kind `petcare`. Parts: `p` pets (each keeps its field-group stamps `fm` inside the item, so `C.merge` still decides per group), `r` records. Travels: every pet, the newest 2800 records by day, photos while they fit 160 000 characters in all (pets in id order; a photo that does not fit stays in the sharer's own book). Attachment names (`sc`) travel, the files stay on the sharer's orOS disk. Sharing COPIES (as Meal Planner): "Only mine" keeps the own book, device-local pref `wh`, initials on records someone else wrote, a deep link to a pet in another book switches to it. Mirror `oros-petcare-hh`; the shell's reminders, Today and the Calendar "Pets" feed read `withShared(own)` = `union(own, sets)`: a pet that is in a household is read from there with its records (the own copy of it is left out), so it reminds once. `house.js` loads without `household/whole.js` for these readers (the Calendar loads it next to `petcare/core.js`).
- **Together (`together/house.js` `TogetherHouse`, wave 7d):** document kind `together`, ONE relationship per document (title = its name). Parts: `r` the relationship, `mo` moments, `d` special days, `me` meetings. Gift ideas (surprises), prefs and the PIN never travel; photo paths travel as names, the pictures stay on the sharer's disk. Sharing MOVES (`household/group.js` `OrosHouseGroup.make({ normalize, empty, parent, children, key, keep })`, shared with Garage: `moved(own, rel)` = the own copies get tombstones after the household accepted it); the app shows `union(own, sets)` (own data without what moved + every shared record, own prefs and gifts, own tombstones of shared ids left out), so shared relationships are ordinary tabs ("· shared in …" under the names); `save` runs `split(next, sets)`: a relationship and its rows go to its household copy (`OrosHouseShare.push(data, key)`, which now takes the copy's key, as do `unshare`, `member` and `me`), new relationships, gifts, prefs and tombstones stay own (`sliceGet` = own only). Stop sharing merges the copy back stamped now. Mirror `oros-together-hh`; the shell's morning notice, Today and the Calendar feed read `withShared(own)`.
- **Garage (`garage/house.js` `OrosGarageHouse`, wave 7e):** document kind `garage`, ONE vehicle per document (title = its name). Parts: `v` the vehicle, `f` fill-ups, `s` services, `pl` plans, `ty` tyres, `rn` renewals, `c` costs, `o` odometer. Settings (currency) and reminder prefs never travel; receipt names travel, the pictures stay on the sharer's disk. Same model as Together (`household/group.js`, parent `vehicles`, key `v`): sharing MOVES the vehicle with ALL its rows (the app's merge drops rows of a vehicle that is not there, so they cannot be split): more than 2900 records → refused (`fits`). The app shows `union(own, sets)` (house mark on shared vehicle chips, "Shared in …" on the vehicle card); `save` splits each edit back. Mirror `oros-garage-hh`; the shell's reminders, Today, the Calendar feed and Travel's car costs read `withShared(own)`.
- **Notes (`notes/house.js` `OrosNotesHouse.make({merge, canon})`, wave 7f):** document kind `notes`, ONE notebook per document (title = its name). Parts: `n` the notebook, `pg` pages, `l` labels. notes.js owns the merge and the canonical form, so the file is a factory. Records keep their own clocks (`mtime`, `ct`, `st`, `h`): `build` strips the item stamp `m`, so a built notebook is exactly what was sent and the app's merge (conflict copies, NO-3) still decides between two people's versions. Same model as Together (`household/group.js`, parent `notebooks`, children pages + labels, key `nb`, `tomb(list, id)` maps to the Notes tombstone keys `nb:<id>` / `lbl:<id>` / page id). `state` is the union on screen; `pdata` the own data while something is shared, the only thing stored and synced (`sliceGet` = own); `saveNow` splits every save back (`hhSplit`): records that went to a household get own tombstones, and the tombstones of what moved are kept although the union leaves them out. `copyOf` (stop sharing) stamps `mtime` and `st` now and keeps `ct` and `h`, so nothing reads as a second text. A page over 60000 characters cannot travel (whole.js chunks): when a shared page grows past it the household keeps its last version and the long one becomes an own page marked `cf` (no loss, nothing vanishes for the others); a notebook over 480000 characters is refused (`fits`). group.js `union` now also shows an own row of a shared parent that no set holds (written on another own device before the move reached it): the next split sends it. No shell readers: universal search (`notes/search.js`) finds own notebooks only.
- **A household in a shared folder (`household/folder.js` `OrosHouseFolder`, wave 7g):** instead of the relay, a household can live in a WebDAV / Nextcloud folder (membership entry and pending join carry `dav: { url, user, pass, relay }`, `core.cleanDav`). The engine's `call()` hands such a box to `folder.request(dav, method, box, path, o)`, which answers the relay's routes from files: `<folder>/oros-hh-<box>/meta.json` `{ v: 1, epoch }`, `d/<k>.<rev>` (the highest rev counts; a write creates rev+1 with `If-None-Match: *` so two writers of one rev cannot both win, then deletes the old one; leftovers are removed on the next listing), `i/<ih>.json`, `j/<rid>` `{ ih, at, b }`, `a/<rid>` `{ st: 1, b }` or `{ st: 2 }`, `e/<mid>`. `GET` answers `moved` when the folder's epoch is newer than the entry's. Create, invite, approval, removal with key rotation, leaving, delete, a second device: the same engine code (the engine suite runs again against FakeWebDAV, `tests/household-folder.test.js`). No WebSocket and no wakes (`ping` refused): passes on open, focus, online and every 10 minutes. The folder's own sign-in decides who may write; it travels in invite codes `h3.<box>.<I>.<b64u json>` and `h4.<box>.<salt>.<sealed I‖json>` (password); `share/view.js` accepts h1-h4. `probe(dav)` before creating: lists the folder, refuses a server that lets a second `If-None-Match: *` PUT through (`dav-cond`). Through the relay's WebDAV pass-through (`relay/dav.js`, no relay change) when `relay` is ticked. Household app: `#new-where` (address, user, app password, relay), `#hh-folder` line, `#inv-folder` warning.
- **A copy on the person's own disk (`household/backup.js` `OrosHouseBackup`, wave 8, Chris 2026-10-25 «Να είμαστε σίγουροι πως δεν θα χαθεί τίποτα»):** the engine writes one file per household AND device to the orOS disk, `/internal/Household backup/<box>.<dev>.json` (`dev` = device tag, localStorage `oros-household-bkdev`; one writer per file, so the vault never makes conflict copies of it), `{ kind: "oros-household-backup", v: 1, box, name, dev, at, docs: { k: doc } }` (the roster without `i:` items: no invite secrets). Vault Drive takes it to the person's cloud encrypted with their passphrase (FILES-V), so their other devices hold it too. Written only after a pass that reached the box (`status "ok"`), at most every 10 minutes per household (`EVERY_MS`) and on going to the background, and only when the body (`{ v, box, name, docs }`, no time) differs from what this device's file holds (read once): the same content is never written twice. Never written while the box is gone. Read back (`collect`: every file of a box merged with `core.merge`) only when a pass gets 404: the documents join this device's copy (`dirty: false`), so a fresh device shows everything again and "Remove from this device" (private copies) carries all of it. `restart(box, myName?)` (box gone, or only in a backup): a new household (same name, same folder if any, me as admin), every document shared into it (`shareDoc` from the merged copy), the old box's records dropped WITHOUT private copies, the new box's file written, then the old box's files removed; the others join with a new invite. `backups()` lists the files per box (`live`, `gone`); `takeBackup(box)` (not live) puts every document in the archive with `take` (apps adopt private copies, `why: "backup"`); `dropBackup(box)` removes its files. Household app: `#gone-safe` + `#gone-restart` on a gone household; `<details id="bk">` "Copies on your orOS disk" for households no longer here (Bring back to my apps / Start again / Delete).
- Tests: `tests/house-relay.test.js` (relay), `tests/household-core.test.js` (merge laws, crypto), `tests/household-engine.test.js` (several people against the real relay code), `tests/todo-house.test.js`, `tests/calendar-house.test.js`, `tests/split-house.test.js`, `tests/chores-house.test.js`, `tests/plants-house.test.js`, `tests/maps-hh.test.js`, `tests/household-recent.test.js`, `tests/push-relay.test.js` (wakes), `tests/household-whole.test.js`, `tests/meals-house.test.js`, `tests/baby-house.test.js`, `tests/petcare-house.test.js`, `tests/together-house.test.js`, `tests/garage-house.test.js`, `tests/notes-house.test.js`, `tests/household-folder.test.js`, `tests/household-backup.test.js`.

### Travel wave 31 bridges (BR-TRAVEL-MAIL, BR-SPLIT-NEW, Travel → Maps)
- **BR-TRAVEL-MAIL · Mail → Travel.** Mail's "Other apps" dialog shows "Booking to Travel" only when the message's HTML (or text) mentions `schema.org` and `Reservation` and Travel is installed. It calls `__orosOpenAt("travel", { importMail: { subject ≤ 200, html ≤ 1 MB, text ≤ 1 MB (only when there is no HTML) } })`. Mail writes nothing; the hook is isolated in `appsDialog` (`travelBooking`). Travel's receiver (`openSearchTarget` → `importFromMail`) parses with `OrosTravelBooking.parseHtml`, which uses `DOMParser("text/html")`: an inert document, scripts never run, nothing loads; only `script[type=application/ld+json]` text (JSON.parse) and microdata attributes are read. Results open in the review dialog; nothing is added until "Add". The same path serves "Import a booking" in Travel (an .eml through the lazily loaded `mail/mime.js`, an .html file, or pasted HTML).
- **Parser (`travel/booking.js`, `OrosTravelBooking`, UMD, tested in `tests/travel-booking.test.js`).** schema.org Flight / Train / Bus / Boat / Lodging / RentalCar / Taxi / FoodEstablishment / Event and generic Reservation (also `@graph`, arrays and nesting) → entries `{kind, title, from, to, day, t1, day2, t2, place, ref, num, prov, cost, ccur, note, cancelled, key}`. Times are kept as written (local, offset dropped), like the rest of Travel. One entry per flight leg; duplicates by `key` collapse. "Already in the itinerary" (`sameBooking`) = same kind and either the same booking code on the same day, or the same day, time, number, origin and title; those and cancelled ones start unticked.
- **BR-SPLIT-NEW · Travel → Split.** "Share with Split" calls `__orosOpenAt("split", { newGroup: { name, cur, people, from: "travel" } })` (`splitTarget(trip)`); Split opens its new-group dialog prefilled (see SPLIT v1). Shown only when Split is installed (`orosAssistInstalled`, as Mail's `appThere`).
- **Travel → Maps.** Maps takes at most 5 points by URL and has no multi-point API, so the itinerary map is Travel's own read-only Leaflet map (`../vendor/leaflet.js`, loaded on first use; OSM tiles) with numbered stops and straight dashed lines per day. "Save to Maps as a track" hands a GPX (`tripGpx`: waypoints + one `trkseg` per day) to the shell's BR-FILE-OPEN path (`orosFileOpen.open([File])`, the File built with the shell's `File` constructor because the Travel frame is unloaded when Maps opens); Maps imports it into My tracks. Geocoding is Photon (`photon.komoot.io`, as Maps), only on the user's "Find on the map", ≤ 60 lookups, 1 s apart, the destination first to bias the rest; a 3-letter flight code is looked up as "XXX airport". Journal tracks open with `__orosOpenAt("maps", { track: id })`.

## Part VII — UI standards

- **Scrollbars:** 10px, transparent track, pill thumb (999px radius, 2px border `var(--bg)`), hover `var(--accent)`; Firefox `scrollbar-width:thin`. `overscroll-behavior:contain` on main panes.
- **Hidden guard:** `[hidden]{display:none!important}` is the LAST rule of every app stylesheet.
- **Icons:** inline SVG with viewBox + explicit size (Fork Awesome abandoned).
- **Logo and brand (2026-10-31) [log]:** the orOS logo is drawn in the skin gold `#d4af37` (the `oros` skin's dark `--accent`); the older logo gold `#c8a96e` is retired. `icon.svg` is the source; `node tools/brand-icons.js` builds `icons/icon-192/512.png`, `icons/icon-maskable-192/512.png` (full-bleed square, mark at 0.617 inside the 80% safe circle) and `extension/icons/icon-16/32/48/128.png` (16/32 px with a thicker stroke); `node tools/solo-icons.js` builds `icons/solo/`. App stylesheets' fallback `--accent` (before `inheritPalette`) is the same gold. Colours that are data, not brand (Calendar's brown Contacts-feed label `#c8a96e` in `VALID_COLORS`, House/Package colour lists, Pet care and Plants kind colours) stay as they are, because synced records hold them. `DESIGN.md` (repo root) is the short design brief; where it and this Bible differ, the Bible wins.
- **Toasts:** a stack (newest first, max 5 visible, promote on removal). Default bottom-right; the notifications `position` setting moves it live, and bottom positions grow upward. Text first, action second. Undo toasts ≥ 8 s. **[log]**
- **Centered popups (R32) [log]:**
  1. A native `<dialog>` MUST declare `margin: auto`. Every app stylesheet has `* { margin: 0 }`, which kills the UA default and docks the dialog top-left. Recommended: `margin: auto; max-height: calc(100vh - 32px);`.
  2. An overlay panel (not a `<dialog>`) uses `position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` inside a fixed full-inset overlay (`position: fixed; inset: 0`). No inline `style.top` / `style.left` from JS anchor math.
  3. A flex overlay centers with `margin: auto` ON THE PANEL, never with `align-items: center` on the container: a panel taller than the viewport would lose its top to clipping, unreachable by scroll. Reference: Contacts view card (`#ct-view` + `.ct-view-card`).
  4. Long content scrolls inside the popup (`overflow-y: auto` + `max-height`).
  5. Exception: context menus (`#ctx-menu`) stay anchored at the pointer.
- **Z-index ladder [log]:** boot splash 9999 · `#oros-toast-stack` 10000 · inbox panel 10001. Toasts never fall behind the splash.
- **Observers [log]:** a `MutationObserver` watches the element that actually parents the node. A generic `document.body` observer silently never fires for children of another container.
- **Selectors [log]:** never key CSS or JS on localized text (`[title*="remove"]` broke under Greek). Check specificity before adding an override: an id selector beats a class block.
- **Key handling in a frame [log]:** keys reach only the focused browsing context. Numpad keys are matched by `e.code` (with NumLock off, `e.key` is "End", "PageUp"…). Blur a clicked button so Enter/Space do not re-trigger it.
- **NOTIFICATIONS ≠ TOASTS:** cross-session/event reminders → `emit()` (inbox + badge + history); in-context feedback → transient/local toast.
- **Mobile:**
  - single-thumb reach; touch targets ≥44px; safe-area `env()` insets; breakpoints 480/420/360;
  - long-press 450ms as the touch twin of right-click menus (every right-click/Alt-click feature needs a touch path).
  - **Toolbars wider than a phone scroll horizontally** (single strip, hidden scrollbar), never clip.
- **Desktop:** ≥1024px split views allowed.
- **Editor toolbars:** formatting buttons `preventDefault()` on `mousedown` so the editor keeps focus and selection (touch collapsed it).
- **DOM stability:** don't rebuild a container on click when a dblclick may follow (the 2nd click lands on a new node → no dblclick). Update classes in place.
- **Interactive containers:** no `<input>` inside a `<button>`. Use `div[role=tab][tabindex=0]` with Enter/Space/F2 handlers.
- **Find/highlight:** never move the document selection while the user types in a search field (Chrome moves focus → keystrokes overwrite the match). After unwrapping highlight marks, `normalize()` the parents.
- **Autosave:** debounce, no Save buttons for settings; flush on `visibilitychange→hidden` and `pagehide`.
- **Deleting:** danger styling; Undo toast (R17 resurrection) preferred over confirmations.
- **Language:** EN/EL only; EL dates ηη/μμ/εεεε, no comma after the day.
- **Version badge:** shell Info modal only.

## Part VIII — Release pipeline, checklists, test harness

### Pipeline (`.github/workflows/bump-version.yml`) [verified 2026-10-06]

- Triggers: every push to `main` except docs-only pushes (`**.md`), and manual dispatch. A commit whose message contains `[skip ci]` stops at the loop guard (the message is read from an environment variable, never pasted into the script).
- `APP_VERSION` is read from `shell.js` and NEVER written by the workflow (R23).
- One pass, same version string everywhere: `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION = "oros-v<version>"` · `manifest.webmanifest` `"version"` · `?v=<version>` on every relative `href="….css"` and `src="….js"` in the root `index.html` and in `<folder>/index.html` of every folder that has one (`icons`, `fonts`, `vendor` and dot-folders are not scanned; a `../vendor/x.js` reference inside an app page IS stamped).
- NOT stamped: attributes in single quotes, anything loaded from JavaScript (`ioLoadScript`, dynamic `import`), fonts and images, `apps.json`.
- Guards (each fails the job): G1 `CACHE_VERSION` line exists · G2 every app folder registered in `apps.json` appears in `PRECACHE_URLS` (**2026-10-09:** folders merged before their release PR are listed and skipped, so app-only merges no longer fail the job and block stamping) · G4 every internal `apps.json` entry has a folder (a folder without an entry only warns) · G3 every app's scripts contain `inheritPalette` and `watchPalette` · **G5 (2026-10-06)** every root-level `.js` / `.css` that `index.html` loads appears in `PRECACHE_URLS`.
- Commit: `git add -u` (tracked files only: a NEW file must be in the manual commit), message `chore: sync orOS assets to v<version> (auto) [skip ci]`, plain `git push` (it fails if `main` moved meanwhile; the next push re-stamps).
- Between the manual commit and the bot's commit the site may briefly serve the new `shell.js` with the old `CACHE_VERSION` and old stamps. Harmless: no worker update starts until the stamped `sw.js` is live.

### Workflow limits (CI hygiene) [2026-10-27]

- **`timeout-minutes` on every job**, about three times the longest job time of the last runs (queue time not counted): `android.yml` build 45 (8–16 min), `bump-version.yml` bump 10 (≈15 s), `chess-puzzles.yml` pack 20 (1–5 min), `fdroid.yml` publish 15 (10 s–2 min), `sync-nullfx.yml` sync 15 (< 3 min), `tests.yml` sync 15 (≈2 min); `quality.yml` already had apps 30, new-apps 10. A job that grows past its limit gets a new limit in the same PR.
- **`retention-days: 14`** on every `upload-artifact` step (`android.yml` `oros-drive-android`, `oros-android`, `oros-single-apps`; `quality.yml` `qa-report-*`). Nothing downloads these artifacts later: released APKs go through "Publish APKs" and F-Droid, not through artifacts.
- **`tests.yml` concurrency:** group `tests-<ref>`; `cancel-in-progress` only for `pull_request`, so a newer push to a PR cancels the older run and a push to `main` always finishes.
- **Decided NOT to do (Chris 2026-10-27):** no `cache: npm` / `npm ci` (no lockfiles); `quality.yml` new-apps keeps `fetch-depth: 0`; no `cancel-in-progress` in `android.yml` (main publishes android-apks, runs must finish in order).

### Checklist A — Version bump (user-owned)

`APP_VERSION` → push → verify on BOTH devices → changelog (R21) + Bible (R22).

### Checklist B — New app integration

1. `<app>/` folder (index.html + css + js; boot marker; IIFE).
2. `apps.json` entry (icon key; category in the same case as existing ones).
3. `sw.js` `PRECACHE_URLS` (G2), including dynamically loaded assets WITHOUT query strings.
4. `shell.js` ICONS entry (inline SVG, currentColor).
5. `translations.js`: `app.<id>` + category strings (en + el).
6. Self-registration (5-arg `registerSlice`, local-first load, canonical `serialize`).
7. Palette: `inheritPalette` + `watchPalette` (G3).
8. Shortcut forwarding (Contract Β) + `SC_DEFS` entry if the app gets a global shortcut.
9. Notifications: `emit()` + `KNOWN_APPS`/appToggles + `__orosOpen<App>` + `DL_BRIDGES` + staging key — or a documented exemption.
10. File I/O through `orosDialog` (R33); popups centered (R32); if the app goes online, its `sc.info.extsvc.<id>` line in `showInfoModal()` and `translations.js`.
11. Part XII changelog entry + Bible registry, same response.
12. Third-party anything (library, font, icon set, data set, sound, online service): one entry each in `CREDITS.md`, `CREDIT_GROUPS` in `shell.js` (EN+EL) and the Credits register below, same PR. Ship the licence text when the licence asks for it (OFL, Apache NOTICE, MIT notice).
13. Universal search: if the app holds user text, `<app>/search.js` (Part VI "Universal search provider") + `"search": "search.js"` in `apps.json` + precache entry + a `__orosOpenAt` receiver (or `open()` through an existing bridge) + tests. Sensitive data (health, finance, secrets): `"searchOff": true`, so it is opt-in.
14. Guide pages `<app>/help.en.txt` + `help.el.txt` (R38), precached in `sw.js`; remove the id from `PENDING` in `tests/help.test.js` if listed.
15. Direct-link snippet (DL-1, Part II "Direct app links") as the first script in `<app>/index.html`, with the app's own id; `tests/direct-link.test.js` checks it.

### App Kit: community apps (2026-10-17, Chris approved strategy item 11)

Outside contributors build apps through the kit, and every app joins only as code in this repository through a reviewed PR. Nothing loads apps from a URL at run time, so the "no execution of imported code" rule holds. Chris decides what goes in (`CONTRIBUTING.md`).
- `docs/app-kit/README.md` (quick start) + `docs/app-kit/contract.md`: this Checklist B, written for someone who has not read the Bible, one chapter per rule with the check that enforces it. **Any change to Checklist B updates `contract.md` in the same PR.** `tests/app-kit.test.js` fails when a Checklist B step has no `Checklist B <n>` chapter.
- `docs/app-kit/template/`: a small synced list app (`core.js` pure model with a symmetric merge and tombstones, `app.js`, `search.js`, help EN/EL, `myapp.test.js`). It is not served or precached, and the stamp/guard scan sees root folders only.
- `node .github/app-kit/new-app.js <id> "<EN>" "<EL>"` copies the template to `<id>/` + `tests/<id>.test.js`. It prints the `apps.json` / `sw.js` / `ICONS` / `translations.js` lines and never writes the shared files.
- `node .github/app-kit/check-app.js <id> [--no-tests] [--no-browser]` runs:
  - static checks: registration, precache of everything the page loads, DL-1, G3, R38 outline, 5-argument `registerSlice`, a read-only search provider, no `eval` / `new Function` / remote code, no Google host outside `GOOGLE_APPROVED` (the approved one-time imports, Gemini, Mail look-alikes);
  - `stamp-assets.js` with `OROS_CHECK=1`;
  - the help, direct-link, i18n, release-guards, deeplink-receivers, search* and `tests/<id>*` tests;
  - the quality gate `.github/qa/smoke.js --only <id>` when Playwright is installed.
  Every app on main passes the static part (tested).
- K2: `quality.yml` job `new-apps` runs `check-app.js --added-since origin/<base> --no-browser` on every PR. It checks each root app folder the PR adds that is registered or carries the DL-1 snippet, so a forgotten registration fails; standalone pages are skipped. The `apps` shards open the new app in Chromium, strict because it has no baseline. `--added-since` with no new app exits 0.
- Contributor PRs never touch `APP_VERSION`, the changelog or `CACHE_VERSION`. The maintainer adds them at merge, through the merge queue as usual.
