### Time › Stage decisions (2026-10-13, 1.49.00)
- Stage runs in its own slice so the audited `time` slice (TM-1/TM-2) is not touched.
- The merge does not cascade an event's deletion to its items (that broke associativity in the fuzz). The page tombstones every item when it deletes an event; an item edited on another device after that is kept as data and not shown.
- The live clock is device-local and computed from timestamps, so closing Time and opening it again resumes at the right time.
- Waves 2-4 (second window + messages, paired devices via the Studio Remote rooms, imports/reports/templates) follow per the plan.
- **Wave 2 (1.52.00):**
  - The display window reads storage instead of receiving messages, so it survives Time being closed, a reload, or another app being opened. Auto-advance and sounds still need Time open.
  - A message the operator is typing never reaches the stage. While one is shown, the button shows the new text rather than hiding.
  - A wave-1 device that pulls saved messages drops them on its copy until it updates. That is accepted (same as Studio fx). With no saved messages both versions write the same bytes.
- **Wave 3 (1.54.00):**
  - **Shared link module.** The link layer moved into a shared root module (`remote-link.js`) instead of being copied. A namespace keeps each app's rooms and keys apart. With the default namespace the module stays wire-compatible with Studio, so Studio can switch to it later.
  - **One room per device.** A relay room holds two sockets, so no relay change was needed.
  - **The PC stays where things happen.**
    - Every device command goes through `devCommand` (checked by role), then through the same actions as the PC's buttons.
    - A display only listens; a moderator can only ask.
    - Typed text is capped and drawn as text.
  - **Clock.** The device computes the clock from the PC's start instant plus the measured offset, so a slow link never makes the stage clock jump.
  - **Logo and notes.** The logo stays on the PC (it does not fit a frame). Private notes are never sent.
- **Wave 4 (1.56.00, plan complete):**
  - **Import only adds.** An import or a quick add goes to the end of the open event and never replaces items, so a wrong file can be undone by deleting the new items. Every value is parsed as data and drawn as text.
  - **Calendar gaps become breaks of a fixed length.** They are not "until" breaks, because the plan may land after other items at another hour.
  - **The report is per device.** The actual times are the device-local run log of the computer that ran the clock. Nothing new is synced for it.
  - **Prompter link dropped.** orOS has no teleprompter, so this item from the plan has no target.
  - **Search and Today.** time → time/search.js. It reads oros-time-stage and finds Stage events and rundown items. Opening a hit goes to the Stage tab on that event and item. Today: time → ["stage-core.js", "today.js"]. Shows alarms later today, plus on an event's day the next Stage session at its expected start, and Stage events on the coming days at their start.

### Time wave 5 decisions (world clock, meeting planner, timers, stopwatch)
- **Cities are own data.** `time/cities.js` holds about 550 cities as "English|Greek|zone|country" (no third-party list). `time/clock-core.js` (UMD `OrosClockCore`, tested in `tests/time-clock.test.js`) searches them with accents and case folded, then any zone from `Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")` (fallback: the zones of the city list). Chromium lists legacy ids (`Asia/Calcutta`, `America/Jujuy`); a city keeps its own id, both work.
- **A world-clock row is still one zone.** The synced entity stays `{tz, mtime}`; picking a city adds `city` (English name, ≤ 60 chars). Picking another city in a zone already listed renames the row (new mtime). A zone without a city keeps its exact pre-wave-5 bytes. A pre-wave-5 device drops `city` until it updates (accepted, as Stage wave 2); at equal mtime the merge prefers the version with a city, so the result is the same on every device.
- **Meeting planner is device-local.** Column i = local midnight of the chosen date in the FIRST place + i hours, so every row shows the same instant. Working hours are one setting for all places, Monday to Friday; 07–22 counts as awake. "Add to Calendar" uses the existing prefill bridge `__orosOpenCalendarNew({date, title, start, end, dateEnd?, note})` in this device's time; nothing is written until the user saves in Calendar.
- **Kitchen timers ride the alarm engine.** A running timer owns one shell alarm with id `tmr-<timer>-<n>`, so the shell rings it with Time closed and the Android app gets it as a reminder row (phone.js reads `oros-alarms`; its link is `time:timer`). The shell keeps `tmr-` alarms out of the `shell` slice (`alarmsCanonical` skips them, a pull keeps the local ones, `remove` writes no tombstone): a kitchen timer rings only on the device that started it. Pause / +1 min / rename re-register the alarm. The Time page and Today hide `tmr-` alarms.
- **Per-timer sound in the shell.** `alarmNotify` looks the voice up in `oros-time-timers` by alarm id (`alarmSoundOf`); five WebAudio voices (`ALARM_SOUNDS`), "beep" = the old three pips, every other alarm unchanged. `window.orosAlarmSound(name)` plays a preview for Time's pickers. The Android app rings with the phone's alarm sound.
- **Overlay only for timers of 2 minutes or more.** The fullscreen last-minute countdown would otherwise open as soon as a 1-minute timer starts; it follows the soonest such timer.
- **Stopwatch survives closing.** `{run, start, base, laps}` from the wall clock; laps export as text (clipboard) and CSV (`orosDialog.saveFile`, fallback download), with a final "rest" lap when stopped after the last lap.
- **phone.js:** reminders are also pushed when orOS goes to the background, so a timer started in the last 15 seconds reaches the Android app.
- **Wave 50: chess training and games on two devices.**
  - **Puzzle source.** The Lichess puzzle database (CC0) was the plan, but database.lichess.org is blocked from the build environment (403 by the egress policy). The first pack (`chess/puzzles-pack.js`, about 200) is original: positions from the orOS engine's own games where one move or one forced line wins, checked for legality and that every mate theme ends in mate. The loader (`train.js parsePack`) reads the Lichess CSV layout (10 columns) and a short form (`id,fen,moves,rating,themes`), so a pack cut from the Lichess file drops in as another `OrosChessPacks` entry. Packs are plain data, never code paths.
  - **Lichess puzzle pack (wave 50b).** `chess/puzzles-lichess.js` (`OrosChessPacks` entry `lichess-1`, name `Lichess`, five columns, Lichess ids kept) is cut from the Lichess puzzle database (CC0, https://database.lichess.org/#puzzles) by `chess/tools/lichess-pack.js` (Node 22 built-ins, streams the CSV with readline; not shipped to the browser). The build container cannot reach database.lichess.org, so `.github/workflows/chess-puzzles.yml` runs it on GitHub's runners (manual, or a push to `claude/**` that touches the generator or the workflow), downloads `lichess_db_puzzle.csv.zst`, and commits the pack to the same branch as github-actions[bot] only when it changed (the date line is ignored when comparing). The commit touches only the pack, outside the workflow's paths, so it cannot trigger itself; no `[skip ci]`. Selection: RatingDeviation < 90, Popularity ≥ 85, NbPlays ≥ 1000, the row must pass `train.js parseLine` and end with the solver's move; six rating bands (400–800, 800–1200, 1200–1600, 1600–2000, 2000–2400, 2400+), 500 each; in each band every theme the trainer names (the `th.*` strings, minus the length labels; a test keeps the generator's list equal to them) first gets up to 8 puzzles by round robin, then the band fills. "First" = smallest FNV-1a hash of the PuzzleId (ties by id), so the same database gives the same pack and puzzles keep their ids (and history entries) across re-generations; the database's monthly updates can still swap a few. Until the workflow has run, the file is a comment-only placeholder that pushes nothing. The trainer loads both packs on first use (`TR_PACK_FILES`) and merges them into one list (first id wins; the ids never clash: Lichess ids are 5 characters, orOS ids `or####`); a missing Lichess file (an old cache) just leaves the orOS pack. No pack chooser: the Theme list and the rating pick work over both. The note under the buttons counts each source (`tr.packSrc`). No link to lichess.org/training is shown (the trainer had none).
  - **Puzzle rules.** Lichess conventions: the FEN is before the opponent's move, the first move is the opponent's; any mate is accepted as the last move. Only the first attempt rates; a wrong move is refused (the board never takes it) and you may keep trying; `Solution` counts as failed.
  - **Openings.** The Lichess chess-openings TSVs (CC0) are compacted into `chess/openings-data.js` (families listed once, each line as its parent line + extra moves). Names are looked up by position (placement, side, castling; no en passant), the deepest named position on the game's path wins, so transpositions get the right name. No name during a live Lichess game (fair play).
  - **Two devices (`remote-play.js`).** One shared module for pairing (Show a code / Enter a code / QR / Allow), the badge, reconnect after a reload (24 h) and leaving (`_bye`); no relay change, each game uses its own namespace `oros-<app>-play`. Message types are short lower-case strings (`okMsg`); the meaning and the checks are the game's. Connect 4, Backgammon and Xeri: the host keeps the game and sends the guest a picture after every change, the guest sends intents that the host checks like its own moves (Backgammon and Xeri number the pictures, stale intents are dropped). Xeri's picture carries the guest's own hand and only counts of the host's hand and the deck. Battleship is symmetric: each fleet stays on its own device, a shot is answered by the device shot at (a ship is named only when sunk), the shooter checks each answer (`netResIn`), and at the end the fleets cross and are checked against every answer (`netFleetCheck`); a mismatch is shown, not hidden. Games on two devices never touch the records or the synced slices.

### Encrypted backup files decisions (2026-10-31, BK-E)
- **Optional, off by default** (Chris, 2026-10-31, improvement round item 5: "Ναι, προεπιλογή όχι"). Settings › Backups › `Encrypt backup files`; the switch, the passphrase dialog and the import prompt live in the shell (`shell.js` 5d', `#bkpw-dialog`).
- **Format:** `{ "format": "oros-backup", "v": 1, "enc": { it, s, iv, ct } }` (written compact, `format` first, so `orosSync.backupSealed` only parses text that starts like one). AES-256-GCM; key = PBKDF2-SHA-256 of the passphrase, 16-byte salt `s`, `it` rounds (600 000 for new keys, a file is refused outside 100 000 … 5 000 000); `ct` = the plain backup file's text; every file a fresh 96-bit IV. Code in `sync.js` (`backupKey`, `sealBackup`, `backupSealed`, `openBackup`), next to the vault crypto it mirrors.
- **The passphrase is never stored.** It is asked once (at least 10 characters, `MIN_PASS_LEN`, like the sync passphrase), the derived key is kept non-extractable in IndexedDB `oros-fs` / `handles` / `backup-key` (`{ key, s, it }`), so scheduled folder backups seal without asking. One salt per key. `Change passphrase` makes a new key for the next files; older files keep theirs.
- **Device-local.** `oros-backup-enc` = "1" and the key never travel (a key cannot be synced); each device turns it on. Settings scope `backupenc: "device"`. The factory reset removes both (`oros-*` sweep, `oros-fs` database).
- **On without a key writes nothing.** Site data cleared → Settings shows `b.enc.lost` + `Set passphrase`; export and folder backups stop with `sync.err.backupkey` instead of falling back to a plain file. The folder schedule stamp is kept (no retry storm on every tab-visible).
- **Import:** a sealed file opens the passphrase dialog; a wrong passphrase or a changed file (GCM) keeps the dialog open with `sync.err.backuppass` and imports nothing; plain files (every file before BK-E) import as before. Off makes plain files again.

### Users on one device decisions (2026-11-01, US)

- **Profile per user, not data per user inside orOS.** A browser profile per user keeps every app, sync and storage path unchanged and cannot leak one user's IndexedDB/OPFS into another; the cost is that it works only where orOS controls the browser (Portable, Live USB). Web, PWA and Android show an explanation card.
- **Owner recovery = a recovery code, not the sync passphrase.** Each user may have a different sync (or none), so the launcher has no passphrase to check against; a one-time code (base32, 4 groups of 5) shown at set-up and on request is checked by hash. Chris was told of this change from the plan.
- **No auto sign-out, one user at a time, ≤ 8 users, guest off by default** (Chris, plan questions 1-8, all recommendations approved).
- **U4 per-user encryption = fscrypt, optional, off by default** (Chris 2026-11-01). fscrypt rather than a LUKS file per user: no root at sign-in (a non-root user adds and removes their own v2 key), no fixed-size container, and it sits beside the existing whole-stick LUKS. The vault lives outside the `/home union` overlay because fscrypt does not work through overlayfs; the ext4 `encrypt` feature cannot be set on a mounted file system (a mounted fs writes its old superblock back on unmount), hence the initramfs step. Not for the first user (their profile is the data folder itself and their home is `/home/oros`; the start passphrase covers them). The owner cannot reset an encrypted user's password (that would need the key); each encrypted user gets their own recovery code instead.

### Audit queue (assistant-raised; verify, then fix)

- **A1 · `__orosNotify` sweep (HIGH).**
  - The previous Bible's canonical notification trigger called `window.parent.__orosNotify.emit`, which does not exist in shell.js or notifications.js (0.38.12).
  - Any app that copied that template emits nothing and silently falls back to legacy alerts.

- **A65 · Mail — CLOSED 2026-10-08 (0.46.00):** the app was rewritten from zero, so every point is answered: (a) relay chosen; (b) the slice carries account settings only; (c) passwords sealed in IndexedDB; (d) `mail/index.html`; (e) `inheritPalette` + `watchPalette`; (f) `orosNotifs.transient`; (g) live registration with `mergeMail`; (h)–(i) no such rule, no Ctrl+Alt shortcut; (j) integrated. Original text kept below for the record.
- **A65 (original) · Mail, before anything else is built on it** (from the Wave 0 note of another session and the shell delta; `mail/` files not on the table).
  - **(a) The plan itself.** A browser page cannot open IMAP, POP3 or SMTP connections: there is no socket API for web pages, only HTTP(S) and WebSocket to servers that allow it. "Wave 1: IMAP polling (TLS), SMTP sending" cannot be written as a static app. What exists: a provider's HTTP API (JMAP where offered; Gmail API / Microsoft Graph with an OAuth client registration), or a relay / bridge server. Each is an external dependency or a backend, i.e. a Mantra decision ("No external dependencies", "static") for the owner BEFORE Wave 1.
  - **(b) What is synced.** The note says the slice carries "account config only"; the comment in `shell.js` says "account config + message metadata/content". Message bodies in `oros-mail-data` would sit in localStorage (shared 5 MB, R30) and ride every push of the blob.
  - **(c) Passwords** in localStorage (`oros-mail-creds`) are readable by any script of the origin (Part V: an XSS in any app reaches everything). At least seal them with the device key that `sync.js` already keeps in IndexedDB.
  - **(d) File layout.** The note names `mail.html`, `mail.css`, `mail.js`; the pipeline expects `mail/index.html` (stamping scans `<dir>/index.html`, G2 and G4 key on the folder).
  - **(e) Palette.** The note lists `--accent`, `--surface`, `--text`; there is no `--surface` among the 11 palette variables (Part II, `style.css`). G3 needs `inheritPalette` + `watchPalette`.
  - **(f) Toasts.** "Unified toast notifications (2.6s)" reads like the app's own toast; the rule is `orosNotifs.transient` with a local fallback only when standalone (R12 / Part VI), Undo ≥ 8 s.
  - **(g) Slice.** The live registration in `mail.js` must pass the storage key and a symmetric `mergeFn` (A40, the three slice rules in Part VI); the proxy alone is mergeless.
  - **(h) "All dialogs close on outside click (certified orOS standard)"** is not a rule of this file. The dialog rules are R32 (centred) and R33 (file dialogs).
  - **(i) Shortcut** Ctrl+Alt+N: Ctrl+Alt is AltGr on many Windows layouts (same caveat as Writer's Ctrl+Alt+W/T).
  - **(j) Pending integration** listed by the note: `apps.json`, `app.mail` in `translations.js` (app strings stay inline in the app), `sw.js` precache, `KNOWN_APPS`. "Update GitHub Action: propagate version to precache URLs" is NOT needed (the precache is unversioned by design, SW-D1).

### Lessons — closed incidents (do not re-chase)

**Kernel / earlier:**

- Duplicate seeds on a new device (Notes/To-Do/Kanban) → R16.
- Calendar feed blackout on a new device → feed cache invalidation in `setFromSync()`.
- Contacts wipe → empty-blob guard in `collectPayload()`; recovered from .vcf.
- `window.t is not a function` → transient partial-bundle boot; TP-guards make it non-fatal.
- "Banner not shown: beforeinstallprompt preventDefault()" → expected (menu Install button keeps `deferredPrompt`).
- Kanban legacy board mumfy266amf80 → pre-patch duplicate; manual delete propagates the tombstone.
- Radio FIX-RX: `applyMediaSession` undefined; honest catalog banner; a dead `state.offline` flag poisoned API calls.
- Diagnostic gotcha: `[id*="sync-dot"]` matched the parent button, not `#sync-dot`.

**Sessions 2026-10-02 → 10-05 [log]** (each now a rule, pattern or audit item):

- **Toast stack:** five self-inflicted bugs caught in review: observer on the wrong parent, a rAF opacity flip that undid the limit, z-index tie with the splash, a dead double mount, no promotion on removal (Part VII).
- **Toast position:** a setting that was read and never applied; its 8-position map was dead code.
- **Weather "Athens — waiting…":** two separate causes: the throttle stamped before the fetch, and a stale app cache adopted over a fresh tray cache.
- **Radio tray chip:** the host object stayed in the iframe closure; the shell polls its own window.
- **Calculator keys:** iframe focus; `e.key` on the numpad with NumLock off; a focused button re-triggered by Enter.
- **Bookmarks CSS:** a selector on localized title text; a class block dead against an id selector; `.item.open-btn` matching nothing.
- **Contacts:** one document listener per render; custom events lost on vCard re-import; a view card clipped by `align-items`.
- **`translations.js`:** a "duplicate key" cleanup removed the primary definition (`notifs.on`). Diff the key sets after any key removal.
- **`fs.js`:** renaming public methods broke every Files consumer (R35).
- **Files:** `readAsText` strips the BOM (pass the `File` through); stat before read for previews.
- **Television:** one missing comma in the EL `STRINGS` pack stopped the whole file. `node --check` + key parity before every delivery (Checklist D).
- **`storage-adapters.js`:** two OAuth redirect handlers raced for one one-shot code (R34).
- **Vault "409":** a false alarm that hid two real bugs: a conditional write that was never conditional (rev always `null`), and a queue cleared before the write landed.
- **`todo.js` prompt injection:** treated as data (Part 0, A12).
- **Computed-key literal in a patch draft** (R37).
- **A release without a version step is not a release.** With an unchanged `APP_VERSION` the workflow writes the same `?v=` and the same cache name; the worker then answers every script from its cache. Old code keeps running, and files that were never cached arrive new: a mix. The version step is part of the delivery, not an afterthought.
- **"On error take the other side" is a data-loss path** (`applySlice`, SY-D6). A fallback must keep both sides, never choose one.
- **Comparing two orders through their serialized text** let an empty list outrank a full one, and the merged order was not stable when the same data met again. Compare sequences as sequences; make the result an extension of the winner.
- **"Undo wins, stamp everything newest" (To-Do):** restoring a whole-database snapshot and marking all of it newest made one undone deletion override every edit other devices had not synced yet. An undo is a new small edit: put back what was removed, stamp only that.
- **A dialog that copies all its fields back** before checking what changed reverts whatever arrived while it was open. Read once at open, write back only the differences.
- **Insertion order inside an object is part of its serialization:** two devices held the same tombstones in different key order, so their states never compared equal and both uploaded on every cycle (4 uploads per round, measured). Sort keys in the canonical form.
- **The delivered file must be the tested file (2026-10-07).** Between two messages the working folder held a different, unreviewed build of `notes.js` and `sync.js` than the one that had been tested and described. Before every delivery: compare the files in the output folder with the tested build (byte comparison, plus a search for the function names the changelog entry cites), and rerun the suite on exactly those bytes.
- **"Leave the field alone while it has focus" (Notes):** written to protect the caret, it also kept a stale text on screen after a pull; one keystroke then saved the old text over the new one. Protect the caret, not the value.
- **One clock for a whole object:** the later change wins EVERYTHING, so a pin reverted typed text and typed text reverted a pin. Content and structure need their own clocks when an object carries a long text.
- **Two edits of the same text are not "older" and "newer":** unless the newer one was written on top of the older one, both are kept. Ancestry is recorded once per sync round, not per keystroke.
- **A fix that was written and never called** (`defaultData()` for the v0.36.00 "deterministic seed"): the comment said fixed, the code said random. Dead-function scan on every file (Checklist D) would have shown it.
- **Functions of a closed iframe keep running** when someone still holds them. The sync engine did, for every app opened once in the session.
- **The appendix came back (0.39.13).** Another session pasted a raw "Wave 0 (Mail Skeleton)" changelog below Part XII, in its own format, with a version line, a rule this file does not contain, and a to-do list for the pipeline that contradicts it. It also worked from a copy one delivery behind. Every session starts from the CURRENT Bible and files, reads Parts 0, I and X, and writes its entry inside Part XII in the R21 format.
- **Two sessions, one file:** when files come back changed, diff them against the last delivery first. The uploaded `shell.js` differed from the previous delivery by exactly 2 removed and 33 added lines (the Mail work); everything else was a missing delivery, not a change.
- **Hook the layer everyone goes through.** The Files app had eight hand-placed vault hooks, all dead, none covering folder operations, file creation or the editor. One notification inside `fs.js` covers every caller, present and future.
- **A module that writes to the disk it watches** must be able to recognise its own writes, per path, or it uploads what it has just downloaded.
- **A snapshot is not a diff (Files, 2026-10-06):** "this device has nothing pending" was taken to mean "this device has nothing the incoming snapshot lacks". With two devices each adding a file before syncing, the engine's rule 2 pushed one disk over the other and the receiving device wiped its own new file, toast "Disk restored from cloud". A whole-state snapshot may be merged automatically; it may replace only when the user says so.
- **A timestamp inside the compared value** (`ts` in the disk snapshot): every refresh looked like a change, so applying a remote disk produced a push, which produced an apply on the other device, forever. Compare content, never envelopes.
- **`window.X` inside an app frame is not the shell's `X`.** The vault hooks tested `window.orosVault` in the iframe and silently never ran. Shell APIs are `window.parent.X`.
- **`#id { display: flex }` beats the `hidden` attribute:** "This folder is empty" stayed on screen under a full list. Every stylesheet ends with the `[hidden]` guard.
- **`* { margin: 0 }` un-centres every native dialog.** Known for apps (R32), missed in the shell itself because the shell was always tested with a stub stylesheet.
- **A key cached in memory outlived its file (`vault.js`, found by the suite):** after the cloud vault was wiped, a device re-uploaded everything sealed with a key whose `key.json` no longer existed. Whenever the index is gone, re-establish the key first.
- **A default object stamped "now" (`pet.js`, like the shell slice):** every fresh device created a random pet with the newest timestamp, and "newest wins" replaced the user's real pet everywhere. A default that nobody chose carries stamp 0.
- **Three shapes for one slice (`pet.js` settings):** getter without `ver`, merge with it, setter without it. The value could never equal itself, so every sync cycle applied "1 section" and uploaded. One canonical builder per slice, used by getter, setter and merge.
- **A refresh that overwrote an input every second (`pet.js` rename):** the HUD repaint replaced the name element while the user typed in it.
- **Absence read as deletion (`vault.js`):** "the manifest is not there" was treated like "the manifest lists no files", and a path missing from the manifest is a remote deletion. Three roads led there: a one-minute "absent" cache used after the device's own first upload, a wiped or different cloud, and two devices creating the first manifest together. In all three the device deleted its own files. Absence of the index is never information about the entries.
- **A queue without generations** drops whatever was added while it was being processed.
- **An API that rejects where the caller expects `null`** (`FS().read` of a missing file): the first deletion stopped every later sync. Seen at once when the real `fs.js` and the real `vault.js` ran together.
- **`if (e.code) return e`** (`fs.js`): written for our own string codes, it also matched every DOMException with a legacy numeric code, so on OPFS no error was ever mapped: a fresh disk THREW on `ls` and on export, and the two drivers reported different codes for the same thing. Found only by running the same script against both drivers and comparing the two outputs field by field.
- **A capability that exists is not a capability that works** (`fs.js`): Safari exposes OPFS without the write method the page needs. Detect the method you call.
- **Choosing a storage backend again at every boot** makes data vanish when the answer changes. Pin the first decision.
- **Revoking a blob URL after one second** (`dialogs.js`): fine on a fast desktop, a failed download wherever the browser asks before it starts. Measured: the URL was dead 2 s after the click; now it lives 40 s.
- **A commit message pasted into a shell script** (workflow loop guard): one unbalanced quote would have failed the job and shipped a release that no device ever picks up. Workflow inputs go through `env:`.
- **Offline emulation does not reach the worker (2026-10-06):** the browser context's "offline" switch left Service Worker fetches online; the first "offline" run of the worker tests proved nothing. Stop the HTTP server for real offline.
- **A fallback that loaded the shell inside an app frame** (SWK-3): a navigation fallback must look at `request.destination`.
- **Network-first without a timeout (2026-10-11):** on a bad connection (online, but nothing arrives) a fetch only fails after minutes, so the "offline fallback" never ran and the installed app did not open. A fallback that waits for a failure is no fallback on a slow link; it needs a clock. Reproduce with a server that accepts and never answers; the browser's offline switch does not show it.
- **`lastIndexOf(x) === s.length - x.length`** is true whenever `s` is one character shorter than `x` (both sides are -1). Use an explicit `at >= 0` check.
- **A string that existed and a modal that never used it** (`maps.providers`, A29): check both directions, "used but undefined" and "defined but unused".
- **A merge that never ran (2026-10-06):** `notifications.js` registered its slice with three arguments and merged inside the setter. The engine treated it as mergeless, its getter leaked a per-minute stamp, so the slice was "always changed": every cycle on every device uploaded the whole blob, and inboxes, read states and settings never converged. Nobody saw it because each device kept working alone.
- **The first fuzz of `notifMerge` failed on impossible data** (one id under two dedupe keys). The fix was a simpler identity rule (one key per item), not a cleverer closure; the generator now produces only shapes the code can create.
- **Fuzz found what the scenarios did not (2026-10-06):** the tombstone union was order-dependent (an expired tombstone lent its stamp to a live one). 451 of 20,000 triples failed associativity; fixed by expiring per side before the union. A merge function ships only with the fuzz.
- **A test that "failed" because the code was right:** `applyLang()` repaints the clock, the clock tick fired the due alarm inside the apply. Read the effect, not only the storage.
- **"Local with unpushed work wins" has no notion of a fresh device (found 2026-10-05):** a mergeless slice that is never null and has no baseline beats the cloud. Every always-present slice needs a `mergeFn`.
- **An unconditional overwrite is a lost update waiting for two devices** (A36). The kernel's two-device harness must include "B pushes without pulling".
- **A dirty flag that nothing can clear** made the close warning permanent for everyone without Dropbox.
- **Boot order (found 2026-10-05):** the reminder engines ran from the first `renderClock()` while `notifications.js` did not exist yet. A reminder due at boot used the legacy overlay; four "first sweep" timers were dead from the day they were written. Seen only by running the real file with the real script order.
- **`renderMenu` rebuilds on background events:** scroll, an open `<details>` and a half-typed passphrase were lost. The form-rebuild pattern (Part VI) applies to the shell too.
- **Escape handled twice:** a dialog closed AND the app behind it closed.
- **Process:**
  - Raw notes pasted below Part XII and deltas pasted up to four times instead of being applied (Part 0: no appendix).
  - A note suggested a `shell.js` version number (R23 deviation; not carried).
  - A note cited "OROS_BIBLE.md — Section XI" for the file-dialog rule; Part XI is the handoff template. Cite rule numbers, not sections.
  - `$("…")` pairs in chat text were rendered as math and arrived garbled: wrap selectors and code in backticks in every changelog line.

**Writer audit 2026-10-01** (each now a rule or pattern):

- **Never synced, from day one:**
  - `window.orosSync` read inside the iframe → Writer was absent from cloud sync, DB export and snapshots (R8).
  - Fixing only that would have pushed an empty slice, because live registration does not hydrate (local-first pattern).
- **Sync ping-pong:** a device-local `tabOrder` and unsorted docs inside the slice → two devices pushed forever (R26).
- **Silent no-ops:** five doc dialogs did nothing with no open tab (R28).
- **Data loss:**
  - deleting a comment removed the commented TEXT (unwrap instead);
  - text typed with no tab, or within 500ms before "+", was discarded;
  - version restore was a no-op (debounce re-read the old editor);
  - flush-stamped mtime let stale copies win (R27).
- **Find typing overwrote matches:** selection moved into the editor (Part VII).
- **Quick Format "every other time":** stale `{once}` listeners (AbortController pattern).
- **Tab rename never worked:** DOM rebuilt between the two clicks.
- **RTF import always empty:** a 34-char look-ahead at the root `{` skipped the whole document.
- **XSS:** MD attribute breakout + unsanitized `.orosdoc`/`.json` imports (inert sanitizer).
- **Exports:**
  - Chrome `<div>` lines split into paragraphs and lost formatting (normalize to `<p>`);
  - indented lists (`ul > ul`) dropped;
  - RTF `\pard` without `\plain` leaked bold.
- **Offline:** dynamic vendor loads with `?t=` cache-busters missed the precache.
- **Quota:** raw data-URL photos could exceed the shared quota while `localPersist` swallowed the error (R30).

## Part X-B — Troubleshooting (known symptoms → cause → fix)

Started 2026-10-15 (Chris: "note similar issues in the Bible for future troubleshooting"), collected from the project threads, team memory and Part XII. Each entry: **Symptom** (what the person sees) / **Cause** ("inferred" when not proven) / **Fix or workaround** / **Ref** (PR, version, date or source). **Rule:** when a reported problem is solved, add or update its entry here in the same PR as the fix; check this Part first when someone reports a problem.

### T1. Android install: TWA, WebAPK, APK

**Symptom:** Install buttons on Android (in the APK or on the web) only open the app inside orOS. **Cause:** the TWA / installed orOS captures same-origin links. **Fix:** `installUrl()` sends an intent to Chrome; solo.html shows an install bar (beforeinstallprompt). **Ref:** #354, 2.09.00, 2026-10-14.

**Symptom:** Install from inside the orOS APK does nothing; the same link in a browser works. **Cause:** a Chrome intent fired from the TWA comes back to the TWA. **Fix:** PermissionActivity host `install` opens the default browser (needs the new APK). Chrome, Edge, Brave and Samsung install; Firefox only offers Add to Home screen. **Ref:** #371, 2.21.02.

**Symptom:** Download-page tiles open the app without an install prompt. **Cause:** links open inside the installed orOS (display-mode standalone). **Fix:** install-bar message plus "Open in Chrome". **Ref:** #382, 2.25.02.

**Symptom:** In Brave, download-page tiles do nothing. **Cause:** Brave ignores a Chrome intent from a plain tab. **Fix:** in a plain tab (`inTab`) open `?install` in the same browser. **Ref:** #384, 2.25.04.

**Symptom:** The download page opens inside the installed orOS (Chrome WebAPK) and the tiles are dead. **Cause:** an intent from the WebAPK loops back into it. **Fix:** a notice plus Copy link; in an app window, tiles use the plain address. **Ref:** #385, 2.25.05.

**Symptom:** APK links open the GitHub app and never finish. **Cause:** GitHub release links are captured by the GitHub app. **Fix:** intent to the same browser package (Brave via `navigator.brave`, Edge `EdgA/`, Samsung, Chrome); Firefox keeps a plain link. **Ref:** #385, 2.25.05.

**Symptom:** Single apps cannot be installed from the browser; a fresh Chrome tab gives no install prompt. **Cause:** the orOS WebAPK has scope "/" and claims every useoros.online page (inferred). **Fix:** ship APKs for all 34 single apps on the `android-apks` release. **Ref:** #387, 2.25.07.

**Symptom:** APK download from an installed app's in-app tab (Brave) stops at 100%; the direct link in a normal browser tab works in every browser. **Cause:** unclear. The bytes do arrive; suspected hidden "dangerous file" confirmation or VPN (inferred). **Fix:** `solo.apkHref(id, ua, inWindow)` sends an intent to Chrome with a GitHub fallback. Workaround: ⋮ › Downloads › Keep, or "Open in Brave". **Ref:** #389, 2.26.00, 2026-10-15. Follow-up 2.30.01: in the orOS app and the single-app APKs the links go through `BrowserActivity` (default browser, normal tab); the menu's Get orOS too (its `window.open` inside the TWA also force-closed the app; likely cause, unconfirmed: the browser hands the in-scope link back to the app, a second LauncherActivity starts, PhoneBridge.attach → `reallyDestroy()` of the first launcher → `unbindService` throws "Service not registered" on the main thread; phone thread hardens `reallyDestroy` with try/catch).

**Symptom:** APK section of the download page returns 404. **Cause:** the links go live only after the first main-branch Android build after #380. **Fix:** wait for (or dispatch) that build. **Ref:** #380, 2.25.01, 2026-10-15.

**Symptom:** A Play install and a sideloaded APK don't update each other. **Cause:** they are signed with different keys (Play App Signing vs our keystore). **Fix:** uninstall, then install the other build; sync restores the data. TODO: mark Play builds so they skip the F-Droid notice. **Ref:** oros-store-packaging memory.

**Symptom:** The TWA shows a browser address bar. **Cause:** assetlinks.json is not live yet, the Play App Signing SHA-256 is missing, or Pages hid `.well-known` (no `.nojekyll`). **Fix:** publish assetlinks with both fingerprints and `.nojekyll`. If the bar persists, uninstall and reinstall. **Ref:** #215, 1.12.01, 2026-10-12.

**Symptom:** Play Console rejects the upload. **Cause:** Play wants an AAB, not an APK. **Fix:** upload the AAB from the PWABuilder zip, and keep `signing.keystore` safe (every update needs it). **Ref:** 2026-10-12, oros-store-packaging.

**Symptom:** New share targets or file types (.fb2/.cbz, pictures) don't appear in the Android app. **Cause:** the TWA package was built from the old manifest (before #195). **Fix:** regenerate the package after any manifest change. **Ref:** #195.

**Symptom:** Splash logo is too big and runs off screen. **Cause:** missing high-density splash asset (inferred). **Fix:** add a drawable-xxxhdpi splash. **Ref:** 2026-10-13.

**Symptom:** Users can't download the APK from GitHub Actions. **Cause:** Actions artifacts need a GitHub login and expire after 14 days. **Fix:** publish to the `android-apks` release, which has fixed public URLs. **Ref:** #380.

**Symptom:** PowerShell `[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("signing.keystore")` can't find a file that is in the current folder. **Cause:** .NET resolves against the process working directory, not the PowerShell location. **Fix:** `[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path ".\signing.keystore"))`. **Ref:** 2026-10-13.

**Symptom:** The orOS APK (or any installed orOS) stays on an old version for hours or days ("orOS was updated to v4.66.00" is the last notice) while the live site is far ahead; the desktop updates normally. **Cause:** the APK is a TWA of the live site, so the page comes from the service worker's precache of its own release (SW-F1) and changes only when a new worker finishes its install. Under SW-T2 one precache file the phone's network never delivered (VPN, filter, a request that hangs) failed every attempt, and a hanging request let the browser kill the install before it left a resume marker. Reproduced in Chromium with one file whose connection is cut: 4 loads, still 4.66.00. **Fix:** SW-T4 in sw.js: 30 s limit per file, a second try, the marker written at the start, attempts counted across releases, and from the third attempt the release activates without the unreachable files. Nothing to reinstall: the next open of the app picks up the fixed worker. **Ref:** SW-T4, 2026-11-01 (thread "Διόρθωσε την ενημέρωση των Android apps").

### T2. Phone bridge (TWA postMessage)

**Symptom:** The "On this phone" button is missing after an update. **Cause:** the old version is still running. **Fix:** close the app fully, reopen it, and check the version in What's new. **Ref:** phone contacts/calendar thread.

**Symptom:** Bridge never connects; `validateRelationship` returns false; the channel is re-requested in a loop. **Cause:** Chromium needs `warmup()` first; the app process gets frozen; the page dropped ports with an empty or other origin (Brave). **Fix:** PostMessageService keeps the app awake (#310, 1.82.02); accept a source-less port from any origin (#313, 1.83.01). Diagnose with long-press icon › Bridge diagnostics. **Ref:** #310, #313.

**Symptom:** App crashes after the user grants the permission; no account appears. **Cause:** missing `WRITE_SYNC_SETTINGS` permission. **Fix:** add it to the manifest. **Ref:** #314.

**Symptom:** After installing the TWA the user starts signed out, or it opens in Brave even with Firefox as default. **Cause:** the TWA runs in a specific browser with its own storage; the Firefox default being ignored is unexplained. **Fix:** sign in to sync to restore the data. **Ref:** phone contacts/calendar thread.

**Symptom:** Phone calendar syncs forever with 0 events. **Cause:** only the user's own events were sent. **Fix:** include feeds and holidays (#314, 1.84.00); colours (#315, 1.84.01). Google Calendar needs the calendar toggled off/on; Fossify needs Settings › CalDAV sync on to see "orOS". **Ref:** #314, #315.

**Symptom:** An event is added 3 times; contact edits don't sync. **Cause:** resends, and pre-v2 contacts were read-only. **Fix:** dedupe resends; make contacts writable. **Ref:** #322, 1.88.03.

### T3. Service worker, cache, updates

**Symptom:** Devices get no updates; CACHE_VERSION stuck at 0.45.15 while the app is 0.46.00. **Cause:** the G2 precache guard failed (app folders missing from precache), and a failed bump run stamps nothing. **Fix:** G2 checks only apps.json. **Ref:** #51, #57, 2026-10-09.

**Symptom:** The PWA is slow or never opens on a bad connection. **Cause:** network-first with no timeout; an `isAppsList` bug sent shell.js/vault.js network-first; a half-downloaded update deleted the old version. **Fix:** 3 s timeout, 30 s "slow spell", PARTIAL_MARK resume. Test with a server that never answers; the DevTools offline switch doesn't reach the SW. **Ref:** #184, 0.86.01, 2026-10-11.

**Symptom:** After a release, old and new code run mixed. **Cause:** the release had no version step, so `?v=` and the cache name didn't change. **Fix:** let the version bot (`chore: sync orOS assets`, about 1 min after merge) rewrite `?v`; never ship without a bump. **Ref:** oros-version-collisions / G2 memory.

**Symptom:** SW install fails completely after a release. **Cause:** a duplicate URL in the precache list makes `cache.addAll` reject. **Fix:** dedupe the precache list. **Ref:** bulk release 0.47.

**Symptom:** Clicking a notice doesn't close the notification panel; a system notification only focuses the tab. **Cause:** missing close / navigate handling. **Fix:** #299 (1.74.01) and #306 (1.79.01). A later "does nothing" report was a stale cache, fixed by Ctrl+Shift+R. If the target app is already open, nothing visibly changes. **Ref:** #299, #306.

**Symptom:** The download or privacy page shows an old version right after a merge. **Cause:** these pages are not precached and the browser HTTP cache serves the old copy (inferred). **Fix:** hard refresh. **Ref:** sales/download page thread.

### T4. Sync and storage

**Symptom:** Sync is permanently "failed". **Cause:** (a) the Podcasts normQueue re-upload loop; (b) the real cause, "Browser storage is full", from the legacy `oros-auto-snapshots` key in localStorage. **Fix:** SY-L1/SY-L2 (#123, 0.48.02); snapshots moved to IndexedDB (#128, 0.52.02, 7.0 MB → 2.0 MB). First ask for Device info › Space per app; storage-full means localStorage, not Cache Storage. **Ref:** oros-sync-hotfix-0-48-02.

**Symptom:** "Browser storage is full — sync paused" after a contacts import; Device info shows Contacts at several MB (Chris, 2026-10-15: 4.0 MB of 8.3 MB). **Cause:** contact photos were data URLs inside `oros-contacts-data` (Google imports up to 50,000 characters each); the cloud copy brought them back on every download. **Fix:** CT-PS (128 px, 2.32.01), then CT-NP: no photos at all, initials or an 8-bit avatar. **Ref:** CT-NP.

**Symptom:** The language toggle (or any setting) silently does nothing. **Cause:** localStorage is full (5 MB); `markDirty` throws QuotaExceededError. **Fix:** catch quota errors (SY-Q1). **Ref:** SY-Q1, oros-sync-tests.

**Symptom:** Spreadsheet XLSX import turns Greek text into garbage. **Cause:** `vendor/xlsx.full.min.js` is stored double-encoded. **Fix:** not fixed yet; re-vendor the file as clean UTF-8. **Ref:** oros-budget memory.

**Symptom:** Saving a file from an app produces an EMPTY file. **Cause:** a Blob made in an app iframe fails `instanceof Blob` in the shell (cross-realm). **Fix:** duck-type the Blob in dialogs.js. **Ref:** #35.

**Symptom:** Downloads fail in browsers that ask where to save. **Cause:** the blob URL was revoked after 1 s, before the user answered. **Fix:** revoke after 40 s. **Ref:** dialogs/Files memory.

**Symptom:** Writing files fails on Safari. **Cause:** Safari exposes OPFS but not the write method used. **Fix:** detect the method itself, not "OPFS available". **Ref:** oros-files-dropbox memory.

**Symptom:** Universal search is broken: "failed to load search.js". **Cause:** an apps.json entry pointed at a missing file. **Fix:** fix the entry plus a test that every referenced file exists. **Ref:** #101, 0.48.01.

**Symptom:** WebDAV `Test and connect` says the server did not answer (`dav-unreachable`), while the address opens in a browser tab. **Cause:** the server sends no CORS headers for the orOS origin (Synology, ownCloud, Nextcloud without WebAppPassword). **Fix:** turn on `Through the orOS relay` (relay `/dav`, #477/#481). **Ref:** WebDAV W3, 2026-10-17.

**Symptom:** WebDAV connect is refused with `dav-etag` or `dav-conditions` on a small or self-written server. **Cause:** the server hides the ETag from the browser (no `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: ETag`), ignores If-Match / If-None-Match, or builds ETags from size + whole-second mtime, so two writes in one second keep the same ETag (stock WsgiDAV). orOS refuses such a server on purpose: two devices could overwrite each other. **Fix:** use Nextcloud, ownCloud or Synology, or make the server expose ETag and use nanosecond ETags. **Ref:** WebDAV W2 real-server check, 2026-10-17.

**Symptom:** Through the relay, the request after a `HEAD` of a missing file fails on one test server. **Cause:** that server (WsgiDAV) sends a body with the 404 answer to HEAD, which breaks the kept-alive connection (server bug, seen only locally). **Fix:** none needed for real servers; in E2E use a fresh WebDAV root or another server. **Ref:** WebDAV W3 E2E, 2026-10-17.

**Symptom:** `The orOS relay reaches only public https servers…` (`dav-relay-target`) for a NAS at home. **Cause:** the relay refuses local, http and non-standard-port addresses (443, 5006, 8443, 9443 only). **Fix:** give the NAS a public https address (e.g. Synology DDNS + Let's Encrypt), or wait for LAN sync through orOS Portable (WebDAV W5). **Ref:** relay/dav.js.

**Symptom:** `Move to WebDAV / Nextcloud` or `Move to Dropbox` says the new cloud already holds orOS data (`move-target-used`). **Cause:** the move only copies into an empty place, so it never mixes two orOS clouds. **Fix:** choose an empty folder on the server (Folder field), or empty the other Dropbox's orOS app folder; the old cloud is untouched either way. **Ref:** WebDAV W4, 2026-10-17.

### T5. Dropbox, Google, OAuth

**Symptom:** Files can't see the whole Dropbox. **Cause:** the sync Dropbox app is "App folder", and the access type can't be changed. **Fix:** a second app, "orOS Files" (Full Dropbox), with redirect `https://useoros.online/files/dropbox-callback.html`. **Ref:** #331/#339, 2.00.00.

**Symptom:** Dropbox sign-in fails in Portable (localhost:47800). **Cause:** the redirect URI is not registered. **Fix:** add `http://localhost:47800/` and `http://localhost:47800/files/dropbox-callback.html` in both Dropbox apps; Dropbox allows http only for localhost. **Ref:** 2026-10-14.

**Symptom:** Dropbox sign-in from a single (solo) app fails, or a second handler gets an invalid code. **Cause:** Dropbox refuses to be framed; two OAuth handlers raced for one one-shot code. **Fix:** navigate the top window (`oros-solo-return`), and keep one handler per code. **Ref:** R34 lesson.

**Symptom:** Google contacts sign-in fails for most users. **Cause:** the OAuth app is in "Testing", so only listed test users can sign in; it also needs a privacy page and the People API enabled. **Fix:** add test users or publish the app; privacy.html (#320, 1.88.01); People API (#321, 1.88.02). **Ref:** Google contacts import thread.

**Symptom:** Contact counts differ (Google 437 vs orOS 421-431). **Cause:** loose dedupe; exact duplicates inside Google that Google's Merge misses; " ::: "-joined fields from an old CSV import; re-import created duplicates; photos and type labels were lost. **Fix:** #356 (2.10.01), #369 (2.20.01), #372 (2.21.01). **Ref:** Google contacts import thread.

### T6. Network, mixed content, browser quirks

**Symptom:** Playing an http radio stream makes the installed app show the browser bar. **Cause:** mixed content on an https page. **Fix:** https only; upgrade http→https, otherwise show a message. Podcasts over http likely hit the same issue (unverified). **Ref:** #358, 2.11.01.

**Symptom:** Assistant can't reach a local AI server (`http://192.168…`) from a phone, or a provider fails. **Cause:** an https page can't call plain http on the LAN; every local server needs CORS enabled; some providers block browser calls. **Fix:** use the per-server CORS step and Connection test. WebGPU on some Linux GPUs needs `chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu` (inferred). **Ref:** #366, #367.

**Symptom:** A user's Claude Pro/Max plan doesn't work as an API key. **Cause:** subscriptions don't include API usage. **Fix:** create a separately billed API key in the Console. **Ref:** Assistant Claude thread.

**Symptom:** Battery shows 100% while unplugged. **Cause:** Brave always reports level 1 and charging (privacy); this is also the Chromium spec default. **Fix:** treat 1 + charging as "unknown". **Ref:** #187, 0.86.02.

**Symptom:** Agent live checks of useoros.online, workers.dev, dropbox.com, wikidata or eff.org fail with 403. **Cause:** the cloud container proxy blocks them. **Fix:** Chris runs live checks on a real device. **Ref:** multiple threads.

### T7. CI and GitHub

**Symptom:** A red "Workers Builds: oros-mail-relay" check appears on every PR; on main it is skipped. **Cause:** Cloudflare's Workers Builds makes a preview build for each non-production branch, and the relay uses Durable Objects (REMOTE, PUSH, HOUSE, with `migrations`): Cloudflare generates no preview URLs for a Worker with Durable Objects and does not accept a version upload that changes a Durable Object class lifecycle, so every preview build fails (diagnosis from the docs, 2026-10-27; the build log itself is only in the Cloudflare dashboard). Production deploys from main are not affected. **Fix (applied 2026-10-27):** Chris cleared "Enable Preview Builds" in the Cloudflare dashboard (Workers & Pages › oros-mail-relay › Settings › Build › Branch control). Since then PR commits get no "Workers Builds" check at all (checked on #637 at 7cebcdf and on #643 at 7ff0da4 and b53af7b); production deploys from main continue. If the red check comes back, check that setting first. **Ref:** oros-mail-app memory; 2026-10-27 changelog.

**Symptom:** The sync-nullfx workflow can't open its PR. **Cause:** Actions isn't allowed to create PRs. **Fix:** Settings › Actions › General › "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests", or open the PR by hand from `auto/nullfx-sync`. Until then each daily check of a new release fails at that step and repeats. **Ref:** #311.

**Symptom:** android.yml doesn't run on PR pushes; tests.yml skips release-only pushes. **Cause:** trigger and paths filters don't match. **Fix:** run them with workflow_dispatch. **Ref:** oros-companion-apps memory.

**Symptom:** The agent can't create a repo (403) or a commit is blocked. **Cause:** no repo-create permission; the auto-mode classifier blocks commits touching workflows or assetlinks. **Fix:** Chris creates repos and approves those commits. **Ref:** oros-companion-apps memory.

**Symptom:** A workflow breaks on a commit message containing a quote. **Cause:** inputs were pasted into the script, so a quote broke the loop guard. **Fix:** always pass inputs through `env:`. **Ref:** oros-merge-queue memory.

**Symptom:** Updating orOS in F-Droid fails with "Download failed: IOException Hash not matching", then on retry with ktor `ClientRequestException … repo/oros.apk invalid: 416`. **Cause:** the repository served every build under the same file name (`repo/oros.apk`): after a publish the new index carried the new hash while the GitHub Pages CDN (and the phone's half-finished download) still had the old file, and resuming the partial download against the changed file asked for a byte range past its end (416). **Fix:** `fdroid.yml` renames each APK to `<package>_<versionCode>_<sha256 first 8>.apk` before `fdroid update`, so every build has a new address. After the next publish, refresh the repositories in F-Droid and update again; no cache clearing or reinstall needed (if a stale download sticks, F-Droid › Settings › clear cache, or the app's storage › Clear cache). **Ref:** 2026-10-17.

**Symptom:** Updating orOS in F-Droid fails with "Download failed: NotFoundException … ClientRequestException … repo/<file>.apk invalid: 404" (GitHub Pages "Page not found"). **Cause:** the phone downloads with the index it fetched last (F-Droid refreshes on Wi-Fi only by default), and that file was no longer published: each publish renames every APK, and from 2026-10-17 the version bot's `"version"` stamp in `manifest.webmanifest` counted as an Android shell change, so the repository republished after every release and old files vanished within minutes; a request for `repo/oros.apk` means the index is from before the renaming (2026-10-17). **Fix:** `fdroid.yml` ignores the manifests' `"version"` line in the shell hash and in the `android-v` tag check, and `tools/fdroid-keep.js` keeps earlier APKs for 3 days. On the phone: pull down to refresh the repositories in F-Droid, then update; the signing key is unchanged, so it updates in place, no uninstall. **Ref:** 2026-10-18.

**Symptom:** F-Droid repo stops updating, or the first publish isn't reachable. **Cause:** the deploy token expires about 2027-10; Pages on oros-fdroid must be enabled after the first publish. **Fix:** renew the token; enable Pages. **Ref:** oros-store-packaging memory.

### T8. Merges and versions

**Symptom:** Scripts load twice and conflict-marker text shows on the page. **Cause:** conflict markers were merged into index.html. **Fix:** remove them; tests/conflict-markers.test.js; always grep for markers and diff index.html. **Ref:** #276, 1.57.01, 2026-10-13.

**Symptom:** Two releases share one version number, or script lines are misordered. **Cause:** parallel PRs took the same APP_VERSION (e.g. #342/#345, both 2.02.00); htmlres.py can reorder script lines. **Fix:** the merge-queue rule (one version bump at a time, rebase before bump); check script order. **Ref:** #147; oros-version-collisions.

**Symptom:** The installed orOS shows the "updated to the latest version" toast, but apps keep old behaviour for several releases; opening useoros.online in the browser seems to help. **Cause:** "Bump orOS version" failed on every push to main from 2.26.00 to 2.40.00: guard G3 (palette contract) checked every folder with an index.html, and the standalone `download/` page (#388) has no shell scripts. A failed run stamps nothing, so sw.js stayed at CACHE_VERSION 2.25.00 (same cache names, the old runtime cache never cleared) and most app pages kept `?v=2.25.00`, answered cache-first from that runtime cache. Release PRs hand-stamped shell.js's `?v=` and APP_VERSION, so the toast reported the new number while the apps ran old code. **Fix:** G3 checks only registered apps (like G2); the stamp script moved to `.github/scripts/stamp-assets.js`, and `tests/release-guards.test.js` runs every guard in check mode on each PR (tests.yml also runs on `index.html`/`apps.json` changes), so a guard failure shows before the merge. The first stamp after the fix bumps CACHE_VERSION and every `?v=`, which refreshes installed apps on their next open. **Check:** after a merge, the newest "Bump orOS version" run on main is green and a `chore: sync orOS assets to vX` commit follows. **Ref:** this PR, 2026-10-15.

### T9. Test harness (E2E)

**Symptom:** Greek OPFS file names fail with TypeMismatchError → EISDIR in headless Chromium. **Cause:** the harness locale isn't UTF-8. **Fix:** run with `LANG=C.UTF-8`; not an orOS bug. **Ref:** oros-headless-chromium-locale, 2026-10-12.

**Symptom:** The Today calendar-reminder E2E fails under Europe/Athens. **Cause:** the browser was pinned to UTC while Node used local TZ. **Fix:** set `timezoneId` to the process TZ. **Ref:** oros-today-summary memory.

**Symptom:** An app page opened top-level in a harness redirects away; a UMD library breaks; an audio tail is cut off. **Cause:** the DL-1 redirect to the shell; an element `id="exports"` shadows UMD `exports`; Chromium drops a DelayNode tail once its source ends. **Fix:** add `?standalone`; rename the element; keep the source alive. **Ref:** #260; QR and Studio memories.

### T10. Portable and bootable USB

**Symptom:** Portable data "vanishes", or features are missing. **Cause:** another port is another origin; file:// has no SW or OPFS; Lite uses the host browser, and an older browser may not open the profile. **Fix:** always use the fixed port 47800; Windows SmartScreen: More info → Run. Stick: 64 GB recommended, 32 GB minimum. **Ref:** oros-portable-usb memory.

**Symptom:** The bootable ISO hangs at GRUB; the `oros` user doesn't exist; ISO upload fails; the clock is off. **Cause:** GRUB had no timeout; live-config needs the user-setup package; GitHub Pages has a 100 MB limit; the clock is UTC. **Fix:** 3 s GRUB timeout; create the user in a chroot hook; publish ISOs to Releases. **Ref:** Bootable USB thread.

## Part XII — Changelog

`CHANGELOG.md` was retired; this Part IS the project changelog.

**Format rules (R21):**
- Ascending order: oldest first, the newest entry at the BOTTOM. New entries are appended at the end of this Part in the same response as the change. Dates and APP_VERSIONs never go back: if a parallel PR with a higher version merged first, put yours just before it. `tests/bible-order.test.js` enforces this (since 2026-10-27).
- Heading: `### YYYY-MM-DD — <component> <version/wave> — <title>`. Undated legacy entries keep an approximate date marked "≈".
- Bullets, grouped as needed: **Changes** · **Fixes** · **Schema** · **Decisions** · **Files** · **Next**. Every fact that matters for future work stays (bugs fixed, schema fields, merge rules, decisions); prose is trimmed.
- Version numbers appear as historical records. The assistant proposes the next step (patch or whole version) and Christos decides (R23).
- Code, selectors, keys and file names go in backticks (unfenced `$("…")` text has been mangled before).
- An entry that merges several raw notes says so in its first line.

### Condensed history (before detailed entries were kept here)

- **2025-08 → 2026-09:** kernel lock, sync v0.9.2, OrosFS, unified notifications, 20 apps audited/verified.
- **2026-09-27:** Spreadsheet Waves 1–3 + Five-Axes verified.
- **2026-09-29:** Dice & Coin v0.4 (first Soffitta port).
- **2026-09-30 (summary-only items):**
  - Screen Pet v0.1–v0.3.1 (second Soffitta port, shell component) + calendar feed.
  - Writer Wave 5 I/O complete + audit fixes.
  - Cycle Timeline rewrite + DST hardening + unified-notification migration; Cycle v0.37.05 (back-to-today, date-picker sync, insights trend strip).
  - Radio Waves 1–3 (shell-hosted audio, discovery, mirror fallback) + FIX-RX hotfix series.
  - Minimalism Waves 1–2 + content Days 1–55.
  - Dice v0.38.00 feature wave.

### ≈2026-09-30 — Screen Pet — HUD minimize toggle

- **Changes:**
  - A ◀/▶ button left of the pet's name collapses the HUD to the name row only. The tooltip shows Ελαχιστοποίηση/Minimize or Ανάπτυξη/Expand.
  - When collapsed, these are hidden: age line, palette swatches, the three stat bars and all action groups.
  - Implemented via the `.pet-hud-collapsed` class (`#pet-hud-age`, `#pet-palettes`, `.pet-stat`, `.pet-hud-actions`), with a height/padding transition.
  - `refreshHUD()` is the single source of truth for HUD state.
- **Persistence:** device-local `oros-pet-minimized`, reapplied in `petEnable()`.
- **Guard:** clicks route through `touchInteraction()` (breaks contemplation, resets the 5-min idle clock).
- **Next:** smoke test (collapse, persistence across refresh, icon flip).

### ≈2026-09-30 — Screen Pet — event log full sync (Wave 5b follow-up)

- **Changes:**
  - New synced slice `petEvents` (`oros-pet-events`), merged as a union by id plus `{clearedAt}` wipe propagation. The `pet` entity slice was already synced; only the log had been device-local.
  - `logEvent` marks dirty through the existing `__orosPetSyncApi` funnel (~5s debounced push).
  - Birthday events use a deterministic id `bday-<petId>-<ymd>`: two devices logging the same anniversary collapse into one row (log + calendar feed).
  - `window.orosPet.clearLog` writes a `{clearedAt}` tombstone instead of removing the key, so the wipe reaches every device.
- **Export/import:** both pet slices ride `orosSync.exportData()`/`importData()`; no shell change needed.
- **Mixed versions:** older `pet.js` relays the unknown slice via the carry mailbox (sync.js ≥ 0.9.2).
- **Schema:** unchanged (ver 1); existing local logs merge on the first push. `calendar.js` untouched (reads the same key).

### 2026-09-30 — Calculator v0.1.0 — third Soffitta port

- **Concept:** a standard calculator with an optional Troll mode (in-app toggle).
- **Structure:**
  - New `calculator/` folder (index.html, calculator.css, calculator.js) on the orOS boot pattern: IIFE, `SCRIPT_V` marker, single-pass first render, `wireUI` before any `apply*`.
  - Classes namespaced `calc-*` (pad, display, face, switch, knob, skin-dot, hist-*).
- **Schema:** `oros-calculator-data = { ver:1, hist[{id,e,v,f,mtime}], tombs{}, skin, troll, sound, sm{skin,troll,sound} }`. Decision: ALL state syncs.
- **Merge:**
  - Scalars: per-field LWW via `sm` (Pet `fm` pattern), lexicographic tie-break (R5).
  - History: symmetric union by id (mtime → JSON tie-break); tombstones max-ts, delete wins ties (R17).
  - `HIST_MAX` 20, enforced with tombstoned trims. A strict sanitizer drops invalid rows.
- **Fixes:**
  - `sliceSet` suppresses dirty (R6).
  - `registerSync()` is now actually called in `load()` (it was defined but never called).
- **Shell ownership:**
  - Language and theme are shell-owned: `applyTheme()` deleted, lang/theme buttons removed, language read from `oros.lang` + storage events.
  - `skin-dark` sniffs `--bg` luminance.
- **R14:**
  - `resetAll()` uses a themed `<dialog>` (outside-click + Esc, node removal).
  - Reset history writes tombstones.
- **Features kept:**
  - CSV history export (Five-Axes ⑤).
  - Five skins with WebAudio voices; typewriter quips; truth reveal 1/15.
  - Share-prank clipboard with fallback; reduced motion; scrollbar + hidden-guard CSS; breakpoints 480/420/360.
- **Dead code removed:** `PREFS_KEY`, `evalCache`, an unused var in `flashToast`.
- **Exemptions:** Calendar axis, unified Notifications (Dice pattern), palette G3 (playful skins, Screen Pet precedent).
- **Next:** registry integration (apps.json, shell ICONS, `SC_DEFS` Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C, `translations.js` `app.calculator` + category, sw.js precache), then Checklist D on both devices.

### 2026-09-30 — Shell v0.38.10 — Radio proxy slice

- **Fix:** Radio favorites sync across devices even while the Radio iframe is closed.
- **How:**
  - `radio` slice registered shell-side: `radioProxySliceGet()` / `radioProxySliceSet()` / `registerRadioProxySlice()`, called from `initSyncIntegration()`.
  - It uses `oros-radio-data`, the same contract as the `files-disk` and `shell` proxies.
  - The live iframe registration (merge-capable) overrides the proxy while open; the proxy re-activates on close (LWW).
- **Files:** `shell.js` (~lines 1798–1840 at the time).

### ≈2026-09-30 — Screen Pet v0.3.2 — full sync completion

- **Synced slices:**
  1. `pet` (`oros-pet-data`): per-field LWW. Temporal fields are their own clocks, anchor pairs travel together, `fm` covers name/palette, plus tombstones.
  2. `petEvents` (`oros-pet-events`): union by id, deterministic sort (ts, id), rolling trim 100, deterministic birthday ids, `clearedAt` wipe.
  3. `petSettings` (`oros-pet-settings`): calendar-feed toggle, per-field LWW via `calFeedTs`.
- **Fixes:**
  - `setCalendarFeed` never marked dirty (the settings setter suppresses dirty during its own write) → now armed explicitly after the write.
  - Legacy migration ran before `registerSync()`, so a migrated opt-out was never pushed → `bootLegacyDirty` arms the first push right after `registerSync()`.
  - `settingsSliceSet` keeps the legacy mirror key `oros-pet-calendar-sync` in lock-step, because unmodified `calendar.js` still reads it. `oros-pet-settings` stays the source of truth.
- **Migration:**
  - One-time: if `oros-pet-settings` is absent and the legacy key exists, it migrates in with `calFeedTs = 1` (beats the epoch-0 default, loses to any real write). The legacy key is kept as the mirror.
  - Old v0.3 logs merge on the first push; ver stays 1.
- **Device-local:** `oros-pet-enabled`, `oros-pet-minimized`, `oros-pet-pos`, runtime choreography.
- **Coverage:** auto snapshots, manual export/import and cloud push/pull cover all three slices (they enumerate registered slices).
- **Mixed versions:** carry mailbox (sync.js ≥ 0.9.2).

### ≈2026-09-30 — Calculator v1.1.0 — feature wave 1 (full rewrite)

- **Why a rewrite:** it replaces a broken v1.0.0 that failed CI on missing theme inheritance (v1.0.0 has no entry of its own). `CALC_VER` "1.1.0".
- **Architecture:**
  - Palette bridge on the mood.js pattern (`inheritPalette` before first paint + `watchPalette` MutationObserver).
  - Shortcut forwarding (Contract Β).
  - Sync slice "calculator" registered as `registerSlice(get, set, LS_KEY)` with key `oros-calculator-data`. ⚠ No `mergeFn` → see audit A2.
  - EN/EL lazy packs plus a separate troll pack. Language: `localStorage["oros-lang"]` first, then `parent.orosLang`, then "en".
- **Troll mode:**
  - Teasing language always; plausible lies sized by intensity, never two lies in a row.
  - Three intensities (Subtle ~16% / Balanced ~34% default / Rampant ~66%), persisted as `trollIntensity`.
  - Controls: right-click cycles the level on desktop. Touch uses a 500ms long-press: `touchmove` cancels, the trailing click is swallowed, and the mobile `contextmenu` double-fire is guarded by `touchActive`.
  - Indicator: dots ●○○/●●○/●●● plus a toast.
- **History:**
  - Synced, cap 50, LWW per entry by timestamp, tombstone map (id → ts); Clear = tombstone all.
  - Clicking an entry reuses it (fresh replace).
- **Other features:**
  - Copy result (clipboard API + `execCommand` fallback).
  - Ans key A (never holds "Error").
  - Single-level undo Ctrl+Z (snapshot before mutating presses; no-op presses drop it).
  - Negative results tinted (`.neg`).
  - History panel drag-resizable ≥880px (200–500px, `panelWidth` persisted).
  - Full keyboard support.
  - Unified notifications: `transientNote()` → `parent.orosNotifs.transient` (ns "calculator").
- **Fixes:**
  - `renderError()` was missing (ReferenceError on chained divide-by-zero).
  - `pressAns()` set `fresh=false` (Ans 42 then 5 → "425").
  - `pressEq()` stored "Error" in `lastAnswer`.
  - `lang()` read `window.orosLang` inside the iframe (R8).
  - Dead `stagePendingRemote`/`takePendingRemote`/`REMOTE_PENDING_KEY` removed.
  - EL "calc.key.back" mistranslation → «Διαγραφή».
  - The ⌫ key's `data-i18n` overwrote the glyph (now a translated `aria-label`); a duplicate `aria-label` assignment was deduplicated.
- **Known non-issues:** dead `state.lang` field; `pressAns` indentation drift.
- **Checks:** boot log `[calc] calculator v1.1.0 booted — troll:off intensity:1 history:N`; EL rendering; desktop right-click cycling; mobile long-press without flipping On/Off.

### ≈2026-09-30 — Calculator v1.2.0 — feature wave 2 (memory, scientific row, CSV)

- **Features:**
  - **Memory:** MC/MR/M+ as a half-height row above the keypad. Single value `mem` (null = empty), synced. M+ accumulates; MR recalls with fresh-replace semantics and resets the pending operator; MC clears with a toast.
  - **Scientific row:** an `fx` toggle shows √ (Error on negative), x², 1/x (Error on zero) and ± (the engine function existed since v1.0.0 but had no button). Visibility persisted as `sciOn`. All unary ops join single-level undo, including on the Error path.

  - `applyRemote()` normalizes a local payload lacking `deleted` before the merge loop (was a TypeError).

### ≈2026-10-02 — Notifications — toast stack (GNOME-style)

- **Changes:**
  - Toasts no longer overlap. One container `#oros-toast-stack` (fixed, `calc(58px + safe-area-inset-top)`, right 20px), created lazily by `ensureToastStack()`; column flex, 8px gap; `pointer-events:none` on the container, `auto` on each toast.
  - Every `fireToast()` creates its own node, its own auto-remove timer and its own observer. No single-slot wipe anywhere.
  - Newest first: `insertBefore(toast, toastStack.firstChild)` + `toastQueue.unshift(toast)`.
  - Max 5 visible: `applyStackLimits()` hides toasts at index ≥ 5 (`opacity:0`, `pointer-events:none`); they stay mounted and expire normally. It runs on insertion AND on removal.
- **Fixes (found in self-review of the first pass, before release):**
  - Dead double mount: the legacy `document.body.appendChild(toast)` survived next to the stack insert → removed, with the orphaned `requestAnimationFrame` opacity flip.
  - The rAF flip set `opacity:1` AFTER the limit loop had dimmed the excess toasts (toast #6+ came back) → the 0→1 flip now lives inside `applyStackLimits()`.
  - The cleanup `MutationObserver` watched `document.body` while toasts lived in the stack, so `toastQueue` never shrank (detached nodes, wrong indices) → the observer watches `toastStack`; removal splices the queue and calls `applyStackLimits()`.
  - Z-index 9999 (same tier as the boot splash) → 10000.
  - No promotion on removal (introduced by the fix round itself) → `applyStackLimits()` is called from the removal path too.
- **Preserved:** inbox, badge and sync contracts (`emitCandidate`, `transientToast`, `notifSliceSet`, `markAsRead`, dedup, quiet hours, app toggles, 24h badge fallback); Undo toasts keep ≥ 8 s; deep-link router and bridges; native Web Notifications.
- **Decisions:** this entry pinned the stack top-right and declared the `position` setting inert. **Superseded** by the 2026-10-02 position fix below.
- **Open:**
  - A brand-new toast may appear without a slide-in (insert and `opacity:1` in one frame). Optional: call `applyStackLimits()` inside `requestAnimationFrame` at the end of `fireToast`.
  - Dead code listed for deletion with owner approval: `TOAST_POSITIONS`, `getPositionStyles()`, the unused `position` local in `fireToast`. Do NOT migrate or strip a stored `position` value (the LWW settings merge tolerates it). Re-check after the position fix.
  - Toasts beyond 5 are invisible but mounted; a "+N more" counter was considered and deferred.
- **Files:** `notifications.js`; `style.css` (`#oros-toast-stack` / `.oros-toast` rules appended at the bottom).
- **Checks:** two simultaneous notifications stack without overlap; six or more → exactly 5 visible, closing one reveals the next; dismiss, click-through and timeout remove only the targeted toast; mobile ≤480px fits (`max-width:90vw`, safe area); boot line `[orOS][notifs] Module v1.0.0 initialized`; `toastQueue` shrinks after removals.

### ≈2026-10-02 — Calculator v1.3.0 — keyboard reliability

- **Fixes:**
  - The number row and the numpad work while focus is on the shell. Cause: the app runs in an iframe and the browser delivers `keydown` only to the focused browsing context. New `wireParentKeyRouting()`: a same-origin `keydown` listener on the parent document forwards unmodified keys into `onKey`, with guards for a stale listener (window closed, root not connected) and for shell inputs/modals (`input`, `textarea`, `select`, contenteditable). No double handling when the iframe has focus.
  - Numpad with NumLock OFF: `e.key` is then "End", "PageUp"… → `onKey` maps `e.code` (`Numpad0`–`Numpad9`, `NumpadAdd`/`Subtract`/`Multiply`/`Divide`/`Decimal`/`Enter`) to the NumLock glyphs.
  - After a keypad click, Enter and Space re-triggered the focused button (double `=`) → the delegated pad click handler calls `btn.blur()`.
- **Contracts unchanged:** modifier combos (Ctrl/Cmd/Alt) are not forwarded; Contract Β untouched.
- **Checks:** open Calculator from the menu without clicking inside, then type on the number row and the numpad (both NumLock states); click a key and press Enter → the action fires exactly once.

### ≈2026-10-02 — Shell — weather tray: fetch throttle hardened (`wxBusy`)

- **Fix:** the tray chip intermittently stuck on "Athens — waiting…" at boot.
- **Cause:** the 30-minute throttle (`oros-wx-last`) was stamped BEFORE the fetch started. A killed in-flight request (tab close, PWA `controllerchange` reload) left the stamp armed with an empty cache and the catch-path rewind unreachable: up to 30 minutes locked. An Open-Meteo reply with an HTTP error or rate-limit JSON body took the same path.
- **Changes (`shell.js`):**
  1. `wxBusy` in-flight guard (boot tick + boot call no longer double-fire).
  2. The 30-min throttle is written ONLY in the success branch.
  3. A response without a usable payload rewinds to the 2-minute retry window.
  4. The catch path releases `wxBusy`.
- **Verified compatible:** `weather.js` (per-city `current.temp`/`current.code` cache shape and the 0.15° mirror into `oros-wx-cache`); no change needed.
- **One-time cleanup** on a device already stuck: remove `oros-wx-last`, or wait out the window.

### ≈2026-10-02 — Radio v0.2 — tray host registration (RF-1)

- **Fix:** the Radio playback chip never appeared in the taskbar.
- **Cause:** `ensureHost()` in `radio.js` built the shell-hosted audio host (audio element in the parent document, Media Session, full API) but kept it in the iframe closure. `radioTrayTick()` in the shell (every second) needs `window.__orosRadioHost` on the shell window with `api.getState().current.name`, found `undefined` and skipped silently.
- **Change:** one guarded assignment at the end of `ensureHost()`, after the Media Session try/catch and before `return host`: `if(!w.__orosRadioHost) w.__orosRadioHost = host;`.
- **Effects:** the early-return check at the top of `ensureHost()` now reuses the existing host on reopen (FIX-RX-5 no-duplicate-audio model); playback still survives closing the app.
- **Notes:** the state shape the shell expects (`{ current:{name,…}, paused, playing, flags:{buffering,error}, sleepUntil }`) was already right. `shell.orosTray.register("radio", …)` in `registerTrayIcon()` is a separate mechanism from the `radioTrayTick()` chip; both now see the same host.
- **Checks:** chip within ~1 s of playback; host survives close; no duplicate `audio[data-oros-radio]` after reopen.
- **Next:** favorites/recents on a new device still to be verified.

### ≈2026-10-02 — Shell — weather tray: stale app-cache adoption

- **Fix:** the chip showed "Athens - waiting..." at boot until the Weather app was opened.
- **Cause:** `wxAdoptAppCache()` adopted the Weather app's city cache on every 60 s tick regardless of age. A stale app entry (7 h old in the diagnosis: cache age 420 min vs last fetch 8 min) overwrote the tray's fresh cache, while `WX_LAST` kept the 30-min throttle armed.
- **Changes (`shell.js`, 2 patches):**
  - `wxAdoptAppCache`: adopt only when the app cache is strictly newer (`p.at <= cur.at` → skip). "Newer wins" replaces "app wins".
  - `wxFetch`: when the throttle is armed but the cache is older than the throttle period, the fetch proceeds (self-heals at the next tick).
- **Unchanged:** `wxAdoptAppCache` is still the single nearest-city source (~15 km, `WX_NEAR_DEG`) for the tray chip and the morning briefing; one failure line per day in the inbox; offline never paints a fake temperature.
