#### Solitaire v1.0.0 (new app, Games) + shared `cardkit/`

- **New app `solitaire/`** ("Solitaire" / "Πασιέντζα"): three variants on one table, picked from the toolbar; each keeps its own deal in progress. **Klondike** (Κλοντάικ): draw 1 or 3, classic Windows score (waste → column +5, to a foundation +10, card turned +5, foundation → column −15, turning the waste −100 / −20, −2 every 10 s, win bonus 700000 / s after 30 s) or no score. **FreeCell**: the Microsoft numbered deals 1–32000 (C runtime LCG; #1 and #617 checked against the known layouts), a deal number from the options dialog, a random number otherwise; moving several cards at once as far as (free cells + 1) × 2^(empty columns) allows, halved when the target is an empty column; nothing comes back off a foundation. **Spider** (Αράχνη): 1, 2 or 4 suits, 500 points −1 a move +100 a run; a full K→A run of one suit leaves by itself; no new row while a column is empty (toast).
- **Play:** drag with mouse, finger or pen (the run follows; an illegal drop glides back; the legal target lights up), or tap a card: it goes to the best place (a foundation first, then a column with cards, Spider same suit first, then an empty column, then a free cell); a double tap never moves twice; a card with nowhere to go shakes and the reason is read out (FreeCell: a toast with how many cards can move). Unlimited undo (Ctrl/Cmd+Z, button; 150 steps survive a reload), hint (H: highlights the move, foundation and revealing moves first, else the stock), New deal (N, Undo toast over a deal under way). Auto-complete runs by itself once every card is open (Klondike: stock and waste empty; FreeCell: every column falls in rank toward its top). Enter / Space on a focused pile = tap; every pile is a focus stop with an EN/EL name. Win: the cards bounce off the foundations (tap or key to skip; reduced motion: none), then a centered result dialog with time, moves, score, records beaten, win rate and streak. Options dialog: draw, scoring, suits, deal number, felt or plain table. Spider on a narrow portrait screen suggests landscape once.
- **New shared module `cardkit/`** (not an app, no apps.json entry): `window.orosCards` with cards as ids, decks (Spider: suits × copies), crypto Fisher–Yates with rejection sampling, seeded shuffle (mulberry32), EN/EL card names, DOM faces with inline SVG pips (no images; corner rank and pip on one line with a 12px floor, readable on 33px Spider cards at 360px), card back in the accent colour, canvas faces, and a pointer helper for drag / tap / double tap. Documented API at the top of the file; Xeri will reuse it.
- **Schema:** SOLITAIRE v1 (Part IV); device-local keys incl. the sessions and current streaks (Part III). Same toolbar, dialogs, toasts, palette and sync idiom as the other games.
- **Tests:** `tests/solitaire.test.js` (20): cardkit ids / codes / names, full and Spider decks, crypto shuffle (permutation, chi-square on 10,400 shuffles), seeded shuffle repeatable; FreeCell deals #1 and #617; Klondike deal, draw 1 / 3, turning the waste, building rules, classic score, time penalty and bonus; FreeCell multi-card limits; Spider deal, runs, rows, completed runs; positions never mutated (undo); 60 random games × 120 moves keep every card; auto-complete wins (Klondike, FreeCell); tap targets; hints; stored-game validation; merge symmetric, associative, idempotent, canonical, reset and bad rows drop, totals.
- **Verification (Chromium, real shell + real `sync.js` + mock Dropbox, EN desktop / EL phone):** fresh Klondike, stock tap counts the deal, Ctrl+Z, H; drag of the last card to a foundation then auto-complete to a win, win animation, centered result dialog, records in the slice; FreeCell deal #617 from the options dialog (layout and `#617` in the status), a tap to an empty column then auto-complete to a win; Spider drag that completes the last run; touch drag (CDP touch events) on a phone, illegal drop snaps back, double tap; in-progress deal and undo steps resume after a reload; New deal Undo toast; draw 3; light theme + plain table; records dialog; no overflow and touch targets ≥ 32 px at 360×740 (all three variants), 740×360 (Spider), 768 and 1280; two devices converge, idle cycles upload 0, a reset on the phone reaches the desktop; no page errors.
- **NOT tested:** real Dropbox, Firefox / Safari, a real phone (touch feel, landscape rotation), screen readers.

#### Jigsaw v1.0.0 (new app, Games)

- **New app `jigsaw/`** ("Jigsaw" / "Παζλ"): a picture cut into 12, 24, 48, 96 or 150 pieces, scattered around a frame on a table; drag them back together. **Picture:** a photo from the device (`orosDialog.openFile`, R33) or from the Files disk (an in-app browser of `orosFS`, folders and PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/BMP/AVIF only), or a built-in picture drawn by the Wallpaper generator (`../wallpaper/art.js`, loaded as is: six thumbnails, every style in turn, "Other pictures" for more). A user file is read as a bitmap only: refused by name/type and by its first bytes when it is not a raster format (SVG never reaches a decoder), 40 MB at most, at least 200 × 200; a huge photo is held at 3200 px while cropped. **Setup dialog:** crop with a live preview of the cut (drag, pinch, wheel, slider), piece count (a phone hint above 48), Classic or Squares, Landscape or Portrait (default = the screen's shape), Rotated pieces (off by default). The crop is redrawn at 720–1600 px on its long side with whole square cells.
- **Play:** classic pieces with tabs and blanks drawn on canvas (every inner edge is one seeded curve shared by both pieces, so each tab fits its neighbour's blank) or plain squares; each piece is drawn once to its own canvas and moved with CSS transforms. Drag with mouse or touch; a dropped piece or group clicks onto its place in the frame or onto a right neighbour within a quarter of a cell, then takes in every group that now lines up; groups move as one; a group in its place stays put (dragging it pans). Rotation: a tap turns the piece's group 90° clockwise; only pieces turned the same way join. Solved = every piece upright and in place relative to the others; the picture glides into the frame and a centered result dialog shows the time, the best time and the count. **Helpers:** preview (P), faint picture in the frame (G), edge pieces only (E), tidy loose pieces to the side, edge pieces first (T); zoom with pinch, the wheel, − 0 + buttons and keys, pan by dragging the table. The timer runs from the first move while the app is visible. A new puzzle (N) over one in progress gives an Undo toast (R14); "Same picture, cut again".
- **Storage:** the puzzle in progress and its picture stay on the device in IndexedDB `oros-jigsaw` and resume after closing; records sync (JIGSAW v1, Part IV); prefs device-local (Part III). Same toolbar, dialogs, toasts, palette and sync idiom as the other games.
- **Tests:** `tests/jigsaw.test.js` (14): grids per count, seeded cut, every tab is the same curve as the neighbour's blank (geometry compared point by point, all grids, both shapes, outline closed, tabs inside the canvas margin), table and slots leave room for every piece off the frame, snapping to the place and to a right neighbour (never a wrong one), groups take in what lines up and snap exactly into the frame, rotation of groups, joins need the same turn, solved needs upright, groups stay on the table, tidy order, crop, raster byte check (SVG/XML/HTML refused), saved-puzzle validation, merge symmetric, associative, idempotent, inputs untouched, best time, reset and bad rows.
- **Verification (Chromium, real shell + real `sync.js` + mock Dropbox):** 12 pieces solved by mouse drags (desktop EN) and by touch drags (phone EL 360×740); photo from the Files disk (a `.png` holding SVG refused with a toast, `.svg` and `.txt` not listed); a 6000×4000 JPEG and an SVG through the device picker; resume after a reload and after closing the app (same positions, same progress); pinch zoom; ghost, edges only, preview, tidy; a rotation puzzle solved by taps + drags; Squares; Undo of a replaced puzzle; keyboard; two devices converge, idle cycles upload 0, a reset reaches the other device; no horizontal overflow at 360, 768, 1280; dialogs centered; light theme; no page errors. **Performance (150 pieces, CPU throttled ×4):** cut + draw 0.6 s (desktop) / 0.6–1.3 s (phone emulation), 17 MB of piece canvases; dragging one piece 53–60 fps, a 149-piece group 59 fps, pan / wheel zoom / tidy 60 fps; one stall of 0.3–0.5 s (≈0.1 s unthrottled) on the first touch of a freshly shown table (Chromium's layer commit, not app code).
- **NOT tested:** a real phone or tablet (GPU compositing differs from headless), Firefox / Safari (incl. `createImageBitmap` and HEIC photos), real Dropbox, a real Files disk on OPFS with large photos, memory pressure on a low-end phone.

#### Crossword v1.0.0 (new app, Games)

- **New app `crossword/`** ("Crossword" / "Σταυρόλεξο"): a fill-in crossword (kriss-kross), no clues: the words are given, grouped by length, and you place them in the grid so that every crossing agrees. English or Greek words by an own switch (default = orOS language); Greek in capitals without accents, final sigma as Σ. **Sizes:** up to 9×9 (8–10 words), up to 13×13 (14–18), up to 17×17 (22–28). **Words:** random common words, or one of the 20 Word Search themes (topped up with common words where the theme's words do not cross enough). **Play:** tap a cell and type; a second tap (or Space, or the direction key) switches across / down; arrows, Tab / Shift+Tab (next / previous word), Backspace, Delete; physical keys by position (`e.code`, as in Wordle), so Greek works on an English layout; an on-screen keyboard per language. The word list lights the group of the current word and strikes through every word sitting in its own slot (checked once the slot is full). **Check** letter / word / all (Shift+L / W / A: wrong letters turn red), **reveal** a letter (Shift+R; no record then). Timer (pauses while the app is hidden); records per language × size (solved, best time with its date). **Daily:** one 13×13 puzzle a day per language, the same on every device (seeded from the date, offline); a daily puzzle solved on another device shows solved here. Shift+N new puzzle (Undo toast when one is in progress). The puzzle in progress resumes after a reload, letters and cursor included.
- **Generator:** a connected crossing layout in the size's box (a word crosses only where letters agree and never touches another word side by side, so every run of letters is exactly one listed word), cropped to its bounding box; a backtracking solver counts the ways to fill the slots, and given letters make the solution unique: the first on a crossing of the most crossed word (as in printed kriss-kross puzzles), then, while two solutions exist, one where they differ (at most 3 / 4 / 5 by size). Up to 8 layouts are tried; a puzzle still not unique is accepted (the check dialog says so, and any filling where every word fits counts as solved). Seeded (FNV-1a + mulberry32), so the daily grid is identical everywhere.
- **Word lists:** none of its own: loads `../wordsearch/words-en.js` and `../wordsearch/words-el.js` (`window.WORDSEARCH_WORDS`; precached with Word Search; same sources and credits).
- **Schema:** CROSSWORD v1 (Part IV); device-local keys incl. the session (Part III). Same toolbar, dialogs, toasts, palette and sync idiom as Word Search. Notifications: none (exemption from Checklist B item 9).
- **Tests:** `tests/crossword.test.js` (11): Greek normalizing, keyboards cover both alphabets, physical-key map; the shared list format; placement rules (crossings, side-by-side, ends); every language × size × theme layout connected, every run of letters exactly one listed word, distinct words, tight crop, word counts, theme share; the solver (unique puzzles have exactly one solution, the real one is always found, two swappable words → 2 solutions, a given letter decides); the first given letter on a crossing of the most crossed word; the daily puzzle the same for the same date and language and different otherwise, a month of dailies valid, unique and quick; slots, placed words, solved check (a second valid filling counts), wrong letters, cursor moves; the saved session check; times and streaks; merge symmetric, associative, idempotent, fixed point, inputs untouched, daily / Free rules, reset, bad entries drop.
- **Verification (Chromium, real shell + real `sync.js` + mock Dropbox, ~85 checks; EN desktop, EL phone 390×844, EL 360×740):** EN daily 13×13 solved by typing; a wrong letter marked by Check word and cleared by Backspace; check all with nothing typed explains; struck-through words; result, check, words and stats dialogs centred; Free 17×17 with a revealed letter (no record) and 9×9 with a new record; Tab / Shift+Tab; Shift+N with Undo; a theme puzzle; Greek typed by key position on an English layout; the Greek daily solved on a phone by taps and the on-screen keyboard; the direction key and a second tap switch across / down; the EN daily shows "solved on another device" on the second device with the same grid; two devices converge, idle cycles upload 0; a statistics reset reaches the other device (the daily becomes playable again); R28 toasts on a solved daily and on a size click in Daily; resume after reload (letters and cursor); no overflow and no small targets at 360×740 (all three sizes), 768×1024, 1024×600, 1280×800; dark and light themes; no page errors.
- **NOT tested:** real Dropbox, Firefox / Safari, a real phone, a screen reader.

#### Xeri v1.0.0 (new app, Games) on the shared `cardkit/`

- **New app `xeri/`** ("Xeri" / "Ξερή"): the Greek card game, you against the computer, drawn with the shared `cardkit/` module (loaded from `../cardkit/`, shipped and precached with Solitaire). **Rules:** 52 cards; 6 cards each (option 4) and 4 open cards on the table; a Jack dealt to the table goes back into the deck (at a random place, never on top) and another card is drawn; new hands from the deck until it runs out; you lead the first deal, then the lead alternates. Same rank as the top table card takes the whole table; a Jack always takes it (not an empty table). **Xeri** (taking a lone card) 10 points, Jack on a lone Jack 20; Jack on a lone other card is a plain capture (option: a xeri, 10). At the end of the deal the cards left on the table go to the last capturer (nobody captured: the dealer). Deal points: most cards 3 (none on 26–26), each K, Q, J, 10 one point except 10♦ two, 2♣ one, plus xeri: 21 a deal without xeri, 18 on a tie. Match to 51 (options 101 or one deal); a tie at or past the target plays another deal; one deal can end in a draw. Rule changes apply from the next match (at once when nothing is played yet).
- **Computer, 3 levels:** Easy (a random card; when it can capture it does so 3 times in 4) · Medium (rules of thumb: takes points and xeri, keeps Jacks for bigger piles, avoids leaving a lone card, prefers a card whose twin it holds or whose rank is mostly out) · Hard (counts every open card and weighs the odds that your next card, from the cards it has not seen, takes what it leaves, xeri included; spends a Jack only when the pile is worth it; at the last card it knows the leftovers go to the last capturer). Measured over 300 single deals: Hard 30.2 – 11.0 Easy, Medium 25.9 – 12.5 Easy, Hard 23.1 – 15.3 Medium. **It never reads your hand:** every decision gets only `aiView()` (its own hand, the table, the captured cards, counts), and nothing in its code section receives a game object (checked by the tests). A short pause and a slide-in show what it played.
- **Play:** tap a card, drag it onto the table, or keys 1–6 (Enter / Space on a focused card, arrows between cards); N new match (Undo toast over a match under way, R14); a level change starts a new match. Shows the top table card with up to three under it and the pile count, the deck with cards left, deal number and target, both sides' captured cards and xeri counters, match points and whose turn. A capture slides the pile to the taker; a xeri flashes "Xeri! +10". Centered end-of-deal dialog with the breakdown side by side (cards, most cards, figures & 10s, 10♦, 2♣, xeri, deal points, match) and a match result dialog (final score, deal by deal, your record on that level); a Next deal / Match result button also stays on the table. A refused tap or key explains itself (R28). Rules dialog: target, cards per hand, Jack on a lone card. Sound off by default; optional soft card click. Reduced motion: no slides or pops. Screen readers: every card is announced ("Computer played 7 of hearts, captured 5 cards" / «Ο υπολογιστής έπαιξε 7 κούπα, μάζεψε 5 φύλλα»; xeri, new hands, leftovers, who leads), with cardkit's EN/EL card names; hand cards, table and deck have labels.
- **Data:** XERI v1 (Part IV), same shape as Connect 4; the match in progress resumes on the device (Part III).
- **Tests:** `tests/xeri.test.js` (15): the deal (6 + 6 + 4, no Jack on the table, Jacks put back, 4-card hands), refills; capture rules, xeri, Jack on Jack, the Jack option; the last capturer; card points; 21 / 18 + xeri over 120 full matches; match end (target, tie plays on, one-deal draw); every level plays only its own cards over whole matches; the computer never reads your hand or the deck (aiView fields, no hidden card in it, same choice when your hand and the deck are reshuffled, code structure); xeri / keep-Jacks / card-counting picks; Hard and Medium beat Easy; stored-match validation; merge symmetric, associative, idempotent, canonical, reset and bad rows drop, totals, bumpCell.
- **Verification (Chromium, real shell + real `sync.js` + mock Dropbox, EN desktop / EL phone at 360×740):** full matches to 51 on Easy (desktop, with mouse drags, taps and keys) and Medium (Greek phone), Hard one deal and Hard to 51; deal and result dialogs centered; records land in the slice; rules dialog (one deal); 768×1024 and 1280×800; New match Undo toast restores the match; the match resumes after a reload; Greek ARIA labels for table and hand; records dialog in the light theme; reduced motion + sound on; two devices converge, idle cycles upload 0, a reset on the phone reaches the desktop; no overflow, no small targets, no page errors.
- **NOT tested:** real Dropbox, Firefox / Safari, a real phone (touch drag feel), a real screen reader, sound output.

#### Device Info v1.0.0 (new app, category System)

- **New app `device/`** ("Device Info" / "Πληροφορίες συσκευής"), category **System / Σύστημα** (`category.system` already in `translations.js`). Eight foldable cards (fold state device-local): **Storage** (local-storage total and % of an approximate 5 M-character browser limit, warning above 80 %; `navigator.storage.estimate()` for files, databases and offline copies with Chromium's `usageDetails`; persistent or not, with "Ask for protection"; Cache Storage caches with item counts), **Space per app** (local storage grouped by owner, largest first, 10 shown then "Show all", a row opens the app through `__orosOpenApp`), **Battery** (`getBattery`, Chromium only; says so elsewhere), **Network** (online/offline live, `navigator.connection` where present, no speed test), **Sync** (connected, unlocked, pending changes, interval, last cloud backup copy, automatic file backup mode/last/folder; getters only, never the account or passphrase), **Screen**, **orOS & browser** (version from `oros-last-version`, offline cache version, approximate browser/OS from the user agent), **Browser features** (11 features, each missing one names the installed apps it affects; notification and location permission shown without asking). **Copy report**: the same rows as plain text, EN or EL, no stored values.
  - **Battery truth (2026-10-11):** never show a number the browser may have made up. Brave always reports 100 % + charging → "this browser hides the battery" notice, no number. Any other reading exactly equal to the spec default (level 1, charging, chargingTime 0, dischargingTime Infinity) → "may be a placeholder" notice until the browser fires a real battery event (Chromium hands out that default when it has no data; seen on Chris's phone as 100 % while unplugged at 87 %). Rule lives in `DeviceCore.batteryState`.
- **`core.js`** (UMD, shared with `tests/device.test.js`): `keyOwner` (slice registry first, then the longest app-id prefix, then aliases such as `wx`→weather, `cal`→calendar, `pet*`→Pet World, `alarms`→Time; `oros-wallpaper` / `-art` and engine keys → orOS), `sizeByOwner` (UTF-16 bytes of key + value), `cacheOwner`, `formatBytes`, `parseUA`, `featureImpact`, `buildReport`.
- **Core:** `apps.json` entry (System), `sw.js` precache (5), `ICONS.device` (phone with an "i"), `translations.js` `app.device` + `menu.deviceInfo` (EN + EL), a "Device info" row in the orOS menu before "About orOS", Tests workflow paths `device/**`. `APP_VERSION` 0.47.00. Notifications: none (exemption from Checklist B item 9).
- **Tests:** new `tests/device.test.js` (14): key owners (ids, prefixes, aliases, shell keys, registry, every apps.json id), sizes and order, bytes, percent, caches, user agents (Chrome, Edge, Samsung, Safari iOS/macOS/iPadOS hint, Chrome iOS, Firefox, ChromeOS), feature impact, report text, the app writes only its own prefs key and uses no HTML injection or network beyond `apps.json`, EN/EL string parity.
- **Verification (Chromium, real shell with the release applied, mock Dropbox):** EN desktop 1280, EL phone at 360 px, sync connected and not connected; every card filled; copy report reaches the clipboard and holds no token or passphrase; folding survives reopening; a row opens To-Do; going offline updates the Network card live; the menu row opens the app; no horizontal overflow, no small targets, no page errors.
- **NOT tested:** a real phone, Safari / iOS and Firefox (battery, connection, `estimate` and `persist` behave differently there), real Dropbox, a real installed PWA.

### 2026-10-10 — hotfix 0.48.02 — sync: no endless re-uploads, failure reason visible
- **Report:** Chris, 2026-10-09 20:42 UTC: sync never completes and shows "failed".
- **Fixes:** Podcasts (`podcasts/core.js` `normQueue`) returned an empty queue without `sh: {}` for missing data, so `mergePodcasts(x, null)` (the store path) dropped a field every merge added: on every device with Podcasts data, every pull marked the engine dirty and every reconcile re-uploaded identical content, for ever (same one-line fix as Podcasts PR #120). Engine guard SY-L1 in `sync.js` (`settleApplied`): a slice whose stored content equals the cloud copy after a pull is not stale, whatever shape the merge returned. Failure reason SY-L2 (`sync.js` passes the error to `onAutoSync` listeners and logs it; `shell.js` `syncErrText`, `state.syncAutoErr`; Settings snapshot shows it too).
- **Tests:** `tests/sync-loop.test.js` (fails on the old engine), `tests/podcasts.test.js` store == merge for an empty queue. Real shell (Chromium, mock Dropbox): two devices with a Podcasts subscription uploaded twice per sync round before, zero while idle after; all 97 apps on two devices sync with no failure and no idle upload; a 503 shows "Sync failed — check your connection (upload failed: 503)" in the dot tooltip and the menu, gone after the next success.
- **Open:** the exact error on Chris's devices was not reproduced (the mock never fails like the real Dropbox); 0.48.02 shows it, so the next report names it.
- **NOT tested:** a real phone, Safari / iOS, real Dropbox.

### 2026-10-10 — hotfix 0.52.02 — sync "Browser storage is full": retired snapshots leave localStorage
- **Report:** Chris, 2026-10-10: sync says "Browser storage is full"; Device info showed localStorage at 97% (9.7 MB), 7.0 MB of it "orOS (desktop, settings, sync)".
- **Cause:** the rolling snapshots retired in 0.38 (`oros-auto-snapshots`, up to 5 full DB copies) were never removed from devices that had them. With the data of the new apps the shared quota ran out, the sync mailbox write failed and SY-Q1 paused sync (correctly, nothing lost).
- **Fix (SY-Q2):** `shell.js` `legacyLsMove()` at boot (`initSyncIntegration`): `oros-auto-snapshots` → IndexedDB `oros-legacy` / `kv`, then removed from localStorage, then `kickAutoEngine()`. Zero-loss: removal only after the IndexedDB transaction completed. `factoryResetPending()` deletes `oros-legacy` too.
- **Verification (Chromium, real shell, mock Dropbox):** device B with a 4.9M-character `oros-auto-snapshots` and another device's 600 KB app in its mailbox: old code → push fails `storage-full`; new code → key moved (4,940,477 characters in IndexedDB), pull + push succeed. Tests 1025/1025.
- **Open:** the 7 MB on Chris's device is inferred to be this key (it is the only known shell-owned key of that size); if Device info still shows several MB for orOS after 0.52.02, the next suspect is the sync mailbox `oros-remote-carry`.
- **NOT tested:** a real phone, Safari / iOS, real Dropbox, Chris's own device.

### 2026-10-10 — Mail phase 2: write, reply, forward and send (#154) — 0.66.00
- Mail can now write, reply, reply to all and forward (plain text), with a per-account signature and an offline Outbox. Messages go out through the account's SMTP server via the relay; a copy is filed in Sent (best effort).
- Relay: new `relay/smtp.js` (465 implicit TLS, 587 STARTTLS required, AUTH PLAIN with LOGIN fallback, dot-stuffing); new ops `smtpcheck` and `send` (rcpt 1–50, raw ≤ 380 KB); IMAP `append`; message-carrying requests up to 512 KB, others keep 64 KB. Auto-deploys from main.
- App: new pure `mail/compose.js` (RFC 2047 headers, Bcc in the envelope only, In-Reply-To / References, reply / reply-all / forward drafts); compose dialog, Reply / Reply all / Forward, shortcuts c r a f; SMTP login check when an account is saved; IndexedDB `oros-mail` v2 adds the `outbox` store (auto-retry only when the relay was unreachable, never after a timeout).
- Deep link: the single `__orosOpenAt("mail", …)` receiver also takes `{compose:{to?, subject, body}}`, which opens a prefilled draft that never sends by itself.
- Data: MAIL v1 accounts may carry `sig` (signature, synced). A device on the previous version can drop a signature when it pushes the same account, until it updates.
- Tests: new tests/mail-send.test.js (compose, scripted SMTP 465/587, refused recipient, wrong password, IMAP APPEND); tests/mail.test.js extended. Help pages EN/EL and relay README updated.
- Not tested: a real SMTP server (Papaki / pmail.gr), the deployed Worker, Safari, a real phone.

### 2026-10-12 — Stock v1.0.0 (new app, Business) (#205) — 1.04.00

- **New app `stock/`** ("Stock" / «Απόθεμα»), category **Business**: business inventory, distinct from the home Storage app. Tabs **Products** (totals: products, stock value, to reorder, out of stock; search that takes a USB / Bluetooth scanner; filters, category, sort; product sheet with quantity, average cost, value, prices, days left, full movement history), **Movements** (day by day, type and period filters, void), **Reorder** (low products by supplier, suggested quantity, Copy list, Receive this order) and **Suppliers** (also from Contacts).
- **The quantity is never stored:** it is the sum of the movements (receive, sell, customer return, return to supplier, loss, stock count, correction; several lines each; ref, supplier, unit cost / price, total). Two devices selling at once never lose a sale through sync; a stock count stores the difference, so a concurrent sale still counts. Movements are voided, never edited or deleted; a product with movements is archived, never deleted (and survives a delete racing a sale).
- **Low stock:** shell engine `stockCheckTick` (one notice when a product reaches its minimum, opens it or Reorder), per-device switch.
- **CSV:** import of products from the own export, a WooCommerce product export (EN / EL headers; variable parents skipped, variations kept; categories "A > B" → B) or any sheet with known column names; match by SKU then name; optional "set quantities from the file" as ONE stock count. Export of products and movements (formula-injection guard, `;` + comma decimals in Greek). JSON backup / restore (a merge).
- **Schema:** STOCK v1 (Part IV); device-local keys (Part III).
- **Core:** `apps.json` entry (Business, search provider), `sw.js` precache (6 + 2 help pages), `ICONS.stock`, `translations.js` `app.stock`, `stock/core.js` in `index.html`, engine in `shell.js`, KNOWN_APPS + DL_BRIDGES, Tests workflow paths `stock/**`. The app landed in PR #205 with its tests and help pages; this release commit adds the registration.
- **Tests:** new `tests/stock.test.js` (17): normalizers, line signs per type, quantity under concurrent sales, count difference with a concurrent sale, merge (symmetric, idempotent, void wins, tombstones, resurrection, an item with movements survives a delete, tombstone expiry, hostile input incl. "constructor" ids), average cost, low list + suggestions + notices once, out rate, history, codes, number parsing, CSV parser and exports, WooCommerce import, Greek round trip, search provider.
- **Verification (Chromium, real shell + real `sync.js` + mock Dropbox, EN 1280 × 800 and EL 360 × 760):** see the PR.
- **NOT tested:** a real phone, a real USB / Bluetooth scanner (simulated by typing + Enter), Safari / iOS, real Dropbox.

### 2026-10-12 — Newsletter phase 2 (#243) — 1.31.00
- Newsletter v1.1.0 (phase 2). The sending engine moved into newsletter/engine.js, shared by the app and the shell.
  - newsletter/runner.js runs the engine in the shell, so sending, scheduled starts and Inbox checks (every 10 minutes) work with the app closed while orOS is open.
  - The runner owns the slice "newsletter", always live. It waits for the first sync merge, a sync failure plus 15 s, or 60 s before it sends.
  - Every writer merge-writes through C.mergeNewsletter, so the app, the shell and other tabs never undo each other.
  - Web Locks "oros-newsletter-send" and "oros-newsletter-inbox" stop two windows of one device from working at once. A fresh re-read before each message skips anyone who left or was already sent to.
  - Notices use ns "newsletter": issue sent, paused, scheduled issue started, and new subscribers, unsubscribes and bounces from the Inbox.
  - Scheduled issues have st "sched" with when, and lock.dev is the scheduling device, which holds the passwords. Only that device starts them. Users can cancel or send now.
  - Segments (segs: name, tags, any/all, language) are per list. An issue's seg wins over its tags. A deleted segment gives an empty audience, never everyone, and the preflight check flags it as "segGone".
  - Templates (tpls).
  - Bilingual issues: l2 = {lang, subj, pre, fmt, blocks, md}. Each subscriber gets their language (their own, else the list's). Preview and test cover both versions, and preflight checks both.
  - CRM import reads oros-crm-data through the shell's OrosCrmCore.norm, read only. CRM status and tags become tags. The basis is "customer" only when every pick is an active or past customer, else double opt-in. Source "crm".
  - Today provider newsletter/today.js.
  - Device state (dev, used, inbox) moved from oros-newsletter-prefs to oros-newsletter-dev, migrated on first read. Paused reasons are stored as codes and translated on display.
- Not tested: a real sending provider, real phones, Safari, a background tab over hours.

### 2026-10-12 — Studio effects: NULL JSFX (#246) — 1.32.00
- Studio v1.1.0: NULL JSFX effects.
  - studio/nullfx/ is the web build of NULL JSFX (MIT), copied from koulaxizis/null-jsfx `web/` (translator web/tools/eel2js.js turns each JSFX's EEL2 into static JS ahead of time; nothing is evaluated at runtime). Null test against ysfx below 1e-6 for every effect.
  - Effects run in one AudioWorklet processor per chain (`null-fx-chain`, nullfx/runtime/null-worklet.js), on each track (clip sources -> chain -> gain -> pan) and on the master.
  - studio/fx.js: catalog, Effects dialog (search, categories, bypass, order, remove, up to 8 per chain), the effect's own @gfx interface drawn on a canvas (nullfx/runtime/null-gfx.js, mouse + wheel), "All controls" with every slider, live meters while playing.
  - Latency compensation: a track whose chain delays less than the slowest track's starts its clips later by the difference (not a DelayNode: Chromium drops a DelayNode's tail once its source ends). Export renders the extra samples and cuts them from the start; recording placement adds the master chain's delay.
  - Convolution IR files: picked by the user (≤ 20 MB), written to `/internal/Studio/fx/`, travel through Vault Drive like the audio.
  - Data: projects and tracks gain `fx: [{u, id, on, s: {slider: value}, f?: {slider: path}}]` (≤ 8), normalised by C.normFx. Unknown effect ids are kept (a newer device's effect) and do not play.
  - Not offered yet: Sidechain Ducker (needs a second input routed). Effects reset (@init) at every play, as in REAPER.
- Credits: CREDITS.md, shell credits, Bible credits register. Not tested: sound on real devices and phones, Safari, offline use after precache.

### 2026-10-12 — Newsletter phase 3A: RSS to e-mail, past issues (#249) — 1.35.00
- Newsletter v1.2.0 (phase 3A).
  - RSS to e-mail: new collection `rss` (up to 20 feeds) per list: url, name, every day/week (weekday)/month (the 1st), hour, mode draft|send, max articles (1–20), segment, on.
    - A feed runs only on the device that set it up (`dev`), from the shell runner every 10 minutes (first after 30 s), under the Web Lock "oros-newsletter-rss".
    - Due feeds are marked as run before fetching, so two windows or a crash never run one twice. Offline, timeouts and relay errors give the slot back for the next round; a bad feed waits for its next slot.
    - Articles newer than `last` (the newest article already used), newest first, become a Markdown issue: a heading, an https picture, the snippet as plain text and a "Read more" button per article. Text from the feed can never become a link, picture or button.
    - Mode "send" starts sending only when the pre-send check finds no errors, else it leaves a draft. Notices: "New draft from RSS" and "Sending (RSS)".
    - Feeds are read through the Reader's own network layer (direct, else the relay's "web" op). Newsletter never edits feeds/.
  - Past issues: Settings › Import past issues… reads a .zip export or .md/.html/.csv/.json files (newsletter/archive.js, pure, no DOM, never runs anything in them).
    - HTML becomes Markdown. Scripts, styles, comments, javascript: links, data: pictures and tracking pixels are dropped.
    - Import as past issues (st sent, `imp: 1`, n 0, nobody gets an e-mail) or as drafts. Ids are a hash of subject, date and length, so the same file twice adds nothing.
    - Capped at 500 issues and about 2.5 MB of Newsletter data in all.
- Not tested: real feeds over a real relay, a real sending provider, real Buttondown / MailerLite exports, phones, Safari.

### 2026-10-12 — Newsletter phase 3B: sign-up form, one-click unsubscribe (#251, relay #250) — 1.36.00
- Newsletter v1.3.0 (phase 3B).
  - Lists gain `form`: `{k, sec, priv (RSA-OAEP-256 private JWK), back, dev, at}`. It is registered with the relay op `nl` (`reg`), which keeps only the public key and the secret's SHA-256.
  - The Inbox check (shell runner, every 10 minutes, and before sends) first pulls the waiting rows on the collecting device (`form.dev`), applies them on fresh data, merge-writes, then acks:
    - sign-ups (decrypted AES-GCM + RSA-OAEP) become pending subscribers with src "form" and basis optin, so the engine sends the confirmation request;
    - one-click unsubscribes (`tok` = token() without "nl-") turn the subscriber off.
  - Issues of a list with a form carry `List-Unsubscribe: <https://relay/nl/u/k/tok>, <mailto:…>` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`. The footer link opens the relay's one-click page.
  - The UI lives in the Subscribe link dialog: form HTML (no script, honeypot, list language), thank-you page (https), Collect here, and Turn the form off (relay `drop`). Deleting a list drops its form.
  - A relay without D1 (`nostore`) is not an Inbox error.
- Relay side merged in #250 (relay/newsletter.js, `/nl/*`, op `nl`); until Chris creates the D1 database and its binding `NL_DB` is added, the form pages answer 503 "not available". Not tested: the live relay, real Gmail one-click, phones, Safari.

### 2026-10-12 — Newsletter phase 3C: HTTP API sending (#254, relay #253) — 1.38.00
- Relay (merged in #253): op `papi` (relay/papi.js). It has fixed hosts per provider, an exact path and query allowlist, at most 40 requests, 4 MB per call, 6 at a time, no redirects, and the key is never stored or echoed.
- Newsletter v1.4.0 (phase 3C).
  - Sending accounts gain `via: "smtp"|"api"` and `dom` (Mailgun). The API key is device-local in IDB, like the SMTP passwords.
  - The engine sends API accounts in batches of up to 10 (the daily limit left, about 1 MB; a whole call that fails at the relay is retried with half the batch: Mail thread review on #253, Workers CPU limit). Each answer counts on its own:
    - a refused address bounces;
    - 5xx or timeout is retried;
    - 401/403 pauses the issue with "apikey";
    - 429 waits a minute.
  - The 10-minute check also reads the provider's events and applies them to that account's lists. It reads hard bounces, spam complaints and unsubscribes, but no soft bounces, and an event older than a later sign-up is ignored.
  - The pre-send check adds `apiImg`: Brevo's API can't carry inline pictures.
  - Fix: with no Mail Inbox account, the check time is still recorded.
- Newsletter phase 3 complete. Not tested: real Brevo / Postmark / SendGrid / Mailgun accounts, the live relay, phones, Safari.

Room = SHA-256 of the code; key = PBKDF2(code, 100k) → AES-GCM, so the relay sees only ciphertext. Both sides meet in a relay room, then switch to a direct WebRTC data channel (STUN stun.cloudflare.com); when that fails (VPN, different networks) they stay on the relay. Reconnects by itself; one remote at a time.
- Remote console (from 360px): transport, position bar, tempo, per-track fader / pan / M / S / R / FX on-off / meter, master. Every command is validated and clamped on the PC and becomes a normal edit (undo, sync). Not in v1: effect windows on the remote (phase 2), TURN, offline pairing.
- Relay: `/rt/` meeting rooms (relay/remote.js, Durable Object `REMOTE`: max 2 sockets, 16 KB frames, 400 frames / 10 s, idle close 120 s, bare "ping" auto-answered, nothing stored). Reviewed and approved by the relay owner (Mail thread). Not tested: the live relay deploy (containers cannot reach workers.dev), real tablets / phones, VPN paths, Safari.

    - `devCommand` sets what each role may ask.
    - `clockOffset` keeps the shortest round trip, so the device clock equals the PC's.

- **Changes:**

Research of WiseStamp, HubSpot, Newoldstamp, MySignature, Exclaimer, MySigMail: adopted short reply version, dated banner, CTA button, disclaimers, vCard QR, team CSV, client checks, dark preview; rejected click analytics and hosted images (tracking, free-forever rule).

Tasks move to another list with their subtasks (task window, quick menu, or several with Select; Undo). An older client drops items of unknown ax.k (documented).
  - Business wave 46. Quote takes any ISO currency, formatted per currency, can show the total in another currency at the ECB rate (shared Units helper), and "Send via email" attaches the PDF in Mail. Acceptance by link: the quote travels in the URL fragment to quote/accept.html, the client accepts with a name and sends back an answer link; a random token plus a SHA-256 fingerprint detect an edited or outdated link (integrity, not identity; no server); Make invoice follows. Invoices: own "Pay online" link (Stripe Payment Link or any https page) as link and QR on the PDF and a line in the email; no payment key. Timesheet: time away from the Idle Detection API (after permission) and device sleep, with Keep / Take it out / Take out and stop, also from a new menu on the top-bar timer chip. Stock 1.7: point of sale (grid, search, barcode or camera, cart, price lists, payment method, change, 58/80 mm receipt, daily Z report with close and void); sales/pls/zs written only when used, sales unioned by id, void wins.
  - Passwords becomes a password manager (wave 47). Encrypted vault behind its own master password: Argon2id (hash-wasm, MIT; PBKDF2-SHA-256 600k fallback) wraps a random vault key, whole vault sealed with AES-256-GCM, one-time recovery key. Only sealed data syncs, in its own passwords slice; while unlocked entries merge one by one by mtime with tombstones, deterministic so devices settle without re-uploading; unopenable data and vaults from a newer orOS kept untouched. Entries with usernames, URLs, notes, tags, custom fields and RFC 6238 TOTP (secret, otpauth link or QR). Import KeePass KDBX 3.1/4 (AES-KDF or Argon2, AES or ChaCha20, key files), Bitwarden JSON, CSV; export KDBX 4 and Bitwarden JSON. Auto-lock on inactivity and when hidden; clipboard cleared after 30 s. Generator and strength check stay and can fill an entry.
  - Wave 48 Today and Assistant. Today becomes a customisable widget screen: the four sections plus Clock, Weather, Water, Habits, Upcoming events and To-dos, moved by drag or arrows, small or wide, added and removed in Customise; layout stays on the device (oros-today-layout, never synced), defaults to the old screen; a row shows in one widget only (today/layout.js). The Assistant can change what the user already has (change_item: complete, reopen, reschedule, update, delete in To-Do, Calendar, Budget and Bookmarks): only items shared in the conversation, always behind a before/after card and the user's Apply, written with each app's own stamps and tombstones, an item changed meanwhile left alone, Undo in memory, only applied/not applied goes back to the model (assistant/edits.js). Microphone button turns speech into text in the message box (Web Speech API, EN/EL, hidden where unsupported), with a first-use note that the browser may send audio to its speech service.
  - Games wave 49: Sudoku (Medium), Nonogram (10x10), Flow Free (7x7) and Minesweeper (Intermediate, one try) gain a Daily puzzle, the same for everyone on the same date, made offline from the date, with streaks and spoiler-free Share; Wordle and Crossword share through the same helper. New shared gamekit/daily.js (date -> seed, mulberry32, counting clock, streaks, share). New Games app Game Center (gamecenter/, «Κέντρο παιχνιδιών»): today's six dailies, 15 computed achievements and per-game stats for 37 games, read-only, no slice. Sudoku Killer (cages, uniqueness proven by a cage-sum solver). Solitaire Pyramid. Daily results live in each game's own slice (days{}, better result wins, reset stamp drops).

Offline puzzle trainer: puzzles by theme near your rating, Hint, Solution, retry failed, history, Glicko puzzle rating computed from first attempts; history syncs as pz/pbr (join, reset stamp). Openings named from the Lichess chess-openings list (CC0) by position (hidden in live Lichess games), and an openings trainer. A host's New game asks first while a game is under way.

Maps settings > Offline maps downloads the area in view from the newest Protomaps build of OpenStreetMap (vector PMTiles cut with range requests, no key), size per detail level (zoom 10/12/14/15) first, then progress with pause/resume (also after reload), cancel, update and delete, storage used and free. Packs live in OPFS maps-packs/, device-only, removed by factory reset (shell wipeMapPacks). Own canvas renderer draws them as the "Offline map (downloaded)" layer, switching on by itself when offline over a pack. Search answers from the packs' names (places, streets, POIs, addresses; Greek and Latin letters) without a connection. Real Protomaps servers untested from the sandbox.

### 2026-10-14 — Wiki, wave 2: pictures, infobox, references, tables, PDF — 2.01.00
- **Changes:**
  - Pictures in articles: from this device, the camera (phone) or Files; stored once by `designkit/assets.js` on the orOS disk (Vault Drive), named in the text as `[[File:<sha256>.jpg|left|200px|Caption]]` (EL `Αρχείο:`); tap to open large. `{{gallery … }}` shows several.
  - Infobox `{{infobox … }}` / `{{πλαίσιο … }}` with title, picture, caption and facts, edited through a form; floats right, on top at 360px.

- **Decisions:**
  - Pictures reuse designkit/assets.js (same files and dedupe as Atelier and Email Signature); the slice keeps only ids, so pictures never count against localStorage (R30).
  - Safety: the renderer writes `data-img` only; the app sets `src` from a blob: URL of the disk file, so markup can never point an image at the web. Ids must be `<64 hex>.jpg|png`.
  - Wikipedia-like template words (`{{infobox}}`, `[[File:]]`) with Greek aliases, so pasted habits work and the text stays plain.
  - No new library (jsPDF, Noto and assets.js are already vendored and precached); no credits change.
- **Schema:** none (WIKI v1 unchanged; Part III row notes v1.1.0).
- **Files:** `wiki/{core.js, wiki.js, wiki.css, index.html, search.js, pdf.js, help.en.txt, help.el.txt}`, `tests/wiki-rich.test.js`; `sw.js` precache `wiki/pdf.js`.

### 2026-10-14 — Contacts: split Google " ::: " values, no duplicates on re-import (#369) — 2.20.01
- The Google CSV import splits phones, e-mails and websites that Google joins with " ::: " into separate rows (they were stored as one value and cut at 40 characters). Values stored that way by older imports are split back on every load, with no device-only data, so all devices reach the same result.
- A re-import skips rows whose details are already inside one contact when the names agree, so earlier combined rows don't come back as duplicates; two people who share a number stay separate (BR-CT-IMPORT). Undo keeps the first earlier version of a contact two rows merged into.
- Files: `contacts/contacts.js` (`splitMulti` in `sanitizeContact`, CSV reader), `contacts/importplan.js` (`plan()`).

### 2026-10-14 — Contacts: find photos online (#374) — 2.22.00
- Contacts › Find photos: for contacts without a photo, on request only, orOS looks up each contact's own e-mail addresses (at most 3) on Gravatar, then Libravatar. Only the SHA-256 hash of the address is sent (`d=404`, no generated pictures, no cookies, no referrer). Found pictures are listed with their source and address, all ticked; "Use the ticked photos" sets them as the 128×128 contact photo (never replacing an existing one), and Undo restores.

  - Tests: new `tests/drive-android.test.js`; full suite green; Android CI build green with the AAR; Chromium Files check. Not tested: a real phone, the F-Droid build without Drive, real Dropbox.

Settings › Screen lock (section `lock`, scope device, search topic), menu row "Lock orOS", single-app menu item, "Lock now" also locks other tabs. DL-1: `?standalone` redirects to the shell while the lock is on.

### 2026-10-27 — Sticky Notes: Fold and More no longer make a new note vanish (#648) — 4.02.02

### 2026-10-28 — Layout: Rebuild a print PDF (LY-RB, wave R1) — 4.09.00
- **Changes:** new `layout/rebuild.js` (`LY_REBUILD`): `Open file` › `Rebuild a print PDF (with its pictures)…` picks the print PDF plus optional original pictures and texts (.txt/.md/.html, used for dehyphenation) and builds a new document: page size and bleed from TrimBox / BleedBox (pdf-lib), facing pages, margins per side, body size and line pitch, paragraph and character styles (snapped, Greek names in EL), page numbers as their own frames (`ps-rbpn`), pictures as frames with text wrap beside ≥ 3-line frames, original files matched by thumbnail, rotated text (spines) as turned frames, everything else one locked background picture per page over the bleed (re-rendered at up to 300 dpi). Text colours are measured from the strongest pixels of a render without text; near-black / near-paper colours snap to the seed swatches. A report dialog (lines in place, pictures / originals, styles, fonts with their tracking, first page number, pages where lines moved with buttons that go there). Cancellable progress toast; nothing is added when cancelled. `layout/pdfin.js`: `drawnOps(page, ops)` uses the operator list PDF.js actually drew (render intent) instead of `getOperatorList()`'s, whose indices differ on tagged PDFs (InDesign), so picture frames and the background filter hit the right operators; its browser helpers are exported for rebuild.js.

### 2026-10-29 — Layout: line fitting reads print PDFs that lose their accents or the file's first pages (LY-FIT) — 4.35.01
- **What:** a Scribus file opened with its print PDF now takes the PDF's line breaks also when the PDF's text comes out without accents. Some Greek fonts carry the tonos as a glyph of its own, so PDF.js reads "καλά" as "καλα"; `align` compared character by character and found almost no line (on Chris's private books: 2 to 27 lines of several thousand), so those files opened without fitting. `linefit.js` `norm` now compares without combining marks (NFKC, then NFD minus U+0300–U+036F, U+0384, U+0385) on both sides; a story character whose compatibility form has a space (U+0384 → space + acute) adds nothing. The story's own text is untouched. Second cause of the same symptom: an e-book file with covers before the text and a print PDF without them (file page i is PDF page i − 2), so every frame was given the wrong page's lines. `rebuild.js` `matchPdf` now, when the page counts differ, finds the shift (`pageShift`, −8…8: the shift under which the most distinct words of 4+ letters of our laid-out pages are on the PDF's; taken only when it is ≥ 8 shared words and more than 1.5× the unshifted count) and reports it as `rep.shift`. Measured on the private corpus (outside the repo): five books went from 1–2 matched lines to 97–99% (e.g. 4639 of 4744, 1408 of 1434), one book whose PDF is another edition stays unfitted.
- **Files:** `layout/linefit.js` (`key` exported), `layout/rebuild.js` (`pageShift`), `tests/layout-linefit.test.js`, `help/topics/whatsnew.{en,el}.txt`, `shell.js` APP_VERSION 4.35.01, this Bible (Part IV LY-FIT, this entry).
- **Tests:** `tests/layout-linefit.test.js` (new: the two-page matchPdf case with every PDF span stripped of accents: every line matched and in place, the story keeps its accents; fails before the change; a file with 3 extra first pages: shift 3, every line matched and in place, equal pages give no shift). Private corpus (outside the repo): Scribus books whose print PDFs read without tonos, before and after, in headless Chromium through `LY.io.openSla`.

### 2026-10-29 — Layout: Rebuild a print PDF keeps lines on their baselines with matched fonts, list bullets, books up to 999 pages (LY-RB) — 4.38.01
- **What:** found while converting Chris's private books (outside the repo) from their print PDFs. (1) When a PDF font was matched to a family (LY-FONT), `build` placed each frame from the first baseline minus the family's ascent, but text.js sets lines with the stand-in's ascent, so every line of such a book sat a few points low and the check found almost none in place (two books: 3 of 2655 and 6 of 3142 lines; after: 2622 and 3125). `rebuild.js` now uses `lineKey` (the stand-in's font key) for the frame top and bottom, page-number frames and rotated frames. (2) A list's bullet set smaller than its item (InDesign, Word: "●" at 5 pt before 9 pt text) was a line of its own and became a 5 pt wide frame that showed nothing; `toLines` now lets a line that is only a bullet (`MARKER`) take the text on its baseline whatever its size, and the line takes the item's baseline (a book with lists: 54 % → 63 % of lines in place). (3) `MAX_PAGES` was 400, so a 516-page novel was cut; it is now the model's `M.MAX_PAGES` (999); measured: the 516-page book rebuilds whole, 98 % of its lines in place.
- **Not changed (known):** text that wraps around pictures in narrow justified columns (one book stays at 41 % in place) and books over 999 pages (split them first).
- **Files:** `layout/rebuild.js`, `tests/layout-fonts.test.js`, `tests/layout-rebuild.test.js`, `help/topics/whatsnew.{en,el}.txt`, `shell.js` APP_VERSION 4.38.01, this Bible (Part IV LY-FONT, this entry).
- **Tests:** `tests/layout-fonts.test.js` (new: a matched family whose ascent is 4 pt taller than the stand-in's: every line in place; fails before the change), `tests/layout-rebuild.test.js` (new: a smaller, raised bullet starts its item's line on the item's baseline; a big title beside small type stays two lines).

### 2026-11-01 — Studio Remote: Remote for orOS Studio, the Android app (STUDIO-RA) (#761) — 4.93.00
- **What:** Chris asked (NULL JSFX project, 2026-11-01 12:53, "Προτάσεις: ναι σε όλα") for an Android APK to control orOS Studio, kept with orOS, the same orOS signing key, on GitHub releases, F-Droid, Droid-ify and Obtainium. **Remote for orOS Studio** (`online.useoros.studioremote`) is a new kind of Android flavour, a *page app* (`android/page-apps.json`): the TWA opens `/studio/remote/` (own `manifest.webmanifest`, scope `/studio/remote/`, catches only links under it), which frames `studio/index.html?remote`. In remote mode `studio.js` `bootRemote()` builds only the effects catalog, the remote and the i18n: no project is read or written, nothing syncs, no audio starts.
- **Changes (remote side, `studio/remote.js` section 6, any browser):** `Scan the QR code` in the join dialog (BarcodeDetector, else jsQR from `vendor/jsqr` like the QR app; 150 ms frames; the camera stops on a code or when the dialog closes); Screen Wake Lock while the console shows (asked again when the page comes back); `navigator.vibrate` ticks on fader grab, passing 0 dB or an end, M/S/R and the transport; `Link.kick()` tries the room at once when the page becomes visible; the last code and the remote's id (`rid`) for it are kept device-local in `oros-studio-remote-join` `{code, rid, at}` (7 days, cleared on Deny), and `Link` takes `o.rid`, so a remote the PC already allowed rejoins without a new Allow while the PC still shows that code. In remote mode the join dialog is the page (no close button, Esc/Back keep it), `Stop controlling` returns to it with the code filled in, and a QR scanned while the app is open (only the hash changes) joins at once. Tablets in landscape with touch get bigger strips, faders and buttons; phones in landscape a compact transport.

### 2026-11-01 — Studio 4.93.01 — NULL Drum Machine back after the NULL JSFX 3.0 sync

- **Fixes:** the 3.0 effects sync (#760, in 4.93.00) gave `drum_machine` eight output pins (main + Snare, Hats and Perc pairs, `Outputs` Main/Groups). `loadCatalog` in `studio/fx.js` kept only instruments with `outs === 2`, so the Drum Machine left the instrument list and projects using it showed it as unknown. Instruments now pass with `ins === 0` and 2-16 output pins in pairs (`MAX_OUTS`).
- **Changes:** `studio/fxchain.worklet.js` gives a slot with more than two output pins its own extra buffers (`outsFor`, made in `make()`, never on the audio clock): pins 1/2 are the chain's pair, the rest is discarded, like REAPER on a two-channel track. Main mode sounds as before; with `Outputs` = Groups only the kick (pins 1/2) is heard. The generated effect code pads a short output list itself, but with new arrays every block, so the worklet no longer relies on it. Effects with more than two outputs (Band Splitter, Transient Split, the surround tools) stay out of the effect picker as before.
- **Files:** `studio/fx.js`, `studio/fxchain.worklet.js`, `tests/studio-mix.test.js`, `help/topics/whatsnew.{en,el}.txt`, `shell.js` (APP_VERSION).
- **Tests:** new test in `tests/studio-mix.test.js`: the shipped `studio/nullfx/fx/index.json` through the real `StudioFX().loadCatalog()` lists `drum_machine` (and every instrument passes exactly by the rule); the chain processor with the 3.0 Drum Machine: 8 outputs, pins 1/2 are the chain's buffers, the extra buffers stay the same every block, Main puts kick and snare on pins 1/2, Groups keeps the kick there and moves the snare to its own pins, no `error` or `missing`. It fails on the old `fx.js` and on the old worklet. Full `node --test tests/*.test.js`. Not tested in a browser.
- **Next:** proposal for Chris: in Studio, mix the group pairs into the main pair when `Outputs` = Groups (or hide that control), so the whole kit is heard whatever the setting.

### 2026-11-01 — Studio 4.93.02 — NULL Drum Machine: the group outputs mixed into the track

- **Decisions:** Chris, 2026-11-01 (proposal from 4.93.01): Studio mixes the extra output pairs of a multi-out instrument into its stereo pair instead of dropping them, so the Drum Machine's `Outputs` = Groups sounds whole (each group with its own Drive, Grit and Volume). Hiding the control was rejected: the interface comes from the NULL JSFX sync and would differ from REAPER and the other formats.
- **Changes:** `studio/fxchain.worklet.js` `P.mixDown(outs, n)` after each multi-out slot: pins 3, 5, … added to the left, 4, 6, … to the right (no allocation). With Main the extra pins are zero, so the output is the plugin's own pins 1/2 sample for sample. Comments in `studio/fx.js` updated.
- **Files:** `studio/fxchain.worklet.js`, `studio/fx.js`, `tests/studio-mix.test.js`, `help/topics/whatsnew.{en,el}.txt`, `shell.js` (APP_VERSION).
- **Tests:** the multi-out test in `tests/studio-mix.test.js` now checks: Main = the plugin's pins 1/2 exactly (pins 3-8 silent); Groups puts energy on pins 3-8 and the snare alone comes through the mix-down; Groups mixed down matches Main within 1e-4 for the default kit (no drive). It fails without `mixDown`. Full `node --test tests/*.test.js`. Not tested in a browser.

### 2026-11-01 — Studio Remote: Assisted effects with Learn, MIDI effects, pads and keys for NULL instruments on the remote (STUDIO-RA PR 3, #766) — 4.94.00
- **What:** the next step Chris approved for STUDIO-RA (2026-11-01, "Προτάσεις: ναι σε όλα": full NULL JSFX support on the remote). Studio's and the remote's effect pickers now list the `Assisted` category (Assisted EQ, Compressor, Reverb, Delay, new in NULL JSFX 3.0), and what an Assisted effect's `Learn` writes to its own sliders is saved with the track. On the remote, a track whose first effect is a NULL instrument gets `Pads` (drum instruments) or `Keys` that play it on the PC.
- **Changes (effects, `studio/fxchain.worklet.js` v1.1.0):** sliders an effect moves itself (`sliderchange()` / `slider_automate()` from @slider, @block or @sample; Learn calls `sliderchange` from @block) are collected from `Effect.changed` after each slot's block and reported every 16 blocks as `{ type: "sliders", uid, v: { i: value } }`, only for values that differ from what the page, automation or a file last set (`slot.known`, kept by the new `P.setSl()`), so the page's own moves and automation are never echoed back into the project. `studio/fx.js` `fromAudio()` saves a report as one undo step (`burst("fxa" + u)`), moves the interface and the slider row, and sends the values to the track's other chain (live or preview), not back to the one that reported. Export chains do not report. New strings `fx.catAssist` (EN/EL/DE).
- **Changes (MIDI effects; Chris chose "before the instrument" on 2026-11-01):** the 11 MIDI effects of NULL JSFX 3.0 (`index.json` `midi`: Arpeggiator, Chords, Drum Trigger, Euclid, Humanize, MIDI LFO, MIDI Utility, Note Echo, Pitch to MIDI, Riff, Scale) are synced (`.github/scripts/sync-nullfx.js` now copies `midi` too; run here against the 3.0 tag: 11 files added, nothing else changed) and join Studio's catalog with category `MIDI`. A chain is now MIDI effects, then the instrument, then audio effects: `instrumentOf()` is the first item after the MIDI effects; `withInstrument()` keeps the MIDI effects on top; `addTo()` puts a MIDI effect after the other MIDI effects; `movable()` lets an item move only within its group (both pickers' arrows use it, `moveIn()` enforces it). The `MIDI` category shows only for a chain with an instrument (`cats()`, Studio and remote). Old chains (instrument first) keep their meaning. The worklet passes the block's MIDI through the slots in order: after a slot that uses MIDI, the next slots get what it sent (`midiOut`, sorted by offset); a bypassed slot passes it on. The preview chain (keys, auditions, the remote's pads) is the MIDI effects plus the instrument (`pv.us`, `pv.sig` rebuilds it when they change). The remote now names instruments in a chain (`infoOf` included only effects, so an instrument showed as an unknown effect).
- **Changes (remote, `studio/remote.js`, PROTO stays 1):** the snapshot gains `nt: 1` (the PC takes notes) and per track `ins` (`"drums"` or `"piano"`, from `nxKind`, only for a NULL instrument). New command `{ t: "nt", id, n, v }` (v 0 = let go): the host accepts it only for a track with `ins`, whole numbers 0..127, and a release only for a note it holds (`H.held`); held notes are released when the link drops, the remote goes or the PC stops sharing. `host.note()` in `studio.js` plays it with `nxNote()` on the track's preview chain (like the PC's own keys) and, while that track records MIDI, records it with `recEvent()`. The remote's `rup-dlg`: 16 General MIDI drum pads (36 bottom left .. 51; higher on a pad is louder, 40..127), or two octaves of keys with octave −3..+3 and a finger sliding from key to key; one button switches pads and keys; Space/Enter hold a focused pad; everything held is released on close, when the page is hidden, or when the console closes. Older PCs send no `nt`, so an updated remote shows no pads there; an older remote ignores `nt` and `ins`.
- **Files:** `studio/fxchain.worklet.js`, `studio/fx.js`, `studio/remote.js`, `studio/studio.js`, `studio/index.html`, `studio/studio.css`, `i18n/de/studio.js`, `studio/help.{en,el}.txt`, `i18n/de/help/studio.txt`, `help/topics/whatsnew.{en,el}.txt`, `shell.js` (APP_VERSION), `.github/scripts/sync-nullfx.js`, `studio/nullfx/fx/{arpeggiator,chords,drum_trigger,euclid,humanize,midi_lfo,midi_utility,note_echo,pitch_to_midi,riff,scale}.js` (new, generated by the sync), `tests/studio-learn.test.js` (new), this Bible.
- **Tests:** full `node --test tests/*.test.js`; new `tests/studio-learn.test.js` (5): Chords before Keys in the chain processor turns one note into a chord for Keys, bypassed it passes the note alone; the ordering rules run on their own (instrument after the MIDI effects, MIDI effects kept on top, moves only within a group); every `midi` entry has its file; Assisted EQ in the chain processor learns from a second of noise and reports `Learned` and its bands once, the page's own Learn switch and automation are not reported; both pickers list Assisted; the `nt` checks, the releases and the strings in EN/EL/DE. Playwright Chromium, PC 1280×800 + phone 393×851 (touch) with the relay mocked: strips with a Kick and a Keys instrument show `Pads` and `Keys`; a pad press sends note on 36 (velocity 122 near the top) and off to the preview chain; a slide on the keys plays 60 then 62 and closing lets go; the remote's picker shows One Slider, Essentials, Advanced, Assisted on an audio track and also MIDI on the Keys track; adding Arpeggiator there puts it after Chords and above Keys on the PC; the preview chain for the Keys pads is `[chords, keys]`; EN and EL at 393 px, no page errors. Not tested: Learn end to end in a browser with real audio (covered at the processor level), a real phone, the live relay.
- **Next:** NULL Drum Machine has 8 outputs and is dropped by `loadCatalog`, fixed in its own thread.

### 2026-11-01 — 5.00.00 — Passwords: desktop autofill in the orOS browser add-on 2.0 (PW-AF1) (#778)

- **What:** wave 3 of 5 of the Passwords plan (Part IX PW-AF1, Part IV "Desktop autofill", "Browser add-on"). The add-on ("orOS", 2.0.0) gets a popup: unlock with the master password, logins and 2FA codes for the site, cards / identities / addresses for any site, fill on a click, lock; options for the lock time and "Forget the vault copy". The zip is built and published to the GitHub release `browser-addon` by the new workflow; the download page replaces "Coming soon" with the download and install steps (EN `#addon`, EL `#addon-el`; a `#…-el` fragment opens the Greek page). Help EN/EL/DE: new "Fill on websites" section; the old "no autofill" limit replaced. Field labels are matched without accents (a Greek "Όνομα κατόχου" missed the accented regex in the first e2e run).
- **Files:** `extension/` (`manifest.json` 2.0.0, `background.js`, `popup.{html,js,css}` new, `pmfill.js` new, `pmvault.js` new, `pm/` copies new, `options.{html,js,css}`, `_locales/{en,el}/messages.json`, `README.md`, `PRIVACY.md`), `.github/scripts/ext-pm.js` (new), `.github/workflows/addon.yml` (new), `download/index.html` (+ CSP hash), `passwords/help.{en,el}.txt`, `i18n/de/help/passwords.txt`, `help/topics/whatsnew.{en,el}.txt`, `shell.js` (5.00.00), `tests/extension.test.js`, `tests/extension-pm.test.js` (new).
- **Tests:** full `node --test tests/*.test.js`; new `tests/extension-pm.test.js` (5: copies identical + manifest / CSP / no innerHTML; `fits` table incl. look-alikes, sibling sub-domains, ports and http; `matches` order; payload without PIN / document numbers / notes; `pmvault` with a fake browser API: ciphertext-only copy, merge never drops, wrong password, key-only session with lock time, expiry, newer-format slice kept whole). Playwright with the real add-on in Chromium, vault made with real Argon2id: copy read from an orOS tab, unlock, wrong password message, login + 2FA code filled (input/change events, search field untouched), card filled from Greek labels, address filled, card in a cross-site payment frame filled only after the named confirmation (a 1 px frame ignored), PIN not on the page, look-alike host `shop.example.test.evil.test` offered nothing, a navigation after opening refused, lock empties the session; no errors. Not tested: Firefox, Edge, Brave, a store install, a real Stripe or bank form.

### 2026-11-01 — 5.01.00 — Passwords: autofill on Android (PW-AF2) (#778)

- **What:** wave 4 of 5 of the Passwords plan (Part IX PW-AF2, Part IV "Phone autofill", BR-PHONE v8). The orOS Android app becomes an autofill service: Passwords › Menu › `Autofill on this phone` (only inside the app) seals the fill lists with the phone's Keystore keys and hands them over after every unlock and change; Android suggestions are locked and filled after the fingerprint, face or screen lock; apps by package name (`androidapp://`) or a link confirmed on the phone; browsers by the add-on's site rule.
- **Files:** `passwords/afindex.js` (new), `passwords/pmapp.js` (section 9b, menu item, hooks), `passwords/passwords.js` (option `af`), `phone.js` (v8 messages, `afInfo`, `afKeys`, `afAskKeys`, `afSend`, `afClear`, `afSettings`), `android/` (`AfVault.java`, `AfMatch.java`, `OrosAutofillService.java`, `AfAuthActivity.java` new; `PhoneBridge.java`, `PermissionActivity.java`, `tools/gen.js`, `res/layout/af_item.xml`, `res/xml/autofill_service.xml`, strings EN/EL/DE, `README.md`), `i18n/de/passwords.js`, help EN/EL/DE, `help/topics/whatsnew.{en,el}.txt`, `sw.js` (precache), `shell.js`, `tests/passwords-autofill.test.js` (new).
- **Tests:** full `node --test tests/*.test.js`; new `tests/passwords-autofill.test.js` (5). The new Java compiled with javac against Android 15 (Robolectric android-all); `AfMatch` site rule table, EL/DE field words and the RFC 6238 SHA-1 / SHA-256 vectors run on a plain JVM; a WebCrypto-sealed list opened with Java's `RSA/ECB/OAEPWithSHA-1AndMGF1Padding` + `AES/GCM/NoPadding`. Playwright in the real shell, EL 360 px and EN 1280 px, with a stubbed bridge holding real RSA-OAEP keys: the menu item only with the bridge, switch on → keys asked → lists sealed and sent 2 s later (opened again in the page: names without secrets, index with the password and TOTP), Android settings button, a saved change sends again, switch off clears and stores `af: 0`, no overflow, no errors. The APK is built by `android.yml` on this PR. Not tested: a real phone (Keystore, fingerprint, apps, Chrome / Firefox autofill).

### 2026-11-01 — 5.02.00 — Passwords: saving new logins (PW-AF3) (#778)

- **What:** wave 5 of 5 of the Passwords plan (Part IX PW-AF3, Part IV "Saving new logins", BR-PHONE v8 `af-save`). The add-on's `Save the login from this page` and Android's `Save to orOS Passwords?` hand the typed login to Passwords in orOS, which opens it in the editor (new entry, or a new password for the same site and user with the old one in the history) and stores it only on Save. Also: the Passwords footer now points to the add-on instead of saying orOS fills nothing on websites. First open lighter: `kdbx.js` (KeePass, 38 KB) is no longer in `passwords/index.html`; `pmapp.js` `loadKdbx()` loads it for Import (before parsing a file, so KeePass XML works too) and Export, and sets its Argon2 loader then.
- **Files:** `shell.js` (`__orosPwSave`, `__orosTakePwSave`, the window message, `pwSaveReady` after the app list), `passwords/pmapp.js` (`queueSave`, `nextSave`, `PmApp.saveLogin`, editor `pre.user` / `pre.newPw` / note), `passwords/passwords.js` (`takeSaves`, `__orosPwPoke`), `passwords/afindex.js` (1.1.0: `saveItem`, `findSave`), `passwords/passwords.css` (`.pv-note`), `passwords/index.html` (no `kdbx.js`), `phone.js` (`af-save`), `extension/` (`pmfill.js` `readLogin`, `popup.*`, `background.js` delivery, locales EN/EL, README, PRIVACY), `android/` (`OrosAutofillService` SaveInfo + `onSaveRequest`, `AfVault` save queue, `AfMatch.pickPassword`, `PhoneBridge`, strings EN/EL/DE, README), `i18n/de/passwords.js`, help EN/EL/DE, `help/topics/whatsnew.{en,el}.txt`, `tests/passwords-autofill.test.js`.
- **Tests:** full `node --test tests/*.test.js`; `tests/passwords-autofill.test.js` 4 new. Playwright in the real shell (EL mobile, EN desktop) and with the real add-on in Chromium against orOS served from the checkout (see Part IV). KeePass import (KDBX 4, Argon2id) in the real shell after the change: `Kdbx` absent at first open, loaded on choosing the file, 3 logins read. Java compiled with javac against Android 15 (Robolectric android-all). Not tested: a real phone, Firefox.
